title: Report Card For Ravens Rookie Play Caller After 5 Games: Straight A's?
full_text:
The greatest unknown for the 2027 Baltimore Ravens – a team that was changing its identity in a major way for the first time in nearly 20 years with John Harbaigh gone as coach -was on the offensive side of the ball.
The greatest risks with this team, in terms of roster and coaching, came on offense, with first-time play caller Declan Doyle, basically the same age as quarterback Lamar Jackson , taking the reigns for the first time, implementing an offense that did not previously exist and doing it with some very significant questions about the interior of the offensive line. The degree of difficulty for Doyle was already significant – would anyone besides Zay Flowers make plays downfield?  – and it ramped up further with that offensive line repeatedly collapsing and Baltimore entering Week 6 looking at perhaps it’s sixth different combination of starting linemen.
Oh, and the defense that was supposed to carry the team early has been mostly meh, and it’s already blown two 11-point leads that Doyle’s unit built, and a secondary loaded with top draft picks and huge contracts has been largely suspect in coverage so far . Special teams blunders also had plenty to do with the team’s lone loss (4-1), and Doyle has had to operate without Flowers for large chunks of games or one game entirely, and his alleged move tight end (Mark Andrews on a silly contract extension) can’t actually move much and his left tackle missed time and Lamar Jackson didn’t play last week and hasn’t practiced fully in quite some time.
“There’s challenges every week, whether it’s at quarterback or different wideouts, or different tight ends as you lose guys throughout the year,” Doyle said Thursday before practice. “I’ve said it to the group, ‘It’s all about fixing this week’s problems.'”
And Doyle has navigated it all overwhelmingly with tremendous Aplomb. No, that’s not a typo (though heaven knows I make my share) – that “A” is capitalized for a reason. I’m tempted to go with an A+ here, honestly, but it’s still a little early for that. It’s been a pretty Amazing start, and here’s some of what stood out in him earning that grade:
So some fears were confirmed – at least so far – about Andrews being cooked and the lack of a go-to pass catcher for chunk yards besides Flowers. But man, if he’s going to be a one-man army, let him do it in truly historic fashion where he is showing up in the endzone and in the redzone like never before. And cashing in. His five redzone targets are already half of last season’s total and he’s on pace to shatter his career high of 13 (remember he’s only run 91 routes all season due to injury).
Doyle has already used flowers three times as much in the backfield as he was deployed there ALL OF LAST SEASON, and made sage adjustments to the perimeter run game when in IOL cratered. He ramped Flowers slot usage from 38% in his first three years to 52% this season and he’s been close to unstoppable with a two-way go there.
Flowers has produced like a top five receiver and given that Rashod Bateman remains mostly a decoy and Devontez Walker is super fringy and rookie start Ja’Kobi Lane has played one half of football all season due to injury and Andrews and Bateman lead this team in route runs by a mile with little to show for it because of the injuries, they’ve needed that sort of ascent from an already very good football player.
For all the explosion in this attack and with Doyle rightfully backing up Flowers and Jackson calling him a “genius” this summer, by and large, managing games and managing the clock and playing complimentary football with a struggling defense matters greatly. And it can be very hard for some young coordinators to live with “three-yards-and-a-cloud of dust” when dictated by margin, down, distance, game flow, time remaining.
The personnel problems have put Doyle in situations where repeatedly the KISS method – not pyro makeup; just Keep It Simple Stupid – is what was required and he's leaned into that and accepted the ugliness in the stats that come with it. The fact that Derrick Henry has run more times through five games than any 32-year-old running back since the 1970 merger speaks to that (and that despite Henry sporting a league-average 4.2 yards/carry and not the 5.5/carry from his first two years here).
He’s understood by and large the significant limitations of this offensive line at times and tried to help them out. Recently losing “Joker” blocking tight end Durham Smythe was another hue blow and Doyle had some interesting workarounds in the game plan in Sunday’s comeback win at Atlanta. He also brought along back-up Snoop Huntley in a smart, old-school manner in that game and didn’t have him attacking the middle of the field until the final two-minute drill, and he’s woven Henry more into the screen game than before to help combat pass-protection issues and a bogged-down run game at times.
“I think he is the most brilliant offensive mind in football right now,“ right tackle Roger Rosengarten said. “I think he's done a great job with weaving in those play calls when the right time is called. I think anytime you call a screen, it's about time and operation with those sorts of things. Dec is one-of-one at calling them and making sure they're called at the right times.”
Doyle isn’t repeating the same mistakes over and over. That hasn’t always been the case around here.
When it becomes clear that trying to run between the tackles isn’t going great, he adjusts. When he takes the ball out of Henry’s hands and Lamar’s hands in critical third downs of what became a loss against the Saints, and his offensive line gets further compromised by injury, he leans into old-school stuff on the ground. He has to get major credit – along with the entire staff and especially OL coach Dwayne Ledford – for getting rookie guard Vega Ioane to perform so admirably thrust into center with difficult defensive assignments.
He’s using more pre-snap motion and cadence than ever before, he installed the under-center offense we knew was coming and, yes, there have been too many penalties in part because of some of that, but this offense is exceling on early downs despite all those issues and they are finishing drives despite some short-yardage issues.
The Ravens rank fourth in points scored and sixth in total Offensive Expected Points Added and sixth in points/drive and Jackson looks primed for another MVP run. If Doyle keeps this up, the buzz for possible head coaching openings will be very real by Christmas, maybe even Thanksgiving.
We’ll have another progress report by then.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: 4 Reasons The Browns Could Upset The Ravens Sunday
full_text:
The Ravens have a way of coming up small in Cleveland.
Weird things happen. They tend to undermine themselves. And now they have this Todd Monken thing to deal with, as Baltimore’s former offensive coordinator was pushed out as part of John Harbaugh’s staff only to land as the Browns head coach. Cleveland already has one upset divisional win, beating the Steelers on a Thursday night, and they will be focused for this game coming off a letdown at the Jets on Sunday.
This will be Ravens rookie head coach Jesse Minter’s first AFC North game, the Ravens are once against dealing with a cumbersome injury report (19 names listed on Wednesday really is something) and it’s no sure thing that Lamar Jackson starts at quarterback despite how some want to couch it.
Every game the Ravens have played this season has ended up pretty snug by the fourth quarter, even the two in which they opened up an 11-point lead, and there is reason to believe the Browns (3-2) can hang around and put some pressure on the Ravens (4-1). And maybe even pull off the upset.
Here are the primary reasons why:
The Browns have a diverse pass game right now with some guys who can get deep and guys who win with YAC and underneath stuff and a move tight end who creates real problems on third down and in the redzone and the Ravens are having big issues there. They are young and fast, and that will present problems even with a weak QB. The Ravens have mostly faced weak QBs.
Baltimore’s corners and free safeties haven’t really been able to cover anyone this season and Monken will not be afraid to chuck the ball all over the yard. And given Cleveland’s extreme issues running the ball , all the more reason to attack a secondary that has suffered. The film and the data is rough, Minter has been exposed in dime coverage and maybe a ramped up pass rush will be the difference but even suspect NFL QBs are  not afraid to challenge the Ravens corners.
"They are explosive," free safety Malaki Starks said. "I think they do a lot within the offense, and they create explosive plays, so that is definitely something that we want to stay on top of."
Monken knows how to motivate a team and he has these young Browns eating out of his hand right now and he’d love nothing more than the beat the Ravens, who fired him and a front officed that made it pretty clear it believed the last coaching staff was holding back their roster. Oh, and the Ravens skill guys were calling Monken’s replacement, 30-year-old Declan Doyle, a “genius” all summer in what looked like shade at the former guy.
Monken will call this game in a let-it-all-hang-out manner and hold nothing back. Look out for some trick plays, maybe a fake punt. He knows most of this Ravens roster pretty well. How they play and how many of them think. Should be an advantage for him.
"I think their offense will definitely try to come at us, and I think their defense will too," Ravens corner Marlon Humphrey said. "Their defense is always really good, but their offense, with the versatility that [Browns head coach] Todd [Monken] calls games, we will have our hands full."
The Ravens are getting strong play from young guard-turned-center-turned-guard Vega Ioane. Like, astonishingly good stuff under the circumstances. But the GM made a panic move and overpaid for the Eagles center-turned-guard/injury-liability Cam Jurgens and they really want to jam him in the middle of the offensive line Sunday.
Except, well, he still doesn’t really know anyone yet and hasn’t ever practiced with the team and they traded for him while he was still in the concussion protocol (which is why other GMs were telling me Eric DeCosta looks incredibly desperate here ). So, even if Jurgens practices close to full Thursday, that’s the last real work day of the week and everything is so new and different, do they really need to rush this?
And if they do, and if Jurgens isn’t nearly as ready to hold down center as Ioane was, and if a sixth-straight different offensive line combination creates havoc and the interior isn’t connected and the A Gap becomes a problem, against a game Cleveland defense, that’s a great way to blow a game.
"There's kind of some unfamiliarity, and it's kind of hard to get in the groove sometimes," right tackle Roger Rosengarten said of the constantly changing lineups. "But if we're all playing together and are all on the same page, good things will happen."
They call Cleveland the Factory of Sadness and it’s truly remarkable just how little good has come to this franchise since the Browns emerged from relocation to Baltimore as an expansion team. It’s been incredibly bleak and the one-sided nature of this rivalry – the Ravens win two Super Bowls and Cleveland is still waiting for its first – makes it even tougher.
But over the last decade, a lot of weird stuff has happened to the Ravens in Cleveland. Guys getting hurt. Players dropping interceptions in rampant succession. Ugly, upset losses. It tends to be a struggle, and the crowd is always up for these games and throw in the Monken thing and the gutsy the young Browns have displayed and there is reason to believe this could be anything but a blowout.
"I am hoping that trend ends Sunday," Humphrey said, "but it is just a hard place to play. I think, like you said, it has just always been weird ... There have just been all types of things that have happened in Cleveland. I think one year, maybe when I was a rookie, we threw maybe two interceptions on the 5-yard line. Just crazy things happen, but the biggest thing is stay together."
The Browns are 4-4 in their last eight at home against the Ravens. This is the sixth time in the last nine meetings where Baltimore is a favorite of three points or more. The Browns get up for these games and only three of these eight games were decided by more than a touchdown.

title: Ravens Continue To Exorcise Demons Of Past Failures With Falcons Win
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens went in a different direction at head coach after having John Harbaugh at the helm for nearly two decades was that in recent years, in no small part because his teams kept finding ways to lose games.
Whether it was blowing double-digit or fourth-quarter leads, coming out flat in games they were favored to win or not being able to find ways to pull off and close out comebacks, they became more synonymous with choking than being clutch.
Just five games into the Jesse Minter era, as just the fourth head coach in franchise history, the Ravens have already shown that they're not letting the tendencies that led to shortcomings in the past determine future outcomes.
They held onto a double-digit lead against a talented offense on the road in Week 1, orchestrated the fastest game-winning drive in NFL history at seven seconds in Week 3 and ground out a one-score win in Week 4 despite getting shut out and losing their starting quarterback for the entire second half.
This past Sunday, they went on the road to face what had been one of the hottest teams of the previous two weeks, without their highest-paid players on both sides of the ball available, including Lamar Jackson, and still found themselves on the right side of history again.
With their 30-23 comeback victory over the Atlanta Falcons in overtime in Week 5, the Ravens became the first team to win a game down by eight or more points in the final minute in four years, which, according to E SPN's Jamison Hensley per ESPN Research , snapped a 581-game losing streak for teams that found themselves in those situations.
After hauling in the game-winning interception and his first since  Week 17 of the 2024 season, three-time All Pro safety Kyle Hamilton didn't mince words when talking about the significance of this win not only for him being back in his hometown of Atlanta but for the Ravens as a whole team and their revamped culture under Minter.
"That is a game that we have lost many times. Whether it is, some fluky stuff happening or whatever," Hamilton said. "That is just us getting over some sort of hump or dark cloud. I am excited for the future."
Even the Ravens' lone setback of the season thus far, when they lost to the New Oreleans Saints in their Week 2 home opener , in which they opened the fourth quarter with an eight-point lead, only to get outscored 15-0 in the final period, served a purpose in the maturation of this year's team.
"Confidence is gained by going through things and going through things together, and I do not know if we would have the results of the last three weeks if the Saints game did not happen," Minter said. "I think there are always ways you can take losses like that. You can learn from them and really try to improve, get better, look at the things that you did well and build on things. I think we did that after that game."
Despite looking like the more physical and well-prepared team out of the gate, with the offense moving the ball well with backup quarterback Tyler Huntley and the defense forcing three straight three-and-outs, the Ravens' win in Atlanta was anything but a cakewalk. They had to overcome adversity in the form of bad drops, a fumble recovery returned for a touchdown against them and the Falcons getting hot on third-and-long, starting in the second quarter.
Even when at full strength with their two-time league MVP healthy and under center, the Ravens found ways to lose the type of games rather than find a way to come out on top. The fact they're finding ways to finish late in games with quick or time-consuming drives, coupled with a few key stops on defense, is evidence that these aren't the same old Ravens whose downfall felt inevitable at times because they hadn't consistently shown an ability to be at their best when their best is required.
"[With] this particular team, to be able to do that, I think is definitely a major benefit to the psyche, the confidence and the belief that we can win games like that in the fourth quarter," Minter said.
After avoiding some close calls with prominent players during training camp and preseason, the Ravens were hit extremely hard with the injury bug over the first month of the season. They had standout rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane suffer a fractured wrist that required surgery in the season opener, lost their top two centers in the same game in Week 3 and had prized free agent addition, four-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Trey Hendrickson, suffer a finger injury that caused him to miss the last two games while recovering from a minor procedure.
While their initial injury report on Wednesday looked a mile long with nearly two dozen names, the fact that it featured several key players with encouraging status designations is a sign good news on the horizon.
Wednesday's Injury Report pic.twitter.com/OnTJmaKHOD
Although Jackson missed his fourth straight practice with the ankle sprain he sustained on the second-to-last play of the first half in Week 3, both Hendrickson and Lane were listed as full participants. Two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens, whom they acquired via trade last week, was wearing a red non-contact jersey in his first practice as a Raven, as he remains in the final stages of the concussion protocol, but he remains on track to make his first start this upcoming Sunday.
At 4-1, the Ravens currently sit alone atop the AFC North standings, and with back-to-back games against the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals, they're getting key players back and upgrades at important positions for a key juncture in their schedule. If they want to win the division, return to the playoffs after just missing out last year and establish themselves as the cream of the crop in the conference and league as a whole, they'll need to get healthy and hot at the right time.

title: How Hard Are Ravens Pushing Derrick Henry? The Data Is Alarming
full_text:
Ravens rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle would not back away from the potential for Derrick Henry to carry the ball 300 times or more this season, despite him being 32-years-old and despite him having never hit that mark in three straight seasons in his Hall of Fame.
Turns out, there was every reason to take him at his word.
Henry is being asked to do, already, things no running back his age has done since the NFL/AFL merger through five weeks of a season, and there is not reason to expect that to change much anytime soon. The Ravens have had to navigate through a new offensive line every week and huge issues at center (including moving rookie guard Vega Ioane there ), and they could very well be without two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson again this week, and it’s been a tough slow on the ground this season in ways Henry never experienced previously in Baltimore, but he is nothing if not a workhorse.
And despite this unprecedented load – as we will detail below – Henry still appeared to be one of the freshest and more impactful players Sunday night as the Ravens produced a game-winning, seven-minute drive in overtime, with backup Snoop Huntley at QB, during which Henry went over 100 yards and had the ball in his hands 25 more times and was at his best putting the game away.
“Obviously, we wanted to score, but I think having that drive was great for us to be able to keep the momentum going, keep the drive going, letting the clock run down, and just keeping that energy,” Henry said after the gutsy win. “I feel like guys were just focused on another level, and  great execution by every single body on offense. The O-line - hell of a job. They did a great job in the run game."
Henry is not having his most explosive season, and he is getting hit behind the line of scrimmage more than ever before as a Raven as part of the experimentation up front, but he remains as integral as ever to this offense and to keep a defense suffering from its share of issues off the field . And no Ravens coach has ever ridden him harder through the first five weeks of a season. And perhaps he could use more help from a blocking standpoint , too).
What he’s taking on already is simply historic.
Henry’s 113 carries through the first five games are the most in NFL history by a running back in his age 32 season. The great Walter Payton is second at 110, Curtis Martin has 105 at this point in that season and Otis Anderson (98) and Emmitt Smith (87) are the only others to carry the ball more than 80 times at that age at this point in the season.
Henry leads them with seven touchdowns through five weeks, while his 4.2 yards/carry is basically league average (Payton was at 4.6 at this point, while Ricky Williams, the only age 32 back since the merger to average over. 4.5/carry in that season, had run just 61 times through Week 5 (but at a robust 5.2/carry). We studied 55 years of age 32 running back data this offseason and the general portrait it painted was quite bleak – but Henry has long been a unicorn and if he gets more consistent run blocking there is reason to believe some of his efficiencies could spike.
Henry’s 476 yards are 30 behind “Sweetness” – the Bears legend who proved incredibly durable and consistent – for the most ever by an age 32 RB through five weeks. When Doyle refused to back away from lofty projection in terms of touches for Henry, he was not foolin around .
“He is a special talent,” Doyle said of Henry this summer. “There are not many guys in the league who can do what he does. The vision for him in the offense is an immense role. Obviously, I don't want to put a number on the amount of [carries], because obviously, as you look at every single week, every week is different. You want to be able to deploy things in different ways, and at the same point in time, he's going to have a pretty large workload.”
Only once previously in his career has Henry run the ball this much through the first five games, and that was in 2001 in Tennessee (142). Think about how the Titans ran their offense through him, and only once did he eclipse this 113 carry mark this soon.
Last year, Henry had just 64 rushes at this point in the season, and the year before he had 95. He’s essentially played one more game to this point than either of those two years at mid-October. In those seasons he was averaging 5.0 and 6.0 per carry to this point, so the yards have been tougher to come by now (0.99 yards before contact this season, 1.77 at this point last year and 2.66 in 2024).
Henry also already has eight catches for 62 yards and a touchdown; he’s never had more than 15 catches in a season as a Raven.
So, um, what exactly would it look like if Henry maintained this pace for the full season? Well, it would be painful, that’s for sure.
He is averaging 22.6 rushes per game, with would yield 384 carries if he kept it up. I did mention he’s never run 300 times in three straight years didn’t I? The 384 carries would surpass anything he’s ever done before. That 2021 season – the only time with more carries through five weeks – was cut short due to injury and he only played eight games.
Henry’s never carried more than 325 in a season in Baltimore and 378 is his career high (2000), the year he went over 2000 rushing yards. Perhaps that will truly be put to the test.

title: Lamar Jackson's Ankle Injury Is Still A Problem In Week 6
full_text:
The possibility that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss another game with his ankle injury looms after the two-time MVP was unable to practice again on Wednesday. This week always presented a tricky challenge with Jackson’s health paramount and the team also juggling yet another unusual situation at center.
Head coach Jesse Minter spoke at the time of Jackson’s injury in Week 4 as if he may have had  chance to re-enter the game – that was never happening, by the way – which may have skewed the way some fans view the injury. But ankle issues can he difficult for running quarterbacks and while the team has called this “day-to-day” at times the reality was it was always “week-to-week” with a real chance he does not return until Week 7 as we have been pointing out.
Minter again couched the injury as “day-to-day,” but it also seems less than ideal that Jackson would likely only practice limited Thursday (him coming back from this long out and practicing fully right away would be a surprise) and then go into a walkthrough Friday and play. Minter reiterated that Jackson can play without practicing, but given where this injury is on his body, and how the Ravens have been handling injuries in general early this season , that may end up being empty rhetoric to try to plant doubt with the Browns as to who is playing.
“It’s definitely day-to-day,” Minter said, and alluding to his original description of the timetable added, “I think a lot of times those things, right when they happen, you’re not sure … When he’s able to be out there, he will.”
Back-up Snoop Huntley was excellent in the fourth quarter and overtime of a comeback win at Atlanta on Sunday. If Huntley gets the bulk of the reps with another totally new center – recent trade acquisition Cam Jurgens – and then Jackson gets the start, that would be a little odd.
Jurgens was never going to be able to practice fully right away as he was acquired – for a desperately steep price – from the Eagles last week after just entering the concussion protocol. He must continue to get cleared for more work with doctors and if he is unable to still practice fully on Thursday it further cuts into the timeframe to work with the quarterbacks.
It also remains to be seen if Jurgens is actually an upgrade of rookie guard Vega Ioane, who was doing an exception job all things considered.
Minter essentially confirmed that top pass rusher Trey Hendrickson is getting fully cleared to return after having a procedure on his injured finger two weeks ago. “I expect him to be able to play,” the coach said, adding he is “super excited to get him back.” The Ravens badly need a more consistent edge push on third down, with their secondary getting picked apart on that money down and the cornerbacks the biggest underachievers on this roster by a wide margin.
Receiver Rashod Bateman has been limited but Minter implied he will be good to go and the Ravens are hopeful that rookie receiver Ja’Kobi Lane will be returning from Injured Reserve as well. Rookie tight end Matthew Hibner – who should be in line for way more snaps with starting end Mark Andrews fading fast – is dealing with a hand injury but he was able to return on Sunday night and play the second half after suffering the setback.

title: Ravens Week 5 Rookie Report: Vega Ioane Shines In Primetime
full_text:
Several members of the Baltimore Ravens' 2026 rookie class saw extended action in Sunday's overtime thriller of a 30-23 road win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5. They are in an AFC North division in which every team's record is above .500, and at 4-1, they sit alone atop the standings heading into next week.
Drafted and undrafted first-year players saw extensive playing time in all three phases. The only rookies who were healthy scratches were fourth-round wide receiver Elijah Sarratt and undrafted quarterback Joe Fagnano, who still suited up as an emergency No. 3 option. Fifth-round running back Adam Randall wasn't activated from short-term injured reserve in his first week of eligibility, while third-round wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane is now eligible to be activated from the list. Seventh-round defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny is on the practice squad and has yet to be elevated.
Here’s an overview of how these rookies performed in their late taste of NFL regular-season action.
The first-round interior offensive lineman made his second straight and final start at center before sliding back over to right guard and was superb once again. While some of his non-under-center snaps weren't on point all night, his blocking performance was, as he didn't allow a single pressure on 38 pass-blocking reps and his 71.9 run-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus was the highest on the team. Ioane was leading the way on several of the Ravens' biggest and most important plays, whether it was Zay Flowers' 13-yard run on the first play from scrimmage of the game, Derrick Henry's 18-yard touchdown on a screen play and Tyler Huntley's quarterback sneaks that included the game-winning score.
"For him to be able to do what he has done, play the way that he has played, [it is] pretty remarkable, I would say," head coach Jesse Minter said. "I do not know who votes for Rookie of the Year and all that stuff, and it is really, really early in the season, but he is a very impactful rookie for our team that has done things that I do not know that any rookies have ever done. Having to play those two positions [and] get shifted over to center in a game where you have to go on a drive to try to win the game, then to play the way that he has played in these big moments, [it is] pretty cool to see."
The second-rounder was one of several players for whom this game served as a homecoming, as he wasn't just born and raised in Georgia; Atlanta is his hometown, where he played at Westlake High School. He played a season-high 40.6% of the Ravens' total defensive snaps, set a strong edge on early downs against the run and finished with a pair of total tackles, including a solo takedown of Falcons star running back Bijan Robinson for a minimal gain of three yards in the first quarter.
Young had his first career tackle for a loss negated on the Ravens' huge fourth-down stop in the third quarter after official review ruled that the completion to tight end Charlie Woerner , whom he tackled two yards behind the line of scrimmage, was incomplete. Either way, he was at the right place at the right time to prevent a successful conversion.
HUGE STOP 😤 Tune in on @SNFonNBC pic.twitter.com/1j7Gz2M720
The fourth-rounder made his second straight start, and the only reason he saw a slight reduction in his playing time instead of another increase was that he left the game on a cart at one point due to a hand injury. However, he'd eventually not only return to action but make a key block on one of the biggest plays of the game, where he helped spring Henry into the end zone on the game-tying two
Derrick Henry's game-tying 2 Pt conversion run looks like an option "read", but really isn't. The blocking scheme looks similar to "Down" from the Wing-T, meaning Henry is supposed to follow the block of Matthew Hibner. The future HOFer had other plans. #Ravens @11OnceSport pic.twitter.com/0EJLRETJkS
With the Ravens going up against a run-centric offense, the fifth-round nickel saw his fewest snaps on defense in the four games he's played in, with 19, but he did play a season-high 15 snaps on special teams. He recorded a pair of solo tackles, struggled at times in coverage and had a bad whiff on a missed tackle that came on third-and-long and allowed Falcons rookie wide receiver Zachariah Branch to pick up a first down on a career-long 23.
The fifth-rounder saw an uptick in his playing time for the third week in a row, with 31 combined snaps between offense and special teams, including a season-high 19 on offense and 12 on special teams. While his three-time Pro Bowl veteran mentor, Mark Andrews, had a nightmarish night struggling to hold on to the ball as a pass catcher on half a dozen targets, Cuevas did not, reeling in both passes that came his way for new career highs with two receptions for 26 receiving yards with a long of 17 yards.
¡VENGA! ¡Josh Cuevas 🇲🇽 con la recepción para acercar a los Ravens a zona de puntos! 👐🏈 📺💻 @ESPNmx @disneyplusla pic.twitter.com/GcnnuQIDNF
The sixth-round specialist had back-to-back stellar performances, with a game that saw him be a field-flipping weapon once again, as a key to helping the Ravens win the battle of field position. He pinned the Falcons' offense inside their 20-yard line three times on his four punts, averaged 44.3 yards per punt with a long of 54 and didn't have a single punt returned against him for the second time this season.
With four-time Pro Bowl veteran edge rusher Trey Hendrickson out recovering from finger surgery a second straight week, the undrafted free agent played double-digit snaps on defense again after playing exclusively on special teams through the first three weeks. During his 17 snaps, Burke recorded a career-high three total tackles, including a solo takedown of Robinson for a minimal gain of four yards in the second quarter.
Although he wasn't credited with a pass defensed, he was responsible for forcing an incompletion to Falcons wide receiver Drake London on a flat route on a play where he dropped into underneath coverage instead of rushing. His 22 snaps on special teams were the most among all rookies and the second-most on the team overall.
Play action starts with getting the protection right imo. Ravens slant the D-Line to the right and send Hamilton on a nickel blitz throwing off the protection and killing London as the first read in the flat. Still rushing 5 like they show presnap but changing it postsnap. pic.twitter.com/GhXWVSBV3r

title: Ravens 3 Biggest Needs 1 Month Before Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Ravens already made their biggest swing at the trade deadline, giving quite a haul to the Eagles to find out if Cam Jurgens can still play center.
It was a massive pay in terms of draft-pick compensation including a future second-round pick, and it was a steep price in terms of taking on $15M fully guaranteed next year on top of a $16.5M salary this season for a player who may or may not have been getting benched in Philadelphia who carries extreme injury risk. So there’s that.
Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta has swung big heading into the deadline – which comes in early November, many years in his long reign and he’s only stuck impact once, landing Roquan Smith from Chicago to try to fix the defense in 2023; then he overpaid Smith with a hasty contract extension has felt the sting of that since. So thinking he will navigate this crucial time of the roster landscape expertly demand hopes and prayers, and with a team-record payroll and after the Jurgens trade I wouldn’t expect much.
That doesn’t mean more needs won’t develop between now and the deadline. And it certainly doesn’t mean they won’t do anything to address them.  As it stands now, the Ravens are in expert health from a long-term standpoint and the roster is in good shape overall, especially if the 10 rookies on the roster can increase their timeshare as the season goes on.
These are the areas that still warrant the closest inspection:
It’s a “Zay And Pray” downfield passing game until proven otherwise, with Zay Flowers having a monster season but now one else providing much in terms of explosives or YAC, and certainly no one else when it comes to catching balls that travel 20 or yards downfield. Their alleged No. 1 move tight end, Mark Andrews, has been cooked since late in the 2024 season , though rookie Matthew Hibner should start cutting into his route volume ASAP.
Tall slot receiver Ja’Kobi Lane barely got a target on the NFL before he broke his wrist and that sapped the momentum he established in the summer. At 6-4 and slithery with a flair for acrobatic catches, he could provide a spark immediately in the slot and in the redzone . But, alas, Rashod Bateman is erratic and Devontez Walker might be a more of a tease than a real thing, and this skillset has been an obvious cause for concern for years now.
Marlon Humphrey is not a $19M corner and it ain’t even close . Would he be best inside playing the slot? Probably but they don’t have much they like on the boundary and there is an abundance of options and body types in the slot including hybrid defensive back Kyle Hamilton and rookie Chandler Rivers and youngster Keyon Martin. So um, this is it.
Top wideouts are tearing this defense up pretty good and a better pass rush with the return of Trey Hendrickson from injury could help that cause . But this staff seems very reticent to lean into veteran Chidobe Awuzie nearly as much as last year’s staff and something is giving them trepidation.
Humphrey on No. 1 receivers won’t work and Nate Wiggins had issues Sunday with Drake London and larger targets will do that to him. Baltimore is playing more dime than anyone in the NFL and ranks 20th in opposing passer rating with six DBs on the field, allowing 66% completions. Oh and their corners do not have an INT all season. Here’s what No. 1 receivers have done since Week 2 (and the real challenges from better QBs are still to come).
The corners are allowing a combined passer rating of 101 and 11 yards per completion and they aren't impacting the football (four total pass breakups to go with the zero interceptions. They are the biggest underperformers on this football team and it isn't close .
Drake London (ATL): 7/11, 118 yards, 7 1st D
Carnell Tate (TEN): 9/12, 145 yds, 6 1st D
CeeDee Lamb (DAL): 7/8, 112 yds 5 1st D
George Pickens (DAL): 7/11, 82 yds, 4 1st D
Chris Olave (NO): 8/10, 86 yds, TD, 6 1st D
With the Bengals looming and the Jaguars and the Bills, and even the new-look Panthers, we'll know plenty about if this group is good enough to go deep in the playoffs by their early December bye.
I thought Lucas Scott did enough in the preseason to merit a practice squad spot as a young fullback; with Durham Smythe able to fill a “Joker” role , turns out they didn’t need him, but with Smythe out for the year he’s back. Not sure Nick Vannett is athletic enough to do what Smythe did and the need for a traditional fullback could emerge and it could be Scott isn’t there in his development yet.
Smythe was adding serious impact to the run game and the pass game and Hibner and fellow rookie tight end Josh Cuevas weren’t expected to have to contribute heavily in that regard at the line of scrimmage. Overall, tight end has always looked like a problem area and a body short of where you would like with a QB in Lamar Jackson, still dealing with an ankle injury , getting more deadly the more TEs are on the field.

title: Ravens Most Underperforming Position Group Entering Week 6 Will Shock You
full_text:
The Ravens offense was was brand new. The Ravens defense was supposed to be stout Week 1.
The offense had all the new coaches who had no ties to this organization and a totally foreign system and a coordinator who had never called a play before . They had a totally reconstructed interior offensive line and need a host of rookies to make an impact on that side of the ball.  The offense was going to need time to adjust and adapt and there would be a lot of penalties along the way … and despite those infractions the offense has still been by far the strength of this football team. By far.
And that’s despite the only real winning downfield option, Zay Flowers, missing about half the season to this point and another starting receiver, rookie Ja’Kobi Lane, playing only a few snaps before he headed to IR and with two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson missing a game and iffy to play Sunday and with four players already handling center duties through five weeks.
So color me surprised and give major kudos to that 30-year-old coordinator , Declan Doyle, for managing this transition expertly. But, um, also color me shocked that this secondary hasn’t been much more impactful and specifically the corners and the free safety. Head coach Jesse Minter was already a proven defensive play caller and all the money and resources were in the secondary and this system is a “cousin” of what Mike Macdonald ran to perfection here (as Kyle Hamilton dubbed it).
And all of the corners are back from last season and the only new addition of note to the entire secondary was a veteran box safety and the group has been almost entirely healthy.  They just haven’t been nearly good enough.
Given that Minter’s superpower is coverage and the back end, and given that he is flooding the field with defensive backs more than almost anyone in the NFL (second at 32% - NFL average is 8%) and ranks 20th in opposer QB rating and completion percentage out of dime, we got problems. And considering their late-game third-down issues are coming in dime, and they have only faced one above average QB all season (Dak Prescott) it’s fair to say the corners especially have a long way to go, and the secondary as a whole.
“I don't think we played well, for real,” Hamilton said after Sunday’s comeback win in Atlanta. “We still – the third-down stuff was crazy … Third down, we have to do better. But it obviously feels a lot better fixing those mistakes with a win. I might be a little too cynical or critical, but we can be better."
Nah, he’s just being honest. Here’s where they need to get better, fast.
Hamilton just alluded to another rough night on third down, with Atlanta’s suspect QB Michael Penix, just back from a third ACL surgery, going 7/12 throwing on third down against the Ravens’s dime packages, including three conversions on third and 10 and one on third-and-11 and another on third-and-15. Can’t happen.
On the season opponents are converting 45% of their third downs in the second half of games against the Ravens when they throw the ball; Baltimore ranks just 27th in that metric. Yikes. Better pass rush would help but these are all highly paid guys and/or first-round picks back there with a premier schemer and play caller … unless maybe some of them aren’t quite as good as the GM thinks?
One of the great things about Minter’s scheme with the Chargers is it put everyone in position to make plays on the ball and he had a bunch of mid-round picks at corner and they got off the field with interceptions. They were third in the NFL in INT% in two years under Minter and entering mid-October the Ravens corners have combined for … wait for it … no picks.
Baltimore has three picks all season and they were all on very shallow passes to the middle of the field and all were essentially picked off underneath by linebackers – middle linebacker Roquan Smith and Hamilton in a linebacker role. The corners have played 485 total pass rush reps, combined, by the way, without that INT.
The Ravens have built up many big leads this season and made teams one-handed, and it’s been obvious that suspect QB for the most part would be forced to chuck the ball around and they also have faced many teams with an absolute funnel on where the ball was going – Drake London on Sunday in Atlanta and Carnell Tate with the Titans and Chris Olave with the Saints.
Yet, um, dudes are not making plays on the ball. At all. Even with high volume from weak QBs who are making turnover-worthy throws. Here’s how the Ravens corners have fared in coverage. Hint – it sucks:
Opposing QBs : 49/74 (66%), 537 yards (11 yds/comp), 3 TDs – 0 INTs, 101.0 rating 6 Passes 20+, 31 1st Downs, 2 DPI, 4 pass break ups
Now hold your nose, because here are the numbers for corners + free safeties:
Opposing QBs : 70/100 (70%), 836 yards (11.9/comp), 5 TDs – 0 INTs, 111.9 rating 13 passes 20+, 41 1st downs, 3 DPI, 4 PBUs
=Let’s see what Joe Burrow and Trevor Lawrence and Josh Allen have in store if this doesn’t get cleaned up real quick.
The Ravens were lucky that Daniel Jones was on a wonky Achilles Week 1 and Alec Pierce was never right with the ankle problem and couldn’t even function as a pretend downfield decoy. Since then, here’s how things have been going:
London (ATL) : 7/11, 118 yards, 7 1st D
Tate (TEN) : 9/12, 145 yds, 6 1st D
CeeDee Lamb (DAL): 7/8, 112 yds 5 1st D
George Pickens (DAL): 7/11, 82 yds, 4 1st D
Olave (NO): 8/10, 86 yds, TD, 6 1st D
Yeah, better get to work back there, now.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Bills Defense Must Rebound  vs. Raiders Who Have 'One of Premier Players in NFL'
full_text:
It won't get any easier this week.
After seeing what Puka Nacua did to the Buffalo Bills on Monday, the Bills' defense has to be alert for the Las Vegas Raiders, who have another top receiving threat certainly licking his chops to rack up yards against an ailing back seven in Week 6.
Nacua registered a career-high 17 receptions for 138 yards against Buffalo, and third-year tight end Brock Bowers is arguably the best player at his position in the NFL. He has the potential to replicate what Nacua did and then some.
It wasn't only Nacua who tormented Buffalo's defense on Monday. 33-year-old tight end Tyler Higbee caught five passes for a season-high 83 yards, finding seams in Buffalo's secondary that Bowers and Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak will exploit.
Despite missing the first two games of the season after undergoing a left meniscus trim procedure, Bowers leads the Raiders with 24 receptions for 312 yards and three touchdowns.
Buffalo has allowed 300 yards to tight ends in five games , the 10th-most in the NFL. They also haven't exactly faced the best at the position thus far, with Dalton Schultz, Sam LaPorta and Hunter Henry being the top three they've faced.
Bowers is a completely different animal.
“Brock Bowers is a problem, right? He's one of the premier players in the NFL," said Bills' defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. "I wouldn't even say just at tight end, just in the NFL. So gonna be a challenge. It all has to start through him as far as how we try to stop this offense, and it's gonna be a big test.”
He spends most of his time lined up out wide , and at 6-foot-4, 235 pounds, he is pretty much a big wide receiver. He also spends a fair amount of time in the slot and inline, so defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard will have to be on his toes to prepare for what Kubiak's schemes have in store.
Wherever Bowers, a two-time John Mackey Award winner, may line up, he'll have a great day. Linebacker Dorian Williams has given up the sixth-highest passer rating among qualified linebackers, while Terrel Bernard is mediocre in that area.
In the secondary, cornerbacks Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun and safeties Cole Bishop and C.J. Gardner-Johnson gave up a passer rating of over 107 to Matthew Stafford and the Rams in addition to Williams' perfect 158.3. There could be similar numbers on Sunday, but there is hope otherwise.
If there's one caveat for Buffalo, it's that the Raiders don't have a wide receiver who can consistently threaten the defense elsewhere, with Tre Tucker, their No. 1 wideout, being fourth on the team with 19 catches.
While the Rams have Davante Adams, who caught five passes for 51 yards and two touchdowns on Monday, the Raiders' second- and third-leading receivers are running back Ashton Jeanty and tight end Michael Mayer, with 22 and 21 receptions, respectively. Adams has 55 more receiving yards this season than those two combined.
Even though Buffalo's corners have had their struggles to this point, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard should feel comfortable about them handling the Raiders' wide receivers one-on-one with Bowers being the main target for quarterback Kirk Cousins.
It'll be a tall task handling Bowers, but if Buffalo cannot do so, the Bills could be in for a letdown after an emotional win on Monday night that got them to 4-1.

title: Do Bills Play on Thursday Night Football Again This NFL Season?
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are fresh off a captivating Monday Night Football appearance in which their showstopper of a quarterback carried them to an overtime victory in front of 19.8 million viewers on ESPN platforms.
With the Josh Allen-led Bills having established themselves as appointment television for NFL fans across America, all of the league's broadcast partners naturally want their fair share.
"Are the Bills going to be one of the teams that are at or near the max in terms of prime time games and national television appearances? Yeah, as long as that guy is your quarterback. Yeah," said NFL VP of broadcast planning Mike North via the It's Always Gameday in Buffalo Podcast .
When it comes to Prime Video's Thursday Night Football package, which is kicking off Week 6 by featuring the Denver Broncos hosting the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks on October 15, the Bills have already made their lone scheduled appearance.
Buffalo hosted the Detroit Lions on September 17 in the Prime Video season opener . The Bills' high-scoring 41-31 victory was the first-ever regular season game in Highmark Stadium history.
Even though the game is not part of Amazon's package, the Bills will host one more Thursday night matchup this season. Buffalo is set to welcome the Kansas City Chiefs to Orchard Park for a Thanksgiving primetime show on November 26. Despite being on a Thursday, the holiday game, which begins at 8:20 p.m. ET,  is part of NBC's Sunday Night Football franchise.
The official Week 12 Thursday Night Football show will actually unfold on Black Friday, November 27 with the Pittsburgh Steelers hosting the Broncos for a 3 p.m. kickoff.
Including the Thanksgiving matchup, the Bills have five more standalone features remaining this season. They'll all come after the Week 7 bye.
Buffalo returns to Monday Night Football in Week 9, visiting the Minnesota Vikings on November 9.
Then, after hosting the Chiefs for a NBC holiday special, the Bills will make a true Sunday Night Football appearance in Week 14 when they visit the Green Bay Packers on December 13.
Six days later, the Bills will host the Chicago Bears in a Saturday night game at Highmark Stadium. It'll kick off at 8:20 p.m. on NBC.
Finally, Buffalo ends its primetime obligations in Week 16 with a Christmas Day special on Netflix. The Bills visit the Broncos in a rematch of last January's divisional round game. Kickoff is set for 4:30 p.m. on December 25.
We wrote about the personal dilemma that Allen faces as a result of the Christmas Day assignment.

title: Bills' Week 6 Injuries: Thursday Practice Updates for DJ Moore, Ed Oliver, Dee Alford
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills took to the practice field at UC Irvine on Thursday, and two key starters were still missing.
After showing up on the official Week 6 injury report as non-participants at Wednesday's walkthrough, which was not open to media, wide receiver DJ Moore and defensive lineman Ed Oliver were not present with reporters looking on at the beginning of Thursday's session (h/t WGR's Sal Capaccio ).
Both players were unavailable for the October 12 primetime win over the Los Angeles Rams after being banged up in Week 4 against the New England Patriots.
Remaining out west following their Week 5 victory on Monday Night Football, the Bills are preparing for an October 18 visit to the Las Vegas Raiders. Buffalo, which will fly home after Sunday's game in Sin City, will subsequently embark on its bye week.
"I'm not thinking about the bye right now. We gotta do whatever we gotta do to get ready to play this game. I know all of our guys have that kind of mindset that they're gonna get their bodies as best as they can to go play," said first-year head coach Joe Brady prior to Wednesday's practice .
Despite missing back-to-back practices, Moore and Oliver may still be able to get themselves ready for game day.
"No one's gonna be 100 percent healthy right now. We just played a Monday night game. We're five weeks into the season. It's part of the grind. If guys can be out there, the anticipation is for them to be out there," said Brady
DJ Moore just came out to the field and is standing off to the side. pic.twitter.com/xF44LKMvG5
Moore sprained his AC joint when hitting the ground while diving for a pass in the end zone against the Detroit Lions on September 17.
Having not missed a game since December 2020, Moore was subsequently available in Weeks 3 and 4 before his consecutive games streak ended against the Rams as a result of reaggravating the injury against the Patriots. The Bills' WR1, who was officially questionable heading into the Monday night affair, missed two days of practice before logging a limited session last Saturday.
When asked, on Wednesday, how Moore handled sitting out in Week 5, Brady took a long pause before simply saying "yeah," and moving onto the next question.
Like Moore, Oliver was forced out early in the Week 4 setback to New England. The veteran lineman, who played 24 snaps in the game, took a hit to the knee from Patriots' fullback Reggie Gilliam at the end of a play near the sideline.
Oliver did not practice leading up to the Week 5 primetime game, and the Bills ruled him out on Saturday. It's unknown if the knee injury is related to the issue that kept him out of OTAs. Oliver apparently had a knee scope this past offseason, referring to it as "a little oops oops."
Although he may be out again this Sunday, it's reasonable to expect Oliver back after the bye.
For the second day in a row, right tackle Spencer Brown and slot cornerback Dee Alford were participating on the field in Irvine.
Brown left after 16 snaps on Monday night due to a back flare-up. He spoke to reporters after Wednesday's walkthrough, delivering a positive update.
"Just tweaked it. Nothing major. Disc looks fine. Had an MRI. Looks better than it did last year. Long-term wise that's good to hear. It's [current issue] straight up just muscular freaking out," said Brown.
Meanwhile, Alford did not dress for Monday Night Football due to an ankle injury. He was officially questionable to play after tweaking it in the loss to the Patriots.
It seems as if he was held out more as a precaution, and he'll be ready to return to game action this Sunday.

title: Bills' Bradley Chubb Reveals What Was Said Prior to Postgame Physical Altercation
full_text:
The most recent primetime matchup between the Buffalo Bills and the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football at SoFi Stadium provided NFL fans with plenty of fireworks on the field during Buffalo’s 37-34 overtime victory.
And, afterward, those sparks continued to fly when Rams’ veteran offensive lineman Alaric Jackson and Bills’ veteran outside linebacker Bradley Chubb got into an altercation following the final whistle when players were, supposedly, meeting one another cordially near midfield.
For Chubb and Jackson, however, punches were exchanged instead of pleasantries, as Los Angeles’ starting left tackle seemingly sucker punched Buffalo’s 30-year-old EDGE defender before walking off the turf.
As a result, Jackson was subsequently suspended for two games, which Bills ON SI promptly reported about on Wednesday .
The suspension, though, has since been reduced to one game following Jackson’s appeal to the league, which is a bit of a shocker given the nature of the unnecessary incident that was totally uncalled for . . . at least in Chubb’s mind.
“At one moment, you thought you (were) about to lose the game, and I feel like that’s when, kind of, the front running started, like, the talking junk and all that. And, the emotions get high, and it’s, like, ‘Oh, boom. OK, now we won.’ And, I’m not going to say I don’t have any fault in the situation, you know? I went up to him (first),” Bills’ outside linebacker Bradley Chubb said during media availability following the team’s practice at UC Irvine on Wednesday.
“I’ll tell you exactly what I said: I’ve heard I’ve been talking about (your) Mom, and different things. That’s not true at all, (so) I went up to him and I said, ‘Hey, we’re going to see y’all a** again. And, when we see y’all again, that chip ain’t going to save you—that tight end, that guard—is not going to save you.’ That’s what I said.
“And, then he said, ‘What’d you say?’ He walked up on me . . . people said I put my hand in his face, (but) I said, ‘That chip’s not going to save you, (and) that guard’s not going to save you.’ BOOM . You know what I mean? And, that’s the situation . . . it’s an emotional game. All tempers (are) flaring.”
With the air cleared, it appears that both sides have now moved on from the incident, especially when it pertains to Buffalo’s defender.
The team from Western New York has yet another critical game upcoming in just a few days—this time in the AFC against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday at Allegiant Stadium in Paradise, Nevada—and it’s imperative that all hands are on deck for the next matchup for first-year head coach Joe Brady’s squad.
And, keeping that in mind, Chubb, who finished the game against the Rams with only two total tackles, no sacks, and no quarterback hits, knows that he can’t focus on trivial things like what happened with Jackson.
If Buffalo is truly going to accomplish its goal of going back to SoFi Stadium in February 2027 for Super Bowl LXI on Valentine’s Day , then players can’t waste their time with any extracurriculars not pertaining to bettering their craft on the field.
And, given that Chubb and his defensive teammates have plenty of areas to clean up moving forward this season, he’s seemingly already wiped the incident from his focus.
But, who knows? Maybe the two players will see each other once more in the season's final game at SoFi Stadium.
“They brought me here to play and to be a leader. And, I feel like if I would have reacted—if I would have did anything in both of those situations—like, I’m not doing what they brought me here to do,” Chubb continued.
“Like I told him, ‘We’re going to see y’all again.’ And, how do we see them again? In the Super Bowl. And, that’s one of our goals as a team is to get to that (point).”
Whether or not both squads will actually meet again later on in the NFL’s title game this winter remains to be seen, but it sure would provide an extra story line, wouldn’t it?

title: Bills CB Maxwell Hairston Hit With Concerning NFL Hot Seat Label
full_text:
As a first-round pick, Maxwell Hairston joined the Buffalo Bills in 2025 with plenty of expectations. He got off to a slow start due to a knee injury that cost him the first six games of the season. He also missed Buffalo’s two playoff games after suffering an ankle injury in their Week 18 win over the New York Jets.
Hairston still showed promise when he was on the field, recording 18 tackles, five pass deflections, and two interceptions in 13 games. This year, however, Hairston has been off to a sluggish start and has been targeted often by opposing quarterbacks.
Things have derailed to the point that Hairston was benched ahead of their Week 5 showdown with the Los Angeles Rams, in favor of rookie Davison Igbibosun. That development has Bill Barnwell naming Hairston among 15 players and coaches who enter Week 6 on the hot seat . As Barnwell points out, the issues really got out of control for Hairston when he had his worst game of the season against the New England Patriots in Week 4.
”This season was supposed to be a fresh start for Hairston, but his first month was a mess. The 23-year-old allowed two touchdown passes in the 29-26 loss to the Patriots, leading defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard to publicly encourage Hairston to temper his emotions. Hairston also left the locker room after the defeat without speaking to the media before returning and apologizing a day later,” Barnwell wrote.
Buffalo’s coaching staff continues to support Hairston when asked, but as Barnwell said, “actions speak louder than words.” As he points out, their actions show Hairston being phased out, even though his replacement has had issues of his own.
“Against the Rams on Monday, Hairston's snap share cratered with the return of Christian Benford. The Bills kept Davison Igbinosun in the lineup ahead of Hairston, who played just 15 snaps on defense. Igbinosun committed a pass interference penalty in the red zone and allowed a touchdown catch, which won't help his case, but he still appears to be ahead of Hairston on the depth chart.”
Giving up on Hairston this early would be a mistake. The Kentucky product entered the NFL with game-changing speed and displayed excellent instincts for the Wildcats. He also flashed during his rookie season.
The problem is that he's dealt with multiple injuries and is learning a new system under defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. This doesn't excuse his struggles, and benching him was absolutely the right call, but considering him a bust would be premature.
Take a look at Keon Coleman as an example. After Coleman was benched last season, there were calls for the Bills to simply move on . Buffalo stayed patient and has been rewarded, with Coleman recording 15 receptions for 224 yards and two touchdowns through five games. He might not be the WR1 they hoped for when selecting him in the 2024 NFL draft, but Coleman has found his place in the offense and is producing.
Now, they need to hope for similar growth from Hairston as he attempts to fight out of this slump.

title: Bills' Greg Rousseau Leads NFL During Recent One-Man Defensive Rampage
full_text:
Leading up to this past Monday night’s primetime matchup between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium, it was thought by some outside observers that Bills’ veteran outside linebacker Gregory Rousseau could wind up being the ultimate X-factor for Buffalo.
In fact, Bills ON SI highlighted the massive EDGE defender as a key player to watch out for just prior to the start of the overtime thriller . . . and for good reason.
Entering Week 5, Rousseau had been on a tear for the current leader in the AFC East clubhouse as he led all pass-rushers in the National Football League sacks ( 6 ), tackles for loss ( 8 ), and forced fumbles ( 3 ).
And, although he may not have recorded a sack against Los Angeles, Rousseau was still incredibly impactful during the intraconference meeting between the two teams as he was able to block a potential game-winning field goal by (now former) Rams’ kicker Harrison Mevis in overtime that wound up turning the tide in favor of Bills’ first-year head coach Joe Brady’s young group.
The moment was miraculous, and it’s exactly the type of game-changing play that the pass-rusher has been providing all season long . In case any fans have forgotten, his strip sack of Houston Texans’ quarterback C.J. Stroud down at Reliant Stadium with under one minute remaining in the season opener was also a game-sealing play for Buffalo.
Simply put, Rousseau—who was the AFC Defensive Player of the Month in September—is reaching heights not seen from a Bills’ defender in quite some time, and he’s been able to make an impact in nearly every game thus far.
“We were just saying, like, ‘Block this s**t,’ over and over, you know what I’m saying? So, I had an opportunity . . . and just took advantage of it,” sixth-year NFL veteran Gregory Rousseau, who finished the game with just one tackle and one quarterback hit on defense, said in the locker room on Monday.
“If there’s still time on the clock, (then) we’re good, ready to go. That’s what we work for. That’s what OTAs, training camp, (and) everything’s for. (If) there’s still time on the clock—put the ball down—let’s go.”
With that said, although Buffalo’s 6-foot-6, 266-pound pass-rusher was just leapfrogged by Houston’s Will Anderson Jr. in the quarterback-takedown department after Anderson Jr.’s recent three-sack performance against the Tennessee Titans last Sunday, Rousseau still holds the league lead for quarterback pressures according to Pro Football Focus, as the former University of Miami standout now has a total of 35 pressures through five weeks of the 2026 season per the popular analytical site’s database.
Whether he’s reaching the quarterback or not, Rousseau’s incredible length and surprising spryness for his size are proving to be a nightmare for opposing offensive linemen and quarterbacks to deal with this fall.
It’s precisely what Bills’ general manager Brandon Beane probably envisioned when he selected the pass-rusher nicknamed ‘Groot’ at pick No. 30 of the 2021 NFL Draft.
A one-time ACC Defensive Rookie of the Year as a freshman at Miami, Rousseau has always possessed the tools to be one of the premier EDGE defenders in the NFL.
However, now in Year Six, it appears that Rousseau is finally flourishing in the role of being a prominent playmaker for the Western New York franchise.
And, in spite of all the struggles that coordinator Jim Leonhard’s youthful unit is experiencing as a whole at this point in time, the 26-year-old is on the verge of greatness.
Most pressures this season Greg Rousseau           35 Aidan Hutchinson     32 Dallas Turner              32 Maxx Crosby               30 Will Anderson Jr         30 pic.twitter.com/uWVwcuvB80
If he keeps up this level of play, then there might be another Defensive Player of the Year award incoming for Rousseau in a few short months . . . and maybe even a Super Bowl title for Buffalo.

title: Bills' First Week 6 Injury Report: Updates on Spencer Brown, DJ Moore, Ed Oliver
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills listed 15 players on their official Week 6 injury report as they prepare to visit the Las Vegas Raiders for an October 18 matinee.
There were four new additions with starting right tackle Spencer Brown, rookie outside linebacker TJ Parker, safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson and running back Ty Johnson all apparently coming out of Monday's win bothered by injury.
Meanwhile, defensive lineman TJ Sanders, who made his season debut in Week 5, remains on the injury report, but with a new issue.
Brown, who was limited on Wednesday, is the name that warrants the most attention. The right tackle left Monday's win after only 16 snaps due to a back flare-up.
"No one's gonna be 100 percent healthy right now. We just played a Monday night game. We're five weeks into the season. It's part of the grind. If guys can be out there, the anticipation is for them to be out there," said head coach Joe Brady.
In a positive development, the Bills removed inside linebackers Dorian Williams and Joe Andreessen along with safety Damar Hamlin and running back Ray Davis from the injury report. All four saw snaps during the October 12 primetime win .
Buffalo held a walkthrough practice on Wednesday at UC Irvine, meaning participation status is only an estimation. Five of the 15 players were listed as limited participants. Wide receiver DJ Moore and defensive lineman Ed Oliver, neither of whom were available in Week 5 , were the lone two non-participants.
Brown has a history of back issues, but he's still managed to to average 15 appearances per regular season since being drafted in 2021.
This reliable bookend's latest flare-up doesn't appear serious enough to keep him off the field come Sunday against the Raiders.
"Just tweaked it. Nothing major. Disc looks fine. Had an MRI. Looks better than it did last year. Long-term wise that's good to hear. It's [current issue] straight up just muscular freaking out," said Brown addressing reporters following the walkthrough.
He suggested he should be "good by Sunday."
Along with Brown, Johnson was also limited on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Gardner-Johnson and Parker were full participants.
Johnson is listed with a hamstring injury. It's not known if it's a recurrence of the same issue that sidelined the running back for the month of August.
Moore has been fighting through an AC joint sprain since hitting the turf hard during the September 17 win over the Detroit Lions in Week 2.
Giving it a go in Weeks 3 and 4, Moore was finally forced to sit out in Week 5 after reaggravating the injury against the New England Patriots on October 4. It was the first time Moore missed a game since December 2020, ending a 91-game appearance streak.
Meanwhile, Palmer injured his shoulder in practice last Friday. He missed Saturday's practice while being ruled out for Monday. Although only an estimation, it's a good sign to see him listed as a limited participant for the first practice of Week 6.
Oliver, defensive lineman Landon Jackson and starting slot cornerback Dee Alford all missed the October 12 win after getting nicked up the week prior against the Patriots.
After injuring his knee, Oliver did not practice at all last week. He remained sidelined Wednesday.
Jackson, who was wearing a brace on his injured knee, was held out of Monday's game despite ending the practice week with back-to-back days of full participation. He was full again to begin this week.
Alford, who tweaked his ankle in Week 4, remained limited as the Bills began preparations for the Raiders.

title: When Will Bills Upgrade Underperforming LB Corps By Elevating Vet Shaq Thompson?
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' defense ranks 30th out of 32 NFL teams through the season's first five weeks, and the inside linebacker play appears to be part of the problem.
Bills' first-year head coach Joe Brady protected his players against veiled media criticism on Wednesday, but it doesn't mean potential changes aren't being discussed behind the scenes.
"I think you're not a fan of the way our linebackers are playing, based off some of the questions, but I have no issues with the way our linebackers our playing right now," said Brady.
It's worth noting that Brady confirmed beleaguered cornerback Maxwell Hairston's starting status last week, but when game time rolled around, second-round rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun was the starter opposite Christian Benford.
Therefore, it wouldn't be shocking to see veteran linebacker Shaq Thompson, who is currently on the practice squad, spring into action at some point in the coming weeks, especially with a bye after Sunday's road game against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Co-captain Terrel Bernard's spot is likely safe . Although he's looked slow at times this season, Bernard has built a reputation for being a great communicator with good instincts.
Dorian Williams, however, may be in danger of losing playing time to Thompson or fourth-round rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr . Williams, a 2023 third-round pick, has always struggled when needed to drop back in pass coverage. This season, he has looked confused and out of sync in the new defense.
The Bills decided to bring Thompson back into the mix after the 32-year-old linebacker sat on the free agent market throughout the summer.
Like it did with veteran safety Jordan Poyer last year, Buffalo brought Thompson back into a practice squad capacity prior to the regular season kicking off.
In addition to getting back in the flow physically, Thompson seemingly needed a few weeks to digest the defensive scheme change under Jim Leonhard. The Bills employed a 4-3 front when Thompson played 12 games in what was head coach Sean McDermott's final season.
While his versatility and experience will likely allow him to effectively operate in a 3-4 scheme, Thompson brings intangible to the table, too.
"Shaq knows he was brought here from a leadership component," said Brady on Wednesday. "If an opportunity came up, it's a long season, having a guy like himself, with his background and his history, to be able to come in and play and play meaningful football."
The 2015 first-round draft pick spent his first 10 NFL seasons with the Carolina Panthers, including two under the tutelage of McDermott. He has 135 career regular season appearances, including 118 starts.
The Bills initially brought in Thompson to bolster its linebacker depth prior to the 2025 season, and he proceeded to make 12 appearances (6 starts). In fact, Thompson was arguably the Bills' best defensive player at times, and he stepped up in the postseason, too. Starting both Bills' playoff games, Thompson totaled 13 tackles, 2.0 tackles-for-loss and one interception.
"I love having Shaq here. There's a reason Shaq's here, but I like how, where our linebackers are right now," said Brady.
With all due respect to Brady, Bernard and Thompson, it's time to see the real reason why Shaq's here.

title: Three Buffalo Bills With Most to Prove Entering Week 6
full_text:
Week 5 was full of highs and lows for the Buffalo Bills as they knocked off the Los Angeles Rams in overtime .
It was a thrilling game that seemed to be going in the Rams’ favor, until Greg Rousseau blocked a field goal in overtime . That allowed Buffalo to drive down the field for a game-winning field goal of their own.
That win means they’re now 4-1 and in control of the AFC East . The Bills don’t have time to celebrate, however, as they’re preparing to take on the Las Vegas Raiders on the road in Week 6. Buffalo will be favored in this one, but they can’t take the Raiders lightly. They also have multiple players entering Week 6 with a lot to prove, including the following three Bills.
Dalton Kincaid got off to a hot start this season, hauling in 14 passes for 225 yards and a touchdown over the first two weeks. Since then, his production has dropped significantly. He had three receptions for 38 yards in Week 3 but has just two catches for seven yards in each of the past two games.
When Kincaid is at his best, this offense is nearly unstoppable. When he disappears, everything seems much more difficult. That’s why they need him to turn things around as they get ready to play the Raiders on Sunday.
Monday night was not the best showing for safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson. According to PFF, he allowed five receptions on seven targets for 63 yards and a touchdown. In addition to his struggles in coverage, Gardner-Johnson was penalized for unnecessary roughness on second-and-16, giving the Rams a fresh set of downs and 15 penalty yards.
Gardner-Johnson was added this offseason in an attempt to shore up the back end of the Buffalo secondary. He’s had some great moments, including an interception against the Los Angeles Chargers, but hasn’t been getting it done in coverage over the past couple of weeks.
James Cook is one of the more dynamic running backs in the NFL. After five games, he has 532 rushing yards and five touchdowns while averaging 5.6 yards per attempt. He also has a serious fumbling problem.
Cook already has four fumbles on the season, including a critical lost fumble that nearly cost them the game against the Rams, if not for Rousseau’s blocked field goal. Cook’s fumbling problem has been a hot topic, even leading to Joe Brady making it clear that it has to stop . All eyes will be on Cook, who is still one of the best players on the roster, but is feeling the pressure following his ball security concerns.

title: Bills' WR Week 6 Injury Outlook: When Will DJ Moore, Josh Palmer Return to Action?
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' receiving corps faced the Los Angeles Rams without the services of veterans DJ Moore and Josh Palmer , and their absences were more than noticeable.
In the 37-34 overtime road win , Bills' wide receivers combined for 87 yards on four receptions.
Khalil Shakir's three catches for 80 yards and Keon Coleman's seven-yard touchdown grab accounted for the position group's only production on Monday Night Football in Week 5. Fourth-round rookie Skyler Bell was unsuccessfully targeted twice while Trent Sherfield and Khalil Shakir got no looks.
To say the offense will be better off once both veterans, especially Moore, return is quite the understatement. As for when that will happen, no real hints emerged on Wednesday at the Bills practiced at UC Irvine.
Buffalo held a walkthrough, meaning all practice participation statuses on the official injury report are only estimations. Moore was a non-participant while Palmer was deemed limited.
"We're going through a walkthrough today, so it's really not gonna be able to tell us much. We'll kinda see how it looks tomorrow," said Brady on Wednesday.
Although Brady was specifically answering a question about starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who left Monday's win after 16 snaps , the statement also applies to Moore and Palmer.
Moore has been dealing with an AC joint sprain since Week 2 when he landed hard on his shoulder while diving for a pass in the end zone late during the second quarter against the Detroit Lions.
Fighting through what mainly appeared to be a pain tolerance issue, Moore suited up in Weeks 3 and 4 despite being limited during practice. He reaggravated the injury in the first half against the New England Patriots on October 4, and missed the remainder of the 29-26 loss.
Moore was a non-participant at the first two practices in Week 5. After getting on the field in a limited capacity on Saturday, he was officially questionable for the Monday road game.
Apparently unable to go, Moore was scratched prior to kickoff, ending his 91-game consecutive appearance streak. Even with the bye week looming, one has to think Moore wants to get back out there as soon as possible.
"No one's gonna be 100 percent healthy right now. We just played a Monday night game. We're five weeks into the season. It's part of the grind. If guys can be out there, the anticipation is for them to be out there," said Brady prior to Wednesday's
When asked how Moore handled sitting out in Week 5, Brady took a long pause before simply saying "yeah," and moving onto the next question.
After plagued by a lingering knee/ankle throughout much of a disappointing 2025 campaign, Palmer was healthy as the Bills kicked off 2026.
Unfortunately, his availability streak ended at four games due to a shoulder injury that he picked up during last Friday's practice. After initially appearing on the injury report as limited , Palmer missed Saturday's practice and was ruled out for the game .
"He got kind of twisted up yesterday in practice. We're still kinda going through some of the testing and whatnot," said Brady on Saturday.
The fact that Palmer was estimated as limited, as opposed to a non-participant, on Wednesday is a positive sign. Practice participation, however, has not necessarily been a factor in determining whether the injured player will be available on game day.
"There's going to be guys that aren't going to be out there today that still have a chance at playing, and probably are going to play this weekend," said Brady earlier this month.
The Bills will practice again on Thursday in Irvine as they prepare to visit the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18.
