title: Chargers Could Have Answer to Panthers' Defensive Woes with Familiar Face
full_text:
There are three winless teams in the National Football League, all in the AFC, and two of them are certainly no surprise. The Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans both come off losing campaigns in 2025, the latter tied for the worst record in the league.
Then there are the Los Angeles Chargers, who dropped to 0-5 last Sunday with their third home loss in five weeks. A 23-17 setback to the Denver Broncos means that Jim Harbaugh’s club is the lone member of the AFC West with a losing record. Hence there’s been plenty of speculation on whether the tea, a playoff participant the previous two season, is ready to blow things up in the coming weeks?
Two such speculators are C arter Bahns of CBS Sports and Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report . Among the numerous players mentioned by both writers is a veteran cornerback who could certainly help Dave Canales’s first-place team.
Donte Jackson was a second-round pick by the Carolina Panthers back in 2018. After six seasons in Charlotte, he was traded to the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2024. He came up with a total of six takeaways, including a career-best five interceptions, in his lone season with the Black and Gold.
In 2025, he signed a two-year deal with the Los Angeles Chargers. He played in all 17 games, totaled four picks and a dozen passes defensed. Knox feels that both the first-place Panthers, who are currently shortahnded at cornerback, and the Buffalo Bills are possible landing places for the nine-year pro.
“Teams may not be eager to make a move for Jackson until he's clearly healthy (hamstring),” stated Knox, “but he's a player worth targeting before November 10. The Los Angeles Chargers appear to be going nowhere this season after a 0-5 start and numerous injuries across the roster. Jackson, meanwhile, plays an in-demand position and is set to be a free agent in 2027—trading him would save L.A. $6 million in 2026 cap space.”
“Jackson started 15 games for the Chargers last season,” added Knox,” and allowed an opposing passer rating of only 56.8 in coverage.”
This season, he has been limited to just 113 defensive snaps in four games, and sat out last week’s clash with the Broncos. He’s totaled eight tackles, two passes defensed and one forced fumble this season.
Of course, the Panthers are dealing with the losses of starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, both players currently on injured reserve. Knox projects that Jackson could be had for a fifth-round draft choice in 2027.
Then again, all of this is contingent on the Chargers bailing on the current season. The team is off to its worst start since 2003. Meanwhile, the Panthers off to their best start since 2021, and look to hold down the fort until Horn and Jackson can get back on the field.
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: Week 6 NFL Expert Picks Reveal Panthers' Chances vs. Eagles
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are rested and getting healthier after their bye . They're coming off a brilliant upset win over the Detroit Lions, too.
The Philadelphia Eagles made the long trek back from London after a mindboggling, crushing defeat where victory was essentially secured. The Panthers have the advantage this week, it seems.
Despite that, they're not favored on the road, and some experts aren't willing to pick the Panthers to take the Eagles down.
CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win.
"The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense," he wrote.
His CBS colleague, Jordan Dajani, disagreed, picking the Panthers to win 23-21. "The Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS," Dajani pointed out.
Here's how SI's staff is picking the game:
Bleacher Report's Wes O'Donnell is taking the Panthers to cover the spread and win outright. "I'm done trying to figure out the Eagles. The Eagles clearly cannot figure out the Eagles. And while the Panthers' defense is a great opportunity for any offense to get right, Carolina had a bye week and then some to prepare for Philly. This Panthers team has defied the odds and shown up in tough situations since last season," he wrote.
His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles.
At ESPN , only Pam Maldonado and Dan Graziano picked the Eagles to beat the Panthers. The Athletic's Vic Tafur was obscenely blunt: "The Eagles are coming off two heartbreaking losses, they struggle against play-action passes (a Panthers staple), and it wouldn’t shock me if this is Sirianni’s last game as head coach."
What does this mean? Despite the overwhelming advantages the Panthers have in this game, there's still a perception that the Eagles are the Eagles and the Panthers are the woeful Panthers.
That makes Week 6's contest a perfect opportunity to reshape the narrative, although it's a little unfair that a primetime victory over the Detroit Lions didn't do that for the Panthers.

title: Week 6 Fantasy Projections for Bryce Young, Tetairoa McMillan, Chuba Hubbard & More
full_text:
Fresh off the bye week , the Carolina Panthers are back in action on Sunday to face arguably their toughest road test yet: the Philadelphia Eagles . The Eagles are just 2-3 and have lost three straight, but Lincoln Financial Field remains a tough place to play.
From a fantasy football perspective, the Panthers have been more productive than many would have expected. Bryce Young leads the league in passing yards, and Chuba Hubbard seems to be finding his 2024 form again.
Ahead of the Week 6 matchup against the Eagles, Carolina should feature at least three must-starts, but it's not just Young, Hubbard, and Tetairoa McMillan to look to. Here are the Week 6 fantasy projections for those three, and more Panthers players.
Bryce Young has been on a heater this season. In four games, Young has posted under 20 fantasy points in only one. This week, Young faces an Eagles defense ranked 20th against opposing QBs.
Chicago's third-string QB, Case Keenum, lit up this Eagles defense. So Young, playing the way he has, should be able to be productive. Jalen Coker returns this week, giving Young another top target to throw to.
Philadelphia's defense hasn't been good enough to pivot away from Young in this spot, barring a drastic regression in performance, this is a safe play at QB.
Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker see a favorable matchup this weekend, playing the Eagles defense that ranks 28th against wide receivers in fantasy.
McMillan is coming off his best game of the season, catching 14 passes for 192 receiving yards and 2 touchdowns. Don't expect that type of production now that Coker is back, because McMillan just won't see that many targets every week.
As for Coker, he returns from a minor quad injury that sidelined him for Week 4 vs. the Lions. Before the injury, Coker led Carolina in receiving yards and targets. Now back healthy, Coker will cancel out some of McMillan's target share.
Even after McMillan's stellar Week 4, with Coker back, the targets shouldn't differ much. Both receivers should perform well and collectively take advantage of a good matchup.
Tetairoa McMillan Projection: 18.3 points
Jalen Coker projection: 16.0 points
Hubbard has as high a floor as any RB in the league in fantasy. In four games, Hubbard hasn't finished with fewer than 14 points and has posted over 23 points twice.
The Eagles are a middle-of-the-pack defense against running backs in fantasy, ranking 16th in the NFL. Overall, Philadelphia's defense has been awful in fantasy, ranking 28th in the NFL.
Hubbard should be able to post another week of double-digit production, and if he gets involved in the passing game, then that number will be higher.

title: Panthers Urged to Replace Bryce Young with Justin Herbert in Unwise Move
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have finally solved their QB problem. After cycling through replacements for Cam Newton and desperately trying to develop Bryce Young, the Panthers seem set at the position. Most people agree.
The operative word there is most. Henry McKenna and Steven Ruiz discussed Justin Herbert's trade prospects as the Los Angeles Chargers flounder, and the Panthers incomprehensibly got named as a a landing spot.
If Justin Herbert demands a trade, who might pick up the phone? Where might he actually want to go? Two possible suitors: Panthers, Buccaneers. It's one of many topics that @theStevenRuiz and I hit on in The QB Room podcast this week. 🎧⤵️ https://t.co/AlHpaq43ga pic.twitter.com/tBzi2IejBL
McKenna said, "We'll see what happens with Bryce Young as the season goes on. I could see a team like the Panthers, that would be the type of team, a team that will finish in the middle of the draft and the middle of the league."
Ruiz interjected with excitement over the prospect of Herbert landing on the Panthers. McKenna added, "You're probably talking about more than three firsts because it's that middle-of-the-round pick."
McKenna also said that Young would be included in the deal as a "sweetener," so the Panthers wouldn't have to pay as much in draft capital outside the three first-round picks.
This is patently absurd for a number of reasons. Herbert is a good quarterback and he's probably going to bounce back and continue having a good NFL career, but that's no guarantee. It was supposed to work perfectly with Mike McDaniel, and he's been atrocious.
Young is on the upswing, and Herbert may be on the downswing. Young is also younger and will be cheaper. Herbert's on a monster extension, and Young, while he's earning a big payday, likely won't be as costly.
Plus, the Panthers would have to trade a bunch of assets to the Chargers. Is this team a marginal, if that, upgrade at QB away from being a contender? Not at all, so they'd be mortgaging the future for nothing.
Plus, it's likely that Young would excel in Los Angeles. Many floated the idea of, when Young had been benched, sending the QB to the Dolphins so he could take the Tua Tagovailoa role because of their playstyle similarities.
So, if McDaniel made it work with Tagovailoa, he'd probably love having Young. It would be a tough pill to swallow on all fronts.
Plus, while this may be the sunk-cost fallacy, the Panthers have invested a ton to get Young to this point. Everyone involved has worked so hard to get him to an elite level, and it's all finally paying off.
Why would they trade him for someone who's going to cost a ton of picks and is having the worst year of his career so far?

title: Panthers-Eagles Wasn't Supposed to Look Anything Like This
full_text:
Go back about a month and look at Panthers -Eagles on the schedule. What did you think?
For me, Philadelphia on the road looked like one of the tougher games on Carolina's schedule. I wasn't automatically putting a loss beside it, but I also wasn't looking at that game and thinking this might be where the Panthers get above .500. At that point, we didn't even know what Carolina was going to look like.
I'm definitely not looking at it that way now. The Panthers are 2-2, they just beat Detroit 32-26, and they're coming out of the bye with a chance to have a winning record. I don't know how many people would've believed that if you told them before the season.
And it wasn't like Carolina just hung around against Detroit and stole one at the end. Bryce Young threw for 329 yards, Tetairoa McMillan had 192 receiving yards and two touchdowns, and Chuba Hubbard ran for 122 yards and two scores. The Panthers put up 445 yards and looked like they belonged in that game.
Philadelphia has gone the other way.
The Eagles are 2-3 and have lost three straight. They just lost 19-17 to Jacksonville, and now they're coming home needing a win, probably a lot more than anyone expected at this point in the season.
I'm not going to act like that makes Philadelphia a bad football team. Jalen Hurts is still there, and there is enough talent on both sides of the ball to make this a miserable afternoon for Carolina if the Panthers don't play well. It's also Philadelphia on the road, which isn't exactly where you want to go expecting an easy Sunday.
But I don't look at this game and wonder how Carolina is going to keep up anymore. That's where my thinking has changed.
If the Panthers had started 1-3 and looked anything like they did against Chicago in Week 1, I'd probably be looking at Sunday completely differently. Instead, they followed that disaster by holding Atlanta to three points, had a chance to win late in Cleveland, and then beat Detroit.
I still don't know exactly what to make of this team, but I know it's better than what I thought I was watching after Week 1.
It isn't just that Philadelphia has lost three straight. Carolina has given me a reason to expect more from it.
Young is a big part of that. He has 1,268 passing yards and nine touchdowns through four games, and right now I'm not going into games wondering whether Carolina can throw the football. I'm wondering what Young and this offense are going to do next.
That's a pretty big difference from where we've been.
McMillan has become a problem for defenses, Hubbard is still giving Carolina a running game, and suddenly Young has multiple guys he can go to. Even the defense, as strange as it has been at times, keeps finding ways to get turnovers or make a stop when it needs one.
None of that means Carolina has everything figured out. I watched Chicago put 59 on this defense, and I watched the Panthers let one get away in Cleveland. Four games aren't enough for me to forget about the things that can still go wrong with this team.
But I don't think going into Philadelphia and keeping it close is enough anymore. Carolina had a week off after its biggest win of the season, the Panthers are 2-2, and Philadelphia is 2-3. There's a real opportunity sitting there.
Win Sunday, and Carolina comes out of its bye and moves to 3-2 with people having a completely different conversation about this team.
A month ago, I would've wanted to see if the Panthers could hang with the Eagles.
Now I want to see if they can beat them.

title: Bryce Young's Smartest Play of the Season Won't Show Up in the Box Score
full_text:
There are a lot of ways we judge quarterbacks. We look at yards, touchdowns, interceptions, and, of course, whether their team won the game.
Sometimes, though, a quarterback makes a play that doesn't show up in any of those numbers. Bryce Young had one against Atlanta that I keep coming back to, and there's a good chance a lot of people didn't think much about it at the time.
The Carolina Panthers were facing second-and-7 from the Atlanta 21-yard line when Young dropped back to pass. Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels got a hand on the ball, and suddenly it was floating in the air with defenders closing in.
We've all seen how those plays can end. Sometimes the ball falls harmlessly to the ground, and sometimes it lands right in a defender's hands. Young wasn't taking that chance, so he went after it himself and knocked it to the ground before Atlanta could get to it.
The Panthers didn't gain anything, but more importantly, they didn't give anything away either.
On the stat sheet, it was an incomplete pass. That's it. But if Young doesn't react the way he did, Atlanta might be going the other way with the football.
Instead, Carolina got another down and eventually finished the drive with Young finding Chuba Hubbard for a touchdown. That's a pretty big swing for a play that most people probably forgot about five minutes later.
What I really like about the play is what happened long before Young ever threw the ball.
As Panthers.com reported after the game , game-management coordinator George Li had shown Carolina's players a similar situation more than a year earlier. The lesson was pretty simple: If a pass gets knocked into the air and you can keep the defense from catching it, get it on the ground.
Young remembered it in the middle of a game with the ball hanging in the air and only a second or two to do something about it. That's the part of the play that stood out to me.
Young has already made bigger plays this season. He's thrown touchdowns and made throws that are a lot more fun to watch than knocking his own pass to the ground.
But playing quarterback isn't always about making the big play. Sometimes it's about knowing when a bad play is about to happen and keeping it from becoming worse.
Young has heard plenty about the mistakes he's made since coming into the NFL. That's not going away. He's a quarterback and a former No. 1 overall pick, so everything he does is going to get looked at a little harder.
The smart stuff should count for something, too.
When the season is over, nobody is going to pull up Young's stats and talk about an incompletion in the second quarter against Atlanta. But Carolina kept the football, scored a touchdown a few plays later, and Young made sure they got that chance.
I'll take that incompletion every time.

title: It's Time to Ask the Question Panthers Fans Didn't Expect This Soon
full_text:
Maybe Panthers fans are finally starting to believe in this offense.
During a recent discussion on the Carolina Panthers subreddit , one fan asked a pretty simple question: “Maybe the offense we have here is legit?”
After watching the first four games, it's a fair question.
The Panthers have scored more than 30 points in three of their first four games and have 121 points on the season. That's the most points Carolina has ever scored through the first four games of a season, which is kind of crazy when you think about some of the offenses we've watched around here the last few years.
Carolina put up 37 against Chicago, followed that with 34 against Atlanta and then scored 32 against Detroit before the bye. Cleveland is the only team so far that has kept the Panthers under 30.
Detroit was the game that really made me start thinking about this differently. Young threw for 329 yards, Tetairoa McMillan had 14 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns, and Carolina kept finding ways to move the football.
At some point, three games like that can't just be brushed off as a couple of good Sundays.
The other thing I like is that it doesn't feel like one guy has to do everything. McMillan has obviously been a huge part of what Carolina is doing, but Jalen Coker has made plays, Chuba Hubbard is still a big piece of the offense, and Young has more places to go with the football.
That's a much different feeling from what we've seen in Carolina lately. There have been plenty of Sundays when getting to 20 points felt like pulling teeth. Now the Panthers have gone over 30 three times in four games.
I'm not going to sit here after four games and say Carolina suddenly has one of the best offenses in football. That's getting a little ahead of ourselves, and there are going to be games when it doesn't look this good.
But I'm also done acting like what we've seen so far doesn't mean anything.
Maybe Panthers fans are still getting used to that part. We've watched enough bad offense over the last few years that it's probably natural to see Carolina putting up points and immediately wonder when it's going to stop.
We aren't even a quarter of the way through the season, so there's a long way to go. But three games with more than 30 points are enough for me to at least start looking at this offense a little differently.
That fan on Reddit asked a pretty good question.
Maybe this offense really is legit.

title: 4 Bold Panthers Predictions That Could Turn Week 6 Upside Down
full_text:
If you had asked me after the Chicago game if the Panthers could go into Philadelphia and beat the Eagles, I probably would've laughed. Now? I think they can.
I'm not saying Carolina suddenly has everything figured out because they beat Detroit. I watched the Bears put 59 points on this team in Week 1, and I'm definitely not forgetting that. But I've also watched the Panthers look like a completely different team since then.
Philadelphia isn't exactly rolling right now, either. The Eagles have lost three straight after falling 19-17 to Jacksonville on Sunday, while Carolina got a week off after beating Detroit 32-26. I don't know if the Panthers are suddenly better than Philadelphia, but I'm not looking at this game the same way I was a month ago.
Maybe I'm buying in a little too much. We'll find out Sunday, but here are four predictions I'm willing to put out there.
I'm finally starting to trust Bryce Young, and it's taken me a while to get here. We've done this before with Young. He'll play well, everybody starts talking about how he's turned the corner, and I'm usually sitting there thinking, “OK, show me again.”
I don't think that's unfair after everything we've watched during his first few years in Carolina. Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit, and he now has 1,268 passing yards and nine touchdowns through four games. He's only thrown two interceptions, and Carolina isn't asking him to just stay out of the way anymore.
They're putting the ball in his hands and letting him go win games.
I expect Philadelphia to come after him on Sunday. I'd also expect the Eagles to make stopping Chuba Hubbard a priority after he ran for 122 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit. If they load up against Hubbard and basically tell Young, “Go beat us,” I'm interested to see what happens.
A month ago, I would've said that's exactly what Philadelphia should do. I'm not so sure anymore.
Prediction: Young throws for 315 yards and two touchdowns.
OK, this one might get me in trouble. Tetairoa McMillan just caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit, and now I'm asking him to go into Philadelphia and score twice again.
I'm not predicting another 192 yards because that would be getting a little ridiculous. If he does that again, we're going to have to start having a much different conversation about just how good McMillan already is. But I can't get away from how much Young trusts him.
When Carolina needs a play, everybody watching knows where Young wants to go with the football. The defense knows it too, and lately it hasn't mattered. Philadelphia is obviously going to have a plan for McMillan after watching what he did to Detroit, and I wouldn't be surprised if he sees extra attention, especially around the red zone.
I'm still taking him. Maybe I'm asking for too much here, but McMillan has reached the point where I'm done trying to figure out what his ceiling is every week.
Prediction: McMillan goes over 100 receiving yards and catches two touchdowns.
I don't know what to do with this Panthers defense anymore. I just wrote an entire article trying to figure them out, and I'm still not sure I did. They give up too many yards, they don't get nearly enough pressure, and there are drives where I'm sitting there wondering how they're ever going to get off the field.
Then somebody makes a play.
Carolina has eight takeaways through four games. At first, I kept wondering how long that could continue, but we're getting to the point where maybe I need to stop asking that question. Maybe this is just what this defense is.
I'm not predicting Carolina shuts down Jalen Hurts because I don't believe that's happening. Hurts is going to make plays, Philadelphia is going to move the football, and there will probably be a couple of drives where this Panthers defense drives me crazy. But if Carolina can give Young two extra possessions, that could completely change this game.
And I've got a feeling one of them comes late.
Prediction: Hurts turns it over twice, including once in the fourth quarter.
This was one of those games I looked at before the season and pretty much put in the loss column. Carolina going into Philadelphia and winning? I would've needed to see a whole lot before I was willing to make that pick, and I think I've seen enough.
That doesn't mean I'm sitting here telling you Carolina is better than Philadelphia. I'm not. But the Panthers don't have to be the better team for the entire season. They just have to be better for three hours Sunday, and right now I'm not sure Philadelphia is playing better football than Carolina.
The Eagles have lost three straight, while the Panthers went into the bye after beating a Detroit team that I wasn't sure they were ready to beat. Young is playing the best football we've seen from him, McMillan looks like a legitimate No. 1 receiver, and Hubbard just ran for 122 yards against Detroit. Then there's that defense I still can't figure out, but somehow it keeps getting the ball back.
Maybe this completely blows up in my face. Philadelphia could come out angry after losing three straight, score a couple of quick touchdowns, and have me regretting every word of this by halftime. That's part of making a bold prediction.
A month ago, there's no chance I pick Carolina here.

title: The Panthers Are Making Bryce Young's Job Nearly Impossible. He's Doing It Anyway
full_text:
I'm starting to run out of things to question about Bryce Young , and I didn't think I'd be saying that four games into this season.
I've been hard on Young. I don't think I've been unfair, but I've definitely been one of those people who wanted to see more before I started believing he had finally turned the corner. One good game wasn't going to do it for me, and honestly, two probably weren't either.
How often NFL quarterbacks have been under pressure and how they've fared in 2026 Bryce Young has been terrific despite a shakier #Panthers OL pic.twitter.com/qD73ja5vWT
Then I saw this chart from PFF's Bradley Locker, and it made me look at what Young is doing a little differently. I knew Carolina's offensive line had struggled. You don't watch these games and miss how often Young has somebody coming after him, but I didn't realize it was happening this much.
Young has been pressured on roughly 47% of his dropbacks. That's almost half. Look at Locker's chart, and Young is sitting way over on the right, almost by himself, while still carrying a passing grade under pressure of around 64.
I looked at it and thought, how in the world is he playing this well?
For most of Young's career, I've wondered what he would look like if Carolina could just give him some help. Get him a legitimate receiver. Give him a running game. Protect him. Put something around the guy, and let's find out whether he can actually play.
Carolina has finally done some of that. Tetairoa McMillan looks like a legitimate No. 1 receiver, Chuba Hubbard has been really good, and the offense looks nothing like some of the messes we've watched the last few years.
The protection is where things haven't gone nearly as well.
There are reasons for that. Taylor Moton has been out, Monroe Freeling has had to move to right tackle after playing almost exclusively on the left side at Georgia, and Damien Lewis missed the Detroit game. Corey Bullock had to step in at left guard, so Carolina hasn't exactly had the luxury of putting the same five guys out there every week and forgetting about it.
I get all of that, but 47% is still 47%. At some point, I stopped looking at that chart and thinking about the offensive line and started thinking about Young. Because if we're going to criticize him when he doesn't play well — and I certainly have — then I think we have to give him some credit for what he's doing right now.
Young has thrown for 1,268 yards, nine touchdowns, and only two interceptions through four games. He just threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit in a game I wasn't sure Carolina could win. And he's doing all of this while getting pressured on almost half of his dropbacks.
Maybe I've been looking at Young the wrong way.
I spent a lot of time wondering whether he could be good enough if Carolina finally put the right pieces around him. Now I'm starting to wonder how good he could be if the Panthers actually kept him clean. That's a much different conversation than the ones we've been having about Young for the last few years.
I'm still not ready to go crazy after four games. There's a lot of football left, and Philadelphia coming out of the bye is going to tell us even more about where Young and this offense really are. Ask me again in a couple of weeks, and maybe I'll feel completely different.
But I'm also not going to keep moving the goalposts every time Young answers another question. I wanted to see him do it more than once, and he has. I wanted to see what happened when things weren't perfect around him, and I think getting pressured on nearly half of his dropbacks answers that one pretty well.
Now, for the love of God, can somebody block for him?

title: Chargers Projected to Make Blockbuster Trade Soon & Panthers Must Be on Receiving End
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers entered this season with one unit most in need of improvement: the pass rush. Carolina's pass rush was the worst in the NFL in 2025, making it the focal point of free agency .
Carolina's splash signing of Jaelan Phillips showed how desperate the Panthers were to improve the pass rush, and while it has improved thus far, the room lacks depth.
The Panthers already started the season down a pass rusher, as second-year EDGE Nic Scourton tore his ACL on the first day of training camp. Now, Jaelan Phillips is hurt . It's not nearly as serious, but his status for Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles is in question.
Phillips hurt his hamstring in Carolina's Week 4 victory over the Detroit Lions, and there's been no confirmation that he'll be ready to roll this week and return to where he played last season in Philadelphia.
This isn't just a Week 6 concern either. Hamstring injuries are notoriously prone to lingering and can be easily aggravated or just last longer than expected.
With that said, Carolina should be looking at the trade market , and one veteran could welcome a change of scenery this season.
CBS Sports' Carter Bahns released his list of NFL trade-deadline candidates on Monday. With the deadline is just less than a month away, veterans across the league could head to new teams where they can contribute to winning and fill a need.
Los Angeles Chargers EDGE Khalil Mack certainly isn't in the right situation to contribute to winning, and that's not his fault. The Chargers are horrendous at almost everything, so no one would blame Mack for wanting to leave Los Angeles and join a team that isn't 0-5.
Unless the Chargers pull off a miracle turnaround and make the playoffs after a 0-5 start, something no team has ever done, they should invest in the 2027 NFL Draft.
That starts with trading away veterans to contenders or teams looking to make a playoff push. The Panthers fall into that category.
Still a talented player, but Mack is 35 years old and is on an expiring contract. GM Dan Morgan and the Panthers wouldn't have to cripple their upcoming draft to land Mack.
A reasonable trade package for Mack would just be a fourth- or sixth-round pick. Carolina doesn't have a fifth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, but it does have two fourth-rounders and a sixth.

title: Familiar Face to Bears May Have Provided Path to Open up Ground Game
full_text:
Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor is tasked with finding a way to kick start the Bears running attack a week after it failed miserably against Green Bay .
Considering they are facing an Atlanta defense that ranks No. 4 against the run ane are down running back Kyle Monangai due to a toe injury while D'Andre Swift doesn't look entirely healthy, this might be among the toughest assignments facing the Bears this week.
Then again, they seem to have two factors working in their favor.
For one, Ravens just trampled the Falcons using many of the run-blocking concepts the Bears use.
"Yeah, they did a good job just with some of their downhill schemes," Taylor said. "(Derrick) Henry did a great job bouncing a couple things. There were a couple things they had some gap schemes on that got boxed, and he was able to bounce outside the edge setter.
Derrick Henry bulldozes his way for another first down 😤 @BALvsATL on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/rHZW07dVYP
"Obviously, Baltimore is a talented unit in terms of their run game. Big, physical group, big, physical running back, playing with the backup quarterback as well, they committed to it, they had a lot of success with it. I think it’s something they caught them, were having success and were able to ride the wave of it, and then Derrick Henry is able to find some things and create some big run lanes for them."
And No. 2? The Ravens' offensive coordinator is, of course, former Bears offensive coordinator Declan Doyle.
"I talk to Declan every once in a while," Taylor said coyly.
WICKED play call by Declan Doyle. pic.twitter.com/xGsqKUz244
The implication, of course, is the Ravens coordinator might point the way where the Bears could get something to work better than on the ground against Green Bay last week. After all, Doyle's Ravens just ran for 208 yards against an Atlanta defense that hadn't allowed more than 68 this year.
Even if it isn't quite as simple as Doyle helping out his old team, his Ravens ground game isn't a lot different than what the Bears try to do and the Bears can follow Baltimore's lead.
It's not quite a template, though. The Bears are missing some things.
The Bears don't have Derrick Henry, obviously. They didn't have Monangai at practice Wednesday or Thursday due to turf toe and it would appear they won't again this week. Their running attack tried to compensate last week by using more wide receiver runs and also deploying Roschon Johnson in the Monangai role, but he isn't quite the same back.
The @AtlantaFalcons were great against the run until we met Derrick Henry. Good God!
"Never felt like we were able to get in a rhythm where some of these runs were hitting," Taylor said. "These previous two games, we’ve been very efficient on first and second down. We’re calling a ton of plays. The whole game plan is open for you. Where it just felt like the other day, it was 1st-and-10, 2nd-and-9, you’re kind of playing behind the sticks a little bit more than we wanted to, and then the game kind of gets away from you a little bit in the fourth quarter, you’re kind of in dropback mode, and it changes the way you operate, obviously.
"So, the end of the game, you’re looking back, you got however many carries you got. Well the fourth quarter of the game is a completely different game script than we anticipated playing there."
They do have a back closer to Henry's size in 6-foot-1, 220-pound Zavier Scott, the former Vikings back who is on the practice squad. He was promoted last week but didn't play on offense. Scott has legs the size of tree trunks, but hasn't really been in Ben Johnson's offense to any extent.
Something else could assist their ground game this week and that's Caleb Williams' possible return. He has seven first downs rushing and two TDs to go with 105 yards total for less than two games.  There could be other changes to the ground game to spark it. The Bears still lead the NFL in rushing but definitely didn't look like it last week.
"We'll look at what we've done well, what we haven't done well, and take the quarterback position into consideration when we're looking at that," Ben Johnson said. "But running game-wise, the types of throws that we're asking our quarterbacks to do, our route runners in general, the things we take a lot of pride in on offense are how we go about our business from a fundamentals technique and finish standpoint.
"And those things aren't consistent at the level with which we would like them to be right now."
Maybe Declan Doyle can help ... in an indirect way, of course.
“This game sets up beautifully for Ben Johnson.” @danorlovsky7 and @Hawk preview the Bears-Falcons matchup in Atlanta 💪 pic.twitter.com/4MCfmwzLiq

title: Bears Show Faith in Tyson Bagent Even After Catastrophic Packers Game
full_text:
Life moves pretty fast in the NFL, especially for a backup quarterback like Tyson Bagent. In Week 4, he guided the Chicago Bears to a second straight victory without Caleb Williams, but in the next he threw two picks and eventually got benched in a disastrous loss to the Green Bay Packers .
Many Bears fans expected that to be the end of the Tyson Bagent experiment in Chicago, but it doesn't seem like the Bears have lost faith in their backup quarterback. According to Sean Hammond , a Bears reporter for the Chicago Tribune, Bagent took the second-team reps in Thursday's practice behind Caleb Williams, who was listed as a full participant again in the Bears' Thursday injury report .
This is significant for two reasons. First of all, if Caleb Williams does return from injury in Week 6 , Bagent will likely serve as the backup quarterback. Second, if Williams is still not cleared to play on Sunday, then it is likely that we will see Bagent make his third consecutive start, his second on the road.
Some Bears fans won't like to hear that, and one can hardly blame them. Bagent was flat-out awful in Week 5 and was, in some ways, the biggest reason why Chicago couldn't even get close to Green Bay. According to Pro Football Network , he had -0.41 Expected Points Added (EPA) per dropback and earned just a 65.9 impact grade.
However, if anyone in Chicago has earned the benefit of the doubt by now, it's head coach Ben Johnson. His list of accomplishments is already long for a guy who's only been the head coach here for 22 regular season games, and it includes Chicago's first playoff victory in 15 years. He also went 2-1 without his starting quarterback, which is pretty impressive considering neither backup quarterback had started a regular season game in three years.
Sunday's game is still a few days away, and maybe Case Keenum gets the second-team reps in the Bears' last practice. But it's currently looking like Bagent hsa retained his backup quarterback job. If that is the case, then that is because Johnson believes he gives the Bears the best chance to win. And if Johnson believes that, then that should be good enough for Bears fans.
A former Marine and Purdue Boilermaker, Pete has been covering the Chicago Bears since 2022 as a senior contributor on BearsTalk. He lives with his wife, two kids and loyal dog.

title: Caleb Williams Shuts Down Bears Reporter Over Injury Secrecy Questions, Responds to Ridicule
full_text:
For the first time since his hamstring injury in Week 2, Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams addressed the media after practicing on Thursday.
During Williams' media availability, reporters asked the Bears signal-caller what the severity of his injury was.
Williams revealed that his injury was given a grade and he called it a "hamstring tear, a pretty serious one," but he would not say what that grade was because of "all the false ones" that were put out there.
When he was pushed for an exact answer by another reporter, Williams bluntly shut the reporter down.
"Yeah, we got a grade, but I wouldn't say it's deserved to be put out there after all the false ones," Williams said . "Next question."
"Why keep the details of the injury secret?" a reporter asked later.
"Because it's not deserving," Williams said.
"Why?" the reporter followed up.
"Just not deserving. Next question," Williams responded before reiterating, "Next question. Thank you. Next question" as the reporter continued to push.
Credit to Caleb Williams here My goodness pic.twitter.com/Tx62mohmf2
Clearly Williams had no interest in answering the question and that is his right. The reporter should have backed off and let that be the end of it.
Williams went down with the injury in the fourth quarter of the loss to the Minnesota Vikings. Based on his reaction to the injury, the need for a cart, and the fact that it was of the non-contact variety, everyone thought that Williams had suffered a catastrophic injury.
After it was initially reported that Williams may only have a minor hamstring injury, the Bears quarterback faced a ton of ridicule for how he reacted to it.
Ultimately, it turned out Williams did not suffer a minor injury and it was instead diagnosed as a Grade 2 hamstring strain, per reports, and the injury has kept him out for three games. Now you can understand why he was frustrated with the reporting.
When asked about the ridicule he received initially, Williams said he was unbothered by it. He also noted how he thought he might have suffered a season-ending injury because he felt a "pop."
“Not being able to be out there was frustrating. That was more of the tears or whatever that was. The other half of it was everybody making jokes and all that, but that doesn’t bother me," he said .
"I'm always going to show emotion, especially when I can't be out there with the guys," Williams said , per The Chicago Tribune's Sean Hammond.
“I felt a pop. I did not know if it would be season ending," he added .
While two straight days of full practices suggests that Williams is going to play, the Bears quarterback would not confirm if he will.
Instead, Williams said he isn't sure and he still has to pass some tests before he can be cleared to take the field.
"Before you start asking, (I) do not know if I'm playing yet," Williams revealed.
"This is a big week. I've been going through cutting and planting over the past couple weeks and it's felt good, you've seen me moving around on Fridays and before games," he said . "But it's different when you have to go through a full week of practice, prepare for a game, and take on that stress on the mind, body, and spirit. We'll see how it goes."
The Bears will drop their final injury report of the week on Friday, so we'll know more about where Williams stands then.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Chicago Bears Are Logical Landing Spot For 2 Tampa Bay Buccaneers Trade Candidates
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have a pair of needs on the defensive line and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers could offer a one-stop shop for general manager Ryan Poles.
Those needs come at edge rusher and on the interior of the defensive line, two spots that have been a concern since the offseason .
In an article listing off potential trade candidates, USA TODAY's Nate Davis named Bucs defensive lineman Vita Vea and edge rusher Yaya Diaby as two of them.
"Vea, who’s 31 and got a Band-Aid addendum to his contract as opposed to a lengthy extension after a summer standoff, could also make a much bigger impact for another team than he probably will for the Bucs this year," Davis wrote.
"Diaby, in the final year of his rookie contract, could come much cheaper. He picked off Dak Prescott in last week’s upset of Dallas and had seven sacks and 66 pressures last year," Davis added.
The Bucs are sitting at 1-4 this season and their playoff hopes are on thin ice, to say the least. Only one team in NFL history has ever overcome an 0-4 start to make the playoffs, so things are looking bleak in Tampa Bay.
Vea and the Bucs had a contract standoff this offseason before he was given a band-aid extension , and there could be another standoff in 2027 when Vea enters the final year of that deal.
The Bucs, would be wise to unload him if they continue to look like they won't make the playoffs, as they can maximize the return with Vea still having one year left on his contract.
Diaby is in the final year of his rookie deal and that could push the Bucs to trade him. However, Diaby's value is low because he has struggled to get after the quarterback in 2026 with zero sacks.
The Bears do need help at edge rusher and along the interior of the defensive line.
The former group has been OK but not great, with Montez Sweat, who is now suspended , being a disappointment. Dayo Odeyingbo is hurt, also, and could miss multiple games with his quad injury.
The interior of the defensive line has lacked pass-rush juice, with Kentavius Street being the only one who has posted a sack. And, run defense hasn't been great, either, with the Bears tied for the 11th-most yards per carry allowed this season.
We can do without Diaby considering his lack of sack production. We would prefer the Bears aim higher, although if it's between nothing and Diaby, we'd still take the veteran edge rusher.
Vea is the one we really want.
The two-time Pro Bowler hasn't posted a sack this season, but he does have a long history of solid sack production, as evidenced by his posting 4.5 sacks or more in each of the last four seasons, including a career-high seven in 2024.
Vea has proven to be a plus run defender during his time in the NFL, with the 31-year-old tallying Pro Football Focus grades of 60.8 or better in each of the last three campaigns.
When it comes to cost, the acquiring team may not have to pay more than a Day 3 pick for each considering Diaby and Vea are in the midst of a down year.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Could Rome Odunze's Struggles Open a Door For Zavion Thomas
full_text:
Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze hasn't lived up to expectations through his first two and a half seasons. He entered the league with massive expectations after he was selected with the ninth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.
Nevertheless, his career has been eerily similar to another early-round disappointment who was selected five picks earlier. Marvin Harrison Jr. only lasted 33 games in Arizona before they traded him to the Texans for a second-round pick earlier this week.
Career numbers: Rome Odunze: -115-1,668-9 in 34 games -49.1 yards per game -14.5 yards per reception, 7.6 yards per target Marvin Harrison Jr.: -108-1,578-13 in 33 games -47.8 yards per game -14.6 yards per reception, 7.8 yards per target
Odunze has shown legit flashes of potential, but they've unfortunately come via waves of inconsistency and poor play. He enjoyed one of the best games of his career against the Jets , catching six of seven targets for 94 yards. However, he followed it up with a three-catch (off nine targets), 40-yard, one-lost-fumble clunker against Green Bay.
Five of Odunze's nine career receiving scores came over the first four games of the 2025 campaign. He has only four touchdowns over the other 32 contests (including the Bears' two playoff games last season).
While Ben Johnson and Co. aren't likely to give Odunze the MHJ treatment anytime soon, it's fair to question whether his role could diminish if consistency issues persist. That could potentially open the door for rookie receiver Zavion Thomas to carve out a bigger role on offense .
The Bears surprised the masses when they pulled the trigger on Thomas with the 89th pick of the 2026 NFL Draft. The decision was largely met with confusion, as many expected the LSU product would hear his name called around the fifth round.
Thomas was one of the best return specialists, but many questioned whether he could make an early impact as a pass-catcher. Nevertheless, Johnson saw something he could work with, and the vision was clear as day once he finally made his debut in the preseason finale against Tennessee.
The rookie caught five passes for 140 yards, including an electric 97-yard sprint on Chicago's first play from scrimmage. He also showed some promise on special teams, returning his lone punt return for 39 yards.
ZAVION. THOMAS. 📺: #CHIvsTEN on FOX32 pic.twitter.com/I4NNX2d9KJ
The early promise didn't immediately translate to the regular season, but Thomas finally made a dent in the box score in the team's Week 5 loss against the Packers. He was one of their few bright spots (albeit in limited action) on offense.
He finished the contest with an 11-yard catch and an 11-yard run. The stat line doesn't jump off the screen, but his speed was evident. It was also evident in the return game, where he nearly housed a kickoff (gaining 61 yards) at the start of the fourth quarter.
It's also worth noting that Luther Burden III had a quiet start to his rookie campaign before catching fire late last season. As did Colston Loveland. Thomas might not boast the same draft pedigree, but he has plenty of talent in his own right .
While Odunze's size allows him to do things Thomas cannot, the same sentiment can be applied to the latter's speed. With Caleb Williams looking likely to return to the lineup soon, that could unlock Chicago's deep passing game. That could allow the rookie to carve out a bigger role on offense.

title: An Inconvenient Bears Truth Over Losing Dayo Odeyingbo and Montez Sweat
full_text:
The Bears can be fairly certain they'll face quarterback Michael Penix Jr. this week even after his rib injury because he went through a full practice on Wednesday and Atlanta is talking him up as a starter.
Of course, this isn't the real danger they face against Atlanta's offense. Their pass defense will get challenged by an assortment of dangerous weapons but the real threat comes from running back Bijan Robinson, and they haven't had a strong history of shutting down top runners under defensive coordinator Dennis Allen .
A teammate for two years of Robinson's, Bears defensive tackle Grady Jarrett has a pretty good idea what his teammates need to hear about trying to stop the former Texas standout.
“That it’s going to take everybody doing what we need to do in attacking the line of scrimmage, not playing passively, not playing selfishly," Jarrett said. "It takes a whole unit to attempt to slow down a special player like Bijan
"God-given ability to see, to burst, to separate, to contact balance, I mean this is a really, really special player, special person, and he knows he’s the bloodline of that organization. So we’ve got a heck of a challenge ahead of us.”
. @clayharbs82 doesn't think Bears defensive end Montez Sweat's 2-game suspension is that big of a deal. "He's not even stopping the run that well, he's not getting off of blocks, he's not pressuring the quarterback," Harbor says. "Dayo Odeyingbo will be missed more." pic.twitter.com/8d43G8U5Wg
Robinson leads the NFL with 580 rushing yards this year after he had successive 1,400-yard seasons. The 5-foot-11, 215-pound back averages 5.0 yards a carry while the Bears give up 4.4 a carry to rank 22nd in the league. Robinson ran for 194 yards against the Packers in Atlanta's 35-14 rout of Green Bay on Sept. 24.
Robinson also is a threat as a receiver. He had an eight-catch, 90-yard opener against Pittsburgh.
The Bears haven't completely shut down good runners since Allen became their defensive coordinator, but they have managed to avoid getting completely trampled except in a few instances.
Sweat suspended Dayo missing time Pick up the phone, Poles https://t.co/mrbOGYggON pic.twitter.com/PrAN7nLQpe
Christian McCaffrey hit them for 23 runs and 140 yards last year, and Ashton Jeanty had 138 yards on 21 carries. Jahmyr Gibbs piled up 174 yards on 31 carries over two consistent efforts against them for Detroit.
This year, they gave up 105 yards to 31-year-old Aaron Jones in the opener but no one else has approached triple figures against them.
Watching Bijan Robinson run is art pic.twitter.com/EBVQzofNyU
The problem is they're coming off their worst overall defensive game of the season and got exposed downfield in the secondary by Green Bay and Jordan Love.
"We've got a big challenge coming up in terms of the running game," coach Ben Johnson said. "This is an elite running game in the NFL led by a guy that might be leading the charge for MVP right now. That's first and foremost. Then, of course, we've got to clean up some of the issues that we put on tape last week with the explosive plays.
"It's not going to be a talent-level issue or anything like that. We've got plenty of guys, and now we've just got to play together as one unit, and all 11 on the same page, and we'll take it from there.”
The Packers were manipulating the hell out of the Bears defense when they would put all 3 LBs on the field. Motion widens Bush out of the box, 93 ends up backdooring the zone run making the gap wider, and 48 can't get over. Easy recipe for giving up a 20+ yard run pic.twitter.com/rGGnh0qzDH
Then again, the talent normally assigned with being most stout on the edge to turn back running games will not be available. One of Atlanta's great strengths is running the wide zone blocking scheme like the Bears utilize on offense, so run-stopping defensive ends are critical in this game.
Montez Sweat's all-around ability has been his strength since arriving in 2023, but he's suspended for a PED violation. Dayo Odeyingbo was brought to Chicago as a stout run stopper, not necessarily a standout pass rusher. And he has a quad injury labeled week to week, which usually means missing at least one game, if not more. Edge Austin Booker is regarded as a strong pass rusher but his run-stopping ability has been called inconsistent against coaches.
James Lynch had a nice game after a rough start last week. Really good run defender from the end position very tough block for TEs. Not the most athletic but physical and relentless. Snap count went up from 22 to 28 snaps #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/Z3pxfQcKPN
They'll get Shemar Turner back this week but he has barely played for the Bears. He played only 33 snaps on the outside and 39 in the B-gap or over tackle last year before tearing his ACL. They can't really anticipate what they'd get from someone who is essentially a rookie with about the equivalent of one game of experience.
Edge Daniel Hardy is a pass rusher and special teams player. The only defensive end they'll have available this week with a proven track record as a run stopper is James Lynch. His reputation as a solid run defender goes back four seasons with the Titans, Vikings and now the Bears. Pro Football Focus grades him 34th out of 106 edge players against the run this season, but he's been on the field for only 95 defensive plays, 54 of them runs.
Lynch wasn't even active against the Jets, but one of the most obscure facts about this Bears defense is Lynch actually started three of their five games. They kept Booker on the bench to start every game. Booker's play count will now need to be what starters normally would get and he expects the defense will benefit.
Austin Booker one arm bull rush blows up Belton and forces a fumble. pic.twitter.com/YRPXmSu3nM
"I think that just when you see the snap count go up you see the production go up," he said. "And I think that’s all there is to it."
They have to hope he's right because it's not going to be easy stopping the NFL rushing leader and a pass rush isn't much good when the back is running around end for 100 yards or more.
Allen's defense has often been accused of overemphasizing run defense on the edge in the past and sacrificing pass rush. It's why he wants at least one edge over 280 pounds and preferably two.
Ironically, now they're facing an opponent where this is really essential. And they lack the depth of manpower to pull it off because of Sweat's suspension and Odeyingbo's injury.
Austin Booker hustling to the ball and peanut punch. Excellent play. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/EvL45EfWHX

title: Six Bears Who Need a Bounce Back Game in Week 6 vs Falcons
full_text:
Despite a disastrous Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers , the Chicago Bears are not in dire straits, nor is their season already over. The fact is that they're currently 3-2, tied with the Detroit Lions and Green Bay Packers for second in the NFC North, and they're set to see Caleb Williams return from injury this week . It's far too early to panic, though that won't stop some Bears fans from firing up the mock draft generators.
Just because the team is in a good place, however, doesn't mean that every player is safe. Some Bears' careers are currently circling the drain, and they'll need a bounce back game against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 6 just to have a prayer of sticking around in Chicago beyond this season. Others need a good game on Sunday just to remind the fans and the NFL world who they are.
With that in mind, here are five players and one coach who need to put their best foot forward in their next game.
Jaylon Johnson is the Bears' $76 million question . Can the two-time Pro Bowler pull out of this rut, or is his career well and truly in a tailspin? If the former, then Johnson needs to prove it by playing the best football of his life for the final two-thirds of the season, and that starts on Sunday. If the latter, then I expect this to be the last we see of Jaylon Johnson in a Bears uniform, and what a tragic turn of events that would be.
While his seat is not nearly as hot as the other Johnson's, head coach Ben Johnson didn't exactly cover himself in glory last week. His team was favored to win at Lambeau Field for the first time in 20 years, and yet his offense could muster up only seven points. No, Johnson didn't throw four interceptions or lose a fumble, but as the head coach, the buck stops with him.
The fact is that Johnson has a rivalry problem , and though the Atlanta Falcons aren't a rival, he desperately needs a high-scoring game to remind the league that he's still one of the top offensive minds in the world.
Cairo Santos' missed field goal attempt against the Packers didn't cost them the game, but it robbed the team of any hope of building momentum and catching the Packers in another comeback. Santos, who turns 35 next month, has been arguably the best kicker in franchise history, but his short range and occasional mind-boggling missed kicks prevent the fans from feeling too confident when he takes the field.
In order to put the fanbase at ease, Satos needs to boot a couple of field goals from at least 40 yards away on Sunday.
The 2026 season has not been a good one for D'Andre Swift. Since his explosive performance in the season-opener , Swift has struggled mightily, scoring just one touchdown and averaging less than four yards per carry. Last week, he only got nine rushing attempts even with Kyle Monangai ruled out with a turf toe injury.
If Monangai is still unable to play in Week 6, one would hope that we'd see a heavy dose of D'Andre Swift in the running game, and he needs to be ready to deliver another big performance. The Bears didn't sign him to a three-year extension in August just to see him become a backup running back, after all.
The Bears' first-round rookie is having a terrific debut season so far, but Week 5 wasn't his best effort. He allowed a 112.5 passer rating to quarterback Jordan Love, according to Pro Football Network . He was also in position to break up a 3rd-and-22 heave into the endzone, but he didn't get his head around and allowed a touchdown, which pretty much ended the game.
Thieneman's a rookie, and he's going to take his rookie lumps. That play and that whole game was one of them. But now he needs to show that he's mature enough to not let one rough game beget another. Whether Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. plays through his injury or not, there should be ample opportunities for Thieneman to course-correct in Week 6.
Unlike the rest of this list, Williams is not yet confirmed to be playing on Sunday, though all signs are pointing to his return in Week 6 . If he does in fact play, Williams needs a bounce back game more for the sake of the team than himself. Clearly this offense doesn't work nearly as well without Williams, and a case could be made that they'd currently be 5-0 had he never got hurt back in Week 2.
Nevertheless, if the Bears are to avoid back-to-back losses and a 3-3 start to the season, they need Williams to return with a vengeance. As for Williams himself, some folks around the NFL world were quick to forget the 59-point performance he dropped on the raod against a very good Carolina Panthers team in the season opener. A Week 6 barnburner would be the best way to remind the NFL exactly who he is.
A former Marine and Purdue Boilermaker, Pete has been covering the Chicago Bears since 2022 as a senior contributor on BearsTalk. He lives with his wife, two kids and loyal dog.

title: Everything Chicago Bears Have to Fear About Atlanta Falcons in Week 6
full_text:
The Chicago Bears and Atlanta Falcons enter their Week 6 battle sitting in the same boat.
The Bears are coming off a brutal loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 5 that saw Chicago get blown out by its division rival on the strength of putrid performances from quarterback Tyson Bagent and the defense.
The Falcons, meanwhile, had a much closer game, but the result was the same, as Atlanta lost to the Baltimore Ravens, 30-23, in overtime after blowing a fourth-quarter lead.
Atlanta presents plenty of concerns for the Bears in Week 6. Here's a look at four of them.
The Falcons' pass-rush has generated 11 sacks this season, tied for the 12th-most in the NFL. What makes that impressive is the fact that Atlanta hasn't had its two best pass-rushers, Jalon Walker and James Pearce.
While they haven't been elite at taking down the quarterback, the Falcons are tied for the fifth-most pressures in the NFL and rank fourth in ESPN's pass-rush win rate .
A lot of that has to do with defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich exceling at drawing up blitzes to help create more pressure.
This would be a good week for Caleb Williams to return, as the Bears will need his mobility to counteract the pressures the Falcons can bring. So far, it looks like he might just be back .
Bijan Robinson is playing like the best running back on the planet this season. Not only does he lead the NFL in rushing yards going into Week 6, he also has the elusiveness and vision that makes it look like everyone is moving in slow motion around him.
The Bears actually have the ninth-best run defense in the NFL in 2026, but some of that has to do with the fact that teams are just chucking it down the field on them.
ESPN's run stop win rate metric isn't as kind, with the Bears ranking 29th in that category.
Chicago will have to put its best foot forward on Sunday and even that may not be enough to stop Robinson.
Ever since the Falcons started getting competent quarterback play from Michael Penix Jr., London's fortunes have changed.
In the first two games without Penix, London had six catches for 80 yards. In the last three games with Penix under center, 21 catches for 408 yards.
Given the fact that Tyrique Stevenson and Jaylon Johnson have struggled badly this season , it's hard to envision a scenario in which London, who lines up all over the field, doesn't go off.
The hope is Kyler Gordon can return and push Malik Muhammad to more boundary snaps over Stevenson, but that isn't going to help the Bears hide Johnson.
Even if Gordon plays, he isn't likely to see a full workload. It's also unfair to put the tall task of stopping London on Muhammad.
One way to slow down the Falcons' pass-rush is to get the ground game going. Unfortunately for the Bears, that could prove to be difficult, with Atlanta sporting the fourth-best run defense.
The Bears sport the No. 1 rushing attack in the NFL, but they are also coming off a poor showing on the ground in Week 5 and might not have Kyle Monangai, who is dealing with turf toe.
Not having Monangai for a second consecutive game would be bad news, as he has been Chicago's most consistent running back.

title: Chicago Bears Roster Analysis: 3 Players Ben Johnson Can't Trust
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are 3-2 after an embarrassing and injury-filled 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.
The good news is that Caleb Williams was a full participant in the team's walkthrough and could be on his way back from a hamstring injury.
Chicago's starting quarterback was injured in Week 2 against the Minnesota Vikings and returns at the best time possible.
The bad news is that Bears coach Ben Johnson learned during this stretch that there are three players who can't be trusted in the offense right now.
On Sunday, Tyson Bagent proved why this team is in trouble at quarterback without a healthy Williams.
Case Keenum did too, to a lesser degree, but everyone understood the 38-year-old was an emergency option.
Bagent tanked his trade value during the two-pick, 87-yard, 12-of-21 dud in Green Bay. Worst of all, he may have given Johnson pause about handing him the offense again if Williams has any re-injury concerns.
It's unclear what Chicago's future is at the position behind Williams.
It's hard to imagine it being Bagent after Week 5.
It's very difficult to justify giving Roschon Johnson any of the backup snaps behind D'Andre Swift until Kyle Monangai returns from a turf toe.
Monangai isn't on track to return this coming weekend against the Atlanta Falcons after not practicing this week.
Johnson had six rushing yards on five carries against the Packers, with his longest rush of the day being three yards. While he did haul in five catches for 34 yards, that's not sustainable.
Johnson benefitted from having Bagent play it safe when he wasn't airing the ball down the field to minimal success.
Besides his rookie season, Johnson hasn't seen much success on the Bears. We'll see if Zavier Scott or Salvon Ahmed get a chance off the practice squad against Atlanta at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Garrett Bradbury has had a rough go at it at the center spot for Chicago this season.
While he wasn't the worst offender against Green Bay, he didn't help establish the run with a solid interior push.
Against the Vikings in Week 2, he had four penalties in one half . Things have gotten better for Bradbury, but not by much.
Rookie Logan Jones may not be far off from getting the call to start in the middle, especially if the offense continues to sputter.
Bradbury's best chance of sticking is Williams being too tough to catch once he's back under center.

title: Bengals Must Avoid This Tempting Trade Deadline Mistake
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are 3-2 as they hit the early Week 6 bye week. The win over the Miami Dolphins this past Sunday was massive, but the team left a lot of meat on the bone during that performance.
The passing game has been exactly what everyone expected. Joe Burrow and his merry band of weapons are one of the most dangerous passing offenses in the league. Then you have a revamped defensive line that is causing terror, alongside an offensive line that is a night-and-day difference from the past few seasons. But there's a reason this team is just 3-2.
One of the biggest weaknesses on this team has been the running game. The Bengals are 26th in rushing yards this season at 414. Chase Brown leads the team in rushing with 246 yards, but it hasn't been enough. While there have been issues with the unit, a tempting trade at the deadline would be a bad move.
Trying to upgrade at the trade deadline in this league has to feel like an impossible task. Very few teams would be willing to give up a running back that the Bengals would arguably be their number one option.
So, let's look at a name that could come up before the deadline. Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard may seem like a great trade candidate and one the Bengals may want to look into.
Pollard's numbers are very similar to Browns. The Titans' running back has rushed for 273 yards and one touchdown this season. But what needs to be added to that equation is that the veteran running back is running behind an abysmal offensive line.
Then there's the financial side to a potential trade. If the Bengals were to make a move for Pollard, the cap hit would be a little over $5 million.
Does it really make sense for the Bengals to take that hit for a talent that is putting up the same numbers as the starting running back they already have?
Sure, more backs may hit the trade rumor mill before the deadline approaches. But at the moment, it feels like the talent that could potentially be traded at the deadline in the backfield is scarce.
This could be a case where the Bengals want to make a move, but the talent that can be added isn't going to be enough to move the needle. The Bengals really need to think hard about any potential move at running back.

title: Joe Burrow Ranked Outside Top-Five NFL Quarterbacks as Bye Week Rolls on
full_text:
Sports Illustrated's Matt Verdarame dropped the site's latest 1-32 NFL quarterback rankings, and Bengals passer Joe Burrow fell outside the top five names in the update.
He started the season ranked fifth overall and is down to sixth on the board with Cincinnati sitting at 3-2 overall entering its bye week.
"When Burrow has been healthy, he’s been an elite quarterback throughout his seven-year NFL career," Verdarame wrote . "In 2026, Burrow has started all five games for the Bengals and looked like a superstar, ranking sixth with 1,361 passing yards while tossing 11 touchdowns against three interceptions.  Analytically, Burrow also ranks fourth in CPOE (6.0) and 13th in EPA per play (0.179) while checking in eighth in success rate (51.2%). With Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on the outside, Cincinnati remains one of the more dangerous offenses in football, led by a quarterback whose only true challenge is remaining on the field for 17 games."
Names like Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, Brock Purdy, Lamar Jackson and Jared Goff got slotted above Burrow in that order from 1-5.
Once you get to the top-eight quarterbacks this season, it's hard to really slice one apart from the other. The QB play at the top has been fantastic. If Burrow had 1-2 turnovers instead of four, he'd likely be in that top five, and Cincinnati could be 4-1 or 5-0.
Alas, he faces the easiest remaining strength of schedule on ESPN's NFL FPI. The veteran passer can light things up the rest of the way and cement himself as a top-five hurler by the end of the season.
"We got to be smarter. We got to be smarter. Two fumbles in the red zone. A couple of personal fouls that hurt us, hurt our field position, gave them points on the board. We got to be smarter," Burrow said about the offensive operation on Sunday before touching on his bye week plans. "We'll see. I don't know. It's so early. I want to maintain my conditioning, my strength and conditioning, and certainly want to keep throwing. I'll try to find a plan. This is uncharted territory for me, having a bye this early, so we'll see."

title: Bengals Could Reshape Backfield With Star SEC Running Back in 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
The bye week is here for Cincinnati, prompting a little looking ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft. Pro Football Focus released a fresh mock draft projecting the first round this week, and Cincinnati added an offensive playmaker in the exercise.
The Bengals rolled with Florida running back Jadan Baugh with the 15th pick in the draft.
"The Bengals have fixed their offensive line and have a passing attack that opposing defenses are forced to respect," Gordon McGuinness wrote . "That's the ideal offensive environment in which to add a dynamic running back, and they would be well justified in using a first-round pick on Baugh. The Florida standout has averaged 3.72 yards after contact per attempt and forced 36 missed tackles this season."
Baugh could be a dynamic way to replace Chae Brown as he works his way through the final season on his Bengals contract.
The Florida bruiser has a nation-leading 12 touchdowns this season and is averaging 6.1 yards per attempt.
McGuinness framed his pick slotting to open the article. Cincinnati is right in the middle of the pack even with a winning record at 3-2. There are 11 teams at either 3-1-1 or 3-2 as of this writing.
"With the 2026 NFL season now past the quarter mark, it’s time to take a far-too-early look at how the NFL draft could shake out if the current draft order holds," McGuinness wrote. "This draft class has generated plenty of excitement over the past two offseasons, and it still looks very strong on paper as we approach the halfway point of the college football season.
"The Tennessee Titans currently hold the No. 1 overall pick, giving them the option to select a new quarterback or add an elite receiving prospect to support their current starter, Cam Ward. One note for this mock draft: Arch Manning does not appear in the first round. Given reports that several scouts don't view him as a first-round pick, I'm taking the approach that he is more likely to return to Texas than enter the draft if that remains the case."
Cincinnati has a long way to go before thinking about picking Baugh, and the team is hoping to be picking way closer to No. 32 than 15th.

title: Erick All Opens Up On Discipline from Zac Taylor During Bengals Recent Win
full_text:
Many eyes turned to Erick All last Sunday after he committed an egregious penalty and fumbled his second catch. Fortunately, the Bengals tight end avoided losing the fumble when the Dolphins recovered it out of bounds. He still, however, received an earful from Zac Taylor on the sideline after his costly penalty where he headbutted a Dolphins defender after the play.
All revealed the experience on First Word , saying it was the first mental error he had made regarding a penalty and that no coach had ever yelled at him as Taylor did on Sunday. He said that he did not intend for the headbutt to be egregious.
"I've never been yelled at by the coach like that besides like missing a block," All revealed. "It was my first stupid penalty like that, I didn't intend for it to be egregious, but it was just one of those little quick walk by things that you didn't think nobody was looking at you and it looked bad and it was stupid."
All then explained that Taylor's discipline after the play is something he respects, given how badly he messed up. He also said that, in that moment, he hoped the coaching staff still trusted him and that, if he got back on the field, they knew he wouldn't make that mistake again.
"Whatever he has to say you just respect it because you just messed up," All said. "You wear it on the chin and hope that they still trust you and can put you out there on the field and know that you won't do anything like that again."
Taylor showed what some may see as another side of himself as a coach, one they hadn't seen before, that being his increased aggressiveness toward players on Sunday.
"I look at Zac as that type of coach that's very transparent, he'll tell you how he feels and it just kind of surprised me hearing 'I'm surprised he hasn't done that with people in the past,'" All said. "Zac's a great coach, if he sees something that he doesn't like or that he wants you to fix, he'll voice it to you whether in practice, game, cameras on, it doesn't matter, and that's what I love about him."
With Tanner Hudson's recent injury, All should see an expanded role in the Bengals' offense. He finished Week 5 with three catches for 25 yards, including a 14-yard catch-and-run that extended a drive in which the offense scored and increased its lead by two scores.
He should continue to ramp up on offense and build more chemistry with Joe Burrow as the season progresses.

title: Bengals' Prized Offseason Acquisitions Already Paying Major Dividends
full_text:
Bye weeks can move rather slowly. However, there's plenty to discuss when it comes to the 2026 edition of the Cincinnati Bengals.
First off, the pass game is looking exactly like everyone had hoped. It's early, but Joe Burrow and Tee Higgins are one of the top quarterback/wide receiver duos in the league. Then, you have the major upgrades to the defensive line.
It's only been five weeks, but Dexter Lawrence has already proven that he is still one of the strongest anchors on a defensive line in the league. One stat from Pro Football Focus even backs that up.
PFF has revealed that the Bengals have the highest defensive stuff rate in the NFL, at 30%. Rounding out the top five is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Miami Dolphins, Seattle Seahawks, and the Green Bay Packers.
The Bengals are getting everything they wanted and more with the addition of Lawrence. PFF has Lawrence graded as the third best defensive tackle in the NFL. That overall grade includes the fourth best grade in pass rush at 82.4 and the 10th-best rush grade at 72.8.
Lawrence has given opposing offenses fits all season long, but it's not just him who is reaping the benefits of being a part of this defensive line.
The Bengals' strong interior defensive line is opening doors for the pass rusher. Boye Mafe, who was another offseason acquisition, is having a strong start to his 2026 campaign.
Mafe has recorded three sacks and one forced fumble in five games. Mafe currently ranks as the 12th-best edge rusher in the league, according to PFF .
With a lot of the talk regarding the defense being about the weakness at linebacker and some struggles in the secondary, so far this season, the defensive line has been elite.
The pass game is rolling, the defensive line is playing some of the best football in the NFL, and even the offensive line has elevated its game. The Bengals are so close to getting it all together.
Having an early bye week can be a rough draw for a lot of teams. However, this season, it may have just come at the right time for the Bengals. This team is potentially on the cusp of finding greatness. Now, they will have a full week to dissect the issues in the running game and some areas on the defensive side before they play in an all important matchup with the Baltimore Ravens.
When the Bengals do take the field against the Ravens in two weeks, you'd best believe their AFC North rivals already have some concerns about the defensive line they will be seeing.
