title: Bengals' Offensive Duo Off to an Explosive Start in 2026
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals didn't get a good draw as it pertains to where the bye week landed on the schedule. A bye in Week 6 is brutal for any team.
With so much season left after the bye week, there's no doubt that health is going to play a major role down the stretch. The win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday was a nice way to enter a bye week, but it still felt like the players and coaches knew they left a lot on the table.
There's no time to sulk in the negative, any win is hard to come by in this league and should be celebrated. It's time to highlight the positives, and the Bengals have a dynamic offensive duo that has been one of the best connections in the young season.
On paper and on the field, the Bengals have one of the most dangerous offenses in the league. Quarterback Joe Burrow is basically playing with two number one options at wide receiver. While Ja'Marr Chase gets most of the attention, and rightfully so, Tee Higgins is having a monster 2026.
According to Pro Football Focus , Burrow to Higgins has the fifth most receiving yards of a quarter/wide receiver duo in the league.
The only duos ahead of the Bengals stars is Matthew Stafford and Devante Adams, Jordan Love and Christian Watson, Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, and the dup everyone expected to be at number one, Tyler Shough and Chris Olave.
Higgins had a quiet outing against the Dolphins this past Sunday, but he had a good reason, given that he was dealing with an adductor injury. But before Week 5, Higgins was having the strongest season of any receiver on the team.
With Chase having a monster game in Miami that led to arguably the greatest touchdown reception of his career, it seems this offense is finding its rhythm right before they play a very vital game against the Baltimore Ravens in two weeks.
The offense has a lot of things going its way. Burrow's connection with Chase and Higgins is as strong as ever, and the offensive line is playing some of the best football they've played under head coach Zac Taylor.
If we're nitpicking, the run game is going to be the focus as the team goes through the bye week. For now, letting Burrow throw nearly 60 times a game doesn't sound so bad.

title: Amarius Mims Among Top Early Contenders For Major 2026 NFL Season Award
full_text:
The Bengals may soon sport the best right tackle in the NFL. ESPN's Bill Barnwell dropped his quarter-season awards article last week and has Amarius Mims third on his Protector of the Year rankings.
The young Georgia product has not allowed a full sack in 2026 and is slotted only behind 49ers offensive tackle Trent Williams and Broncos guard Quinn Meinerz in Barnwell's gauge.
"After taking a major step forward a year ago, the Bengals right tackle has leveled up again and emerged as arguably the best pass-protecting right tackle in the league," Barnwell wrote . "The Bengals have a quarterback in Joe Burrow who wants to get five eligibles out into pass routes, and when they do, help a tackle, it's usually Orlando Brown Jr. Mims has been one-on-one against pass rushers at the third-highest rate in the league this season, and he has excelled in a pass-happy offense, allowing just a half-sack and two quick pressures on 169 pass-rush snaps. He's also 12th in run block win rate, suggesting that the 2024 first-round pick is holding his own as a run blocker, too."
Mims somehow only has a 62.8 Pro Football Focus grade despite all those great marks. There's a huge gap between that RBWR listed by Barnwell and his career-low 45.5 PFF run-blocking grade, but all in all, he's been exactly what fans should expect in Year 3.
At this rate, Mims will reset the offensive tackle on a contract extension sometime next offseason. Cincinnati should try to do it as quickly as possible once the season ends to get ahead of other deals that will happen in the ensuing months.
Bengals coaches have been impressed with 6-8, 350-pound mauler this season.
"There's a lot of really talented people, but there's a fraction of the players in this league that truly can be special, and he is in that fraction," Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher said after facing T.J. Watt and the Steelers. "T.J. Watt is one of the best to ever do that job. To be matched up one-on-one as often as he was without help yesterday (he got some, but not a lot), and to just be consistent and to take the right set.
"There's such confidence for him in knowing, 'If I just take this set on the angle that I need to take it on and my eyes are in the right place and I strike when I'm supposed to strike,' there's very little the guy across from him can do to counter that. He just has to stay on the path he's on."

title: 'Circle On The Schedule' - Elite NFL Cornerback Praises Ja'Marr Chase, Looks Forward to Each Matchup
full_text:
Since joining the Cincinnati Bengals in 2021, Ja’Marr Chase has cemented himself as one of the league’s most dominant wideouts.
This season already, Chase has notched 27 receptions for 289 yards and 4 touchdowns, for 10.7 yards per catch and 57.8 yards per game. Continuing his rising legacy, that has already seen the former LSU Tiger tally five Pro Bowl appearances in his first six seasons.
Earlier this month, when talking on the PFF NFL Show , Browns star Denzel Ward spoke on the difficulties of playing Chase.
When asked who the toughest receiver he faced, Ward responded, “I would say definitely in the division, I'd say Ja'Marr Chase.”
“…I feel I've definitely done well against him, but I just know the type of matchup and type of game it’s gonna be going against him and Burrow. I think their connection makes it even tougher to go against. But, he's one of the guys, I think, that I definitely circle on the schedule, like, ‘okay, this is gonna be one of the harder games I play,’ and it's gonna be a great matchup."
Ward then elaborated on what makes Chase a difficult player.
“He's able to make plays after the catch. So he's able to catch a ball and go all the way to the end zone. So it's like, you gotta tackle him right there once he catches it 'cause if not he's someone that could take it all away, and score on one play. Burrow's gonna give him chances, but he's just a physical route runner, and then it's really, I think, the hardest part is once he gets that ball in his hands.”
Last summer, when appearing on The Sitdown w/ Malik Wright , Chase was asked his toughest opponent, where he was quick to answer Ward.
“It’s easy. I mean, Denzel,” Chase said. “It’s twice a year. It’s one on one majority of the time. He got great feet. He knows leverage, he knows splits. He’s one of the best I like playing.”
In his career against the Browns, Chase has totaled 42 catches for 481 yards and 4 touchdowns, with his best game against the AFC North rival coming in early 2022, where he went for 119 yards through 10 receptions and 1 touchdown.

title: Latest 2026 NFL Draft Class Ranking Leaves a Lot to Be Desired for Bengals
full_text:
The start of the 2026 season has not gone the way the Cincinnati Bengals had hoped. After a 2-0 start, the Bengals dropped two straight games before their meeting with the Miami Dolphins in Week 5.
Week 5 became a must-win situation, and the Bengals did just that. It wasn't the prettiest performance, but the Bengals secured a winning record before their bye, taking down the Dolphins 31-24.
A bye week is usually a time for reflection. It's a shame the Bengals' bye comes so early in the season, but it's never the wrong time to take a closer look at how the team arrived at a 3-2 record. Speaking of reflection, NFL Draft On SI recently ranked the performance of each team's 2026 NFL Draft class. The rankings show the Bengals' 2026 class has a lot to prove.
Justin Melo of NFL Draft On SI has put the Bengals' 2026 draft class as the 20th best class after five weeks in the season. Melo gives the class a C+ while acknowledging the group as a whole hasn't had a lot of opportunities.
"Cashius Howell has been among the top-performing rookie pass rushers. No other members of this seven-prospect class are really playing meaningful snaps yet, but it remains early, and Howell looks like a real find," wrote Melo .
According to Pro Football Focus , Howell had one of his stronger games in his young rookie season. The rookie defensive end earned his highest run grade of the season at 67.8.
Howell looks to be on the trajectory of being an impact player for the Bengals. But will there be another player who takes the leap this season?
Coming into this game, there was a real chance the Bengals could have been without Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Both were active and made an impact on the game, which means rookie wide receiver Colbie Young may have to wait for his moment.
Young turned some heads during training camp, and it feels like sooner rather than later, fans will get to know his name well.
One of the biggest reasons the Bengals' rookie class hasn't made a bigger impact is that those ahead of them on the depth chart are simply the better talents at the moment. That's a good problem for any team to have.

title: Bengals' Offense Has Finally Found Strength in One Major Weakness
full_text:
The worst week of the NFL season is the bye week. That's where the Cincinnati Bengals find themselves in Week 6.
After a sloppy 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, the Bengals will have a week to recover and prepare for a major matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.
Everyone can agree this team has a lot to work on if they want to avoid a 0-2 start in the AFC North. But there are a lot of positives to take away from the first five weeks of the season. One of the biggest positives has actually been the play of the offensive line.
Since Joe Burrow took his first steps on the field as a member of the Bengals, the team has struggled to protect their star quarterback.
Every season, the conversation turns to how the Bengals cannot protect Burrow, and every fan feels that is one of the biggest hurdles holding back this team. Well, that hasn't been the case in 2026.
According to Pro Football Focus , the Bengals have a pressure allowed rate of 20.6%, which is fourth best in the league. Only the Atlanta Falcons, Kansas City Chiefs, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers have posted a better percentage.
Protecting Burrow is the most important goal for this team every time they step on the field. The Bengals' offensive line has allowed just nine sacks this season. That ties them with the Indianapolis Colts for seventh-best in sacks allowed.
After Sunday's game in Miami, it's clear that the offense is clicking. The Bengals were dominant in the red zone, and Burrow connected with four different targets on touchdown passes in the win. If everyone stays healthy, this offense could reach heights that would even surprise the likes of Burrow and his explosive collection of offensive talent.
However, the defense is another story. For now, just celebrate the wins, and this offensive line is giving the fans something to be proud of. After years of discussion around protecting Burrow, the offensive line is in position to keep the franchise signal-caller upright.
Burrow has thrown for 1,361 yards, 11 touchdowns and three interceptions in five games. He has a 71.4% completion percentage, 104.4 QB rating and a 75.3 QBR. He also received a major compliment for his recent play from national NFL analyst Mark Schlereth.

title: Browns Rookie Receives Highest PFF Grade among 2026 Draft Class
full_text:
After five weeks of the 2026 NFL season, PFF put out their rookie rankings by overall grade.
While many believe Cleveland won the 2026 NFL Draft , the rookie who ranks atop all the others may not be the one you're thinking of from the Brown and Orange.
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is looking special pic.twitter.com/zcF1Nj0Bsb
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has the highest PFF grade of any rookie this season through the first few games.
Somehow, the prospect fell all the way to pick 58 overall in April.
McNeil-Warren currently has a PFF grade of 89.9.
This number not only ranks him as the best of all rookies, but also the best of all 96 NFL safeties.
As for the stat line, EMW has 22 total tackles with only 4 targets allowed over 109 total snaps. Additionally, his average passer rating allowed per game is only 27.6.
But it's not necessarily the numbers that are the reason why the rookie is so great.
If you showed a regular fan highlights of the Browns defense, they could never tell McNeil-Warren is only five games in to his pro career.
The reason? His instincts.
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is ready for primetime Watch how he closes QUICK on both of these balls intended for DK Metcalf to make two high quality pass breakups 👀 pic.twitter.com/brnADB0XoX
Just watching the young stud is incredible. He is already out there jumping passes, making reads, and ultimately playing like a seasoned veteran. The Browns truly have found a playmaker for their secondary
At this point, he is just having to split snaps with Ronnie Hickman. Ultimately, the Browns may decide at some point in the future to move on from Hickman as well, which would free up more snaps for EMW.
Something else we can't just overlook is the other rookie on this PFF top-graded list, who you may have thought sat at the top. Denzel Boston has simply been a beast for the Browns this season.
In five games, the second-round pick out of Washington has 16 catches, with three of those being touchdowns.
Not only does he lead all rookies in receiver yards with 330, but here are some elite NFL names who Boston has out gained:
Clearly, the Cleveland Browns knew what they were doing in the 2026 NFL Draft, especially in the second round.
Outside of Emmanuel McNeil-Warren and Denzel Boston, the Browns have had great success from KC Concepcion, Austin Barber, and Spencer Fano.

title: How Audric Estime Could Work His Way Into Legitimate Playing Time With Browns
full_text:
The running back room has been depleted with injuries and ineffectiveness . Backup Dylan Sampson landed on the injured reserve list during the first game of the season and his replacement Reheim Sanders joined him this week. The Browns signed Jaleel McLaughlin to replace Sampson. The next man up for Sanders is now Audric Estime.
Estime comes from the Minnesota Vikings practice squad and he will look to contribute to the Browns’ offense right away. Quinshon Judkins has struggled so far this season and the running attack has stalled as a whole. The running game could use a new look after five games to allow the offense to thrive.
The 5’11 227 pound back runs hard and never stops moving his legs. Estime has been in the NFL for two seasons and has amassed over 500 yards with a 4.2 average per carry. That average is greater than Judkins’ average per carry by over a whole yard. McLaughlin only has two carries all season and the Browns will have to give carries to all the backs to try and find any improvement.
When he played for the New Orleans Saints in 2025, he had rushing attempts out of the shotgun formation. The Browns’ offense mainly plays out of that formation, which has led to them struggling to run the ball. The running back needs terrific vision as he does not start with momentum before getting the ball and has to find cracks in the line. For the Saints, Estime showed that he has the patience to find an opening and a large frame that does not allow him to get tackled by the first defender.
Deshaun Watson got sacked eight times last week with pressure coming from everywhere. The running backs did not do a good job of stepping up to chip or block defenders. Estime has taken interior defensive linemen one on one to help protect the quarterback. The offense was exposed last week with all the blitzing and Estime can gain serious playing time if he can help buy Watson additional seconds to throw the ball.
Estime’s ability out of the shotgun formation will help him earn legitimate playing time for the Browns this season. Todd Monken insists that Watson and the offense operates best out of shotgun and Estime will bring experience and production to the position group.
He will be in on obvious passing downs to block an extra defender and with the injuries to the other running backs, he should get carries as well. While he will not be an every-down back, he can use his abilities to get legitimate playing time for an offense that needs any type of positive change running the football.

title: Is Shedeur Sanders’ Time in Cleveland in Jeopardy?
full_text:
So far in the 2026 season, Deshaun Watson has surprised pretty much everyone.
After being named the starter right before the season, many thought Watson would only last two games before being removed for Shedeur Sanders .
However, Watson continues to be the guy for the Browns. So far this season, Watson has led the Browns on three game-winning drives in just five games.
While the Browns organization has expressed that they do not want to move on from the second year quarterback, there may be a new development from Sanders' side of things.
Last week, Sanders signed with a new agent for representation.
While it may be a bit of a stretch, former Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. did the same thing and was traded just a week later.
Marvin Harrison Jr signed with an agent & was traded the same wk.. Shedeur Sanders now has an agent.. https://t.co/A2JGviWe6V
While there is still an unlikely chance the Browns deal Shedeur Sanders, getting an agent may sway his mind.
At the moment, Sanders has been content being the Browns backup. According to the media, he is taking the time to watch and learn from Deshaun Watson.
However, if the new agent comes in and pursuades him to push for a trade due to a starting job potentially somewhere else, you never know what may happen.
Regardless, Sanders has a ton of young and raw talent. It is most likely better for him to get this time to watch and develop, knowing he may take over the starting job for Cleveland soon.
Cleveland simply can't afford to lose Sanders.
The Browns finally have a somewhat stable quarterback room. For the past few seasons, its been the story of the starter going down or playing bad, and having to be replaced multiple times per season.
Now, with Deshaun Watson winning games and the young Shedeur Sanders developing on the bench, the Browns are actually looking alright for the future.
There have been many talks about when Sanders could see the field. It may be this season, it may not even be next year.
But let's look at the facts. If the Browns go on a slide and start losing games, let's say they fall out of playoff contention.
The moment that happens they should put Shedeur in to at least let him get in game starting reps when you know when your season will end.
Now let's say Deshaun Watson takes the Browns to the playoffs, and even gets resigned next year.
No matter how much they pay him and for how long, Deshaun Watson is still currently 31 years old and will be 32 by this time next year.
Clearly, the Browns will need another option in the near future. If Sanders can be patient and take more time to develop and learn, he can be ready to go the second the Browns call on number two.

title: Browns Receiver Criticized by Former Star After Disappointing Jets Defeat
full_text:
After the Cleveland Browns lost their week five matchup against the New York Jets, former Browns receiver Jarvis Landry had comments for Isaiah Bond .
In the game, Bond had to step in for the injured KC Concepcion.
By the end, Bond had been targeted seven times. Out of those targets, he had three catches for 74 yards.
However, the second-year man also had numerous plays where he had bad drops, including one that was late in the close game.
Jarvis Landry calls out Isaiah Bond for his costly dropped pass against the Jets, insisting the Browns receiver needs to adjust after the mistake and live up to Cleveland’s high standards for its wideouts. "Isaiah Bond, my dog, if you can't catch that s**t without gloves, you… pic.twitter.com/wZXYKe9Fem
Not only did Landry rip the young receiver for his mistakes, but he also continued to talk about how Bond wasn't "living up to Cleveland's high standards for its wideouts".
In the contest at MetLife Stadium, it did not stop raining throughout the entire contest.
With that being said, Bond was playing the game without gloves on. This was something Landry also made note on, even inserting himself in the situation.
"I'm catching that s**t. Period. Ain't no ifs, ands, or buts. If I drop one without gloves, best believe the next time I come on the field, I got gloves on or I got tape on my fingers or something." Landry said.
Coming into this offseason, Isaiah Bond was someone who flew under the radar for the Browns.
We knew he was going to have to come in and compete for a job on the team, especially after Cleveland drafted two receivers in the 2026 NFL Draft .
A lot of speculation the #Browns should trade Jerry Jeudy Im on board with anything that gets Isaiah Bond more targets Two weeks in: 1 target 1 catch- he’s way too talented to not get the ball pic.twitter.com/N0lwLzfKah
Throughout training camp, the former Texas Longhorn stood out. Day after day it seemed as if Isaiah Bond was the big name who was contantly making big plays and scoring touchdowns.
It almost seemed as if the Browns found another stud who was going to have a breakout season.
But then came game days. At the start of the season, Bond was barely being used. Through the first four games, he only had two catches on his only two targets for a total of 12 yards.
So how can the Browns use him more?
KC Concepcion's health is the main question at the moment for Bond's playing time. However, even when the rookie comes back, I think Bond deserves to get more reps over a guy like Jerry Jeudy.
Bond has showcased in both games and the offseason his breakaway speed. If the Browns utilize him as a deep threat, that will open up the field for KC Concepcion who had been getting great separation off the line of scirmmage.
Tough day for Isaiah Bond. I truly believe he’s better than what he put on tape, but man… Can’t help thinking about what could’ve been. Head up, 007. Still a long season ahead. #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/3iQtpwRgsg
Overall, if Bond wants to redeem himself, he will just have to do it on the field. Going forward, he needs to be able to catch wide open passes. If he can't, adjustments need to be made.
Who knows, maybe Jarvis Landry himself will help out the young pup with some pass catching drills.

title: Browns Should Consider Flipping Jerry Jeudy For This Overshadowed Wideout
full_text:
The current situation of the Cleveland Browns ' wide receiver room is headlined by the excellent play of both rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, who have combined for 34 catches for 449 yards and three touchdowns through the first five games of the season. Cleveland’s next leading receiver is second-year guy Isaiah Bond with 86 receiving yards. Bond struggled with a couple of drops vs. New York, but has gotten just nine targets this season.
Past those three, the rest of the room seems to be up in the air, and the one guy who is the odd man out is popping up in more and more trade rumors. That would, of course, be Jerry Jeudy, who is currently sixth for Cleveland in receiving yards and receptions.
Jeudy’s cap hit of $10.3 million this season, as well as $13.4 million in 2027, does not seem worth the price at the moment or in the future. Cleveland will be looking to trade him ; that’s no secret, but could it be for another receiver who has also seemingly lost his place in the room?
That would be the Jags wideout Brian Thomas Jr.
Thomas is now in his third season with Jacksonville, and after an unbelievable rookie season that showed him producing 87 receptions for over 1,200 yards and 10 touchdowns, his play has slowed down. The Jaguars hired Liam Coen last season, and since then, it doesn’t seem like Thomas has been a focal point of the offense.
An ankle injury also caused Thomas to miss three games last year, but through five games this season, the Jags offense has pivoted towards Parker Washington, Brenton Strange, Jakobi Meyers, and even sixth-round pick Josh Cameron over Thomas.
Now, a trade involving Jeudy for Thomas would have to come with some sweetening on the end of Cleveland, as Thomas is three years younger than Jeudy, and Thomas is making just $4 million on the cap this year, and just $4.6 million next season.
The Browns would most likely have to give up at least a fourth- and fifth-rounder alone, but if the Jags don’t see much value in Jeudy, Cleveland would have to ramp it up to a third, possibly.
Cleveland and Jacksonville have a recent history of trading with each other, as we know from the Travis Hunter & Mason Graham trade, along with the trade that brought Tyson Campbell to Cleveland in exchange for Greg Newsome.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: Why Denzel Boston’s Case For ROTY is Rock-Solid Through Five Weeks
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have two rookies of the year on the defensive side of the ball and now may have found one on the offense. Second-round pick Denzel Boston has broken tackles, ran past, and out jumped defensive backs on his way to leading all rookies in receiving yards. Through five weeks of the season, Boston finds himself the front runner for Offensive Rookie of the Year.
The 6’4 receiver has 330 yards and three touchdowns through five games. During key moments of drives Deshaun Watson looks for the big-framed target for crucial first downs. Boston has taken the top off of the secondary and has multiple touchdowns over 30 yards and is averaging over 20 yards per reception.
The Browns have a surprising 3-2 start, which is due to Boston’s play-making ability. In Tampa Bay he caught a post pass and broke multiple tackles, rumbling his way to a touchdown, bringing life to the offense. In the win against the Carolina Panthers, he used his strong hands and great route running to secure a crucial two-point conversion. He caught a would-be game-winning deep pass against the New York Jets, until the special teams and defense made it null .
No other rookie has meant more to his offense than Boston. He was the 39th pick in the 2026 draft, but he has looked like he should have been drafted much higher. Ohio State’s Carnell Tate was drafted fourth overall to the Tennessee Titans and he is behind Boston in rookie receiving yards with 274 and zero touchdowns. Tate has not helped a maligned Titans’ offense as they are 0-5.
Boston’s teammate and 24th overall pick, KC Concepcion is fourth in rookie receiving yards with 149. The Arizona Cardinal’s third-overall pick at running back, Jeremiah Love, leads rookies in rushing with 245 yards. However, that is only good for 23rd overall in the league and the Cardinals are 1-4.
Jalon Daniels has been the best rookie quarterback so far this season for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers; however, he will get benched when Baker Mayfield returns from injury. First-overall pick Fernando Mendoza has not made a start this season as the Las Vegas Raiders have been relevant under Kirk Cousins.
Boston is averaging 66 yards per game, which, played out in a full season, would be over 1,000 with 10 touchdowns. While those expectations may be too high, it is very realistic. Concepcion was injured in last week’s game and rumors are swirling that Jerry Jeudy will be moved at the trade deadline. Boston will get many opportunities to make plays for the offense as the running attack has been one of the league's worst.
Watson is gaining chemistry with him every week and his production will be greater as the season progresses. Todd Monken coached the similarly framed Mike Evans during his best statistical season, so he knows how to use the big target. Boston is just getting started in the NFL and by the end of the season he will be considered a legitimate threat, and not just for a rookie.
The race for Offensive Rookie of the Year may be over before the halfway point. Nobody is close to Boston’s importance on their offense and the stats back that up. The future looks bright in Cleveland as they will have three rookie of the year winners on their roster.

title: How the Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade Benefits the Cleveland Browns
full_text:
Marvin Harrison Jr. was just traded from the Arizona Cardinals to the Houston Texans.
Obviously, the deal does not directly involve the Browns, but it actually does impact the team more than it may seem.
With Cleveland shopping Jerry Jeudy , his value just increased if teams are looking at the numbers.
This season, both receivers have been in similar situations on their respective teams. Each guy was slated to be the team's number one receiver, yet did not see much action to begin the season.
For Harrison, he only had 13 targets through the first four games. Out of those targets, he had five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown.
For Jeudy, he has only been targeted 15 times. His stat line currently sits at eight catches for 81 yards and zero touchdowns.
While the stats are close, there are some other key factors to argue against the Browns getting a similar trade package.
Marvin Harrison Jr. was drafted number four overall just two years ago. We cannot forget that he was one of the best college prospects we've seen in a long time out of Ohio State.
Mike LaFleur on Marvin Harrison Jr.’s effort: "I think his running style is different than some other people's." ( @BoBrack ) pic.twitter.com/k8m26OtpKm
With that being said, there is still much to be seen from Harrison. At only 24 years old, he has a long NFL career ahead of him.
As for Jerry Jeudy, teams already know what they are going to get. A diva receiver who can step up given the right situation. Otherwise, he won't fit in and will constantly drop passes.
At 27 years old, there is still some time for Jeudy, but obviously not nearly as much as Harrison.
With the recent injury to KC Concepcion, Cleveland may wait longer to trade Jeudy.
In the case they still decide to move him, what could they get in return?
TRADE: Cardinals trading WR Marvin Harrison Jr. and a 2027 7th-round pick to the Texans in exchange for a 2027 2nd-round pick and 2027 6th-round pick. (via @rapsheet , @adamschefter ) pic.twitter.com/abCg6guHE0
For Harrison, the Cardinals got back a 2027 second and sixth. While the Browns are unlikely to get the exact same package for Jeudy with Harrison being the better player, they can still get close.
If the Browns just want draft capitol in return for their receiver, they will most likely be able to get a mid round pick and late round pick. Some say they could manage to get a third, but I think that depends on which team they trade with.
Another option could be a player swap. The Browns have some gaps in the running back, offensive line, and secondary rooms, and could look to use Jeudy as a way to level out their team.

title: Browns Injury Report Highlights Concerning Trend Following Team Ahead of Week 6
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are headed into Week 6 with a 3-2 overall record on the young 2026 regular season.
Losing in Week 5 to the New York Jets on the road, the Browns have some work to do to bounce back in a Week 6 meeting with the Baltimore Ravens at home. However, being at full strength may be an issue.
On Wednesday, Oct. 14, news broke that the Browns were expected to be without multiple players for practice due to injury.
Of the bunch, defensive tackles Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr. stand out as big misses, with running back Quinshon Judkins and linebacker Carson Schewsinger also pulling eyeballs.
Both Graham and Hall Jr. missed Sunday's game against the Jets, but both second-years, Judkins and Schewsinger, are new additions. They left MetLife Stadium in boots.
Wednesday Pre-practice injury report - expected DNPs due to injury: Barnett (ankle), Collins (foot), Graham (knee, ankle), Hall (ankle), Howard (knee), T. Jenkins (back), Judkins (ankle), Ryan (calf), Schwesinger (ankle). RB Dylan Sampson has been designated for return and is…
Schwesinger, Judkins, Hall Jr. and Graham will all be the talking points for the injury report, especially because of how important each have been to their respective side of the ball.
But it is impossible to ignore that other relied-upon role players that may not practice much this week.
Defensive end Derek Barnett is working through an ankle injury, while defensive tackle Maliek Collins also likely sits out because of a foot injury. On the offensive end, Tytus Howard is fighting to get healthy following a knee injury he suffered in Sunday's loss to the Jets, while Teven Jenkins remains out with a back injury that has kept him sidelined all season.

He was seen walking around the practice field as his practice window finally opened, following a knee injury that landed him on the injured list after a Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. He wasn't doing much, as showcased by a video from ESPN's Danile Oyefusi.

The Browns not only need to get a bit more productivity from the running back room after the first five weeks of the season, but with Judkins and Rahiem Sanders out , the depth is running thin at the position.
Hopefully, Sampson can begin to ramp back up his workload and make a return to the offense.

title: Recent Report Shares Controversial Value For Browns WR Jerry Jeudy
full_text:
The Browns are in an interesting position with veteran wide receiver Jerry Jeudy ; Jeudy is now in his third year with the team, and many are sure his future is somewhere else. In his first year with the Browns, Jeudy posted career-highs in receptions, targets, and yards as he hauled in 90 passes for over 1,200 yards. 235 of those yards came in a single game where Jeudy really took it to his former team in Denver, as it set a record for the most receiving yards in NFL history for a wide receiver vs. his former team.
Last season really tested Jeudy and many of the Browns' players, as the three different starting quarterbacks for Cleveland never seemed to get good chemistry with Jeudy. In his second season, the wide receiver took a huge step back, posting just 50 receptions on 106 targets for 602 yards. Along with not developing chemistry, drops were a huge problem for Jeudy last season.
Cleveland drafting two receivers (KC Concepcion & Denzel Boston) in the top 40 of this year’s draft was a clear signal that they could be moving on from Jeudy in the near future. Through the first five games this season, Concepcion and Boston have both been targeted 29 times to Jeudy’s 15, for comparison, through the first five games last season, Jeudy was targeted 35 times.
But the question is, what’s the value of a player like Jeudy? According to NFL insider Jordan Schutlz Cleveland would like a 3rd or 4th rounder in compensation for Jeudy. The initial reaction to this was controversial, as many think that there is no way a team would be willing to give up that capital for Jeudy.
In the recent market for receiver trades though, a guy like Marvin Harrison Jr. just went for a 2027 2nd rounder and 2027 6th rounder, with a 2027 7th rounder going with Harrison to the Texans. The main bet on this trade for Houston is upside, Harrison is just 24 years old in his third NFL season, and when he was coming out of Ohio State, he was hyped to be one of the next great receiver talents, hence why he was taken fourth overall in the 2024 Draft.
Harrison and Jeudy’s first two years in the league are relatively comparable as Harrison tallied 103 receptions for 1,493 yards and 12 touchdowns, Jeudy caught 90 passes for 1,323 yards, but just 3 touchdowns on 20 less targets.
Looking at other recent receiver trades , players like DJ Moore also commanded a 2nd round pick, while guys like AJ Brown and Jaylen Waddle commanded more compensation that involved a first round pick.
Realistically, though, Jeudy compares to players like Dontayvon Wicks, who was moved to Philadelphia for a fifth and sixth-rounder, or Jakobi Meyers, who was traded from Vegas to Jacksonville for a fourth and sixth-rounder in 2025. That may be the top of what Cleveland could get for Jeudy, and if not, the Browns may have to settle for a late rounder if they want to move on from him.

title: Browns Aren’t in the Clear Yet As Lamar Jackson Injury Concerns Make a Turn

title: Christian Parker Shuts Down Cowboys Insider's Antagonizing Mike Pettine Question
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys entered the 2026-27 NFL campaign with high hopes after a complete offseason overhaul of the team's putrid defense under Matt Eberflus in 2025 .
Dallas kickstarted the change by hiring a bright, young defensive mind in Christian Parker to lead the rebuild, but it has gotten off to a slow start. With several new starters, a new scheme, and a flurry of injuries, the Cowboys have sputtered through the first five weeks of the season.
The Cowboys are ranked No. 31 in total defense, No. 21 in pass defense, and No. 32 against the run entering a Week 5 showdown with the Green Bay Packers. In an effort to spark an immediate improvement, the Cowboys went out and hired former Packers defensive coordinator Mike Pettine to serve as a senior defensive assistant under Parker.
Since the hiring, there has been some discourse in Cowboys Nation sparked by veteran beat writer Clarence Hill Jr ., who said Parker was "set up for failure" by the front office after hyping the hire throughout the offseason. Throughout the offseason, the moves were praised by Hill and other Cowboys personalities, but suddenly, the tune has changed because of the slow start.
That same energy carried over into a press conference this week, which led to Parker shutting down a question from Hill that seemed set up to put Parker in a no-win scenario.
Parker was asked whether adding Pettine was a "save the day" hire, which he immediately shut down.
Asked about the idea that Mike Pettine is a "save the day" hire, Cowboys DC Christian Parker somewhat bowed up: "I don't need to respond to that." pic.twitter.com/Bi5vb8S14E
"I don't need to respond to that," Parker responded. Nor should he.
While the question appears to be set up to generate further discourse and drama around the discussion about the defensive struggles, Parker isn't biting. And when you read reports from other Cowboys media members who are dialed in, you understand why.
Pettine's connection to Dallas is nothing new. He wasn't brought in to "save the day." In fact, the team has been trying to bring him onboard for months.
Patrik Walker of the team's official website has been very clear that the team reached out to Pettine in the spring . Instead of immediately accepting a gig, Pettine wanted to enjoy some time off. Parker has since confirmed this , and head coach Brian Schottenheimer added, "Christian Parker is our defensive coordinator, and everything — all decisions will run through him. We're supporting him."
Hopefully, everyone can move on from the nonsensical discourse about whether Parker was set up to fail and whether the team is looking for an escape from the Parker hire.
He is the defensive coordinator, he has a previous relationship with Pettine from their time with the Packers, and he wanted to bring in a mind he trusts to bounce ideas off of. There's no reason to drum up any unneccessary drama, so let's move on, get that popcorn ready, and prepare for Sunday night's game.

title: Von Miller Takes Accountability For Disappointing Start With Dallas Cowboys
full_text:
Through five games of the 2026 season, Von Miller has not made the impact the Dallas Cowboys were hoping he would when they signed him during the offseason.
Miller has been a great teammate as he promised , but Dallas also needs him to make an impact in the pass-rush. Unfortunately, the Cowboys are still waiting for that impact, as Miller has yet to get a sack and only has six pressures, per Pro Football Focus .
Miller addressed his slow start during the latest episode of his "Free Range w/ Von Miller" podcast and made no excuses for failing to record a sack.
"It's time for me to get rolling, too," Miller said. "I would like to point the finger at myself. If I get two plays, I need to find a way to make an impact on those two plays. If I get 10 (plays), I definitely should be able to have an impact on 10 plays.
"And don't let me get 15 and 20 plays. I have to be able to do something. And this Sunday, I'm just pointing the finger at myself. I have to make an impact with the type of burn that I'm able to get."
Playing at Lambeau Field against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday might be a good omen for Miller, who tallied his first Washington Commanders sack there last season.
Miller's lack of an impact has become even more glaring when you consider just how poorly Dallas' pass-rush has performed overall.
When the Cowboys do actually get pressure, the defense has not been able to finish them off. PFF has Dallas with 76 pressures this season, yet the Cowboys have just five sacks, which ranks as the third-fewest in the NFL.
If this defense is ever going to improve, that needs to change. The Cowboys just cannot afford to miss opportunities to sack the quarterback, especially with how bad the coverage has been.
Miller has only played a total of 72 snaps this season, which amounts to 22% of the plays on defense.
After playing 15.9% of the snaps in Week 1, Miller saw an uptick to 29.6% in Week 2, and then he was on the field for 25% and 25.5% the next two games before seeing a season-low 13.9% of snaps during the loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Now, the Cowboys are looking to make changes to the defense and get rookie Malachi Lawrence more run after he notched his first career sack in Week 5.
"He's played very well," head coach Brian Schottenheimer said of Lawrence earlier this week. "I think he's starting to show the flash and the acceleration and the ability to rush the passer that we knew we were getting when we drafted him."
"I think he had a very good game against Tampa Bay, and you'll see him get more opportunities," Schottenheimer added.
One has to wonder if Lawrence's increased run will come at the expense of Miller.
We'll know more on Sunday, when the Cowboys meet the Packers at Lambeau Field.

title: Christian Parker Rejects Negative Perception of Cowboys' Players-Only Meeting
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are at somewhat of a crossroads headed into Week 6's primetime matchup with the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.
In danger of falling to 2-4, the Cowboys have a chance to turn their season around with a win against a Packers team that has not lost to Dallas in six straight meetings, including the playoffs. The two teams finished with a thrilling 40-40 tie last season in Arlington.
But before preparation began for Green Bay, the Dallas defense held a players-only meeting. Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker's unit is one of the worst in the NFL through five weeks, and it's clear the one's coming up short on the field are drawing a line in the sand before it's too late.
Parker spoke with reporters on Thursday about the players-only meeting and shared some honest thoughts about the whole ordeal.
Despite the fact that the lack of defensive production within Parker's scheme is one of the main reasons a meeting happened in the first place, he thinks that the players' decision to come together is productive.
"I think it depends on when they happen and how they happen," Parker said, per ESPN's Todd Archer. "I think that guys have been talking about being able to talk collectively anyways. I think often the long weekend is kind of the perfect timing for them to kind of discuss some things internally, getting on the same page about some things in terms of operation and spending more time together, that kind of thing. So I think it's productive."
Cowboys defensive tackle Quinnen Williams said he was one of the players who called for the meeting.
“I take full personally responsibility for it," Williams said, per Nick Harris of the Fort Worth-Star Telegram. "I look in the mirror at myself and know that I need to do better, play better. I take full accountability and I’m fully responsible for where this defense is going at the moment. I took a break this weekend and reset to learn and grow and focus on getting better.”
Hopefully Parker and the coaching staff -- which recently added former Cleveland Browns head coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant -- have had some heart-to-heart meetings of their own.
As much as the players have come up short, equal blame goes to Parker, Brian Schottenheimer and the entire staff.
Fans will see if the meeting pays off or if it was just another hopeless attempt at saving the season when the Cowboys kick things off against the Packers on Sunday Night Football at 7:20 p.m. CT.

title: Dallas Cowboys Could Bench DaRon Bland to Avoid Paying Massive Injury Guarantees
full_text:
From being a fifth-round pick to making NFL history, Dallas Cowboys cornerback DaRon Bland deserves a ton of credit for the career he's made for himself.
However, the magic from his record-setting 2023 season has quickly faded. Despite signing a four-year, $90 million contract extension last August, Bland has become a liability this season on a Dallas defense that already has enough problems to deal with.
Bland hasn't had an interception since Week 7 of last season. And if he's not jumping routes and running it back for a touchdown -- something he's done six times in his career -- Bland is getting burned down the field for huge gains.
As a result of his fading production and hefty contract, the Cowboys face an interesting dilemma when it comes to how they handle Bland's involvement in the defense moving forward in order to help themselves both on the field and in the bank.
As pointed out by ESPN's Bill Barnwell, the Cowboys would be in a frustrating financial hole if Bland were to suffer an injury this season.
Dallas would owe Bland $13 million in guaranteed money if he suffers "a significant injury." Should he stay healthy, the Cowboys would avoid having to pay up.
"The Cowboys don't want to be on the hook for that money, so it would hardly be a surprise if they took Bland out of the lineup altogether once (Cobie) Durant and (Joey) Porter Jr. are back on the field to avoid triggering those guarantees, which would happen if Bland suffers a significant injury," Barnwell wrote.
This situation makes it perfectly reasonable for the Cowboys to bench Bland moving forward. Until he proves he can produce at the level that his contract demands, Dallas faces a lose-lose situation: continue to suffer on defense while simultaneously running the risk of owing Bland millions in injury guarantees.
If the Cowboys are going to be awful on defense, they might as well do it with cornerbacks that won't put them in a tough spot financially.
When everyone is healthy, Dallas has multiple options that certainly feel like an upgrade from the current version of Bland. The Cowboys signed former Los Angeles Rams cornerback Cobie Durant this season before making the blockbuster deal for former Pittsburgh Steelers star Joey Porter Jr. earlier this month.
The Cowboys are also still figuring out exactly what they have in Shavon Revel Jr., who impressed during training camp but has had his own share of struggles this season.
And on top of that, Dallas has versatile defensive back Caleb Downs, who brings a bit of everything as a slot corner or a safety.
It's hard to imagine Bland being outright ruled inactive for Week 6's matchup against the Green Bay Packers but the Cowboys could certainly benefit by slowing decreasing his snap count as the season goes on.

title: New Cowboys 2027 NFL Mock Draft Lands Impact CB to Replace DaRon Bland
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys spent the entire offseason trying to fix their defense and through five games, it's clear they still have a lot of work to do.
A lot of finger pointing has taken place with first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker taking the brunt of the blame . There's a hope that the recent hiring of senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine will help Parker improve, but the fact remains that Dallas has several players who have massively underperformed expectations.
One prime example of this is DaRon Bland , who was one considered among the top cornerbacks in the NFL. In 2023, Bland recorded nine interceptions, returning five for touchdowns. Since then, foot injuries have slowed him down and he's now been one of the league's lowest-rated cornerbacks on a weekly basis.
That's why Bleacher Report's Brent Sobleski has Dallas replacing the veteran cornerback with their first pick in his latest 2027 NFL mock draft.
Sobleski called Bland a "feast-or-famine" cornerback , adding that the Cowboys can save $13 million by cutting him in the offseason. Should they decide to make that move, he sees Brown as a suitable replacement to play opposite Joey Porter Jr., assuming he gets re-signed.
"Brown comes to play when the lights get bright and his instincts can take over. He has ideal size and length working on the perimeter and won't back down to any assignment. At this stage in his career, he's better in zone coverage than man but has the length and athleticism to develop further. While Brown didn't have his best showing against the Georgia Bulldogs, expect him to bounce back as an impact defender," Sobleski wrote.
Listed at 6-foot-0 and 196 pounds, Brown had a strong sophomore campaign in 2025 for Alabama. That season, he recorded 39 tackles with six pass defenses and two interceptions. Both of his picks were returned for touchdowns as well.
While adding a cornerback would be a huge help for this porous pass defense, Dallas also desperately needs help in the front seven.
Right now, they have just five sacks on the season and not a single player has more than one. Their inability to get the opposing quarterback down is a major part of their problems in coverage. If they can find someone to consistently pressure the quarterback, it would go a long way toward helping their cornerbacks who are currently being asked to stay in coverage for far too long.

title: Cowboys Named Possible Landing Spot for Shedeur Sanders Amid Recent Trade Buzz
full_text:
There is a growing sense Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders might be working his way up to a trade out of Cleveland and one analyst believes the Dallas Cowboys could be a landing spot .
The buzz surrounding a possible Sanders trade started to gain some steam on Wednesday, when ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sanders was hiring an agent.
"Browns QB Shedeur Sanders, who went through draft night and the early part of his NFL career without an agent, has signed with Adie von Gontard, CEO of Young Money APAA Sports, for representation," Schefter reported.
Sanders' decision to hire an agent is intriguing for a few reasons. It's a departure from the norm, as Sanders didn't have an agent before, and we know when players make an agent change, it can be because that player is looking for a change from their current situation. Adding to that, the decision comes with less than one month to go before the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10.
The hire has many believing Sanders might push to be traded.
One analyst who believes this is a sign Sanders could push for a trade is CBS Sports' John Breech .
Breech also thinks Dallas is a possible landing spot because of owner Jerry Jones' relationship with Deion Sanders , who played for the Cowboys during his Hall of Fame career.
"If you're making a list of landing spots for Shedeur Sanders, you might as well include the Cowboys," he said. "Deion Sanders spent five seasons in Dallas during his Hall of Fame career, and, given that fact alone, Jerry Jones might be intrigued by the idea of bringing in Shedeur as a possible backup to Dak Prescott."
Could we see Deion going to Jerry behind the scenes and asking him to trade for his son? That's certainly plausible, but it wouldn't really make sense for Shedeur or the Cowboys.
While it would be fun, this is most certainly a trade the Cowboys do not need to make.
The Cowboys already have an established backup quarterback in Sam Howell, who is more proven than Sanders is, which is ideal because of the Cowboys' win-now situation. And, Dallas is also developing a quarterback on the practice squad in Joe Milton.
Playing devil's advocate for a second, Sanders does at least offer the possibility of upside and there is a small chance he could end up being the future replacement for Dak Prescott, who will be 35 when his contract expires after 2028.
But that's a long ways away from even being a possibility and the fact of the matter is the Cowboys can't look that far ahead right now. Howell is the safer bet as a backup and Dallas can't carry three quarterbacks on its roster because space is needed for more depth on defense.
The bottom line is that Dallas doesn't have a need at quarterback right now and the Cowboys should be solely focused on using draft capital to fix actual problems, all of which come on the defensive side of the ball .
And it remains to be seen if Shedeur would even want to come to the Cowboys. Chances are he'll want a situation that offers him a path to start and Dallas won't offer him that.

title: Jerry Jones Gives Video Tour Of $33M Dallas Mansion In Rare Glimpse At Personal Life
full_text:
This week, Dallas Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones celebrated a monumentous moment. No, the franchise did not return to a conference championship or Super Bowl in the first time in over 30 years, but Jerry did get to celebrate his 84th birthday.
This week, as he geared up to ring in another year of life, Jones offered a rare glimpse into his personal life and opened the doors to his $30 million Dallas mansion . (To be fair, estimates on his home range from $27-$33 million online, so we're settling right in the middle).
Jones welcomed FOX & Friends host Steve Doocy into his not-so-humble abode to check out some of his favorite spaces and most treasured belongings.
Of course, there were Super Bowl trophies and rings, photographs of the iconic Dallas Cowboys Triplets (Troy Aikman, Emmitt Smith, and Michael Irvin), and other luxurious items that come with price tags that would make the normal person gasp.
Jones showed off his mansion in an MTV Cribs -style video, as he and Doocy strolled through the walls.
During the tour, Doocy took a playful jab at Jones for only having three Super Bowl trophies. "Where are the others?", he joked.
To Jerry's credit, he took everything in stride and discussed the massive changes that the Cowboys' roster and defense underwent during the offseason.
"Well, let's say this, we've changed everything on the defense. Not since I bought the team have we had more changes," Jones said.
"We've changed out the personnel dramatically. We've changed out the coaching staff totally. We've changed out the schemes involved. That first year we won one game. We're evolving, but it's probably a little more time needed than I had anticipated when we made these changes this year."
In his home, Jones also boased "Norman Rockwell’s 'The Toss,' and rare Leyendecker paintings, then step into a custom library with a star-covered ceiling, a hidden door, and original Thomas Jefferson documents."
One of the coolest pieces of memorabilia for Cowboys fans would have to be Troy Aikman's first $3 million contract check, which only Jones can make look so casual.
You can check out the full 15-minute video tour of Jones' Dallas mansion in the video above. Hopefully, Jerry can continue his birthday celebration this weekend with a Cowboys win over the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.

title: Everything Dallas Cowboys Have to Fear About Green Bay Packers in Week 6
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys will be looking to rebound following a brutal loss in Week 5 when they take on the Green Bay Packers on Sunday night in Week 6.
Dallas had a miserable letdown last week against a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team that was 0-4 and was started an undrafted rookie quarterback.
Since then, the Cowboys have been taking a long look in the mirror, especially when it comes to their defense, which was remained awful despite a total overhaul this offseason .
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer promised there will be changes this week, and the Cowboys better hope those changes on the defensive side of the ball are effective because the Packers present an extremely tough challenge for Dallas' unit.
That challenge is just one of the things the Cowboys have to fear about the Packers in Week 6.
The Packers' passing attack finally broke out last week and showed just what it is capable of, especially down the field.
The Packers connected on five passing plays of 36 yards or more, with four of those going to explosive receivers Christian Watson, who scored two long touchdowns, and Matthew Golden.
The good news is, Joey Porter Jr. will likely be back this week after missing last week's game with an illness, although his status is worth monitoring as he's listed with an ankle injury and was a limited participant in practice on Wednesday.
The bad news is, the Cowboys still need to cover the other side of the field and that will likely rest on the shoulders of DaRon Bland, who has been one of the worst cornerbacks in the NFL .
With the Cowboys struggling to run the football this season, there is a lot of presure on Dak Prescott and the passing attack to carry the offense. However, it might be tough to do that this week.
The Packers boast the fifth-best pass defense in the NFL this year and they have done a good job getting after the quarterback, with Green Bay tied for the seventh-most sacks.
Turning the ball over through the air has been a strength for Green Bay, also, with the Packers tied for the most picks in the league with seven.
The good news for the Cowboys is the Packers sport one of the worst run defenses in the NFL, so maybe Dallas can get Javonte Williams going to slow down Green Bay's pass-rush and take pressure off the passing attack.
The Packers rank top 10 in kick return average (27.2 yards per return, ranking eighth) and punt return average (15.5 yards per, ranking second).
It doesn't look like the Packers will have their top returner in Skyy Moore this week due to an ankle injury , but Green Bay still has a few effective options to replace him. Bo Melton is averaging a robust 27.3 yards per return on kickoffs and Matthew Golden ripped off 13.5 yards per punt return last week.
The Cowboys are going to have a difficult enough time stopping the Packers' offense and allowing shorter fields because of long returns is only going to make that more difficult. Dallas' special teams unit has to be a lot better this week.

title: Cowboys Legend Troy Aikman Addresses Joe Buck Tension, ESPN MNF Contract Drama
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are no strangers to being in the headlines because of on and off-field drama, and it looks like the soap opera continues even after you remove the star from your helmet.
Three-time Super Bowl champion Troy Aikman is the latest former Cowboys to find himself in the headlines because of contract drama, and it's reportedly boiled over into a confrontation with fellow Monday Night Football commentator Joe Buck.
Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports reports that there "has been tension" between Aikman and Buck after the latter signed a new five-year deal with ESPN. The tension apparently spilled over into an argument at SoFi Stadium this week after Buck "broke the ice" on the topic.
While Buck has received a new deal, Aikman has not received an offer, and now everyone is left wondering whether this could be the final year of their long-standing partnership.
Cowboys Hall of Famer @TroyAikman joined The Musers this morning, and the guys gave let him have the floor to address the headlines over the last 24 hours about his situation over at ESPN, regarding his contract status. @georgedunham @junior_miller @gordonkeith pic.twitter.com/9vY8y9R2jr
Aikman was asked about the tension during an appearance on Dallas' 96.7 The Ticket on Thursday morning, and he played coy on any current drama.
One thing Aikman made clear, however, is that he is open to all options following the season.
“ There’s probably a time and a place for all that . I don’t know if now is the time. I don’t know if it’s hard to figure out kind of what happened," Aikman said, via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News. "I’ll broadcast through this season and I’ll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens.
"I’m looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot may be.”
If Aikman does move on from Monday Night Football, it will be interesting to see what he does next.
Will he continue his broadcasting career, or could we see Aikman get back to the football side of things like he did with the Miami Dolphins during the offseason?
Aikman has been working in an unofficial role advising Miami Dolphins owner Stephen Ross, taking part in the general manager search after the departure of Chris Grier. Aikman helped the Dolphins land new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan.
When Aikman began helping the Dolphins, many Cowboys fans were wondering why Jerry Jones and Dallas wouldn't reach out to the legendary quarterback for a similar role with America's Team.
Aikman said that the Cowboys never reached out to use him as a resource .
"I think the Dolphins were wise in understanding my relationships around the league and knowing that I have information that they don't have or can't get," Aikman said. "And I think they were smart in taking advantage of that, whether it was through me or through somebody else.
"The Cowboys have never elected to do that, at least with me. Maybe they have with others, but I don't feel there's a conflict. But I will say I'm pulling for the Dolphins because now I have something at stake."
If Aikman becomes a free agent after the season because the tension with Buck is too much to get over, let's hope that Jerry Jones and the Cowboys give him a ring and don't miss out on a second opportunity to get one of the franchise's all-time greats involved in improving the future of the team.

title: 4 Perplexing Takeaways From Broncos' 17-14 OT Win Over Seahawks
full_text:
The Denver Broncos were the home underdog against the Seattle Seahawks , and Sean Payton and company seemed to take that personally.
Offensively, the Broncos put together their best first-half performance of the season against Seattle, scoring 14 points and showing signs of life in the run game, while their defense was outstanding and smothering. Denver walked away with the upset win to move to 4-2, though it wasn’t easy, as the Seahawks surged in the fourth quarter.
With that 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks, the Broncos have now defeated the reigning Super Bowl champions in each of the past three seasons. But as elating as it is for Denver to get through this first six-game gauntlet at 4-2, this win tastes sour for so many fans because of how Nix and the offense played in the second half.
What did we really learn from the Broncos' fourth win of the season? Here are four key takeaways.
The Broncos' best first-half showing of the season came against one of the NFL's best defenses. The Broncos put up 14 points on two touchdowns, with both scores capping extended drives that saw them move the chains and convert third downs.
The offensive line, the running game, and Bo Nix were the best they've been all season — in terms of first-half showings. Was it perfect from the offense?
No. There were still too many dead plays in the run game —16 runs for 52 yards — with J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey logging 15 carries for 46 yards combined. Both had rushing touchdowns, but their run-game consistency was still lacking. That said, it was a major step forward and a positive sign of life for this run game.
In the first half, the Broncos got Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle involved, with the latter catching two and the former catching one. Sutton had a key third-down play and also drew a pass-interference penalty that set up the Broncos' second touchdown on the one-yard line.
Payton has been working for faster starts and wants Nix to " let it rip ." Again, despite some issues, this was at least one step closer, and against a tough defense.
Unfortunately, it didn’t carry over to the second half, especially with the defensive adjustments the Seahawks made, so the offense was still unable to put together a full game.
It wasn’t all pretty from Nix, but it was better than what Denver's got out of him in the previous two weeks. Outside of two throws, he didn’t push the ball deep and took the underneath throws, which is what the Seahawks aim for defensively, but he wasn’t always looking for the checkdown.
On top of that, Nix played tougher in the pocket. He didn't constantly bail on clean pockets or panic at even the slightest pressure. He had multiple first-half throws where he stood tough and tall in the pocket, took some contact, and still delivered a catchable ball, especially on third down.
One-read throws and plenty of option plays made things easier for Nix, like Payton putting the training wheels back on. That isn’t necessarily a bad thing; with Nix's confidence so clearly shaken, he needed these types of plays to build it back up, which hopefully leads to Payton opening up the playbook again later in the season.
The Broncos can't give up on trying to massage Nix through this slump and help him regain his pre-2026 footing. At the same time, they can't become overly reliant on the training-wheels type plays, because it's likely to catch up with them.
The offense faltered a lot in the second half, and some of it was on Nix, though not all of it. Far from it.
Even amid the second-half offensive collapse, Nix showed modest signs of progress, compared to what we saw from him in the Broncos' two-week road trip to California.
The Seahawks' offense has its fair share of issues, with a run game that was almost as bad as the Broncos' for the first five weeks. The Seahawks have also dealt with bad protection issues and questionable quarterback play that led to ball-security issues.
With Patrick Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga out and Riley Moss limited, there were concerns about how the Broncos would handle the Seahawks' explosive passing game.
Denver shut down the run for most of the game and largely stonewalled Seattle's passing game, outside of a handful of plays. It was an elite showing, especially with three starters out and Moss mostly watching from the sideline.
Kris Abrams-Draine came up with a clutch interception at the end of the fourth quarter, while Jahdae Barron played sticky, physical coverage that helped limit Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the first half. Throw in Ja'Quan McMillian's overtime interception, and I'm not sure anyone could have expected this beleaguered secondary to play any better than it did against the defending champs.
Ja'Quan McMillian read this PERFECTLY. SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1igvuDtROG
The Broncos sacked Sam Darnold five times and harrassed him all game long. He battled in the fourth quarter, but eventually, his bad decision-making under pressure came home to roost.
The Broncos have improved each week defensively and have shown they can generate takeaways, which was an issue last year. This is a great unit on the cusp of being elite.
The Broncos will get there if they can fix some of the explosives they've allowed, while improving their run game and tackling inconsistency.
With the Broncos sitting where they are in the standings, it's hard to justify trading a player away, let alone one as impactful as Mims has been. However, his lack of effort on offense is becoming a detriment, especially when the Broncos go max protect, and he doesn’t even look for the ball.
Mims isn’t getting as much run as a kick returner, and his play as a punt returner hasn't been good. Troy Franklin can make up for Mims on offense, and the Broncos have other options to return punts, including Kolbe Katsis on the practice squad.
If there's an opportunity to trade Mims, who's playing on an expiring contract, the Broncos should do it.

title: Several Broncos Could Make History vs. Seahawks on TNF
full_text:
The Denver Broncos will try to get to 4-2 on Thursday night with the Seattle Seahawks coming to town .
The Seahawks also stand at 3-2, and they won their last meeting with the Broncos, which happened to be the first start of Bo Nix's career back in Week 1 of 2024. Broncos-Seahawks will be fought at Mile High under the bright lights of Thursday Night Football .
The Broncos are focused on getting the win , and we all know it won't be easy against the reigning Super Bowl champions. But in each of the past two years, the Broncos have defeated the defending World Champions in the regular season.
Several Broncos have some individual milestones and records on the table in Week 6's matchup with the Seahawks. And the Broncos, as a team, has a head-to-head record against the Seahawks to defend.
Here's what to watch for on Thursday night.
The Broncos are 35-21 against the Seahawks all-time, with a 23-5 home record. Up until 2002, the Seahawks were an AFC West rival, dating back decades.
When the Seahawks left the AFC West, they didn't just leave the division, they left the conference, become an NFC West team. The Broncos have dominated the Seahawks historically, but Seattle has the ultimate bragging rights of having defeated Denver in Super Bowl XLVIII.
The Broncos need just two sacks to tie for the NFL's fourth-longest streak all-time with multiple sacks at home. The Broncos have had two-plus sacks in 19 straight home games.
Expect the Broncos to get to Sam Darnold a few times.
With a touchdown grab, Sutton would tie Riley Odoms for the seventh-most receivng scores in Broncos history. Sutton broke the touchdown ice on this season last week, finding pay-dirt at SoFi Stadium.
Sutton is due for a touchdown in front of the Mile High Faithful. Hopefully, it comes against the Seahawks.
If Waddle can get over the century mark as a receiver tonight, he'll become the fifth player in Broncos history to record multiple 100-yard games in his first season with the team. It hasn't happened since 2014, when Emmanuel Sanders pulled it off.
Waddle's first 100-yard game came in Week 2 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, finishing with 138 yards on the day. Like Sutton, Waddle is due for a big game, but the Seahawks' defense is formidable.
Allen just one sack to become the ninth player in Broncos history to reach five sacks in four consecutive years. Five sacks doesn't sound like a lot, but it is, and pulling it off in five straight years is tough to do in this league, especially as an interior pass rusher.
Allen sacked Justin Herbert last week. Here's to hoping he gets home against Darnold.
With 2.5 sacks, Bonitto would tie Pryce for the third-most sacks by a Bronco in his first five seasons in team history. It's a pretty cool stat, given that Bonitto didn't become a starter until 2024.
Bonitto was drafted in 2022, so while it took him a couple of years to find his NFL footing, he made up for lost time by posting 27.5 sacks the past two years. This season started slowly for Bonitto, but he's posted three sacks in the past three games.

title: Why ESPN Put Broncos QB Bo Nix On Hot Seat — And Why He's Not
full_text:
Considering the multitude of aggravating factors within the struggling Denver Broncos offense, the opinions on quarterback Bo Nix have varied wildly in recent days.
The discourse has turned to the long-term viability of Nix as Denver's franchise signal-caller, with ESPN's Bill Barnwell speculating that he could be on (some form of) the hot seat entering Week 6 .
"Let's frame this one appropriately and be clear," Barnwell wrote in part on Thursday. "I don't think the Broncos are about to bench Nix for backup Jarrett Stidham, who hasn't been particularly impressive as a pro and didn't play well in last season's AFC title game loss to the Patriots while filling in for the injured starter. The hot seat here is more in the big picture, with Nix becoming eligible for a contract extension after the season and a decision on his fifth-year option in 2028 (at a projected $29.9 million) coming due next spring."
"The Broncos were hoping Nix would take a step forward after his great performance in the postseason and the addition of Waddle. If Nix doesn't get there, will the Broncos want to commit to him as their quarterback of the future on a second contract?"
Barnwell went on to allow that Nix's slump might be attributed to the ankle injury (and subsequent surgeries) he suffered in last season's Divisional Round win over the Bills. Nix currently ranks 29th in yards per attempt and 22nd in yards per dropback through five games.
The Broncos offense collectively ranks 30th in total yards, 26th in scoring, and 25th in passing and rushing as Nix has completed only 59.9% of his attempts for 942 yards, six touchdowns, and three interceptions. He's also largely been a non-factor on the ground, managing 35 yards and one TD on 18 carries.
Nix is the first one to tell you that he isn't performing up to standard. He's touched on potential confidence issues relating to turnovers and taking deep shots downfield. In many respects, he's the farthest iteration from what the fans saw in 2025.
But some perspective is warranted, too. The Broncos are 3-2, surviving a brutal schedule that begins to ease up in a few weeks. They'll get back rookie RB Jonah Coleman in Week 7 and WR Pat Bryant a bit thereafter following both players' stints on injured reserve.
Head coach Sean Payton recently took over control of play-calling, and the core talent level — Jaylen Waddle, Evan Engram, RJ Harvey, JK Dobbins — is good enough to make hay with. After all, this is the same team just eight months removed from what should've been a Super Bowl appearance.
Most importantly, Nix still holds the trust of Payton, who hand-selected and developed him into his version of ideal. And that work isn't about to end now, abruptly, with the Broncos above .500 and very much in the early playoff picture.
“I think as coaches, like I said to him, ‘Man, you’re the guy we want here. Let’s go. You’ve done a ton of things well.' But I think there’s a lot that goes into that," Payton said after last Sunday's victory over the Chargers. "In that old TBS series 'The Bear', where they say 'just let it rip.' I want him to make sure that we can let it rip.”
Winning cures everything in this business. Beat the Seahawks on Thursday Night Football, and a lot of this talk — magically — will evaporate into the ether.

title: 5 Bold Predictions for Broncos-Seahawks That Might Surprise Fans
full_text:
The Denver Broncos face the unenviable challenge of hosting the Seattle Seahawks on a short week. On top of that, injuries continue to pile up , and the Broncos' offensive struggles appear to have no end in sight.
That's a tough prospect to face against a team like the Seahawks, whose defense is one of the NFL's best. The Broncos will have to turn in an inspired performance if they're going to overcome all the factors working against them this week.
As for my bold predictions for this game, not all of them are favorable toward the Broncos. I can only call it like I see it, so let's get to it.
The Seahawks' defense is tough, disciplined, and the players trust each other to do their job. It's also a style of defense the Broncos' offense has typically struggled against since 2023, almost like Sean Payton can't fully figure it out.
That doesn't mean the Broncos won't have some moments, but it'll be another ugly showing as they end the game with their second-lowest yards total, barely beating out their offensive showing from the season opener in Kansas City.
The Broncos fail to reach the red zone as an offense, except for at least one possession that starts inside Seattle's 20-yard line thanks to a takeaway on defense.
Outside of the defense turning the ball over, the Broncos' offense has too many issues to overcome and fix in such a short-week turnaround. A few days and one true practice aren't enough time to turn the ship around, especially against a quality defense like Seattle's.
Ball security has been a major issue for the Seahawks' offense, especially their running backs, and that opens the door for some takeaways. Denver is able to force two fumbles and falls on them both.
One of those fumble recoveries puts Bo Nix and the offense in their one-and-only red-zone possession.
Sam Darnold can be tough to get to, with nine sacks in four games, but five of them came against the San Francisco 49ers this past Sunday.
Denver has the horses up front and the different looks to generate pressure, which can result in multiple sacks on Darnold, but the Broncos will need their secondary to hold up long enough to allow Bonitto, Allen, and company to get home.
Darnold will look to counter Denver's pass rush with the quick-pass game, but the secondary has to hold up.
Everything points to a high-volume game for the kicker. The Seahawks are allowing an average of 21 points per game, which is the eighth-fewest in the NFL this season.
The Seahawks do well in the red zone and have allowed only 10 touchdowns this season. With the Broncos' offensive woes, they turn to Lutz often in this game, and while he's not perfect, he mostly comes through.
