title: 3 Things Broncos Must Get Right to Beat Seahawks
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have faced some of the NFL's best teams to start this season.
That trend continues on Thursday night against the reigning World Champion Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos will host the Seahawks at Mile High in a game that could be viewed as a potential Super Bowl preview.
In an alternate universe not too far away, Bo Nix never suffered a broken ankle in the divisional round of the playoffs, and he was on the field to host the New England Patriots in the AFC championship game at Mile High. We all know which team would have represented the AFC in the Super Bowl if Nix was on the field that day.
Now, whether a Nix-led Broncos team would have prevailed against the Seahawks in the Super Bowl is anyone's guess; but I would have wagered that Denver would have kept things close, even if it meant trading field goals.
When the fourth quarter rolled around, Nix and the "Heart-Attack Horsies" — who had become so resilient and battle-tested in late-game, big-moment situations — would have found a way to get it done against Seattle, instead of unraveling as Drake Maye and the Patriots did.
That would have been my guess, had Nix not gotten hurt. But that's not the football universe we live in. The Broncos' magical season came to an abrupt and bitterly disappointing end. But the Seahawks know the truth, too. It should have been Denver.
For these reasons and more, you can believe that both teams have had this game circled on the schedule since it dropped. Both teams are 3-2, with all their goals and aspirations still on the table in front of them.
If the Broncos are going to win against another tough non-conference opponent, three things will need to fall into place. Instead of calling them 'keys to victory,' here are three things the Broncos absolutely must get right to beat the Seahawks.
Amid Nix's early-season slump, many people have lost sight of what this kid has accomplished and what he's capable of. He's no stranger to starting slow, either, whether it's individual games or seasons.
Nix didn't storm out of the gate in Year 3 with Josh-Allen-circa-2020 numbers. So what? Allen's Year 3 rise was a thing to behold, but he didn't have to face the murderer's row of competition to start the season that Nix has.
According to Gridiron Stats and Info , the Broncos have faced the toughest schedule of opposing offenses to start this season, and the second-toughest schedule of opposing defenses . And yet, they're 3-2.
In all the years I've been watching football, let alone covering it, I've never seen the NFL hand a team such a schedule. On one hand, the Broncos earned their first-place schedule by winning the AFC West and earning the conference's No. 1 playoff seed; on the other, the NFL could have done a better job of spreading out some of these matchups.
The Kansas City Chiefs, Los Angeles Chargers, and the Las Vegas Raiders all have to face the teams of the NFC West and AFC East — just like the Broncos — but the NFL didn't expose them to the buzzsaw consecutively out of the gates as it did Denver. What am I getting at here?
The intense, singular level of competition Nix has faced to start this season is obviously one of the reasons why he has struggled. I believe there's more between-the-ears stuff going on with Nix, but some fans are losing sight of just how insane his schedule has been.
But if you think back to last year, Nix started off pretty slowly. He didn't really find his groove until the fourth quarter of Week 7's historic comeback win over the New York Giants, when he became the first player in NFL history to score two touchdowns on the ground and through the air in the same period.
From there, Nix turned a corner, and he didn't face anywhere near the level of competition he is facing this season. If the best predictor of future outcomes is past outcomes, he will find his footing and then BOOM — he's off and running.
"You were the underdogs..." - @tracywolfson "We're the overdogs" - Bo Nix 😂 pic.twitter.com/sVx3izRHc0
Clutch-time play has been one of the hallmarks of Nix's tenure in Denver. But another hallmark is how he elevates against tougher opponents or in big-time situations. A primetime showing against the Seahawks would qualify.
Nix hasn't been perfect, but he is 6-2 in primetime. If you count last year's Christmas Day game against the Chiefs, he's 7-2 in primetime games.
In Week 3, Nix faced the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football , and while it wasn't always pretty, he turned it on when he needed to and stormed back to beat a Super Bowl contender 30-26. The Broncos need that big-game version of Nix if they're going to beat the Seahawks.
The good news is, Nix views this Seahawks matchup as one of those moments, and he acknowledged that both teams will have their dander up.
"Absolutely. There'll be some extra juice on both sides, and I think this is why you play the game," Nix said of the Seahawks. "This is why you want to be an NFL quarterback."
Nix doesn't have to be perfect. But he does have to excel in critical situations, like third down, red zone, and end-of-game.
The Seahawks' defense is a tough draw, but Nix is due for a game that reminds everyone who he is and what he's capable of.
Without a ground game, the Broncos will be dead in the water against Seattle. As it applies to Nix's slump, Sean Payton said it best after the Broncos' ugly 23-17 win over the Chargers last week: "The hardest thing to do in this league is play that position if you're not rushing the ball.”
The Broncos currently rank 25th in rushing, averaging just 86.2 yards per game. But with Payton calling the plays again in Week 5, the Broncos did take some steps forward as a rushing offense.
Payton stayed committed to a run-pass balance , allowing running back J.K. Dobbins to find a bit of a groove late in the game to help salt it away at SoFi Stadium. Dobbins had his best game of the season, rushing for 68 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries against a tough Chargers defensive front. The Broncos eclipsed the 100-yard rushing mark as a team — a step in the right direction.
The Seahawks have a great defense, but the run game is one of the few chinks in their armor. Seattle ranks top-10 defensively in all the major categories, with the exception of run defense (11th) and red-zone efficiency (27th).
The Seahawks barely rank outside the top 10 in run defense, but that's where the Broncos have to focus their first- and second-down attack because if Nix is faced with third-and-longs against this defense, it's a recipe for disaster. Seattle leads the NFL in takeaways, with 11, and ranks No. 7 in sacks.
With how much Nix seems to be worried about turning the ball over against one elite defense after another, the best way to cool Seattle's jets is to get the run game rolling. I'm not talking 'three yards and a cloud of dust,' but if that's what it takes, I'd rather see Nix faced with 3rd-&-4 than 3rd-&-7 or 3rd-&-9.
The onus falls on Payton to call some well-designed rushing plays and to stick to it throughout the game. And let's not forget about the Broncos' starting five; they're a big reason the ground game has been so impotent this season, but it's time to break out of this run-blocking funk.
This can't be a game where RJ Harvey only gets three carries (like last week). Payton has a formidable one-two punch in Dobbins and Harvey, but he's got to use them that way to get the full effect.
If the Broncos don't rush for north of 100 yards in this game as a team, it's going to be a very long night for Nix. If they are able to establish the run and be productive, it should help insulate Nix and coax him out of his shell by setting him up in much more favorable third-down situations and keeping the Broncos on the field on extended drives that lead to points.
There's a chance Riley Moss could play this game, as he's listed as questionable with the rib injury that kept him out of action last week. However, Patrick Surtain II has been ruled out, along with safety…

title: Broncos Week 6 Injury Report: Final Decisions on Surtain, Hufanga
full_text:
The Denver Broncos will officially be without star safety Talanoa Hufanga for Thursday's game against the Seattle Seahawks.
Releasing their final Week 6 injury report , the Broncos ruled out Hufanga with the ankle injury he picked up in last week's victory over the Los Angeles Chargers — an injury that's expected to sideline him for the next few games.
Hufanga was marked as "DNP" (Did Not Practice) on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday, making it evident that Denver was bracing for his absence .
The Broncos also ruled out perennial All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II with his own ankle injury sustained in Week 4. 9NEWS' Mike Klis reported " there is hope " Surtain can return for next week's matchup against the Arizona Cardinals.
Fellow cornerback Riley Moss was listed as questionable after getting in three straight limited practices. Moss missed Week 5 with a ribs issue.
Jahdae Barron and/or Kris Abrams-Draine are the next men up on the depth chart if Moss joins Surtain on the inactive list.
“I would say this, it’s time," head coach Sean Payton said Monday regarding the challenges of preparing on a short week. "There are two things, time and then the second thing is proper recovery from the last game. For each player, getting their body ready for a short work week, so that the time and the recovery—those are the two things that hit me right away with that question.”
Elsewhere on the injury report, safety Brandon Jones (foot), left guard Ben Powers (biceps), and defensive lineman Sai'vion Jones (shoulder) were all full practice participants and given no game designations; they will play versus Seattle .
Unfortunately for the Broncos, the Seahawks gave the all-clear to the NFL's current receiving leader, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who emerged from Week 5 with a minor ankle injury. Smith-Njigba was limited on Monday and Tuesday before being upgraded to full on Wednesday.
“You feel great football I.Q, and then you put that with great talent and hips," Payton said of Smith-Njigba on Tuesday. "He can really transition, and then he’s a really good YAC player. So he’s catching it cleanly with his feet on the ground. All of the above.”
The Seahawks did rule out three of their own: running back Zach Charbonnet and linebackers Chazz Surratt and Drake Thomas. Every other player on their roster is expected to be available for Thursday Night Football .

title: Talanoa Hufanga Expected to Miss Time—But Broncos Have Answers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos expect to be without safety Talanoa Hufanga for the next two to three weeks. That hurts, with the Seattle Seahawks coming to town on a short week and the Broncos already being down two secondary starters, potentially.
ESPN 's Jeremy Fowler reported the Hufanga timetable on Wednesday, but he did qualify it with "depending on how he recovers."
Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga is expected to miss multiple weeks with an ankle injury, per sources. One source estimated about 2-3 weeks, depending how he recovers. pic.twitter.com/8Eo02Dmbd0
Hufanga suffered the injury late in the third quarter of the Broncos' 23-17 win over the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, making a tackle for a loss. He's now set to miss his first game since joining the Broncos as a free agent in the spring of 2025.
Through five games, Hufanga has been an impact player, totaling 23 tackles (12 solo), three tackles for a loss, one sack, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, and two interceptions, one of which he returned to the house.
Hufanga earned AFC Defensive Player of the Week honors for that pick-six game — a 30-26 win over the Los Angeles Rams at Mile High. He picked Matthew Stafford off a second time in the end zone to end the game on Sunday Night Football .
Hufanga started all 17 games in his first year as a Bronco, totaling 106 tackles on his way to being named a second-team All-Pro. He was viewed as a big injury risk when the Broncos originally signed him, due to how his last couple of seasons with the San Francisco 49ers played out.
Hopefully, Hufanga is back in time to host the Kansas City Chiefs for the Broncos' rematch at Mile High in Week 8. But it might not be until after the Broncos' Week 10 bye, if he doesn't recover as quickly as the team hopes. Ankle injuries can be fickle.
The good news is, the Broncos haven't placed Hufanga on injured reserve, which hints that the team believes he'll be ready to return inside of four weeks. Until then, though, the Broncos need a plan at safety.
Devon Key stands to be the Broncos' starter at safety next to Brandon Jones while Hufanga is out. The Broncos still have JL Skinner and Tycen Anderson on the 53-man roster, but don't be surprised if they elevate veteran safety Taylor Rapp from the practice squad.
The Broncos wanted Rapp for a reason , and he's had a month-plus to settle in and assimilate the playbook. It wouldn't be a complete shock to see Rapp go from the practice squad to the starting lineup while Hufanga is out, given his extensive experience, but the Broncos are likely to give Key the first bite at the apple.
But if Denver was waiting for the right time to deploy Rapp and make use of his veteran experience, there may not be a better one than this. Since entering the league in 2019, Rapp has more career starts (72) than Hufanga does NFL games (71).
Rapp has played in some huge games with the Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills. He won a Super Bowl as a starter with the Rams a few years back.
That's a lot of experiece to let languish on the sideline or practice squad with Hufanga out of commission. Jones has been playing lights-out himself, and he and Rapp could make a solid safety duo.
Key is talented but very inexperienced. He may be a first-team All-Pro special teams ace, but he's yet to turn the corner as a reliable safety on defense.
The Broncos rolled the dice by letting P.J. Locke go in free agency this past offseason, hoping that Key could step in and serve as a bona fide No. 3 safety. The fact that Denver went searching for Rapp at the end of training camp may hint at how the team views Key from a reliability standpoint.
The Broncos have the horses to survive Hufanga's absence. But it's going to be dicey without cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs), too.
There's a chance Moss could play against the Seahawks on Thursday night, but the Broncos might be shorthanded again at cornerback.

title: Detroit Lions Defensive Line Has Exceeded Expectations
full_text:
The Detroit Lions’ defense has been one of the league's worst units through the first five weeks of the season. Yet, not all has been bad for defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit.
The defensive line, for one, has been quite reliable. And EDGE Aidan Hutchinson and interior defensive lineman Alim McNeill have arguably been the defense's most consistent performers.
Hutchinson has continued his steady play from seasons past, and continues to wreak havoc against opposing quarterbacks on a weekly basis.
He's generated the second-most pressures of any defender in the NFL this season (32). Plus, he's recorded the second-best Pro Football Focus overall grade among 106 qualified EDGE defenders (91.4), along with the highest pass-rush mark at the position (91.1).
The fifth-year pro is the Lions’ best defensive player and one of the most prolific pass-rushers in the game today. And he doesn't appear to be on the verge of slowing down anytime soon.
While Hutchinson's production has become a given, it wasn't quite as big of a certainty with McNeill entering the 2026 campaign.
The interior defender spent the majority of the 2025 season on the sideline recovering from a torn ACL. And when he did return to play, he wasn't exactly effective. In fact, he proved to be much more of a liability than a reliable contributor to Sheppard's defense. He generated just 23 total pressures and a single sack in 10 games a season ago, earning a measly PFF overall grade of 52.2.
Luckily for Dan Campbell's squad , McNeill has bounced back in a major way this season. The 26-year-old has already amassed 3.5 sacks and the same number of pressures he did a season ago. Additionally, his 23 pressures rank first among 133 qualified interior defensive linemen, and his PFF overall grade of 79.4 ranks ninth at the position.
McNeill is back to his productive ways, and it's been a godsend for Detroit's defensive line through the season's first five games.
While Hutchinson and McNeill have carried the D-line, it has also received production from a couple of unsung heroes: rookie interior lineman Skyler Gill-Howard and veteran EDGE D.J. Wonnum.
Gill-Howard, a sixth-round pick of the Lions this past April, has been a pleasant surprise for Detroit thus far in 2026.
Quite notably, he's been fairly proficient at getting after the quarterback, with 13 pressures to his name (the most among all rookie interior defensive linemen). That figure also ranks third among all first-year players.
Then, there's Wonnum, who has compiled five sacks, tied for fourth-most in the NFL and two more than he produced all of last season. And for his performance, he's earned a pass-rush grade of 65.5, ranking 43rd among all qualified EDGEs.
Through the collective efforts of these aforementioned linemen, the Lions have secured the most sacks in the NFL through five weeks (20.0).
So, even in an overwhelmingly disappointing season so far for the defense, all has not been lost. Detroit's pass-rush department , spearheaded by the defensive line, has managed to be productive, and has undeniably exceeded preseason expectations.

title: Detroit Lions Add Veteran WR, Returner to Practice Squad
full_text:
The Detroit Lions did not wait too long to add a veteran returner to be in the mix to replace Tom Kennedy.
Former Bears and Browns receiver DeAndre Carter will reportedly be inked to the teams practice squad.
Following the unfortunate MCL injury to Kennedy that will keep him away for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season, head coach Dan Campbell indicated the team would be in search externally for a new returner.
According to the transaction wire, the team worked out two wideouts, including Steven Sims and Carter.
The 33-year-old played collegiately at Sacremento State (2011-2014). He went undrafted in 2015, but landed with the Baltimore Ravens as an undrafted free agent. He has bounced around the league with stints at Oakland, New England, San Francisco, Philadelphia, Chicago, Washington, Los Angeles Chargers, Las Vegas and Cleveland.
During the 2024 season with Chicago, he averaged 31.9 yards per kickoff return, including 67-yarder. He returned a total of 17 punts and averaged 9.3 yards per return.
In late September of 2025, Carter was placed on the injured reserve list due to a knee injury suffered against Detroit in Week 4 of the regular season.
Special teams coordinator Dave Fipp was recently asked if the team was aiming for a certain starting spot average during returns.
“We have a lot of individual goals I'm not going to get into because you start saying those to people and then they start holding you accountable to all that," said Fipp. "We have our own metrics that we use. I certainly have mine. We have our own standards. We compare ourself to our standard after every single game in all areas, not only on kickoff, kickoff return. And the drive start is a major one for that. Obviously, we look at all the penalty stuff. That's really important in the return game.
"And then punt and punt and punt return, as you guys know, I mean, I do like stats," Fipp added. "I just don't like the way that they're publicized, like punt is terrible. The statistic for punt right now, I mean, I don't even know. They say gross punt's a good thing. Well, if you punt from the plus 40-yard line, your gross punt's not going to be very good. If you say net punt, same thing. If you punt out on your own 10-yard line a whole game, you're going to have a good net versus if you punt from the 50."
Fipp said the Lions have extensive information regarding return stats and compare themselves to league averages.
"We break down the punt into a bunch of different areas of the field and compare ourself to the league's numbers over the years," said Fipp. "And so, we do that after every single game, so we know exactly where we are in all areas. We have a high standard. It's not average. Our goal is to be well above that in all phases.”

title: One Advanced Metric Showcases Just How Important Brian Branch Is
full_text:
Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch could be returning to action soon from a torn Achilles. After continuing his rehab throughout the bye week, the team is hoping the former second-round pick can suit up against the Green Bay Packers in Week 7.
One advanced metric showcased just how vastly different the Lions' defense operates with Branch in the lineup and when he has been out due to injury.
According to TrueMedia, the Detroit Lions rank 30th in the league in defensive success rate without Branch in the lineup (2023-2026). With him patrolling the back end, the defensive success rate ranks third.
Defensive success rate is an advanced football metric that tracks how regularly a defense keeps the opposing offense "on schedule" rather than just counting total yards, according to Sports Reference .
Detroit's defense should feel quite comfortable with Branch returning. The safeties unit has been plagued with coverage breakdowns and communication issues, through the first quarter of the 2026 NFL season.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard recently addressed if his defense was trying to overcome trust issues.
"I kind of just alluded to that. I just mentioned that when a guy feels like this guy isn't in his gap now, 'Okay, I'm going to play my gap, but then I'm going to go try to peek to his and see if I can kind of help over there too.’ And then the ball hits in your gap. And this is happening a little too much," said Sheppard. "So now we've got to do one or two things. I told the guys this, 'We've got to make sure the guys you don't trust aren't out there or you guys get it corrected and you get it corrected in a hurry.’ Because we don't want to start doing that and guys feeling like they have got to carry the weight for another guy out there."
The former NFL linebacker indicated players cannot overcompensate for players that are in the wrong position.
"We should have an 11-man, that's why it's an 11-man defense," said Sheppard. "Everybody doing their one-eleventh. We can't have a guy play 10-man defense, now we've got two guys playing a gap and a half trying to overcompensate for somebody. We're done doing that.
"But again,  it's all lip service. I can stand here and give you the right answer and tell you things. It has to show up on game day.”

title: 'His Career Just Got Launched': Jon Gruden Praises Lions Rookie Defender
full_text:
Detroit Lions rookie cornerback Keith Abney II has earned a reasonable amount of praise for his performance at safety against the Arizona Cardinals.
The struggling NFC West squad was the perfect team to give the 2026 fifth-round draft pick an opportunity to gain experience at a new spot.
The Cardinals struggle this season to throw it deep, and without wideout Marvin Harrison Jr., who was ruled inactive in Week 5, the Lions' defense had an easier time defending the other Cardinals' offensive weapons.
Former NFL head coach and current analysis Jon Gruden named Abney his "Gruden Grinder" this week, praising the first-year defender for his play in a Lions 45-21 win.
"A lot of people ask me, 'What a Gruden grinder is?' They're versatile. A bit tough. Mentally tough. They don't come unglued when things go wrong," Gruden explained to his nearly 437,000 followers on social media. "They're team oriented and they're clutch. They feel no pressure . They apply it. Guys like Keith Abney II of the Detroit Lions. You know, nobody's been criticized more than the Detroit Lions defense. Their defensive coordinator, Kelvin Sheppard, has held this group together.
"One of the best things he did was put in Keith Abney II. He wears No. 6. He's 21-years-old. He's a fifth-round rookie out of Arizona State. Why was he in the fifth round? Well, maybe he not big enough. 5'9, 187-pounds. He goes to Arizona State, has limited play time in 2023," Gruden explained further. "But in 2024, he bursts onto the scene. Three interceptions, Nine pass breakups, 52 tackles. Then in 2025, he's All Big-12. Two picks, two forced fumbles, lot of ball production, 12 passes broken up."
Abney was inserted at safety to replace veteran Christian Izien, who struggled significantly against the Carolina Panthers. Playing alongside veteran Chuck Clark helped to stabilize a back end that had given up far too many explosive plays to start the season.
"Against the Arizona Cardinals, Abney returns home to Arizona, where he built the foundation that got him to the NFL," Gruden said. "He gets his first start. He has six solo tackles. He has his first interception and a pass broken up. And the Detroit Lions, not nly got five sacks, they have five straight three-and-outs against the Arizona Cardinals. A lot of it has to do with Keith Abney II. Instincts, versatility and mentality. This guy is a true grinder, and his career just got launched. Keep it up Keith."
This weeks Gruden Grinder is a Detroit Lion! Keith Abney II showed out in his first start, way to make your mark young man!! pic.twitter.com/tOg7UnGmv0

title: Lions 2026 First Quarter Risers and Fallers
full_text:
Through five games, the Detroit Lions have managed to secure a winning record.
Though they've had bumps along the way, the Lions are 3-2 with a chance to make a statement within the division with two NFC North opponents awaiting them out of the bye week.
While they've had some success to start the year, upcoming games against the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings at home should be telling about where this team ultimately stands.
Here are risers and fallers for the Lions through the first quarter of the 2026 NFL season.
The Lions were hoping they could find an ideal running mate for star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson in Wonnum after signing him to a one-year contract. Through five games, he's out-performed those expectations and is looking at a possible career year.
He currently leads the team with five sacks , and has three straight games with at least one. His career-high in a season is eight, and working opposite of Hutchinson has proven to be ideal for him. Not known for being an overly dominant pass-rusher, Wonnum is currently wreaking havoc.
Wonnum has a pass-rush win rate of 11.6 percent, which ranks behind only Hutchinson and Alim McNeill amongst Lions. He has also held his own against the run, and is looking like one of the team's better offseason signings.
Gibbs was entrusted with being the team's bell-cow back after they traded David Montgomery, and to this point he's lived up to the hype and then some. He ranks fourth in the league in rushing and is on pace for a career-high in receptions as well.
While there are rightfully some concerns about the level of usage that Gibbs has had to endure up to this point, he's certainly one of the league's most dynamic talents . He's quelled any concerns about the workload he's dealt with, and as a result there are high expectations for him moving forward.
The Lions were open about the fact that Mahogany would have to earn his starting job back heading into the season. In fact, they brought in veteran Ben Bartch and had plans of recently acquired Juice Scruggs also competing for the job.
However, due to injuries, the competition never materialized quite the way the team envisioned. That hasn't been to the detriment of the franchise, though, as the Lions have stuck with Mahogany and he has played at a high level through his first four starts.
The Boston College product missed the team's Week 2 loss to Buffalo, but has been one of the top-performing players. He's helped stabilize the interior amidst some offseason changes, and is currently the team's third-highest Pro Football Focus graded player with an 86.4 overall offensive grade.
While there were some concerns about Mahogany, he has ultimately found a way to cement himself as a starter moving forward and has taken his performance up a notch.
The Lions have needed Reed to be a shutdown corner, and he simply hasn't delivered at that level since signing a three-year deal prior to last season. While he's had some good moments, he's also been a big part of the team's struggles in the secondary.
Up to this point in the season, Reed has allowed an opposing passer rating of 124.2 and has drawn four penalty flags. He's been solid in run defense with a miniscule missed tackle rate of 7.5 percent, but has been beat for two touchdowns and allowed 17 completions on 27 targets.
It will be interesting to see whether the Lions elect to add cornerback help before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Reed will need to continue improving to help the defense bounce back from its early season struggles.
It has been a quiet start to the season for Detroit's second-round pick. Moore got a spike in snaps with a career-high 20 snaps against Arizona last week, but had played just 17 combined the previous two.
He has four total pressures in his pass-rush opportunities, and the emergence from Wonnum has further cut into his chances. Moving forward, he may not get as many opportunities given the state of Detroit's EDGE rotation unless he's more productive.
Expected to be the team's backup behind Gibbs, Pacheco has yet to appear in a game. He suffered a pair of injuries in training camp, and after undergoing a procedure he's expected to be out until December.
For a running back who already had an injury history entering the season, this isn't the most positive development. Pair that with the consistent improvement of Sione Vaki in the second running back role, and Pacheco may not get the opportunity to make a big impact after signing a one-year deal.

title: How Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade Negatively Impacts Detroit Lions
full_text:
The Detroit Lions should be among several NFL teams that are active at the trade deadline.
Unfortunately, the Houston Texans may no longer be a team that is selling at the deadline. Last week, Texans general manager Nick Caserio made the decison to trade for Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr.
"We had talked for a few weeks, and then the deal, he and I agreed to the deal Friday night," Caserio told 95.7 The Fan. "Like, the deal was basically done Friday night. We kind of had an agreement in place. I gave him my word, he gave me his word. That's how you do business, that's how (Cardinals GM) Monti Ossenfort and I do business.
"But he wanted to handle it a certain way as it pertains to the communication. and some of the other things. So, we certainly didn't have a problem with that at all. We kind of followed his lead there a little bit. I think he communicated with Marvin that he was going to be inactive Saturday morning."
The AFC South squad is off to a slow start this year. Through Week 5, the team has a 1-5 record. Prior to their victory against the Tennessee Titans, many began to speculate Houston may be a team that could sell at the deadline.
When teams start the season struggling, a few general manager may make the decision to part ways with talent, in order to begin looking to the future.
The value of accumulating draft picks, which offer the flexibility to package together to move up in the draft or trade for proven talent, can entice teams to part ways with players on expiring contracts or those who have not lived up to expectations.
Detroit is desperately in need of upgrading their secondary , as Kelvin Sheppard's unit is the worst defending the pass in the league to start the 2026 season.
Houston was not likely going to put Derek Stingley Jr. or Jalen Pitre on the market. But there could have been room to discuss the possibility of landing former second-round pick Kamari Lassiter.
His rookie contract expires at the end of the 2027 season and may have been a target for Lions general manager Brad Holmes.
Other teams to pay attention to in the coming weeks are the Los Angeles Chargers, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Arizona Cardinals, New York Jets and New Orleans Saints.
This year, the official deadline falls on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. (E.T.)

title: Should Lions LB Injury Lead to More Snaps for Jimmy Rolder?
full_text:
The start to the 2026 season has been a quiet one for Detroit Lions fourth-round pick Jimmy Rolder.
Through five games, Rolder has made three appearances and been limited to a role mostly on special teams. He has logged defensive snaps in just one game, when he played seven first quarter snaps against the Carolina Panthers.
In that game, Rolder was active over Devin White. However, White returned to the active lineup last Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals and as a result Rolder was relegated to special teams duty.
A wrench has been thrown in Detroit's plans against the Cardinals, however, as White suffered a forearm injury that is expected to require surgery and as such will sideline him for a significant amount of time. This creates an opening for an opportunity, one that Rolder could be poised to fill.
With the injury to White, more snaps could be heading Rolder's way in the coming weeks. There are pros and cons to the team giving him a bigger workload in coming weeks, with what could be a defining stretch ahead with games at home against the Packers and Vikings out of the bye week.
The Michigan product had a strong start to his first offseason as an NFL player, with a good showing in organized team activities and the start of training camp. However, he suffered a hamstring injury that sidelined him for a significant stretch of camp and ultimately led the team to sign White in the first place.
He got healthy near the end of camp, and wound up being inactive for Detroit's first two games. However, he seems to have found a role on special teams and has been active each of the last three games.
He got his first taste of life on defense in the loss to Carolina, where he notched a tackle for loss amidst his seven defensive snaps. A longer leash and a bigger workload would only add to his development, which will be beneficial for Detroit in the long run.
However, there is also a downside with the team giving more run to the rookie. The linebacker group is a veteran one, with Jack Campbell, Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, Trevor Nowaske and Amen Ogbongbemiga all having at least three years of NFL experience.
With the injury to White, the team could also add another veteran from the practice squad in Joe Bachie. The former Michigan State Spartan began the year on the active roster before being released and retained on the practice squad.
Furthermore, the Lions have deviated some from their traditional three-linebacker packages in favor of nickel with an extra defensive back, and Campbell and Barnes have the top two spots down pat. As a result, any snaps for Rolder would come at the expense of Rodriguez, Nowaske or Ogbongbemiga.
Especially in a pivotal stretch, the Lions would likely benefit more from leaning on their veterans than thrusting Rolder into a bigger role. However, he could also provide a spark for the defense.
Ultimately, the state of the Lions' defense would benefit from someone emerging and sparking the defense. Rolder's range and athleticism could be exactly what the group needs, and it may be time for him to get more extended work beginning after the bye week.

title: Why Detroit Lions Did Not Take Out Key Players After Comfortable Lead
full_text:
The Detroit Lions were able to secure a comfortable Week 5 road victory at State Farm Stadium, defeating the Arizona Cardinals, 45-21, to earn their third victory of the 2026 NFL season.
Given the game was out of reach in the fourth quarter, many supporters wondered why several key Lions' players remained in the contest.
For a team that has dealt with a myriad of injuries the past couple of seasons, taking unnecessary risks ahead of the bye week appeared a little risky.
Speaking to reporters earlier this week, Dan Campbell was asked at what point he is willing to take out starters in a game.
“ Look, I'm with you. I think there is a fine line, and I've mentioned this before. First of all, we've gotten in a couple of these games where they've, just for this season alone, to where all of a sudden, something didn't go our way and now within four or five minutes we're back in this tight game that doesn't need to be a tight game," Campbell said. "And so, you want to make sure, you want to feel dang sure, that you've got it wrapped up. But you also, when you feel like you're starting to play some of your best football, you want them to get that feel, that flow.
"But those are valuable reps to get on offense and defense," Campbell added. "And so look, there's an argument to have pulled some guys on defense on that last drive. But I just felt like it was important that our guys play together. It's the best defensive performance we've had to date in 2026, and I wanted those guys to play together. To me, that was important in the moment."
The former NFL tight end has shared in the past about a past game, when he was the interim coach of the Dolphins, where the team let up and starters were forced to go back into the game.
"To go back with what you said about Miami, what happened, we were up huge. We were up three touchdowns, and I think there were eight minutes left and I pulled the starters," Campbell recalled. "And all of a sudden, within a matter of three minutes or whatever, they scored two touchdowns and we couldn't do anything on offense. I had to go and put starters back in the game.
"That's the worst scenario," Campbell continued. "Because now, you hate to say it, but if you're going to do that, your mind, it's different. 'I'm out of the game now' and now you've got to try to get them restarted again. That's not fair to the players. It's not. Right, wrong or indifferent, that's what it was.”

title: One Detroit Lions DE Whose Stock Is Rising
full_text:
Detroit Lions defensive end DJ Wonnum has been a welcome addition to the defensive line. A recent stretch of solid play has the veteran defender trending in the right direction, especially after a solid outing in Week 5 against the Arizona Cardinals.
Wonnum, a free-agent acquisition of Brad Holmes and the Lions this past offseason, recorded two sacks and three total pressures in the winning effort. And for his performance, he earned a 67.4 Pro Football Focus pass-rush grade, including a season-best 69.6 overall mark.
Additionally, he logged a sack, a couple of pressures and a season-high PFF pass-rush grade of 76.5 in Week 4 against his former team: the Carolina Panthers.
Furthermore, Wonnum possesses five sacks through five games, tied for fourth-most in the NFL and two more than he generated all of last season.
And his pass-rush grade for the 2026 campaign now stands at 65.5, ranking 43rd among 106 qualified EDGE defenders.
Slowly but surely, he's been proving his worth as a pass-rusher; in the process, he's provided a much-needed boost to Detroit's pass-rush unit over the last couple of weeks.
“He’s playing at a high level,” Lions head man Dan Campbell said of the veteran EDGE on 97.1 The Ticket. “I thought he really bounced back from last week. He played really well in the run and certainly in the pass game. He’s creating issues opposite of Hutch (Aidan Hutchinson). And man, he keeps doing that, with the firepower we have on that D-line, and you become very dangerous.”
Quite notably, Wonnum has also provided the Lions with a solid EDGE complement to Hutchinson. And the former Michigan sack artist, who has four sacks to his name so far this season, has certainly taken notice.
“Yeah, I love it,” Hutchinson said of his pass-rushing counterpart. “It's great, because if I get more attention during the game and he's winning his one-on-one's, then teams look at that and go, 'Maybe we don't send the slide here every time. Maybe we gotta switch it up.' So to me, it's a win-win all the way around. We just gotta keep rushing like that and keep playing fast.”

title: Detroit Lions 2026 First Quarter Grades: Offense
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have had plenty of success offensively early in the 2026 season.
Through five games, the Lions rank sixth in yards per game (393.8) and tied-for-first in points (32.8) under first-year coordinator Drew Petzing. While they've had to deal with some slow starts, the group has proven to be just as explosive as in years past.
Moving forward, putting forth more consistency in this area will be key to the team reaching its goals of contending for another division title.
Here are grades for each Lions offensive position group for their performance in the first five games of the 2026 season.
Through five games, Jared Goff has been playing at a very high level. He remains without a turnover, and became the second quarterback ever to have at least 12 touchdown passes and zero interceptions through five games.
While Goff hasn't had many explosive throws, he's done exactly what he's done best in Detroit. He pilots the offense efficiently, and has distributed the ball amongst his plethora of playmakers across the board.
The veteran has had some issues with sacks, as he's been sacked 11 times through five games. Some of this deals with his overall lack of mobility, which has been a drawback throughout his career.
Still, Goff remains one of the top performing passers in the league through the first quarter of the season and could be in line for another big year.
Jahmyr Gibbs has been electric for the better part of his first season as the team's true bell-cow running back. He has two games of over 150 rushing yards, including last week against the Cardinals, and just passed Barry Sanders for the most touchdowns by a player under 25 years old.
Gibbs also has 27 receptions already, which puts him on pace for a career-high in that category. He has proven to be a reliable option in the short game, which allows the offense to continue to stay ahead of the chains.
With Isiah Pacheco on injured reserve, the second running back role has belonged exclusively to Sione Vaki. Though it hasn't resulted in many opportunities, as he's carried the ball 15 times for 51 yards, it's the closest to an extended look that Vaki has gotten in three NFL seasons.
Pass protection also remains an area of concern, as the two backs have been inconsistent in this area. However, both appear to be improving and capable of handling the workload that comes with the position.
Amon-Ra St. Brown leads the NFL in targets through five weeks with 57, and is tied-for-fourth in receptions with 37. The USC product has been consistently utilized heavily throughout his time in Detroit, and the start of the season has been no different.
It was a quiet start to the season for Jameson Williams and Isaac TeSlaa, but both have put together strong games in recent weeks. Williams scored his first two touchdowns of the season last week, and had his first 100-yard game of the season the week.
TeSlaa, meanwhile, had just two catches in the first two weeks before delivering some big moments in weeks 3 and 4. He didn't have a catch last week, but adds another threat in the passing game.
One area of concern that the team has is their depth, as Tom Kennedy is expected to be out for the season with an MCL injury. Tay Martin is the only other option on the active roster, so Detroit could look to the practice squad for more depth moving forward.
Sam LaPorta has had a strong start to the season with 27 catches and three touchdowns. There's been some lingering drama off the field regarding his contract, but on the field he appears to be in top form.
LaPorta has anchored the run game with his blocking ability as well, performing well in this aspect of the game as well.
However, the backup option hasn't been as good as Brock Wright has struggled up to this point. The third spot has been revolving, as Tyler Conklin has been active in the role for three games while Jackson Meeks has been active for two.
The Lions' new-look offensive line has yielded some good returns. The biggest piece has been rookie Blake Miller, who has started four games and allowed nine total pressures in that span. While he has taken some lumps, returns have been overall encouraging regarding his performance up to this point.
Penei Sewell has been advertised amidst his change from right to left tackle. Meanwhile, they've gotten good performances from their interior line with guards Christian Mahogany and Tate Ratledge and center Juice Scruggs.
Change could be coming to the group, as Cade Mays is set to return in the near future from a training camp wrist injury. It remains to be seen what fallout that will have on the group, as Scruggs could slide over to left guard but it won't be easy for the team to move away from Mahogany.

title: (Bell-Ringing) Endorsement Speaks Volumes for Packers TE Mark Redman
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich delivered a ringing endorsement for tight end Mark Redman.
Or, perhaps it was a bell-ringing endorsement.
“He’s kind of messed up in the head,” Stenavich said on Tuesday.
Redman smiled when relayed the quote after Wednesday’s practice.
“My wife sent me a picture of that tweet from somebody the other day,” he said. “Isn’t everyone a little messed up in the head? Aren’t we all a little weird in our own sense?”
Football is played by big, tough, athletic men who seek and embrace the contact that almost everyone else in society would prefer to duck. Redman, who was acquired in a trade at the end of training camp, has found his niche as the team’s tough-guy blocker.
Most of the team’s big running plays have featured the 258-pound Redman sprinting across the formation and delivering a jarring blow against a defender with similar size and strength.
“Literally, I was just thinking about that a minute ago, you’re paid to play a sport where sometimes it takes running full speed at another grown man who’s 250 pounds, and yeah, I think logically you would say, ‘Don’t do that,’” Redman said.
“But that’s part of the job description, and honestly, it’s fun for me. It’s the challenges that not everyone can do in this game, in this league. So, when your number’s called and you’re asked to do that – absolutely, whatever it takes. Maybe that’s the one that bounces MarShawn (Lloyd) or Kaleb (Johnson) or any of the guys for a 20-yard gain. So, if that’s how I can play and help support the team, then I’ll do whatever they ask me.”
Among Redman’s greatest hits were the two biggest runs of the season against Tampa Bay, the first by Chris Brooks …
Here is Mark Redman with a big block against Tampa Bay. The Packers' run game has been poor overall but he's been really good and sprung some big runs with these in-motion blocks. pic.twitter.com/9vD5uR9qnH
And the second by Kaleb Johnson …
When the season is over, it will be interesting to see the percentage of explosive running plays by the Packers in which TE Mark Redman is a factor. Here he is leading the charge for Kaleb Johnson. pic.twitter.com/kXfmziZrmL
As well as Pierre Strong’s fourth-and-1 pickup against Chicago …
Mark Redman motions right and has the point-of-attack block on Pierre Strong's fourth-and-1 conversion. pic.twitter.com/UBJkisHmzM
And MarShawn Lloyd’s walk-in touchdown against Chicago.
Mark Redman motions left and serves up a pancake on MarShawn Lloyd's walk-in touchdown. pic.twitter.com/jrEhONocJX
On all four runs, Redman sprinted across the formation and inserted himself as the point-of-attack blocker.
“Yeah, he definitely is” giving the Packers a different look than their past tight ends, Stenavich said on Tuesday. “You definitely need guys like him to run our offense. He’s a versatile player, he’s intelligent. You can move him around. He’s physical. He’s kind of messed up in the head. So, it’s good.
“He’s a physical player, and he loves that part of the game, which is awesome. So, he’s one of my favorite guys I see every day. He’s got a smile on his face. He’s excited. He’s ready to go. So, it’s been really fun to have him. Picking him up was a good pickup, for sure.”
The Packers never addressed the role of a blocking tight end during the offseason. So, with the Packers having an obvious need and the Rams having an obvious surplus, general manager Brian Gutekunst sent a 2028 seventh-round pick to Los Angeles at the end of the preseason.
“Yeah, I love it. We can’t have enough of those guys,” coach Matt LaFleur said of Redman’s mentality. “Physicality is part of our game and in order to be physical, you better have the right mindset. He’s a fearless guy that will throw his body in there, and he’s been doing a great job for us, and I’m really glad we have him.”
And Redman is glad to be here. He went undrafted in 2025 and spent his rookie season on the Rams’ practice squad. With the Rams, there was no pathway to playing time. With the Packers, he’s been a staple of the offense. In five games, he’s played more than 20 snaps in four.
“It’s just a mentality/mindset type thing of someone’s got to do this, so why not it be me?” he said. “Pop the big ones, and it’s really fun. Kaleb popped that one against Tampa Bay. I think you can see me on film, kind of hooting and hollering and pointing. It’s really fun to see that hard work and doing some of the dirty stuff, see it pay off, and spring a big one for 20 or 30.
Redman has two receptions for 29, with both passing-game targets coming in the win at Tampa Bay.
The 25-yard catch against Tampa Bay was exciting, but he knows his role is to make big blocks more than it is to make big catches.
“Everyone wants the big spotlight and shine,” he said. “If I could go for 1,000 yards, I would do that — absolutely. But you’ve got to play to the best of your ability, and everyone wants to get paid at the end of the day and be the greatest player of themselves.
“But, at the end of the day, it comes down to winning, too. If you’re on a winning team and you keep winning and keep winning, go to the playoffs, make it to the championship, make it to the Super Bowl, you’re going to get noticed that way. So, whether it’s 100 yards that you catch for or none, and you spring 10 runs with great blocks. As long as you win at the end of the day, I think that’s kind of the main thing here, and then everyone will see that on tape, too.”
It’s been a rewarding start to Redman’s career in Green Bay. The Packers believed in him, obviously. So did his wife, Jenna. After not playing in a game since his final season of college at Louisville in 2024, he’s become a vital part of a team that looks like a playoff contender heading into Sunday night’s home game against the Dallas Cowboys.
“It’s awesome being on the other side of things,” he said. “I was on the practice squad last year, and just being able to play and kind of showcase your talents [has been great]. My wife’s my biggest sporter. She’s like, ‘I knew you could do it. I knew you could make it.’ So just doing that, and putting your head down and grinding and, like I said before, it’s whether you catch five balls for 100 yards or you just spring a couple big blocks, or you’re on special teams if you’re winning, you’re going to get noticed.
“So, that’s kind of what it is to me. The Tampa game was fun, obviously, but the Chicago game, (I) didn’t get passed to at all, and who cares? I mean, we blew them out. That was really fun too. So, as long as you’re winning and putting out more points on the other team, that’s all I really care about.”

title: Packers-Cowboys Thursday Injury Report: (Really) Big Help on the Way
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers needed to beef up their run defense last season. So, they grabbed 6-foot-5, 338-pound Jordon Riley off the Giants’ practice squad.
Riley impressed in four games with Green Bay but suffered a torn Achilles during the Week 17 game against Baltimore. Now, with veteran Javon Hargrave having suffered a torn Achilles last week, the timing of Riley’s comeback could hardly be better.
Riley was designated for return from the PUP list on Wednesday and went through his second practice on Thursday. While he probably will need more than one week of practice, he will be a huge asset – literally and figuratively – whenever he’s cleared for game action.
“Definitely rusty,” he said after being limited participation at practice. “Just trying to knock the rust off. We got a saying, ‘Got to vs. get to.’ I get to get coached. I get to get those reps in practice, which are very expensive, as I like to say, expensive reps. So, I take those very seriously and it's been good. I’m good physically. No sores or aches. I’m just in a good spot. Taking it day by day at a time.”
Riley was a seventh-round pick by the Giants in 2023. He played in eight games as a rookie and 13 games (with five starts) in 2024. He didn’t make their roster in 2025 but joined the Packers on Dec. 3.
It was a career-changing move. Imagine going from the practice squad of one of the worst teams in the NFL to the active roster of a Super Bowl contender.
And then, it was all taken away from him.
“Man, it sucks, but it’s part of the business,” he said. “It’s part of the game we play. We love to play. You can’t really be so stuck on the past. You just got to continue to look forward, so when it happened, I just knew I’m going to recover from an Achilles injury. Few seconds to get down a little bit, but after that’s over, the emotion’s over, I told myself I’m going to return from an Achilles injury.”
The Packers need help on the defensive line. It was one of their strongest positions coming out of training camp but Warren Brinson is on injured reserve and he’ll soon be joined by Hargrave. That leaves the Packers with only five players at a position group in which coordinator Jonathan Gannon prefers to rotate players in and out of the lineup.
“That is above me,” he said of his potential return. “I just stick on one day at a time. Today, we had padded practice, so that’s what my focus was on – padded practice today. No really looking forward; just taking it each day at a time.”
Cornerback Keisean Nixon and defensive tackle Jonathan Ford did not practice on Wednesday. Nixon returned on Thursday and was limited participation. Coach Matt LaFleur before practice said “I would expect (Ford) to be out there today,” but, while he went through the pre-practice warmup, he officially did not practice.
Their importance for Sunday night can’t be overstated .
Nixon, who is having a strong season, is a key part in a Packers secondary that must contend with Dak Prescott throwing passes to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Plus, veteran cornerback Benjamin St-Juste missed a second consecutive practice with a hamstring injury.
Ford, who has played in all five games with one start, could be in for a heavier workload following Javon Hargrave’s torn Achilles if healthy. He’s averaged 23 snaps per game. If he can’t play and Riley isn’t ready, the Packers would have only four defensive tackles available.
Nixon and safety Evan Williams (illness), who went from limited participation on Wednesday to full participation on Thursday, were the only changes.
St-Juste, Ford, Hargrave and receiver/returner Skyy Moore (ankle) did not practice.
For the Cowboys, only one starter did not practice on Wednesday due to injury. That was linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who missed the last four games with a hamstring injury. He progressed to limited participation on Thursday.
Ageless pass rusher Von Miller got a rest day on Wednesday and was full participation on Thursday.
Only cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and offensive tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring) did not practice for Dallas, which is coming off a Thursday night game so is well-rested.

title: Packers Thursday Update From Practice: Two Texas-Sized Sighs of Relief
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers walked onto the practice field on Wednesday with two enormous question marks on defense.
Twenty-four hours later, their outlook has brightened at both.
At cornerback, starting cornerback Keisean Nixon returned to practice after, as coach Matt LaFleur put it, Nixon “was feeling a little something in his groin” on Wednesday so got the day off.
There’s no doubting Nixon’s toughness. This is his fifth season with the team and he hasn’t missed a game. He started all 17 games last season.
This season, he’s allowing only 8.7 yards per reception, 5.4 yards per target, and a 65.3 passer rating according to Stathead. Those are big improvements over 11.6 yards per catch, 7.5 yards per target and a 105.1 passer rating last season.
At defensive tackle, Jonathan Ford didn’t practice on Wednesday because of a calf injury but returned to the field on Thursday.
The availability of both players will be critical for the Packers against the high-powered Cowboys.
At cornerback, Benjamin St-Juste missed most of last week’s game with a hamstring injury and has not practiced this week. Dallas’ offense, of course, features quarterback Dak Prescott and the elite receiver duo of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. It would be huge for the Packers to have their starting corners, Nixon and Brandon Cisse, available.
At defensive tackle, Warren Brinson is on injured reserve and Javon Hargrave will land there following last week’s torn Achilles. Plus, first-year player Anthony Campbell is coming off an ankle injury that sidelined him the past three weeks.
Not practicing today: CB Benjamin St-Juste WR Skyy Moore DT Javon Hargrave Returning: CB Keisean Nixon DT Jonathan Ford Here is Savion Williams. pic.twitter.com/PnuV85FI3W
Five players didn’t practice on Wednesday. With the returns of Nixon and Ford, that was down to three on Thursday as the team practiced inside the Don Hutson Center because of the rain. Along with Hargrave and St-Juste, the only other player who didn’t practice was receiver/returner Skyy Moore.
Practicing again as their return-to-play windows have been opened were receiver Savion Williams, who’s in his second week of practice, and defensive tackle Jordon Riley, who returned this week.
Riley’s return will be important considering the absence of Hargrave and Brinson.
“I think he can do a lot of things,” coach Matt LaFleur said before practice. “I thought he played good football for us last year. Watching him and getting him back out on the practice field was great to see. This guy’s worked his tail off with our trainers, with our strength staff and really put himself in a pretty good position.”
At receiver, the Packers lost Jayden Reed early in the season and now Moore is out. That could mean more opportunities for J. Michael Sturdivant, the undrafted rookie whose first career touchdown last week was nullified by pass interference.
“We talk about it all the time – next-man-up mentality,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “I think for J-Mike, and we always say this, but for rookies it’s just how fast can you continue to evolve and learn from mistakes and learn from everything that happens in the game and learn from other people’s reps. There’s just so much put on you as a rookie.
“Another guy that hasn’t got too many reps with the 1s and now injuries, things like that happen, now he’s put in that role. I think he’s done a great job so far.
Cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who was acquired by the Cowboys in a trade with Pittsburgh a couple weeks ago, didn’t play in last week’s loss to Tampa Bay due to illness.
“On my way to the game, I was throwing up outside of my Uber,” he told DallasCowboys.com . “It was brutal. I'm not going to lie. … You go into the week thinking you're going to get more of a workload, and you're ready to go, and then that's ultimately what doesn't happen.
“It was very frustrating. I was prepared to play all week. My mindset was on playing, the mindset was to get the dub and, obviously, I didn't get to do that and we didn't get the dub. I was pretty pissed.”
Porter is past his illness and expects to be in the starting lineup on Sunday night.
The teams will file new injury reports after their Thursday practices. For now, here are the reports from Wednesday.

Riley and Savion Williams have been designated to return from injured reserve and are within their 21-day practice windows.

title: Packers’ Christian Watson Blazing Pace That’s Second to None in NFL History
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – In five games, Green Bay Packers receiver Christian Watson has 474 receiving yards and six touchdowns.
It’s a small sample size, but not so small as to render the statistical projections completely useless. If Watson were to keep up that production over 17 games, he’d finish with 1,612 receiving yards and 20 touchdown catches.
That season has never been accomplished in NFL history.
In fact, even if you dial it back a bit, no player has ever reached 1,500 receiving yards and 18 touchdown catches in a season. Only five players have had 18-plus touchdown receptions in a season, with Davante Adams the most recent in 2020. From that quintet, Randy Moss’s 1,493 yards and NFL-record 23 touchdowns is the best season.
After practice on Wednesday, with the Packers getting ready for Sunday’s game against the Dallas Cowboys, Watson was asked about being mentioned in the same breath as Moss and Jerry Rice.
“It definitely motivates me to keep going, but I’m trying to continue to be the best version of myself,” he said. “I want to look back at the end of the season and be able to have those same comparisons rather than looking at it during the season.”
Watson is off to an incredible start to the season, bookended by six catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns in the opener at Minnesota and six catches for 143 yards and two touchdowns against Chicago on Sunday.
This is the fourth season together for Watson and Love. They’ve never connected for more than the six touchdowns that Watson has already.
“I think he’s just playing at a high level right now,” Love said on Wednesday. “He’s making plays. We know what type of speed Christian has – everybody knows what. He’s making plays when the ball is in his hands. Like that [second] touchdown catch he had [against Chicago], he’s making contested catches. That’s the area that everybody’s talked about, growth, and he’s been making huge strides in that area.”
Of the 56 receivers who have run at least 20 routes, Watson is fourth with a passer rating when targeted of 139.7 and sixth with 2.86 yards per route, according to Pro Football Focus. He’s caught 8-of-12 contested-catch opportunities, with the 66.7 percent success rate tied for 12th.
He’s third with 11.9 yards per target. The players ahead of him are Atlanta’s Drake London, who has zero touchdowns, and Baltimore’s Zay Flowers, who has two.
Obviously, Watson has elite physical tools. The growth has come through experience – he’s turned himself into a complete receiver and not just a deep threat – and the additional opportunities that have come through health and the evolving depth chart.
“I think he’s just a consistent player for us right now,” Love said. “He’s in the right spots, both the passing game, the run game. He knows what to do, he’s been in the system for a while and he’s a smart guy. So, now it’s just seeing how far we can take this thing with me and him and our connection.
“Really, for me, it’s just fun to watch. When you’ve got a guy that you can get on any route, you never know, he can take it to the crib at any time. For me, it’s finding ways to continue getting him the ball, putting him in great places and just keep letting him succeed and go do what he does.”
The interesting line there was Love saying “how far we can take this thing.” Does that mean they can be even more productive?
“Oh, yeah, for sure,” Love said.
“There’s more out there,” he said with a smile. “There’s more out there. There’s always more out there.”
“There's definitely more. Honestly, I could probably look back at the game and go back and say there's five plays. whether it be run game or pass play, that I wish I would have been better on or executed better,” he said.
“There’s always ways to still learn and grow from stuff. Even when you have success, there’s still things that we left out there that we want to have back. Obviously, perfection is almost impossible, but we’re still always trying to chase that. So, just finding ways to still clean things up and not leave anything out there.”
Green Bay’s single-season records are 1,553 yards by Davante Adams in 2021 and 18 touchdowns by Adams in 2020 and Sterling Sharpe in 1994. The only season of 1,400 yards and 14 touchdowns was Antonio Freeman’s 1,424 yards and 14 scores in 1998.
“I think he’s getting more opportunities,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “I think he’s done a great job of coming in – he’s always been in shape but he’s been able to stay on the field. Certainly, that’s something that we’ve challenged him. Like, ‘Hey, man, I know you run a lot of these deep routes but we need you in there as much as humanly possible,’ and he’s answered the bell. I think you’re seeing the growth of a player.
“For all these guys, the more they play, usually the better they get.”
While Seattle’s Jaxon Smith-Njigba is having an even better season than Watson – he’s fourth with 37 receptions and first with 583 yards and seven touchdowns – Watson among players with 20-plus catches is No. 1 with 18.2 yards per catch. Watson is the only player with more than 16.5 yards per catch and at least one touchdown.
“I think I’m right where I’m at but, obviously, I’ve got to keep on climbing,” he said after the game. “There’s a lot of individual goals I want to achieve, but I’ve got to keep on doing what I’m doing if we want to have success as a team. Obviously, they’re relying on me a lot, so I’ve got to keep on doing what I’m doing to obviously get the team the best chance to continue winning.”

title: Packers-Cowboys Wednesday Injury Report: Two Enormous Problems Emerge
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have some potentially significant injury issues ahead of Sunday night’s home game against the Dallas Cowboys.
First, it’s the state of the defensive line. With Warren Brinson on injured reserve and Javon Hargrave headed to injured reserve, the Packers have only five available defensive tackles on the roster.
However, the starting nose tackle, Jonathan Ford, didn’t practice on Wednesday due to a calf injury. Following Hargrave’s Achilles injury against Chicago, Ford would have been in line for a considerable bump in playing time.
Plus, starter Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and backup Anthony Campbell (ankle) were limited participation. Campbell missed the last three games but will be counted on to help pick up the slack.
At least Jordon Riley was designated for return following last year’s torn Achilles. The Packers almost certainly will give him more than one week to get ready, though, following a major injury.
“We’ll work that throughout the course of the week,” LaFleur said of Campbell. “If he’s ready to go, he’ll be in there; if not, we’ll have to get somebody else ready to play.”
The Packers really don’t have anyone else, though, with undrafted rookie David Blay the only player on the practice squad.
The surprise absence at Wednesday’s practice was starting cornerback Keisean Nixon. Nixon, who is off to a strong start to the season, was sidelined by a groin injury. He played the first 58 minutes against the Bears before joining some starters on the bench after the 2-minute warning.
Of course, it’s too early to rule out Nixon. He signed with the Packers in 2022 and has played in all 73 games.
Combined with Benjamin St-Juste sitting out practice due to the hamstring injury sustained on special teams against Chicago, the Packers might have to roll with rookie Brandon Cisse and veteran Carrington Valentine against the Cowboys’ high-powered passing game of quarterback Dak Prescott and receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
“Well, I think it all starts with the quarterback,” Packers coach Matt LaFleur said before Wednesday’s practice. “He’s a baller. But then you’ve got two wideouts – really multiple wideouts that can make big-time plays – but obviously the two stars. You’ve got a tight end [Jake Ferguson] that’s a really good player, a running back [Javonte Williams] that’s a really good player.
“I think all those, just the whole collection of them, I think Schotty [Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer] does a really good job as an offensive coordinator. So, it’s a great a challenge.
Ford, Hargrave, Nixon, St-Juste and receiver/returner Skyy Moore (ankle) were the five players who did not practice.
Left guard Aaron Banks, who has missed the last three games after dropping out at halftime of the Week 2 game of the Jets, was limited participation.
What will the Packers do at that position considering Laken Tomlinson has played well? LaFleur called it a “fluid” situation.
“Just trusting the process, trusting my training in the offseason,” Tomlinson said of his first two games. “I did have that surgery in February and got healed up from that, but just trusting the process, trusting my training and I knew I still had it in me and I wanted to give that a legit shot.
“I trained my tail off this past offseason and watching film, doing anything I can, gained like 10 extra pounds of body mass, just give myself the best shot. Fortunate enough to have the opportunity here.”
With Dallas coming off a Thursday game, it is in pretty good shape. While 12 players are listed on the initial injury report, six of those players are full participation. That includes premier receiver CeeDee Lamb (thigh) and two starting offensive linemen, left tackle Tyler Guyton (back) and left guard Tyler Smith (thumb).
Cornerback Joey Porter, who allegedly was plagued by a back injury while with the Steelers, was limited participation on Wednesday with an ankle injury.

title: Packers Wednesday Update From Practice: Help Arrives in Nick of Time
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers felt so good about their defensive tackles during training camp that they took seven into the regular season.
Attrition, however, has been cruel. Warren Brinson missed the start of the regular season with a calf injury, returned to practice and promptly suffered a groin injury that sent him to injured reserve. Next, productive veteran Javon Hargrave suffered a torn Achilles during the waning moments of Sunday’s win over Chicago.
That leaves the Packers with five players. One of them, Anthony Campbell, went undrafted in 2025, suffered an ankle injury in his NFL debut in Week 2 against the Jets and missed the last three games.
Fortunately for the Packers, help is on the way. Jordon Riley has been designated for return from the physically unable to perform list.
The Packers grabbed Riley off the Giants’ practice squad late last season to help with the run defense. He was an immediate asset but suffered a torn Achilles in his fourth game with the team.
In the NFL, it’s funny how things work out sometimes in terms of depth and injuries. Headed into the season, the Packers seemed to have one of those good-problems-to-have with the glut of talented defensive tackles.
Injuries, however, intervened. Now, the Packers are short on defensive tackles. There’s timing. And then there’s perfect timing. Riley’s return could hardly have come at a better time.
Really, the only way the timing could have been better would have been for him to be a couple weeks into his comeback so he could play against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night. It’s hard to believe the Packers would allow Riley to play after just one week of practice, but better late than never.
“He was here all summer long with our trainers and our strength staff. I don’t want to speak for anybody, but it appears to me he’s ahead of schedule and he will be a big bonus for us,” coach Matt LaFleur said during training camp.
“I thought he did a really nice job. He’s come in here, he’s been a great teammate – and that’s paramount. I think he’s really fit into what we do here. So, I’m excited for when he does come back.”
Riley was a seventh-round pick by the Giants in 2023. He played in 21 games during his first two seasons with them, including five starts in 2024.
He’s listed as 6-foot-5 and 338 pounds.
“Just stopping the run,” he said of what he’d add to the team when he joined the Packers last season. “We got so much talent in the pass rush, but we ain't going to get there if we don't stop the turn. So, I think I'll come in just stopping the run, making it my priority to stop the run, and then, obviously, first-, second-down pass, if that comes then making my rushes to go get a sack.
“But at the end of the day I feel like they brought me in to come stop the run. Like help out on that end and then let our edge rushers eat.”
Not practicing CB Keisean Nixon CB Benjamin St-Juste WR Skyy Moore DT Javon Hargrave (obviously) DT Jordon Riley has been designated for return. pic.twitter.com/BoVI4c0j9R
Four players were with the rehab group to start practice. That includes starting cornerback Keisean Nixon. He played all but the final eight snaps on Sunday’s win over Chicago, exiting with other players at the 2-minute warning.
Also not practicing were cornerback Benjamin St-Juste and receiver Skyy Moore, who dropped out of the Chicago game with hamstring and ankle injuries, respectively. The fourth player was Hargrave, who will wind up on injured reserve.
Receiver Savion Williams, who was designated for return from injured reserve last week following a preseason ankle injury, was back on the field.
Also practicing on Wednesday after returning on Friday were left guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and guard/center Jacob Monk (quad).
“Yeah, I would say it’s going to be pretty fluid,” LaFleur said of handling Banks, who has played in only one-half of a game this season, given the success of his replacement, Laken Tomlinson. “We’ve got to see where he’s at. He hasn’t practiced in a really long time, and I think those other guys have come in and done a really good job.”
At right guard, the success of Travis Glover the past two weeks appears to have carried over to the start of this week, with Glover getting the early work instead of Kevin Zeitler.
Without Moore, the Packers will have to sort out who will be back to return punts and kickoffs. Against Chicago, star receiver Matthew Golden returned punts and rookie receiver J. Michael Sturdivant joined Matthew Golden on kickoffs.
Given Golden’s production on offense, would the Packers want to risk him in that role?
We’ll kind of work through that through the course of the week,” LaFleur said before practice. “Certainly, MG’s value, he’s so valuable as a wide receiver for us, but it could be a week-to-week thing with that.”
Coming full circle at defensive tackle, the Packers will roll with starters Devonte Wyatt and Karl Brooks, nose tackle Jonathan Ford, rookie Chris McClellan and Campbell.
How much could Campbell reasonably contribute after a long layoff?
“We’ll work that throughout the course of the week,” LaFleur said. “If he’s ready to go, he’ll be in there; if not, we’ll have to get somebody else ready to play.”
There isn’t anyone else, though. Undrafted rookie David Blay is the only player on the practice squad, and he only recently joined the team.
So, would the Packers have to line up with only four against Dallas’ powerful offensive line?
“Potentially,” LaFleur said. But, “That would be less than ideal.”
Five games into their careers, and with a huge test coming up against Dallas, here's how I'd grade each member of the Packers' small-but-mighty draft class. ⬇️ https://t.co/R2hFy6Q1s9
