title: 3 Most Important Things Jaguars' Liam Coen Said About Week 6's Texans Matchup
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The AFC South race is about to heat up.
The Jacksonville Jaguars will kick off the first of six AFC South games this season in Week 6, facing the Houston Texans in the second of their pair of London games. The Texans have long been seen as the greatest theat to the Jaguars in the AFC South, and this battle comes a year after the Jaguars posted their best record against the AFC South in franchise history in 2025 (5-1). The Jaguars split the season series against the Texans last year, and each of their last five games have been decided by one score.
“We had two really tight games against them. Obviously, have a have a tough feeling in our stomachs from the last time we played against these guys," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday from the United Kingdom. "Know that every time that you line up against this team, it's going to be a fight. It's going to be a brawl. That's what's great about football, that's what's great about rivalries, is that you have a level of respect for each other."
So, what are the most important things Coen had to say about the battle in his first remarks on Houston on Wednesday? We break it down below.
The Texans' 1-4 start certainly was not expected by anybody considering most picked the Texans to win the AFC South entering the year. It has instead been the Jaguars who have opened the season on fire with a 4-1 start that, frankly, should be 5-0 were it not for a blown second-half in Denver. The Jaguars are higher across the board in rankings and metrics, but the Jaguars know they can not take this game lightly.
Two of the the five worst games of the Coen-era in terms of offensive EPA/Play came against the Texans last year: the Week 3 17-10 win is the fourth-worst, while the 36-29 loss to the Texans in Week 10 was the worst offensive performance. The mix things up, the Texans now have head coach DeMeco Ryans calling plays on defense instead of defensive coordinator Matt Burke. They had a great game with that set-up against a bad Tennesee Titans team, but it remains to be seen just how much has changed.
“No, it was similar. I mean, they kind of do what they do in a lot of ways. Have historically played a little bit more man coverage against us at times, to kind of take some of the air out, I think, and not give as much free access and challenge us a little bit on the perimeter," Coen said Wednesday. "He calls what they call, what they do. Their whole deal is built on the front, the rush, the way that they fly around and play and their run defense is really good this year right now. They've got a group of guys that have some confidence. Records don't mean anything. We know that in this league and we understand what this team is, what they're about, how they're going to come in and play us. So, this is going to be a test of physical strain, fight, and that's what it's going to be."
Whether the Jaguars' offensive line can hold up against the Texans' front will likely be the biggest storyline of the week, but Coen's comments make it clear that the battle on the outside may be just as important.
It remains to be seen just how large of a role the Texans envision for their new weapon after the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade over the weekend. The Jaguars traded for Jakobi Meyers mid-week last season and he was able to play that Sunday against the Texans, though, so perhaps Harrison will play in some kind of capacity. Harrison was disappointing in Arizona after being a top-five selection, but the Texans are clearly expecting plenty out of him after what they sent to Arizona.
So, how do the Jaguars prepare for a player who has not yet taken a snap for the Texans? Coen addressed that Wednesday, noting that the study has already been done on Harrison and how he may be used in Houston, though there will still be the element of the unknown until the ball actually gets snapped.
“We showed some of Marvin's clips today in terms of what he's been able to do in Arizona, maybe what areas of the field they may try to use him. It's probably going to be hard to get him into a full game plan, but shoot, we did it with Jakobi [WR Jakobi Meyers] last year, and I know Marvin's smart and he works hard," Coen said.
"So, I would imagine that he's going to be a part of their game plan and C.J. and him have a lot of chemistry and history together. There's some unknown to truly how they'll use him, but their system, they kind of run what they do, and they put the guys in positions to make plays and I think Marvin will probably be no different that way.”
The Jaguars have frequently seen Nico Collins have major days against their secondary, and slowing him down has to be the first priority. But the Jaguars can also not overlook Harrison and the impact he might have on the Texans' offense out of the gate.
The Jaguars had some absolutely brutal moments in the red-zone last week. The Jaguars went 0-for-3 on converting red-zone trips to touchdowns, which included two different trips where they had the ball on the Eagles' one-yard line on first down and didn't score. They got outright stopped on the first of those two drives, but the second one included a comedy of errors as false starts and a delay of game doomed the Jaguars before a fourth-down turnover on downs.
It remains to be seen if the Jaguars will run into the same problems on Sunday that they did against the Eagles considering most were self-inflicted. But the Jaguars will have to ensure their operation is much cleaner tis week when the stakes are even higher. Coen noted Wednesday that part of the solution falls on him as a play-caller.
“That was probably one of the louder atmospheres I've been in a while, especially in those critical moments, to where, hey guys, I can help you out with my play call," Coen said.
"Maybe shorten it up, trim the verbiage or call something a little bit more simplified down there where it was in that end zone specifically that got loud, and some of those critical downs. So, I showed the players and coaches a ton of clips of the TV copy, different versions of it to show them, look, we broke the huddle with eight seconds. That's not giving you a chance. That's not giving you guys the best chance to succeed, and that's directly on me."

title: What the Jaguars' Week 5 Win Changed About Its Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- When it comes to the needs facing each NFL squad entering Week 1, few things are written down in stone.
The early-season results can change what a team needs week-to-week, whether because of unexpected winning or losing streaks, injuries, or star players becoming available. Such is the case for the Jacksonville Jaguars in the wake of Week 5 with several weeks to go before the trade deadline.
So, how did the Jaguars' Week 5 win over the Philadelphia Eagles impact the Jaguars and their potential trade deadline plans? We break it down below.
The biggest concern facing the Jaguars right now is undoubtedly the left tackle situation after the injury to Anton Harrison. The Jaguars' starting left tackle was placed on injured reserve Tuesday after being carted off the field with a knee injury in the third-quarter of Week 5, and it still remains to be seen whether is out for a few weeks or out for the entire season. The answer to that question could be what ultimately sets the tone for the Jaguars' trade deadline plans.
“We'll just figure it out when we get back. You guys saw last night that when we get back, he'll have a little procedure; see what it looks like in there. Don't have any new news on what it could really look like until we get in there," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday.
The Jaguars are set to start Walker Little at left tackle against the Houston Texans in Week 6's battle in London, and that easily could be the Jaguars' plan moving forward. But if Little struggles and Harrison is out for the season, the Jaguars might find it worth it to examine the offensive tackle market. This would not have been even close to being a thought before Harrison's injury, but the onus is now on Little (and Cole Van Lanen) to make sure the Jaguars don't have to go that route.
It still feels unlikely that the Jaguars would make a move considering the depth they have with backup offensive linemen Wyatt Milum, Daniel Faalele, and eventually Patrick Mekari, but this is one spot that now at least deserves some consideration when it comes to the trade deadline plans. The Jaguars' offensive line has been up-and-down throughout the 2026 season so far, and we will see starting in Week 6 how the unit responds to Harrison's injury.
"Anytime you lose a player for a game, it's always a challenge, but I have a lot of confidence in Walker [OL Walker Little] and Cole [OL Cole Van Lanen] to go in there. And these guys have played these guys so many times and have had success against them and know what they're in for in terms of the battle and next man up mentality," Coen said.
The next spot to watch is, of course, Brian Thomas Jr. It did not make much sense for the Jaguars to consider moving Thomas in the offseason, but things have changed since then. We already knew that Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers were likely to be ahead of him on the depth chart, but the Jaguars have now also added rookie wide receiver Josh Cameron to the mix and Cameron has out-produced Thomas through five games despite playing a much smaller role.
With Cameron now in place and thriving, perhaps the Jaguars reconsider. Sunday was the first game in Thomas' career that he did not register a catch, and he has just three catches over the last three games. He has become a smaller and smaller part of the offense as the season has gone on, but that does not mean he doesn't offer plenty of value on the trade market if the Jaguars deem him a player they want to move on from.
The Marvin Harrison Jr. trade offers a good baseline for any potential Thomas trade, too. Until we see Thomas as a sustained piece of the Jaguars' offense for an extended period of time, his name is going to continue to come up when it comes to potential trade deadline plans. Thomas is a talented player, but his lack of production mixed with the Jaguars' depth at wide receiver makes this something to watch for the second year in a row.

title: Week 6 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Jaguars Take Over the Consensus Top-5
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are 4-1 entering arguably their biggest week of the season so far, which gives them more and more room to keep rising.
After their 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5, the Jaguars are currently tied with the Buffalo Bills and the Baltimore Ravens for the second-best record in the AFC, behind only the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs. So after their latest win, where do the Jaguars land in the latest power rankings across the NFL? We break it down below.
The only team ranked ahead of the Jaguars are the 49ers, which makes a ton of sense. The Jaguars are clearly a better overall team than the Minnesota Vikings, while the Chiefs are just one spot behind the Jaguars. Jacksonville and the 49ers have been the two best teams this year on a snap-to-snap basis.
These are the rankings the Jaguars have climbed the highest in since Week 1. A win against the Texans in London and entering the bye week with a 5-1 record would likely go a long way to not just keeping the Jaguars in the top-5 for the long-term, but also help them rise higher and higher. The Texans were their preseason AFC South darlings, and the Jaguars can make them eat those words with a win in Week 6 against their AFC South rivals.
I get that the Vikings are undefeated, and they do have a special defense right now. But their offense is still miles away from the Jaguars' offense, and that has to be factored in somehow and in some fashion. The Jaguars' offense has gotten in its own way in the last two weeks, but it is a much better unit right now than Minnesota's is.
The Jaguars have a rightful place in the top-5 here, though the analysis on Liam Coen's fourth down attempts seems off. Coen did not go on multiple red-zone fourth downs last week because of "analytics." His long-snapper was hurt, which led to the Jaguars having to approach each red-zone series with a different outlook.
Three of the four teams ahead of the Jaguars this week are the NFL's three final undefeated teams with the Kansas City Chiefs, San Francisco 49ers, and Minnesota Vikings. The only other team ranked ahead of the Jaguars is the Buffalo Bills on the heels of their overtime win against the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night. The Bills and Josh Allen beat the Jaguars in the wild card a year ago, but the Bills lost to a Patriots team a few weeks ago who the Jaguars destroyed.
The top two undefeated teams are understandably ranked ahead of the Jaguars, but then so are the Seattle Seahawks and Baltimore Ravens. The Jaguars will get their battle with the Ravens later in the season, while the Seahawks lost a close game to the 49ers but also lost to a bad Washington Commanders team earlier in the season. It feels like they should be behind the Jaguars right now.
This is the only ranking that has seen the Jaguars take a step back this week. Part of that is likely due to the fact the Jaguars did not play their best football against the Eagles last week. But it also had the Ravens leapfrogging the Jaguars after their unlikely overtime Sunday Night Football win against the Falcons without Lamar Jackson.
The only two teams above the Jaguars here are the undefeated 49ers and Chiefs. The Jaguars are slotted one spot ahead of the Buffalo Bills, which seems fair. The Bills did beat the Jaguars in the Wild Card last year with mostly the same squads, so it would also be fair to give the Bills an edge. But right now, the Jaguars seem to have played better team football week-to-week

title: ESPN Matchup Predictor Analyzes Chiefs vs. Chargers Divisional Showdown in Week 6
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs should be well-rested coming off their bye , but Andy Reid's squad is getting right back into the action with a divisional matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. It's a classic example of an unstoppable force versus an immovable object: an unbeaten Chiefs team hosting a winless Los Angeles squad desperate for answers.
KC is among the favorites in the AFC to reach the Super Bowl in early projections. Patrick Mahomes is back to his MVP form after tearing his ACL against this same Chargers team a year ago, and the addition of running back Kenneth Walker has transformed the offense into a juggernaut. Can LA turn its campaign around and pull off an upset in Arrowhead Stadium this weekend? Let's take a look at what ESPN's Matchup Predictor says heading into kickoff.
Justin Herbert and Mahomes have had some great battles over the years, though this matchup comes under unusual circumstances. The Chargers haven't started a season 0-5 since the team was still based in San Diego more than 20 years ago.
ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 73.5%, Chargers 26.3%.
Despite their dismal record, the Chargers still have a decent chance of coming out on top Sunday, according to the matchup predictor. For context, before the bye, the computer model only gave the Chiefs a 3.5% greater chance of beating an undefeated Raiders team on the road.
The Chargers are far out of the divisional race and likely out of playoff contention, but Jim Harbaugh's squad isn't as awful as its start suggests. It's hard to imagine a team of this caliber finishing with just four or five wins.
LA suffered inexplicable defeats to the Raiders and Cardinals early in the season. Just when they appeared poised to finally get into the win column last week, the Chargers collapsed in the fourth quarter against fellow AFC West opponent, the Denver Broncos. The matchup predictor gives the Chargers better than a one-in-four chance against KC, suggesting a win may not be too far off the radar for Los Angeles, whether it comes this week or next. The Chargers can't head into November without a single victory... right?
One thing to monitor is the Chiefs' receiving situation, as Tyquan Thornton will be sidelined for an extended period and Rashee Rice is likely to miss the game with a lingering hamstring injury. That means the offense will lean heavily on Walker and Travis Kelce to carry the load.
If the Chargers are going to put up a fight, Herbert has to pick up his play — point-blank, period. It's been a humiliating stretch for someone who is usually considered one of the AFC's best signal-callers, as he's thrown seven interceptions to his five touchdowns in 2026.

title: Chiefs First-Round DT Peter Woods Pops Up on Injury Report Days Before Chargers Game
full_text:
With each passing second, the Kansas City Chiefs are getting closer and closer to their Week 6 showdown at home versus the Los Angeles Chargers. Head coach Andy Reid's crew is hard at work preparing for a bitter division rival to come to down, but the club's injury situation is less than ideal.
Following Thursday's practice, that became even more obvious. In addition to left tackle Josh Simmons and cornerback L'Jarius Sneed being limited and wideout Rashee Rice not participating, another standout player was added to the list.
Per the team on Thursday afternoon, rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods appeared on an updated version of the injury report. The first-round pick is now nursing a neck ailment after not being listed at all on Wednesday when the club had three players (safety Chamarri Conner, fullback Ben VanSumeren and quarterback Patrick Mahomes) deemed full participants.
The silver lining here is there's no reason to worry about Woods just yet. According to Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest , the neck issue is "not considered a big deal."
Two changes on the Chiefs’ injury report for Thursday: * DT Peter Woods (neck) is added to the report as limited. I’m told it’s not considered a big deal, he should be fine. * FB Ben VanSumeren (thumb) no longer listed. pic.twitter.com/enGJAYpdYt
Woods, the No. 29 overall selection out of Clemson, has played 126 defensive snaps thus far, good for 46% of those available. He hasn't made a sizable impact in the box score, amassing nine tackles and a pass deflection. With that said, the athletic interior lineman is credited with one pressure and three "stops" by Pro Football Focus . Tracking is a bit different on NFL Pro , which gives him seven stops in four games.
Simmons continuing to be a limited participant shouldn't surprise anyone. The 2025 first-rounder is coming off a significant back injury and is clearly being eased back into the fold following over a half-dozen weeks off. Sneed being limited with knee management is a non-story.
Rice, who hurt his hamstring in Week 4's triumph over the Las Vegas Raiders, is a player to keep an eye on. Given that he hasn't gotten any work for consecutive days, it's becoming increasingly difficult to see him being active this weekend against Los Angeles. Reid typically prefers noteworthy participation in the final practice of the week, so there's still some hope, but Rice would have to be brought along quickly.
Once Friday's practice is over with, the overarching takeaway could be whether Woods bounces back and receives a full workload.

title: Three Ways Josh Simmons' Eventual Return Can Help Chiefs Moving Forward
full_text:
Despite being 4-0 after their bye week, the Kansas City Chiefs still have plenty of things they can improve on . As the team heads into the middle portion of its 2026 schedule, help appears to be on the way via the eventual return of standout left tackle Josh Simmons.
The 2025 first-round pick practiced for the first time since August on Wednesday, albeit in limited capacity. It remains to be seen precisely when the former Ohio State star will make his regular-season debut, but it's bound to boost the club in multiple regards once that happens.
Aside from Simmons himself benefitting from being back in the lineup in the foreseeable future, how could it impact Kansas City? Matt Lane and Craig Stout discussed that and more on an October episode of the KC Laboratory podcast on KC Sports Network .
For as promising as Simmons was when playing as a rookie, it's important to remember that the jury is still technically out on him at least a bit. The 32nd overall NFL Draft selection played 94% of available snaps in contests he appeared in, although that overall number saw him active for just eight weeks. He missed time due to a wrist injury and a personal matter, so he isn't exactly the most dependable piece on the roster.
Simmons flashed both good and bad in his debut campaign for the Chiefs. According to Pro Football Focus , his 75.4 pass blocking grade and 18 pressures surrendered on 337 opportunities (5.3%) were sparkling. On the flip side, he struggled with power rushers at times and also earned just a 48.1 run blocking mark from the outlet.
Coming into year No. 2, Simmons outlined his ideal playing weight and goals. It isn't too late for him to still provide hundreds of meaningful reps the rest of the way, but time is certainly ticking for him to prove he's indeed a franchise cornerstone and long-term blind-side protector for quarterback Patrick Mahomes.
Not having the left tackle you planned for can knock any offense off track a bit. The Chiefs have done a fantastic job of navigating life minus Simmons to start the year, but each week shows more and more why he's so important to the sustainability of the attack. In order to string together multiple postseason wins, explosive passes and deeper-developing concepts simply must be staples to make life easier on Mahomes and to threaten defenses.
To this point, per TruMedia , Kansas City has the third-highest share of passes at or behind the line of scrimmage at 32.0%. It's also in the bottom 10 in average yards to the sticks at -1.6, as well as in the top 10 in percentage of throws faster than 2.5 seconds (44.5%). A quick-game passing attack isn't fun for anyone and, more importantly, it leaves infinitely less margin for error. Just ask the 2024 and 2025 Chiefs.
Losing wide receiver Tyquan Thornton to an ankle injury hurts, surely, but the return of Simmons figures to potentially unleash the version of the Kansas City offense that was imagined during training camp.
Just like the reintroduction of any other starting-level player, it pushes everyone else at the position down a rung on the proverbial ladder. For Kansas City, that means undrafted rookie tackle Kahlil Benson either moves to a swing role or overtakes veteran Jaylon Moore for the first-string gig on the right side. The latter is something that many predicted as the offseason program and camp passed — could it become a reality once Simmons is active?
PFF credits Benson with a 44.0 pass blocking grade, a 75.1 run blocking grade and 10 pressures in 143 opportunities (7.0%). Moore's respective grades are 61.1 and 64.1, and his pressure number is eight in 142 chances (5.6%).
During the Week 5 bye, both players were in the top 10 in pressures ceded via FTN 's tracking. Moore's quick pressure rate of 69.2% was downright alarming:
not all pressures are created equal pic.twitter.com/HkagOTdNKc
It isn't like Mahomes is under constant duress; Kansas City's 28.9% pressure rate is the second-lowest in all of football. With that said, the offense is facing the third-lowest share of times blitzed per dropback (24.6%), and it's been discussed how fast the ball is coming out. Simmons and the best right tackle candidate figures to help offset any regression if play calls become more aggressive.

title: Chiefs Preaching 'Trust' Despite Unproven WR Options After Losing Tyquan Thornton
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline still weeks away but a need at the wide receiver position being present right now, the Kansas City Chiefs find themselves in a strange spot. Coming out of a Week 5 bye, Andy Reid's team hasn't made any major additions to boost the ceiling of the room.
Perhaps the acquisition of Justin Watson can elevate the floor, but there's ample reason to be skeptical of such a prospect. The club whiffed on or simply didn't express enough interest in moving for new Houston Texans pass catcher Marvin Harrison Jr., so the in-house options will be rolled with until the next domino falls.
With no Tyquan Thornton on the field for the foreseeable future, who should Kansas City turn to as a long-term replacement? Is it one player or multiple? Speaking to the media on Wednesday, Reid expressed that he has faith in each person on the depth chart.
"That's the way things worked out for Tyquan," Reid said. "He was having a very good year, and I'm sad to see what happened to him because of that. And he's a great kid on top of all that. But one man's loss is another man's opportunity to jump in and do that. Whoever that might be that's got the call, if they make the play, then that's a positive. But I have trust in all the guys, and Xavier (Worthy) is still in there, too. He's coming off a couple of good catches the last couple of games."
Subtracting Thornton from the equation leaves KC with Worthy, Rashee Rice, first-year man Cyrus Allen, second-year man Jalen Royals, Nikko Remigio and Watson as the main non-tight end targets. Complicating things is that Rice suffered a hamstring injury early in Week 4's win over the Las Vegas Raiders and isn't practicing right after the bye . That leaves his status for Week 6 in question, thus underscoring how dire things could be for the Chiefs.
Can a cast of some shaky vets and the intriguing-but-quiet rookie get the job done versus the Los Angeles Chargers this weekend? Quarterback Patrick Mahomes echoed the same sentiment as Reid, saying his message to the Chiefs' wideouts is nothing but belief.
"It's that they're ready," Mahomes said. "They've put in the work. Obviously, we've had guys in front of them with Tyquan going out there playing great football. They've had to put in the work at practice, and they've been doing that and doing that. Now their number gets called, and they're going to step up to the role and do their job. I'm excited for them. We'll put them in positions to succeed. I have a lot of trust in those guys — a lot of confidence in them — so we'll just continue to push it forward."
Through four games, Worthy is tied for the team lead in targets with 22. He tops the wideout collective with 14 receptions, although both Thornton (219) and Rice (190) who have more yards. Royals' stat line is just three catches for 17 yards; Allen has two targets but no receptions on all of 10 offensive snaps.
If Kansas City has a high-scoring offensive output without Thornton and potentially minus Rice, it'll have to stem from someone like Worthy and perhaps an unsung hero stepping up. With the expectation and standard set at practice, Mahomes thinks the depth is prepared.
"It's going to make it easier for them," Mahomes said. "When you're kind of getting thrown in, you never know which position you're going to be at and what route you're going to be on. It's hard. That's part of playing in the NFL, you don't get those reps that you necessarily would've had in college and high school and stuff like that."

title: Josh Simmons Returns to Practice, Rashee Rice's Status Uncertain for Week 6
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs announced a mixed bag of injury news on Wednesday, as two key offensive starters entered Week 6 with injury uncertainty.
Beginning his Wednesday media availability, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid provided an update on wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring) and left tackle Josh Simmons (back).
"As far as the injuries go, Rashee will be the only one that doesn't go today," Reid said. "Everybody else is scheduled to do something."
Reid's statement means that Simmons will return to practice in some capacity on Wednesday, marking his first return to the field since mid-August, when he suffered a back injury late in training camp .
On September 30, Reid explained that Simmons has been dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back, which had "kind of hindered the strength of his leg," according to Reid.
On Wednesday, Reid clarified that Simmons still has some hurdles to clear before fully returning.
"We're just gonna ease him back in," Reid said. "Ease him into practice. He's gonna practice, but it'll be on a limited basis."
In Simmons' absence, undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has played left tackle, while veteran Jaylon Moore has remained on the right side. Reid was asked what the plan would be at right tackle when Simmons returns.
"I haven't even gone there," Reid said. "I'm just glad that [Simmons] is having a chance to come back, for sure. You start dealing with backs, you've got to ease it back in if you can get back in at all, so we'll just see how he does. So I haven't really even gone there. I know [Simmons] has wanted to get back out there, and this is the first step of that."
Rice exited the Chiefs' Week 4 matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders due to a hamstring injury that ultimately sidelined him for the rest of the game.
On Wednesday, Reid was asked if he anticipated Rice returning to practice later this week
"We'll see how it goes," Reid said. "He's actually feeling pretty good as he goes here, so we'll see. Those things, you start dealing with hamstrings, and it could be a week, could be two weeks, you don't know, but I know he's eager to get back in."
The Chiefs are already dealing with one serious injury in the receiver room, as Tyquan Thornton has been placed on injured reserve due to his season-threatening ankle dislocation that he suffered later in the Chiefs' win over the Raiders. As Thornton was placed on IR, the team reunited with veteran receiver Justin Watson , who signed to Kansas City's practice squad.

title: Chiefs On SI Mailbag: Will Cyrus Allen Step Up After Tyquan Thornton's Injury?
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs' bye week is over. Now, focus turns to the Los Angeles Chargers. With the Chiefs undefeated and the Chargers still winless, there's a bizarre undertone to this AFC West showdown. Meanwhile, the Chiefs still have uncertainty at left tackle and wide receiver.
Those are the topics we'll begin with on this edition of the Chiefs On SI mailbag .
What happens first? Cyrus Allen reception or Justin Watson reception? -@ReidsNuggies
I'm completely fine with the Chiefs' decision to reunite with Justin Watson on a practice squad basis, but for the season-long health of the receiver room, Cyrus Allen has to start seeing the field more. While Allen has played just 10 offensive snaps, resulting in two targets and zero catches through his first four weeks of NFL action, I do expect him to see an increased workload on Sunday against the Chargers, and I sure hope that includes his first NFL catch.
I could see Watson's role landing in any number of places. It wouldn't surprise me if Watson doesn't see the field for another week or two as he reacclimates to the offense, and it wouldn't surprise me if he took a decent handful of snaps on Sunday as a de facto decoy to keep LA's safeties honest as a theoretical deep threat.
My expectations for Allen's timeline have always been measured—rookie receivers have a learning curve in Andy Reid's offense—but a well-timed bye should help him add a few responsibilities to his plate.
The obvious part about Allen's potential involvement is that the Chiefs simply need one of their receivers to take more reps in Tyquan Thornton's absence. The exciting part is that Allen has the potential to provide much more than a handful of adequate snaps.
Is it Cyrus Allen time in KC? ⏰👀 pic.twitter.com/edTcQOI7Nn
On 3rd and long, what 11 defenders do you want on the field to get the stop? -@youjustreadmym1
This is a great question to cut through some of the challenges of picking favorites (and least-favorites) in a defensive rotation. Some of these picks are easy, some are toss-ups.
George Karlaftis and Chris Jones have to be on the defensive line. I'll leave Jones in the interior, with R Mason Thomas on the other edge. I'm still very bullish on Peter Woods, but right now... Felix Anudike-Uzomah as an interior pass rusher has been one of the more interesting developments of the season! Throw Anudike-Uzomah inside, next to Jones.
I'd be tempted to roll with only one linebacker, but having both Nick Bolton and Drue Tranquill seems almost mandatory, even though Tranquill may be playing better than Bolton so far this year .
That leaves me with five defensive backs: Mansoor Delane, Nohl Williams, Chamarri Conner, Alohi Gilman , and... whoever gives you the best chance in the slot. While L'Jarius Sneed has taken most of those snaps so far this year, I'd be inclined to give Chris Roland-Wallace my final spot against a smaller slot receiver, while Sneed gets the nod in a more physical matchup.
If Josh Simmons doesn’t return anytime soon, what is KC’s plan, and how do they avoid a repeat of the 2024 season? -@jacklerner.bsky.social
I think it's interesting to view the Chiefs' current left tackle situation through the lens of 2024, when the issues on Patrick Mahomes' blindside significantly impacted the offense all the way to the Super Bowl.
In 2026, the Chiefs have really had their share of issues from both tackle positions, but if Josh Simmons does return soon, KC can pick their choice of Kahlil Benson or Jaylon Moore at right tackle while sending the other to the swing tackle role. Without Simmons, of course, that gets murky.
I'm not surprised that we haven't seen him through the first four weeks, but undrafted rookie Diego Pounds, who the Chiefs acquired from the Baltimore Ravens just before roster cuts , had some very intruiging film from Baltimore's preseason. He's been a pure left tackle, so the idea of putting Pounds on the left side and Benson back at his natural right side does excite me... at least until I remember that would require Mahomes to be protected by a duo of undrafted rookies. That's not ideal, but it is an answer.
I can't see the Chiefs making a significant pre-deadline move to acquire a left tackle unless they have lost all confidence in Simmons in 2026 and beyond, and a tackle as good as Simmons almost certainly won't hit the market anyway. The best version of the Chiefs' offense depends on having Simmons back as soon as possible.
Do you think the Chiefs will be judicious with Kenneth Walker going forward? Will they be wary of keeping him fresh for the playoffs? -@toptrevor.bsky.social | Do you think we will mix Emmett Johnson in more post-bye, and should we? -@oscarbobo.bsky.social
Before the Chiefs' game against the Miami Dolphins, I wrote that it could be Emmett Johnson's time to shine . (He went on to have six carries for 17 yards.) Last week, I wrote that Johnson should be a bigger part of the mix after the bye week —this time, for sure! Ultimately, I understand why it's easier said than done.
The Chiefs have a one-man offensive easy button with Kenneth Walker in the backfield; if the passing game stalls this Sunday against the Chargers, my desire to see Walker's workload lessened will be overtaken by my desire for the Chiefs to, you know, win the game.
I stand by the idea that Johnson has proven enough to show that he can be a worthwhile No. 2 back behind Walker, and the team ideally would take a few hits off Walker's shoulders during the middle act of the season, but they'll need to have more offensive confidence in other areas before that can be put into practice.

title: The Jury Is Still Out on Chiefs' Safety Room Following Bye Week
full_text:
Change was the theme of the offseason for the Kansas City Chiefs' defense, especially in the secondary. It wasn't just the cornerback position that underwent a shakeup, either, as safety Bryan Cook departed for the Cincinnati Bengals and was replaced by Alohi Gilman in free agency.
The acquisition of Gilman, paired with Chamarri Conner returning to his more natural spot in Steve Spagnuolo's lineup, seemed to set the tone for a productive and disruptive pairing. For multiple reasons, however, that hasn't been the case through four games.
Lumping in a roller coaster of a campaign for Jaden Hicks and a limited workload for Chris Roland-Wallace does nothing but further complicate things. The bad news is that things must improve coming out of the bye week, although the good news is there's ample reason to believe that'll happen.
Starting with Gilman, the former Los Angeles Chargers and Baltimore Ravens standout isn't exactly lacking statistically compared to his last couple of seasons. Across Pro Football Reference , Pro Football Focus and NFL Pro 's data, his coverage data averages out to 10 targets and six completions, 8.3 yards per target and a 120.6 passer rating.
He's being tried more often down the field (13.9-yard average depth of target) and performing at his recent — albeit underwhelming — standard, but it's the lack of ball production that's really hurting. One of Gilman's main draws is his ability to make splash plays, evidenced by his 28 career pass breakups, six fumble recoveries, five forced fumbles and five interceptions. Four games in, he's been quiet, which is a concern.
Hicks is hands-down the most frustratingly inconsistent player in this group. In some instances, he flies around the field and looks like a heat-seeking missile who's oozing confidence. In others, though, he's lost in the shuffle, slow to react and ends up totally out of place. He leads the safety collective with eight "stops" on the year, yet it's coming with a unit-worst mark in yards per reception.
The low-key player to keep an eye on is Roland-Wallace, who played 190 defensive snaps in 2025, good for 30% of those available in his 11 games played. This year, that number is 55 (20%), and it's hard to see that share going up too much with Conner back. Roland-Wallace has some corner-safety versatility, so perhaps he occupies some slot snaps (he has 12 right now) in due time.
Conner stands out as quite easily the biggest X-factor here. The fourth-year man is in a contract season but started it on the shelf due to a knee injury that lingered for a while. While he was far from perfect in his regular-season debut in Week 4 versus the Las Vegas Raiders, the former fourth-round pick finished with six tackles and made multiple plays that showcased his quick trigger when running downhill.
There wasn't much of a runway for Conner to ramp up, as he played 63 snaps down in Paradise against the Raiders (75%). If he's back to being an unquestioned starter at safety, he'll form a heavy-involvement duo with Gilman and send someone like Hicks down a rung on the ladder. That may assist the latter man in finding the optimal role for his skill set.
Progress isn't linear, which might be the best way to sum up a group that's flashed some good and bad in the first month of the 2026-27 campaign.

title: Here’s Why Chiefs Rookie Cyrus Allen Could Finally Be Featured in Kansas City’s Offense
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs' bleak wide receiver circumstances worsened before the bye when Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton went down in the same game. While Rice's hamstring issue is minor and shouldn't keep him out long, Thornton will miss most, if not all , of the regular season with a dislocated ankle. Between rumors about a reunion with Tyreek Hill and bringing another proven wideout on board before the trade deadline, KC fans are starved for help in the receiving corps. However, a viable option may be waiting in the wings of the Chiefs' offensive unit.
Remember Cyrus Allen, who quickly transformed into a fan favorite with his strong training camp? There was a time when he looked like he'd be facing an uphill battle for playing time, but a scenario where he assumes a significant role in this offense looks a lot more realistic with the current injury situation.
Allen was selected No. 176 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft and brings plenty of versatility, as he's capable of lining up in the slot or on the outside. He led the Big 12 with 13 touchdowns as a senior, which helped his draft stock skyrocket. A shin bruise during camp slowed Allen's progress and has been cited as a reason why the coaching staff has been hesitant to use him. Before that, though, reporters viewed Allen as perhaps the team's best pass catcher not named Rice or Xavier Worthy.
During the Chiefs' Week 4 win over the Raiders, when the two aforementioned receivers got hurt, Allen only saw the field for five snaps and recorded his first NFL target. That could change now that the coaching staff has a week of preparation to get him more involved.
What Kansas City is truly missing in the receiver room is a playmaker who can make things happen with the ball in his hands. Rice is great in the intermediate game, but he isn't necessarily someone defenses are going to key in on to open things up downfield. And despite Worthy's tremendous straight-line speed, he's been largely ineffective in all areas of the offense in 2026.
Allen generated a lot of buzz in limited preseason action, with the biggest highlight coming on an impressive snag in the exhibition opener. Insiders and other observers have made it clear that he has as much burst and is shiftier than anyone in the short passing game.
When speaking to the media on Monday , head coach Andy Reid mentioned the possibility of Allen seeing increased snaps with Thornton heading to the IR. Those opportunities would only grow if Rice is unable to suit up this week versus the Chargers. "Yeah, I think he would probably work into the mix there a little bit more," Reid said. "He's a good football player, and even though he's young, he's got good ability."
Andy Reid on if rookie WR Cyrus Allen will receive more playing time moving forward: “Yeah, I think he would probably work into the mix there a little bit more. He's a good football player, and even though he's young, he's got good ability.” pic.twitter.com/mMeGf7WVX1
Those words don't necessarily mean Allen is going to see a dozen targets on Sunday, so his biggest supporters should take Reid's comments with a grain of salt. Reid tends to have a level of comfort with the players he trusts to catch passes from Patrick Mahomes, which helps explain why the front office brought two-time Chiefs Super Bowl winner Justin Watson back to the practice squad during the bye.
Depending on Rice's injury status before the upcoming matchup, this could be Allen's biggest chance to earn a consistent role in Eric Bieniemy's offense. If he makes the most of his snaps, even in a limited role, he could earn a bigger place in the game plan moving forward.

title: The Chiefs' Highest-Paid Linebacker Hasn't Been Their Best, and That's Alright
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs rolled into the year with plenty of questions on the defensive side of the ball, especially after an offseason filled with change. That applied to the linebacker position as well, with Leo Chenal departing for the Washington Commanders in free agency and leaving someone else to fill his spot.
With that said, the starting duo of Nick Bolton and Drue Tranquill remained. The former is regarded as the on-field coach and leader of the defense — essentially an extension of coordinator Steve Spagnuolo. The latter, meanwhile, was coming off a couple of down years and took a pay cut to return for what could be one last dance in Kansas City.
Four games into the season, the expectations of many haven't aligned with reality. Bolton and his $19.25 million cap hit have been outplayed by Tranquill and his $5M mark , although that isn't necessarily the end of the world. It's less of an indictment on Bolton and more a praise of Tranquill's performance thus far.
Coverage numbers tend to vary by site, so it's better to paint a picture of a player's output by coming up with an average. After sorting through Pro Football Reference , Pro Football Focus and NFL Pro 's data, the stat line matches the eye test.
Both players combined for an average of 12 targets in the passing game in Weeks 1-4. Bolton surrendered 10.3 completions, 7.0 yards per target and a 103.0 passer rating. Tranquill, on the other hand, ceded 5.3 completions, 5.3 yards per yarget and a passer rating of 60.0. Add in that Bolton's facing the lowest average depth of target of his career (3.1 yards) and Tranquill's is his highest since 2022 (4.8), and you get a pretty clear read.
Tranquill is also faring better as a disruptor in all phases despite Bolton having 22 "stops" to his 18. The 31-year-old maintains an 11.8% pressure rate to his peer's 9.1% figure, along with a 3.3% missed tackle clip to Bolton's 9.8%. There wasn't a much better game to sum up Tranquill's efforts than him terrorizing the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4.
Spagnuolo is using Tranquill in a variety of ways, including lining him up along the defensive line on 36 occasions. The 'backer owns a 27.9% blitz rate, which clears 2025 (24.4%) as his most significant usage in that role as a Chief. Bolton himself admitted back in August that there would "never" be a true replacement for Chenal, but Spagnuolo throwing multiple things at the wall and hoping something sticks seems to be the plan. Tranquill is a part of that attempted solution.
The same can't really be said for Jack Cochrane or Jeffrey Bassa. Neither player is making much of an impact on defense, but Bassa did notch a forced fumble on special teams in Las Vegas. The signing of Cam Jones to the 53-man roster signals that Cooper McDonald isn't ready to return, and Cole Christiansen's game-day elevations from the practice squad are capped. This is a depth chart that's extremely top-heavy entering Week 6.
Bolton enjoyed plenty of plus moments before the bye, but it's Tranquill who's been the plus player at that position to this point. The blend of better-than-expected coverage, relentless attacking in run defense and quality fundamentals as both a tackler and blitzer is tough to argue against. The Chiefs can't ask for much more and should instead simply hope this level of play can be sustained.
If the rest of the linebacker room ascends as well, the Kansas City defense will continue to jell post-bye and down the stretch of the regular season.

title: Why Didn't the Chiefs Trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.?
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs need wide receivers.
After Tyquan Thornton suffered a gruesome ankle injury , the Chiefs made a patchwork move, reuniting with Justin Watson . The Chiefs still need wide receivers, both short-term and long.
Many of my pre-draft opinions revolved around my desire for the Chiefs to use one of their premium picks on a pass catcher. They didn't. Much of this summer's training camp hype cycles belonged to fifth-round rookie Cyrus Allen . So far, he's played fewer offensive snaps than defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga.
Looking to the future, there's just as much uncertainty. The Chiefs' No. 1 receiver, Rashee Rice, is in a contract year. Former first-round pick Xavier Worthy is under contract through 2027, but the Chiefs will need to make a decision regarding his fifth-year option after this season. Thornton is under contract for 2027 with a $7.5 million cap hit.
I would make the argument that the Chiefs' biggest need for the rest of the 2026 season and their biggest need for the next several seasons all revolve around the wide receiver position. Why am I rehashing this opinion in mid-October?
Because even I don't think the Chiefs should have beaten the Houston Texans' bid to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.
To be clear, I was at least somewhat interested in the Chiefs being the "change of scenery" destination for the embattled former No. 4 overall pick, but those delusions were shattered by the reports of what Houston gave up in the deal.
In exchange for Harrison and a 2027 seventh-round pick, the Texans gave up a 2027 second-rounder and a '27 sixth. Essentially, a second-rounder for Harrison and a largely cosmetic late-round pick-swap. Here's the even wilder part: the Texans are 1-4! Right now, that pick would fall at No. 39 overall according to Tankathon . The Texans certainly hope to make a playoff push, but even if they go 8-4 the rest of the way, ending at 9-8 and just outside of the postseason, they'd ultimately be sending a top-50 pick to Arizona in the deal.
From the Cardinals' perspective, that's a worthwhile return. For the 4-0 Chiefs, the apparent only realistic path to Harrison would have included Kansas City's 2027 first-round pick. Even if KC would've gained a mid-round pick from Arizona in this hypothetical, I wouldn't have blamed general manager Brett Veach for hanging up the phone before Arizona finished their pitch.
Should the Chiefs be willing to offer their most precious pick, the 2027 first-rounder, for some wide receivers? Possibly! Do the Philadelphia Eagles want to move DeVonta Smith to jumpstart their rebuild? I'd listen! But for a player in the midst of as disastrous of a season as Harrison? Not even I am receiver-starved enough to make that call.
WR Separation Score vs TPRR 📊 -- Carnell Tate building chemistry with Ward -- Downs, Doubs, Odunze, Pickens prime targets for positive regression -- MHJ in a league of his own pic.twitter.com/kDtxG8H22T
For further context, Bill Barnwell of ESPN took a longer look at just how bad things have been for Harrison in Arizona.
"He hasn't been getting much separation, hasn't hit high-end speed, and isn't winning on contested catches very often," Barnwell wrote. "He needs to be a different player altogether in Houston."
Brutal, right? ...Well, that was just Barnwell's summary on Twitter ! The deep-dive brings some of the stats that underscore the disappointments that have come with Harrison's career so far.
"During his time with the Cardinals, Harrison ranked last in the NFL among all wide receivers (with 50 targets or more over the past three years) in separation, averaging just 2.1 yards of separation when targeted, per NFL Next Gen Stats," Barnwell continued on ESPN.com . "Great receivers—even ones who get plenty of attention from opposing defenses—are typically able to create more space for themselves. The likes of Ja'Marr Chase and Justin Jefferso n average over 3 yards of separation on their routes. In Arizona, McBride averaged 3.3 yards of separation on his targets during that time, while Wilson was at 2.5 yards."
Barnwell's assessment continues at length, with unflattering statistics couched by a few fair criticisms of the Cardinals' offense throughout the dissection.
There's certainly a chance that Harrison does become "a different player altogether" with the Texans, but looking at the deal from the Chiefs' standpoint, there's no way I would have beaten that price for a receiver who needs to be nearly unrecognizable on his new team.

title: Only 1 Rare, Unexpected Justin Herbert Trade Scenario Makes Any Sense
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers won’t trade Justin Herbert. Reportedly, the Chargers themselves have even shot down the Herbert trade buzz behind the scenes when asked.
But this is the NFL. Speculation won’t stop. And superstar trade outliers like Micah Parsons, Myles Garrett, Maxx Crosby, to name a few, are pretty hard to ignore.
Still, those aren’t quarterbacks. Herbert also happens to have a big no-trade clause written into his contract, a deal that also happens to hit the Chargers with wicked amounts of dead money if they do a deal.
But again, quarterback. And that position creates maybe the one scenario where projecting a Justin Herbert trade might make a small bit of sense.
The Chargers aren’t going to give up on Herbert. He’s a top-10 quarterback under the age of 30 when clicking. Unless he explicitly wants out, it’s not going to happen.
Only one scenario is even worth talking about on this front: The Chargers boast a top-five draft pick after this season and can recoup multiple first-round picks in a Herbert trade.
That’s it. If the Chargers want to blow everything up in a full-blown reset and start building around a rookie quarterback contract, then fine. The upcoming quarterback class could be loaded and if they really like one of those prospects, getting potentially multiple first-round picks back in next year’s draft, letting them add two or three first-rounders ASAP, might just move the needle. Ask the Titans how picking early in a "down" quarterback year is going with Cam Ward.
A disclaimer: Trading Herbert is foolish. But a top-five pick, combined with shocking trade offers? That’s at least worth a raise of the eyebrow.
Smartly, the Chargers are far more likely to move on from Mike McDaniel and Jim Harbaugh. Exposing Herbert to yet another coaching change, when that’s been one of the biggest issues of his career to date, comes with its own risk. But it feels unavoidable.
They’re also more likely to move on from general manager Joe Hortiz, because frankly, his record largely stinks.
Better to take more risks with Herbert than roll the dice on quarterback purgatory. The Chargers have been sneakily good at finding great quarterbacks over the years, but that doesn't mean the next one will follow the trend.
Make no mistake, resetting yet again around Herbert is a recipe for disaster. The Chargers organization needs to figure out what went wrong and why, and where Herbert’s head is at as they regroup. But 99 percent of trade scenarios and ideas fall flat, outside of this one unlikely outlier that requires them to keep tanking with the worst of the NFL.

title: Chargers Injury Updates Have Torn 53-Man Roster in Half by Week 6

The Los Angeles Chargers are facing their long time division rivals the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead stadium this week for their final game before their bye week. Los Angeles is trying their best to field a competitive team in Week 6 but the football gods are working overtime to make that a more difficult task.
The Chargers start the week with more than 50 percent of their original 53-man roster either on injured reserve or this week's injury report. wednesday's injury report for week 6 at KC pic.twitter.com/ItqkPJJEmk
Los Angeles has injuries everywhere, even to rooms and position groups where depth was considered a strength. There are two massive hurdles the Chargers will have to overcome this week if they hope to hand Kansas City their first loss of the season and notch their first win.
The Chargers' receiving room was nearly gone in week five with Ladd McConkey available only in emergencies, Quentin Johnston out, Tre' Harris hurt in the first half, Brenen Thompson out, and Keandre Lambert-Smith was still on injured reserve. The only remaining receivers were Derius Davis, who has been a non-factor in 2026, Marquez Valdez-Scantling and Theo Wease Jr., who was just recently signed to the active roster.

Who will be available and effective in week six is still a mystery. We have have to keep a sharp eye on this week's injury reports.
This is a new development. The Chargers defense has kept the Chargers alive the past three weeks and in large part due to the defensive front putting forth a dominant performance against opposing offenses.
Jamaree Caldwell, Justin Egboigbe and Dalvin Tomlinson all being limited to start the week is a concern. Those three being joined by Bud Dupree, Elijah Molden and Daiyan Henley makes the strength of the team now concerningly thin with Derwin James Jr and Donte Jackson not practicing yet.
The Chargers need rest in the worst way and Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker and the Chiefs are standing in their way before they get to their bye. Will they do so with their first win of the season or staring down 0-6? Managing

title: First Rumblings of Mike McDaniel on Hot Seat: Experiment Might Be Over Before We Know It
full_text:
When the Chargers brought Mike McDaniel to Los Angeles, the hope was that he could give the offense a new identity.
Five games into the 2026 season however, the Bolts are still searching for answers.
The offense has become one of the biggest concerns surrounding the team. McDaniel was hired to help the Chargers take a step forward, not a step backward. His first season coordinating the offense has gotten off to a disastrous start. The question now is how long the organization can wait for things to change.
NFL and ESPN Insider Ian Rapoport stated that things could change if the struggle continues, though nothing has been publicly stated by the Chargers organization. He also notes that the backup plan if this were to happen, would most likely be promoting Adam Gase as the interim offensive coordinator.
From The Insiders on @nflnetwork : A look at where it stands for the #Chargers during a frustrating start to the season. pic.twitter.com/g3qqPibZvM
There is plenty of football left to play, but the early results have simply been very difficult to defend.
The Chargers have struggled to maintain consistency, protect the football and finish games. Against the Broncos, they entered the fourth quarter with a 17-10 lead before watching the game slip away. A failed fourth-down attempt, a Justin Herbert fumble and late interception helped turn a potential first victory into another disappointing afternoon.
For McDaniel, those are the kinds of moments that make an already difficult situation even more complicated. Offensive coordinators are judged on their ability to prepare a unit, make adjustments and put players in positions to succeed. When the same problems continue to show up on Sundays, questions about the system and the person running it are inevitable. Still, blaming him for everything would be an oversimplification. The Chargers have dealt with significant offensive line injuries, making life difficult for Herbert and limiting what the offense can consistently accomplish. A new coaching staff and a different offensive system also require an adjustment period.
Those factors deserve consideration when evaluating what has gone wrong. Herbert is too important to this franchise for the offense to spend an entire season searching for its footing. They need to find ways to get him comfortable, reduce the mistakes and create more opportunities for the offense to operate. Without constantly playing from behind.
Head coach Jim Harbaugh publicly defended McDaniel, indicating that the coordinator’s job was not in jeopardy at that point. That support should not be overlooked. However, another loss has only intensified the situation.
The most frustrating part for Chargers fans is that this was supposed to be an exciting new chapter.
Instead of watching the offense build momentum, fans are left wondering whether the current approach can produce the results this team needs. McDaniel still has an opportunity to change that conversation. One strong performance will not erase five losses, but meaningful improvement would give the Chargers something to build on. The offense needs to show that it can execute consistently rather than relying on brief flashes of potential.

title: Adam Schefter Weighs in on Chargers Trading Justin Herbert Idea Ahead of NFL Deadline
full_text:
No matter how poorly things are going for Jim Harbaugh and the Los Angeles Chargers , it’s near-impossible to imagine the organization trades away Justin Herbert.
It’s fair enough for outsiders to wonder, though. The Harbaugh era seems like it could be ending far sooner than anyone expected as the Chargers look like the worst and least-prepared team in the NFL.
A combination of horrendous roster building and an apparently ill-advised addition of Mike McDaniel has led Herbert and the Chargers to disaster.
Naturally, then, it sounds like all of the dire circumstances pushed ESPN’s Adam Schefter to ask the Chargers about a Herbert trade.
As expected, the Chargers aren’t exactly entertaining even the question of trading a 28-year-old superstar quarterback.
On his podcast, Schefter revealed that he reached out to the Chargers about the idea.
Schefter said that "the person basically cut me off mid-sentence, stopped me in my tracks, and said, 'let me be very clear about this. We have never even discussed that idea. The sentence should we trade Justin Herbert has never once been uttered in our organization, nor will it be.'"
Not that the Chargers could trade Herbert. He’s under contract through 2029 and has a full no-trade clause, so he could veto any possible deal, if desired. And a post-June 1 trade would mean absorbing dead money north of $19 million in each of the next three years, among other problems.
While other have debated whether Justin Herbert should be traded, the Chargers have not. Cc: @tyschmit 🎧 https://t.co/9tlm7cvFNz pic.twitter.com/Yuk4jNSKhK
Trade valuation needs to be part of the topic, too. Herbert would demand multiple first-round picks. But his value isn’t as high as it used to be, if we’re being honest. He’s mostly looked horrible, with just 937 yards and five touchdowns with seven interceptions while leading the NFL in turnover-worthy throws.
There’s a lot that goes into Hebert’s poor performance and he’s more likely to return to top-10 play than anything else. But that wouldn’t stop other teams from trying to get leverage in a deal with these factors.
Regardless, the idea of the Chargers trading Justin Herbert is just that: an idea. The organization is far more likely to dole out consequences to Harbaugh and even general manager Joe Hortiz before it considers giving up a star passer, no matter how sexy the trade package from another team might be.

title: Jim Harbaugh's Latest Quote About Chargers Disaster Might Have Hidden Message
full_text:
Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh had a damning quote about his team in the aftermath of the 0-5 start to the season.
Just a day later, Harbaugh had another notable quote: And it sort of feels like there is a hidden message in there somewhere.
Speaking with reporters to start the week, Harbaugh responded interestingly to questions about whether he’s feeling any pressure from the overarching organization right now.
"John Spanos, Dean Spanos, Susie Spanos, the whole Spanos family. It's shoulder to shoulder where we're in this fight together," Harbaugh said, according to ESPN’s Anthony Gharib .
It’s a great question, before anything else.
But the answer sure seems interesting, too.
Here’s the thing about the latest coach-speakism from Harbaugh: It probably means Harbaugh’s had a chat or two with those above him about how this Chargers season has gone off the rails.
And it probably means the seat is heating up.
Don’t just duh this one away. Harbaugh probably talks to Chargers brass semi-often, if not weekly. But the fact he’s publicly bringing them up after an 0-5 start feels like a pretty big deal.
Harbaugh is also known to lie. He’s fallen under fire for the “greatest quarterback of all time” stuff with Justin Herbert. His “in this fight together” with Chargers ownership is probably just as big of a stretch. Ownership isn’t leaving. The coaching staff could be.
The cold reality of the NFL in a situation like this is pretty straightforward: The rest of this season is about self-preservation. There are jobs at stake at all levels and future health to consider, too. And the front office, if not ownership, will now likely keep a closer eye on the NFL draft order than they do the playoff standings charts.
If the Chargers lose in Kansas City in Week 6 and hit the bye at 0-6, it’s pretty safe to assume that one or two folks will be fired during the break. There’s simply no excuse, even after another big bite from the injury bug, for a football team to look as unprepared and lost as the Chargers have for five weeks.
Harbaugh might be safe through the rest of the season, sure. But his quote here is going to look like sour milk pretty quickly by December because very few things outside of a full-blown reset can salvage a team that has fallen this far off the track in Year 3, which is supposed to be the height of the rebuild and climb up into serious contention.

title: Would Chargers Actually Entertain Offers for Tuli Tuipulotu?
full_text:
He has made steady improvement each year since he entered the National Football League as a second-round draft choice in 2023. Los Angeles Chargers outside linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu is off to a solid start this season despite the team’s 0-5 record.
The Chargers Defense gets the INT off of Sam Darnold on his first pass of the game! #BoltUp #LACvsSEA pic.twitter.com/TGS22K4QXJ
The 6’3”, 266-pound defender is tied for third on the team with 22 tackles, to go along with a pair of sacks and a team-high eight quarterback hits. He’s totaled one interception, come up with two forced fumbles, been credited with three passes defensed and recovered a fumble.
1st and 10 · Denver Broncos Bo Nix ( @BoNix10 ) runs up the middle for 1 yard to DEN 41, fumbles, recovered by Tuli Tuipulotu ( @TuipulotuTuli ) at DEN 42 https://t.co/B3495YSvR2 pic.twitter.com/7zdiKxkD6F
Go back to Tuipulotu’s rookie campaign in ’23. He played in 11 games but made zero starts. There were 53 stops, 4.5 sacks, a dozen QB hits and two forced fumbles. A year later, he appeared in all 17 contests and made nine starts. There were 38 tackles, a team-high 8.5 sacks, and another forced fumble. He also added four special teams stops. Tuipulotu also appeared in the team’s playoff loss at Houston.
The third season proved to be the charm for the former Trojan. He finished ninth on Jim Harbaugh’s squad with 45 tackles and led the Bolts with career-bests in sacks (13.0) and quarterback hits (23). Add two more forced fumbles, a fumble recovery, and four more stops on special teams. Tuipulotu, who was named to his first Pro Bowl, came up with two more tackles and one sack in the Bolts’ wild card loss at New England.
There’s little doubt that the four-year pro is a player on the rise. But the question here is whether the Chargers are a team headed in the right direction? Last Wednesday, Tuipulotu was one of 15 players that Bradley Locker of Pro Football Focus speculated could be the subject of trade talks. The Chargers’ defender ( PFF's 14th-ranked edge rusher ) is in the final year of his rookie contract, and the organization has not yet extended him.
The team appears very loaded at edge rusher with ageless Khalil Mack (who leads the team with 3.0 sacks), and 2026 first-round pick Akheem Mesidor. The latter is tied with Tuipulotu in terms of total tackles (22), is second on the club with 2.5 sacks, and has one forced fumble.
Of course, Mack could also be a player a contender may be interested in, but considering he’s in the midst of his 13th season, he likely would not net a bigtime haul in terms of a deal.
The Chargers head to Arrowhead Stadium this week to face the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs. A season ago, the Bolts swept the series for the first tine since 2013 . This time around, Harbaugh’s club is one of three teams in the league still looking for its first victory in 2026.
Could general manager Joe Hortiz and the franchise already be looking to the future after the team’s disappointing start? Tuipulotu could certainly net a respectable haul. And for those believing he is an emerging star that the Bolts wouldn’t part ways with, nothing is ever off the table when it comes to today’s NFL.

title: Eyes to the Future: It's Time  For These Young Chargers to Get More Snaps
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-5 and their season is shifting to a salvage operation. The Chargers entered week five with over a third of their active roster already on the injury report on top of several starters being sent to injured reserve.
The Chargers will travel to Kansas City to take on the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium in week six. Arrowhead is one of the toughest environments to play in and the Chargers should look to take advantage of the matchup to start giving more opportunities to younger players. They should do this in particular at Arrowhead but also going forward the rest of the season.
Los Angeles has to operate with eyes to the future and determining which players are quality depth options or even potential starters going forward should be a main priority. Let's dive in to which players and position groups should get opportunities for snaps and roles.
The Chargers wide receiver room has been decimated by injuries this year. Keandre Lambert-Smith has missed weeks two through five on injured reserve and had his practice window opened to start week six. Head coach Jim Harbaugh already announced that Tre' Harris will be week to week with a hamstring injury, Quintin Johnston will be limited at practice this week on top of Ladd McConkey and Brenen Thompson trying to work back into practice.
If Lambert-Smith is able to be practice and go full speed, he should instantly slide into the top receiver role. The Chargers should make sure to utilize he and Theo Wease Jr., who was just signed to the active roster from the practice squad, in the game plan.
Wease put forth a surprising performance in his first action with the Chargers, he played hard in week five despite not having many practice reps. Both Lambert-Smith and Wease should get opportunities to prove their value as depth pieces for the rest of this season and going forward.
Ornde Gadsden may be a receiving tight end but the Chargers are lacking options. With Charlie Kolar and Scott Matlock returning to the lineup, Gadsden should get an extended look in the slot.
Trade rumors continue to circulate with the Chargers potentially eyeing 0-6. The most common name being floated as soon to be moved is veteran Khalil Mack, and frankly he deserves it. Mack trusted the Chargers and came back for another year, he deserves to play for a contender of his choosing. If Mack is moved, the Chargers only have Bud Dupree behind Tuli Tuipulotu and Akheem Mesidor on the active roster.
Dupree is nursing a neck injury and Los Angeles has Andre Carter II and Caleb Murphy on the practice squad. They will need depth going forward and into the future. Carter and Murphy should get an extended look to see if they can factor into the defense and special teams for the remainder of the 2026 season and audtion for next year,
Second year lineback Marlowe Wax did get additional packages on defense against the Broncos and that should continue. With most of the linebacker room not signed beyond this season, the Chargers need a better understanding of who will have roles beyond this season.

title: Calvin Ridley May Be Up For Grabs at the Trade Deadline: Chargers' Need to Make the Move
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers need to give Justin Herbert more help, the current situation with the receiving core just isn't working.
It’s no secret that the Chargers have had their share of problems staying healthy, and those issues become even more concerning when you look at the depth of the receiving room.
NFL reporters Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano recently noted that Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley could be a potential trade candidate. With more rumors starting to take buzz around the veteran.
Ridley would give the Chargers another experienced receiver who knows how to get open and make plays downfield. He has the speed to stretch a defense and his route running ability to create separation against opposing cornerbacks.
The biggest reason I like this potential move is that it would take some pressure off the rest of the receiving group. We need more consistency at that position, and that is honestly an understatement.
Ladd McConkey has shown what he can bring to this offense, but the Chargers need more than one reliable option for Herbert to lean on. Injuries have made that even more important, and relying on the same few players to carry the passing game isn’t a great position to be in over the course of a season.
Adding Ridley would give Herbert another receiver capable of making defenses pay when they focus too much attention on McConkey. The Chargers have a quarterback who can make just about every throw asked of him, but the offense needs to do a better job of giving him dependable targets. Bringing in a receiver with Ridley’s experience could help open things up and make this passing attack harder to defend.
Of course, this isn’t a move the Chargers should make just for the sake of making a trade. Ridley’s health, the asking price and his contract would all need to make sense.
But if the Titans are willing to move him for a reasonable price, the Chargers should absolutely explore it no matter what.
This team doesn’t need to completely rebuild its offense. It needs to give Herbert more help, improve its depth and find ways to keep the passing game productive when injuries hit. It sounds easier said then actaully done, but it just has to happen if they want to be competitive. Look, we all know the state of this offense, bringing in a veteran with proven success only makes sense.

title: Chargers Work Out Multiple Big-Name Veterans Amid Injury Bug Onslaught
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are coming off another loss, this time to the hands of the Denver Broncos. The team is 0-5 and is currently tied for the worst record in the entire NFL with the Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins. On top of losing five games straight to begin the NFL season, they are also dealing with a massive injury bug, causing the team to be short-handed for the upcoming weeks.
This injury bug saw 18 names on the Chargers injury report before the Broncos game, with guys like Tre Harris and Bud Dupree also getting hurt in the loss. We have yet to see the injury report for the Bolts' matchup in Week 6, but expecting it to be much better would be a poor idea. That said, the team is working out a plethora of names, hoping to add some roster depth during this injury-riddled stretch.
full game status for week 5 vs DEN pic.twitter.com/Ph53lJP3zb
Armour-Davis was a Baltimore Ravens fourth-round draft selection in 2022, giving the team three starts in three years, and played the 2025 season with the Titans, where he had 10 starts and recorded 34 tackles. During the season, he suffered a season-ending injury, likely giving a reason why he has not signed with any team. Amour-Davis' finds himself with a workout opportunity likely due to his connection with Joe Hortiz, who was a part of the Ravens scouting staff when he was draft.
Bell was a seventh-round selection of the San Francisco 49ers in the 2023 draft, playing for the team for two seasons, recording eight catches for 90 yards and three touchdowns. He spent 2025 with the New Orleans Saints, where he recorded two catches for 23 yards and a touchdown. Bell spent his college years with Michigan, having a connection with Chargers' head coach Jim Harbaugh yielding the likely reasoning for his workout beyond the need for another receiver.
Luke Grimm spent the 2025 and 2026 pre-seasons with the Chargers, becoming a reliable slot receiver who also had a special teams return touchdown, giving some validity to his ability to be on an NFL roster. He worked out with the team, being one of two names on this list to sign with the practice squad.
Hilton Jr. was an undrafted free agent after the 2026 NFL Draft ended, signing with the Washington Commanders. After being released in early August, he found his way to the Green Bay Packers, where he had no receiving stats other than a drop during the preseason. He was released shortly after. Hilton Jr. played at LSU, having 4.4 speed and five years of minimal production, giving the Bolt fans the reality of the current situation the team is in at the receiver position.
Tejhuan Palmer was an Arizona Cardinals sixth-round selection in the 2024 NFL Draft, becoming one of very few UAB players to be drafted into the NFL. Palmer spent time on the Cardinals' practice squad for both the 2024 and 2025 seasons, being elevated in one game in 2025. He played with the New England Patriots in the 2026 preseason, recording three catches for 33 yards.
Smith-Schuster is the headlining name of all the players who were worked out by the Chargers. He is a former 1400-yard wide receiver who has been in the NFL since 2017. Smith-Schuster never hit his 2018 season high of 1400 yards ever again, but has carved out a nice career as a role-playing wide receiver across three different teams. Smith-Schuster spent the off-season with the other Harbaugh brother, John, in New York. He did not make the team, but his 345-yard season in 2025 gives him more production than all of the other names combined on the list.
Jake Browning was an undrafted free agent pickup by the Minnesota Vikings in 2019, after being a strong QB at the University of Washington. Browning spent 2019-2020 with the Vikings, eventually moving on to the Cincinnati Bengals, where he would make a name for himself. He spent multiple seasons with the team, headlined by his 2023 run, where he filled in for Joe Burrow for seven starts, recording a league-leading 70.4% completion rate followed by 1936 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions.
In 2025, when asked to start once again, Browning did not play as well, recording three starts, earning 771 yards, six touchdowns and eight interceptions. After this season, he moved on to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, losing the QB2 job to UDFA Jalon Daniels. Browning was signed to the Chargers roster after impressing the staff in his workout. This is likely due to Trey Lance finding himself on injured reserve due to a random practice injury he suffered.
The final name that was worked out was Trask, who was likely the competition for Browning. Trask was once a second-round pick in 2021, where he was supposed to replace Tom Brady after he retired once and for all. That obviously did not happen, as Trask could never break into any sort of real playing time. He is viewed widely as a bust, but his 6'5 frame and strong production at Florida still gives him opportunities. His 2026 preseason with the Panthers was not bad, recording 252 passing yards, two passing touchdowns and two interceptions.
