title: Rams Midweek Report: Favorable Schedule Ahead, Myles Garrett Update, Sean McVay Concerns
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams sit at 2-3, it’s easy to be down on them after their loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. It wasn’t just that the Rams lost, but how they lost that was so deflating. The Rams should have won, but it was special teams that cost them once again .
Given the issues on special teams, it’s hard to put a lot of faith in this team. They continuously invent new ways to lose. For the first time this season, the Rams are no longer Super Bowl favorites as that belongs to the San Francisco 49ers.
At the same time, if the Rams can figure it out, there is the potential for them to go on a serious run. Here is their schedule before the bye week in Week 11:
The combined record for those teams is 6-18-1. That’s the lowest strength of schedule over the next five games in the NFL.It’s important not to look too far ahead in the NFL, but those are five very winnable games. The Rams could easily go into their bye week with a 7-3 record. At that point, the Rams may only be one or two games back in the NFC West behind the 49ers.
Future Strength of Schedule (Next 5)
A 7-3 record isn’t guaranteed. The Rams still need to go out and take care of business. However, they are past the grueling opening stretch of their schedule. They are also set to get healthier as Myles Garrett gets closer to his return and they should get Terrance Ferguson back in three weeks.
The next game that the Rams will have to be concerned about is Week 13 against the Kansas City Chiefs. Even then, that’s a winnable game and the Rams are at home. Let’s say the 49ers lose to the Seahawks in Week 12 as well as one more game.That would set up a Week 14 matchup between the 9-3 Rams and the 10-2 49ers. A win there would put the Rams back on top in the NFC West.
The Rams might NEVER LOSE another game this season 😲 @heykayadams pic.twitter.com/yk5VMwL0Sq
That doesn’t mean that it isn’t still a long shot. There’s a reason the Rams have only a 14 percent chance of winning the NFC West right now. However, a lot can change in two months, especially as the Rams get Garrett back and they hopefully start to find their stride.
As the weeks have gone on, there has been growing anticipation for when Myles Garrett will make his return to the Rams. Over the past several weeks, I’ve been writing that Week 7 was the most realistic. While the team was optimistic that he could be back on Sunday, Week 7 was the more realistic timeline with Week 8 being a worst-case scenario. NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport confirmed that this week.
“My understanding was it was a six-week recovery from a knee surgery. He had the knee surgery on the Monday after Week 1, so Week 7 should be around when he’s ready, which could mean practicing this week and then playing next week. We’re getting to the window.”
. @RapSheet shares an update on Myles Garrett's knee injury and when he will return to play 👀⬇️ (via @RichEisenShow ) pic.twitter.com/u5pLuhvURk
McVay has already said that the team wouldn’t be opening Garrett’s window this week. The Rams’ head coach was asked about it on Tuesday and said, “We will not. Not this week.” Right now, as long as things go well, Garrett could make his return when the Rams play the Raiders next week.
Following Monday night’s loss to the Buffalo Bills, left tackle Alaric Jackson was caught on camera throwing a punch at edge rusher Bradley Chubb. It adds to the growing list of off-field issues from Jackson. On Tuesday, the NFL announced that Jackson would be suspended without pay for two games for an act of unsportsmanlike conduct.
WOAH... Alaric Jackson punched Bradley Chubb after the game finished 😳 pic.twitter.com/377C2MNuBX
However, watching the video, it can be seen that Chubb potentially makes contact with Jackson first. Now, to be clear, that doesn’t give Jackson the right to react in the way that he did. With that said, Jackson appealed the two-game suspension and won. His suspension was officially reduced down to one game. Jackson will be eligible to return next week against the Las Vegas Raiders.
That will be good news for the Rams. On Sunday, they go against a Cardinals defense that has struggled to generate pressure. However, the Raiders will present more of a challenge with Maxx Crosby. They’ll appreciate having Jackson back for that game.
Through five weeks, some have wanted the Rams to make a change at their special teams coordinator spot. While there’s no doubt that the Rams need more production out of their special teams unit, making a change at the coordinator spot after just five games likely wouldn’t fix anything. The issues run far deeper than the coordinator or even the kicker for that matter.
“I have a lot of confidence in Bubba Ventrone,” said McVay on Tuesday. “There are no changes that are going to be made there. We're going to keep working. This isn't the first time that we've had adversity and the first time that we've had some different things that I have to do a better job of.”
In a matter of three weeks, the Rams have made changes at both the returner and kicker positions, cutting Xavier Smith and moving on from Harrison Mevis. Given what Ventrone has said about Ethan Evans, it’s fair to assume he’s on a short leash as well. These are changes that should have been made in the offseason, but the Rams are working on it now.
Earlier this week, I wrote about how McVay has played a larger role in the Rams being 2-3 than some would like to believe. With that said, something seems off about McVay this year. When the Rams returned home from Australia, an episode of 60 Minutes aired. In the episode, McVay appeared to be on edge because of a "bad practice." In the episode, McVay appeared to be on edge because of ‘bad practice’.
“I feel bad that you guys are doing this incredible story and you know, and I'm not in a good place right now. I'm not happy with how practice went,” Los Angeles Rams Coach Sean McVay tells 60 Minutes. https://t.co/MCHgGz2psB pic.twitter.com/r2k0pogPRq
After the loss to the Denver Broncos, McVay spoke to the media for two minutes before ducking out of the press conference. The Athletic’s Mike Sando noted in a recent column that, “Some who know McVay suspected from afar that something has been bothering him this season. They thought he seemed too cranky over traveling around the world for the opener in Australia.”
You can go all the way back to the draft, when McVay didn’t seem pleased after the Rams invested a first-round pick in a new quarterback. When McVay and Snead addressed the media following the Simpson pick, McVay almost seemed mad.
I’m not sure what it is specifically and it would be unfair to speculate. Still, McVay seems to be more on edge than he has in recent years.
As expected, the defense is getting a lot of criticism for its performance on Monday night against the Bills. Josh Allen and James Cook combined for 232 yards rushing. It was almost reminiscent of the Divisional Round playoff loss to the Philadelphia Eagles two years ago.
However, I do think they were better than the numbers would suggest. On Monday night, 73.7 percent of Josh Allen’s passing attempts were considered “short”. Allen’s 12 completions were his fewest in a game that he’s started since Week 5 of 2024. In the fourth quarter, Allen had an average depth of target of 5.3 yards. Without Allen’s 44-yard arm punt in the second quarter, Allen would have had an average depth of target of 5.47 yards for the game.
Shannon Sharpe says why are the  LA Rams paying Trent McDuffie $33 million and Jaylen Watson $20 million if they can’t cover Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir pic.twitter.com/eCTSRnOLZa
This is a secondary that is very difficult to throw on. Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson combined to allow zero receptions and zero yards while recording an interception and two pass breakups. There’s no doubt that the Rams need to do better when it comes to tackling at the second and third levels. That’s where the Bills really exploited them.
Sometimes it's easy to forget that…

title: Rams vs. Cardinals Week 6 Prediction: Preview, Matchups, and Players to Watch
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 6 sitting at 2-3 ahead of a game against the Arizona Cardinals. A game against the Cardinals might be exactly what the doctor ordered after the Rams lost in overtime on Monday night to the Buffalo Bills.
While the Rams enter at 2-3 and need a win, the Cardinals are in a much different spot. The Cardinals just traded away one of their more talented wide receivers in Marvin Harrison Jr. After beating the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 1, they have lost four straight.
The Cardinals have typically provided the Rams a ‘get right’ opportunity in past seasons. After losing two straight last year, the Rams beat the Cardinals in Week 18 before going into the playoffs. It was what the Rams needed to feel good heading into the postseason. Following the loss to the Bills, the Rams need that more than ever.
Heading into Sunday, the Rams will be without left tackle Alaric Jackson as he serves a suspension from the NFL following an incident after the Bills’ game. That will leave the Rams with David Quessenberry at left tackle. The last time the Rams were without Jackson against the Cardinals, they lost, 41-10, and Dennis Gardeck had three sacks. The Cardinals have generated pressure on just 30.3 percent of dropbacks this season, which is the second-lowest rate in the NFL.
The Rams will likely help Quessenberry as much as they can with a tight end and try to slow down Sweat. However, Sweat still has the ability to blow up a gameplan if he can get to the quarterback, and Sunday provides an opportunity. If the Rams are going to beat the Cardinals, they need to protect Stafford, and that starts with slowing down Sweat.
It’s very possible that the Cardinals are short-handed going into Sunday. Harrison Jr. didn’t play a big role in the offense but was still talented. First-round pick and running back Jeremiyah Love could miss the game with an ankle injury. Without Harrison and Love, it’s been difficult for the Cardinals to generate explosives. Sunday should be an opportunity for the defense to get back on track.
One of the few options that the Cardinals will have available to them in the passing game is tight end Trey McBride. McBride has 19 receptions for 139 yards against linebackers this season, which is the most in the NFL. The Cardinals will likely look to get McBride matched up on Nate Landman. Meanwhile, the Rams will look to use Lake on McBride. Rams defensive backs have allowed the fewest receptions and yards to tight ends in 2026.
This is the first time that McVay will be going up against Mike LaFleur after he left to be the head coach of the Cardinals. McVay is 5-8 all-time against his former coordinators, but five of those losses are against Matt LaFleur. Unfortunately for Mike LaFleur, his roster may not be talented enough to win on Sunday.
With three receptions in Week 6, Nacua can surpass Michael Thomas for the most receptions by a player in his first 50 games in NFL history. If he gets 100 yards, he’ll have the third-most games with at least 100 yards by a player in his first four seasons. Nacua had 17 receptions last week and has 100 yards in each of his last two games. There’s a good chance that he hits both milestones.
The Rams will have a new kicker on Sunday against the Cardinals. It’s unlikely that Sunday’s game comes down to a last-second kick like last week, but it’s certainly something to keep an eye on. Blake Grupe will make his Rams debut, and it will be interesting to see how much the Rams test him, if at all.
Last season, Blake Corum had the first 100-yard game of his career as the Rams beat the Cardinals, 45-17. Corum rushed 12 times for 128 yards and had two touchdowns. Corum hasn’t been as involved in recent weeks, but I believe that changes on Sunday.I’m predicting Corum will display some of the explosiveness he showed in the early weeks of the season and have a big game.
Technically, Donald got his first sack on Josh Allen last week. However, it was called back because of a penalty in the secondary. Donald has been quiet this season and hasn’t shown up often on the stat sheet. The Cardinals just placed guard Isaiah Adams on injured reserve. That could open things up for Donald to finally get to the quarterback.
Through the first five weeks, the Rams h ave had a special teams mistake of some sort in every game . Those mistakes reached a breaking point against the Bills as the Rams lost because of a blocked field goal. With so much focus on special teams, that unit will have a lot of pressure to perform. For the first time this season, I think we get a clean game out of that unit.
McVay said it best on Monday night when he emphasized that the Rams can’t let the Bills beat them twice. A game against the Cardinals should allow the Rams to get past that, move on, and feel good about themselves going forward. While the Cardinals have been feisty at times, they simply don’t have the playmakers or depth. The only way the Rams lose this game is if they beat themselves with turnovers and special teams mistakes. Prediction: Rams 34, Cardinals 17

title: Rams Special Teams Struggles Reveal a Flaw in  Roster Construction
full_text:
Through the first five weeks of the season, special teams has been a hot topic for the Los Angeles Rams. It’s the one thing they can’t escape and it came under the microscope again on Monday night as the Rams lost to the Buffalo Bills in overtime because of a blocked field goal.
During the McVay era, the Rams have struggled to find consistency on special teams. Only twice have they ranked inside of the top 10 in special teams DVOA. That happened in McVay’s first season in 2017 and during the team’s Super Bowl season in 2021. Outside of those two years, the Rams have ranked in the bottom half of the league and five times they’ve ranked inside the bottom 10. The Rams are well on their way to another bottom 10 special teams performance this season.
Earlier this summer, Rams head coach Sean McVay told The Athletic’s Mike Sando , “It needs to be more important to me,” when talking about special teams. “Special teams wasn’t as important to me as offense and defense,” McVay said, “But now, I think it is more important because there are more action plays.”
Many look at the demise of the Rams’ special teams unit and point to letting John Fassel go following the 2019 season. That’s not to say that McVay made the correct decision in letting go of Fassel, but there also may be some revisionist history.The downfall was already happening.
Sean McVay was not happy about John Fassel's fake punt attempt. "What are you doing?!" pic.twitter.com/xdVRNul5Bq
While the Rams ranked second in special teams DVOA in 2017, that dropped to 17th in 2018. By the end of the 2019 season, the Rams ranked 23rd in special teams DVOA. It’s easy to point to Fassel being let go, but this is an issue that runs far deeper.
Some will point to a lack of commitment, but when the Rams ranked 30th in special teams DVOA in 2020, they ranked fifth in special teams commitment according to The Athletic’s research. Between 2020 and 2022, the Rams ranked inside of the top five in special teams commitment. In two of those three years, they still ranked in the bottom 10 in the NFL. It wasn't until 2023 that the Rams started to lag behind in that department.
In a sense, the “F Them Picks” roster-building approach is partially to blame. When everything came crumbling down in 2022, the Rams were forced to draft players who could step into starting roles immediately. It was an impressive turnaround, but the depth on special teams took a hit.
In 2021, Terrell Burgess ranked second on the roster in special teams snaps. He was drafted in the third round. During the 2023 draft, the Rams selected starting players in Byron Young and Kobie Turner. Young had 20 special teams snaps as a rookie and Turner had 84.
Instead of being able to focus on roster depth, the Rams had to prioritize high-floor, low-ceiling players who could step into starting roles right away. Yes, the Rams had 24 draft picks in 2023 and 2024. However, all five of their Day 2 picks were either starters or key depth pieces.
It goes beyond investing in a kicker or punter. The Rams have actually done that. During the McVay era, the Rams have drafted two kickers and a punter. The core special teams players, however, have been lacking. None of the players listed above played a key role on special teams.
That left undrafted free agents such as Jake Hummell and Christian Rozemboom as the team’s core special teams players. This season, four of the Rams’ top-10 players in special teams snaps were undrafted free agents. Four others were taken on Day 3 of the draft. Those may be players expected to step into special teams roles, but it’s also unrealistic for those players to make up the vast majority of that unit without some repercussions.
Comparing that to the Seattle Seahawks who have consistently had a top-10 special teams unit, only two of their top-10 players in special teams snaps are undrafted free agents. Three more are former third-round picks and two others were taken no later than the fifth round.
Additionally, the Rams are fielding a group of 10 special teams players with an average Relative Athletic Score (RAS) of 6.4. Players such as Jaylen McCollough and Josh Wallace have RAS scores of 2.3 and 3.8, respectively.
Comparing that to the Seahawks, they aren’t fielding a single player under a 4.5 RAS and their group of 10 averages an RAS of 7.7. It’s certainly possible to find gems late in the draft. Good athletic testing also doesn’t always result in a good player. However, it does speak to the difference in athletic profiles between the players the Rams are fielding on special teams and those on a team like the Seahawks.
The quality of athlete certainly plays a role. In 2022 and 2023, the Vikings ranked bottom three in special teams DVOA. In 2023, This season, through five weeks, the Vikings have the best special teams unit in the NFL after ranking ninth last year. Under Kevin O’Connell, who comes from the Kyle Shanahan and McVay coaching tree, the Vikings have figured out special teams.
In 2023, the Vikings' top 10 players in special teams snaps averaged an RAS of 6.1. Only one player had an RAS over 8.0. That’s a drastic change over the special teams construction in 2026. This season, the Vikings don’t have a single player in their top-10 special teams snaps under a 5.0 RAS. They have five players with an RAS over 9.0 and they average an RAS of 7.9.
The Vikings still have their share of UDFA players contributing, but two of them have an RAS over 9.0. Linebacker Jake Golday has the third-most special teams snaps and has an RAS of 9.9 and was drafted in the second round. The Rams’ second-round pick was inactive last week.
For too long, McVay has had a set-it-and-forget-it mindset on special teams. They’ve gone through the coordinators and kickers. In 10 years, the Rams have had six different special teams coordinators. Since moving on from Matt Gay after 2022, the signing of Blake Grupe makes it six kickers in just over three seasons.
Early in McVay’s career, he was infamous for leaving the defense to Wade Phillips. When the defense was on the field, McVay could be seen sitting on the bench with his quarterback and going over still shots from the previous drive.
McVay has taken a larger role in the defense since then, but that hasn’t been the case on special teams. The approach has been to hire either an experienced special teams coordinator or one of the better up-and-coming candidates and let them do their thing.
After losing Matt Gay, the Rams took the approach of signing an experienced kicker in Brett Maher only for him to be cut midseason. During the next draft, the Rams selected one of the more promising kickers in Josh Karty, who was cut during his second season.
That hands-off approach to special teams hasn't produced a sustainable solution. It has simply created a carousel at both spots with no long-term solution. There’s no doubt that McVay holds that group to a high standard, but it’s likely been a much more hands-off approach.
It speaks to the overall lack of commitment. The Rams signed 18 undrafted free agents this year, and not one had player was a wide receiver with return experience. Despite the red flags last season, the only changes the Rams made to special teams was hiring Bubba Ventrone and signing two core players in Joe Cardona and Grant Stuard. The Rams kept Harrison Mevis, Ethan Evants, and Xavier Smith who all played roles in some of last year's inconsistency. No competition was brought in, and two of those three players have been cut to start the year.
Special teams is the one thing that McVay has consistently gotten wrong . Of the five offensive coordinators McVay has hired, four have become head coaches, and Nate Scheelhaase appears to be on his way.
On the defensive side of the ball, McVay’s last two defensive coordinators were hired as head coaches, and Chris Shula is also likely on his way. Wade Phillips is the only one of McVay's defensive coordinators who hasn't gone on to become a head coach.
“Wade Phillips…

title: Rams Injury Report Brings Much-Needed Good News Ahead of Week 6 vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to enter Week 6 the healthiest they’ve been in weeks ahead of their matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. While the Rams didn't practice on Wednesday, each player's status is an estimation. On the injury report Rams had only one player who was estimated to not participate. That player was tight end Davis Allen, who would have missed practice with a foot injury. Outside of Allen, the Rams only had five other players listed, with four of them limited.
It’s a welcome change from recent weeks. Last week the Rams started with nine players on the injury report. Ahead of the Rams’ game against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 3, they also had nine players, including multiple starters.
While Allen is the only player who was estimated as a non-participant, linebacker Nate Landman (wrist/shoulder), wide receiver Alex Bachman (wrist), tight end Colby Parkinson (shoulder), and cornerback Josh Wallace (shoulder) were all limited. Both Landman and Parkinson have been on the injury report over the last few weeks as they manage various injuries. The Rams have managed Landman during the week before the last few games and will likely do the same with Parkinson.
For the first time in two weeks, Aaron Donald did not show up on the injury report. He will likely only miss Friday’s practice as that has been his typical rest day. After showing up on the injury report last week, cornerback Jaylen Watson and Quentin Lake were absent from Wednesday’s report. The same was true for edge rusher Josaiah Stewart , who had appeared on the injury report ahead of the last two games.
While Omar Speights was listed on the injury report with a knee injury, he was estimated as a full participant.
On the Cardinals’ side, running back Jeremiyah Love will be a player to monitor throughout the week. Love was listed with an ankle injury. Given that this is Love’s second ankle injury, there is a chance that he doesn’t play against the Rams.
Jeremiyah Love's (2nd) ankle injury will keep him out of practice Wednesday and there is a chance he doesn't play against Rams. "The rest for him will be vital."
The Rams will certainly be watching Love’s status leading up to the game. While Love has had an inconsistent start to his rookie season, he had 21 carries for 90 yards against the San Francisco 49ers back in Week 3 and is still a dynamic playmaker.
Arizona had multiple players who did not practice Wednesday due to rest. However, safety Wydett Williams didn’t participate as he goes through the concussion protocol. Additionally, safety Kitan Crawford and wide receiver Devin Duvernay were both limited.
There are still a few situations to monitor throughout the week on the Rams’ side, particularly at tight end with Allen and Parkinson. However, compared to where things stood over the previous few weeks, they are in a much better position from a health standpoint. With the Rams looking to get back to .500 against the Cardinals, having most of their key contributors available should give them every opportunity to do just that.

title: Grading Rams Signing of Blake Grupe: Another Band-Aid on a Bigger Problem
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams signed their sixth kicker since the start of the 2023 season when they added Blake Grupe on Wednesday . There’s no doubt that a change needed to be made and the Rams needed to move on from Harrison Mevis. An argument can be made that the move should have been made weeks ago. At the same time, it’s fair to remain skeptical that Grupe is the long-term solution.
This is the same dance that the Rams have gone through at kicker since moving on from Matt Gay. In 2023, the Rams started with Brett Maher before signing Lucas Havrisik midway through the season. By the time the playoffs rolled around, the Rams were right back where they started and had re-signed Maher.
The next season, the Rams drafted Josh Karty. Karty made it through his rookie year, finishing the season strong. However, before the midway point last year, the Rams moved on and signed Mevis.
As a contending team, you never want to be in a position where you’re actively looking for a kicker, especially midseason. At that point, it becomes like spinning the Wheel of Destiny. Are you going to end up with one of the good kickers or one of the bad ones? The Rams have too often ended up with one of the bad kickers, and with Grupe, they are spinning the wheel again.
The Rams have now reached a point where they are signing a kicker off the Jets’ practice squad. It’s the same Jets team that has spun the wheel itself and ended up with Jason Sanders. If the Jets had the utmost confidence in Sanders, it’s hard to think they would have had a second experienced kicker ready to go on their practice squad.
At the end of the day, the Rams are in this position because they opted not to bring in competition for Mevis. While Mevis had added some stability to the kicking operation, he remained unproven from range. It always seemed odd that the Rams didn’t at least bring in some competition for Mevis.
The Rams could have drafted Trey Smack in the sixth round, but instead opted to take wide receiver CJ Daniels who has yet to be active in a game. Smack is 7-for-10 on field goals but has two makes from 50-plus yards, including one from 59 yards. He was 3-for-3 on kicks of 50 or more yards in the preseason.
his name is literally Trey Smack, what else do you expect? pic.twitter.com/Q5hJQ6i5Zu
Dominic Zvada has had some inconsistencies with the New York Giants, but is 11-for-14 and was an undrafted free agent. He wouldn’t have taken draft capital. The same can be said about Drew Stevens. If there was interest in Grupe, he was a free agent in March and signed for $1.4 million with the Colts. Instead, the Rams stuck with the status quo.
This isn’t to say that Grupe won’t end up being good for the Rams. With the Colts last year, Grupe was 11-for-11 with a long of 60 yards and was 10-for-10 on extra points. The Rams had to do something, but signing Grupe doesn’t fix the Rams’ issues with the field goal unit. Yes, Mevis missed from 50 yards against the Bills. However, it was the protection that allowed Greg Rousseau to get through and block his attempt from 48 yards in overtime.
Given the players available, Grupe may have been the best option. He hit from 60 yards last year in Seattle, which isn’t an easy environment. However, in a competition this summer, Grupe was great in practice during training camp, but struggled during games.
BIG BOMB BLAKE GRUPE HE WANTS OLD MAN RIVERS TO WIN pic.twitter.com/4wHIWwK8ES
Prior to joining the Colts, he had made just 69.2 percent of his field goals with the Saints, going 18-for-26 with at least one miss in six games. The Saints finally moved on after Grupe went 1-for-3 in a loss to the Falcons.
There is hope that Grupe can give the Rams a legitimate threat from long range and add some stability to the position. He’s an experienced kicker. Still, it’s fair to be skeptical. The Rams continue to put a Band-Aid on a bullet wound as their special teams bleed out .
It’s possible that the Rams get some stability at kicker with Grupe . However, the D+ grade reflects how they’ve handled the position in general. There is some reason for optimism with Grupe, but he’s been inconsistent and streaky throughout his career. There’s a reason he was available, and he enters a kicking operation that has allowed the most blocked kicks in the NFL since 2023.
The Rams made their bed, and now they have to lie in it. This is the path that they chose by not bringing in competition or addressing the issue this summer. Hopefully, Grupe works out, but this isn’t a special teams group that has done enough to inspire confidence that he will.

title: Alaric Jackson's Latest Suspension Raises Serious Questions About His Rams Future
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to be without their starting left tackle for the next two games. On Tuesday, the NFL announced that Rams starting left tackle Alaric Jackson would be suspended for an incident following Monday night’s game against the Buffalo Bills.
Following the loss to the Bills, Jackson was caught on camera throwing a punch at Bradley Chubb. It’s not clear what Chubb said to Jackson, but this is another example of the careless and selfish decisions that Jackson has made over the past few years.
Since Jackson took over as the starting left tackle in 2023, the Rams are 2-3 without Jackson in the lineup and have lost three straight. Without Jackson in 2024 against the Arizona Cardinals, the Rams leaned on Warren McClendon at left tackle. Dennis Gardeck had three sacks in that game as the Rams lost, 41-10. Last year, DJ Humphries struggled on the left side against the Atlanta Falcons. It was a game that the Rams should have won, but lost, 27-24.
On Sunday against the Cardinals, the Rams will lean on David Quessenberry in Jackson’s absence. Quessenberry hasn’t started a game since 2023 with the Minnesota Vikings. In 2024, Quessenberry filled in for 25 snaps for the Vikings against the Rams. In 14 passing-blocking reps, Quessenberry allowed two pressures.
It makes sense that the Rams would go with Quessenberry over the next two games. The Rams may be able to get by with him against the Cardinals, and using 12 and 13 personnel could help him in pass protection as well.
Still, the loss of Jackson is a big one. Again, for a team that preaches a "we, then me" mentality, Jackson’s actions continue to go against that mantra. Jackson was suspended in 2024 for an incident in which he recorded a sexual interaction with a woman without consent. This past offseason, Jackson was arrested on felony domestic battery charges , and his case was later assigned to a pre-filing diversion program. It’s possible that Jackson could eventually be suspended for the latter incident, but the legal situation is still ongoing.
Now, Jackson has been suspended again for two games for an incident that could have been avoided. There’s no doubt that when Jackson has played, he’s provided stability at the left tackle position. However, he’s missed games in each of the last four seasons as the starter, and sometimes for reasons that were in his control.
Given Jackson’s history, the Rams will have a decision to make on him this offseason, especially as they have so many players up for contract extensions. Going into 2027, the Rams have a few options with Jackson.
They can keep him and pay him his full salary as he accounts for $24.4 million against the salary cap. However, if they cut him before the third day of the league year, they would take on just $5 million in dead money and save $19.4 million.
From there, the Rams could use the money saved by cutting Jackson to bring back a player like Warren McClendon , who has been solid and better fits the culture. They would have the option of either moving McClendon to left tackle or keeping him on the right side and making third-round rookie Keagen Trost their left tackle. The Rams could also draft a tackle in the second round if that’s a route they want to go as well. There is some projected tackle depth in the second round of the draft with players like Elijah Paige, Melvin Siani, or Trevor Lauck.
Last year, the Rams paid Jackson to be their franchise left tackle. However, he continues to put himself in situations that are avoidable off the field. It even goes back to his college days at Iowa. Back in 2018, Jackson was suspended for a game for violating team rules. Monday night was just the latest example.
The Rams have been healthy on the offensive line all season, and the first change that they have to make to their starting five won’t even be because of injury. At 2-3, the Rams need their best players available as they look to turn their season around. Instead, they are being forced to adjust their offensive line because of another avoidable decision from their starting left tackle. Jackson has proven his value on the field, but at some point, the Rams have to decide whether that value outweighs the continued questions about his reliability.
For a team that has emphasized accountability and putting the team first, Jackson continues to fall short of that standard. The Rams have invested in him as their franchise left tackle, but that investment comes with expectations off the field and representing the organization. The Rams aren’t in a position to afford these self-inflicted setbacks. Jackson's latest suspension puts the team in a difficult position, and with a potential financial escape available this offseason, the Rams have to seriously consider whether it's time to move in a different direction.

title: Rams Make Flurry of Roster Moves as Kicker Blake Grupe Headlines Three Additions
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams announced a handful of roster moves on Wednesday morning. While it was previously r eported that the Rams were signing kicker Blake Grupe off the New York Jets' practice squad, the team made the move official on Wednesday. Additionally, the Rams also signed edge rusher Garrett Nelson and cornerback Damarion Williams. In corresponding moves, the Rams officially released Harrison Mevis from the active roster and outside linebacker Jamie Sheriff from the practice squad.
Given the Rams' struggles on special teams , Grupe is the most significant of the three additions. Grupe has made 81.9 percent of field goals in his career and has made 96-of-98 extra points. Throughout his career, Grupe has made 18 field goals of 40+ yards and 19 field goals of 50+ yards, with a career-long of 60 yards last season against the Seahawks.
“This guy has experience,” said head coach Sean McVay on Tuesday. “He did a great job for Indy last year. He has kicked in a lot of big-time professional settings. We felt like he was the best guy available that had real game experience.”
Grupe competed for the Colts' kicking job this offseason, but Indianapolis ultimately went with Spencer Shrader. While Grupe was steady in training camp, he had two misses during the preseason. The Rams will hope Grupe can add some stability to the position.
Among the other signings was edge rusher Garrett Nelson. Nelson was an undrafted free agent signing out of Nebraska by the Miami Dolphins in 2023. Nelson spent time on the Seahawks ' practice squad earlier this year and was most recently with the Saints. During the preseason with the Saints, Nelson had six pressures and two sacks.
Nelson also played in the UFL for two years as part of the San Antonio Brahmas. With the Brahmas, Nelson had 27 tackles, four tackles for loss, and 2.5 sacks in 19 games played. The Rams have done well developing edge rushers in the past, most recently with Wesley Bailey.
Additionally, the Rams signed cornerback Damarion Williams to give them some depth on the practice squad. Williams was a fourth-round pick by the Baltimore Ravens in 2022. Given Jaylen Watson’s injuries, the Rams need some cornerback depth. Williams spent time with the Seahawks in 2024 and has also been with the Buccaneers over the last two years.
Williams is a smaller cornerback at 5-foot-10 and 180 pounds, with arms measuring less than 30 inches. However, he may bring some special teams value. He played 134 special teams snaps in 2022 as a rookie, but has not played much since.
While Grupe is the most significant addition given the Rams' ongoing special teams struggles, Nelson and Williams provide much-needed depth at two positions impacted by injuries. Neither is likely to make an immediate impact on defense, but both will have an opportunity to develop on the practice squad.

title: Sean McVay Shares Significant Blame for Rams' Disappointing 2-3 Start
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams haven’t started the season in the way that many have expected. Very few would have predicted the Rams to start the season 2-3. If you were to ask anybody what the reasons are for that start, most would point to special teams . While special teams have certainly played a large role, it may be time to look deeper and start pointing a finger at the head coach, Sean McVay.
Now, this isn’t to say that McVay should be on the hot seat or that the Rams should consider firing him. Let’s make that abundantly clear. For whatever role that McVay has had in the Rams’ 2-3 start, he’s still one of the best head coaches in the NFL. The Rams would not be able to do better than McVay.
At the same time, McVay has played a much larger role in the Rams’ 2-3 start than some would like to believe. For once, when McVay points the finger at himself in press conferences, he might actually be right.
Coming into the season, the Rams were scheduled to play Week 1 in Melbourne, Australia against the San Francisco 49ers. Leading up to the game, the Rams sent players and team personnel to Australia before deciding to arrive just over 24 hours before kickoff.
The Rams were criticized for this decision by the media, especially as the 49ers arrived almost a week before the game. While I didn’t have the same resources as the Rams, the data that I gathered from traveling to Australia showed how much of a negative impact that can have on the body. My sleep efficiency in the early days of arriving in Australia dropped almost 30 percentage points.
Yes, it was the same plan that the Rams had taken the previous year when they went to London. However, the Rams spent that week in Baltimore and took a seven-hour flight to London the day before. That’s almost the equivalent of the Rams going from the West Coast to the East Coast. A flight from Los Angeles to Melbourne is almost double what their trip from Baltimore to London was.
The Rams came out sluggish against the 49ers and crashed out by the second half. They allowed 20 unanswered points on their way to a 27-7 loss. Throughout the week and after the game, McVay was adamant that it wasn’t because of the travel plans. With that said, it was clear throughout the game that the Rams were out of sync and lacked cohesiveness.
Following the win over the Giants a week later, McVay finally seemed to admit the misjudgment in the team's travel plans. “Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn. Sometimes you have a dumb ass coach that makes travel plans that put you in a bad spot,” said McVay.
After beating the New York Giants, the Rams headed to Denver to take on a vulnerable Broncos team. The Rams came out hot and took a 16-0 lead into the half. Despite the Rams leading that game by multiple scores, Matthew Stafford came out of it with 55 passing attempts.
McVay seemed to lose control of the game-script. While McVay is typically great with second-half adjustments, he was getting outcoached by adjustments that the Broncos had made. Neither of the Rams’ offensive drives in the third quarter lasted more than five plays. The Rams had minus-six net yards in the third quarter as the Broncos tied the game.
Against the Broncos, the Rams averaged 0.13 EPA per rush with a 47.8 percent success rate and still threw the ball over 50 times as if they had been trailing, not leading by more than 10 points for much of the game. The Rams had a +9.3 pass rate over expected, whic was the fourth-highest for the week.
The only teams ahead of them were the Bengals, Seahawks, and Packers. The Bengals trailed the Steelers for much of their game while the Seahawks and Packers trailed by double digits in their losses. Despite having a lead, McVay let the game-script get away from him.
After a relatively quiet first half against the Bills, the Rams’ offense went into full-on attack mode in the second half, scoring touchdowns on four of their five possessions, including their last three. The Rams trailed by a touchdown late, needing to go 63 yards in just over 1:30 with one timeout. It took 1:29 and the Rams didn’t even use their timeout before they were in the end zone.
When the defense got a turnover in overtime, it seemed like almost a guarantee that the Rams would win the game given how the offense had moved the ball. Early in the drive, they did just that. With 21-yard completions to Davis Allen and Puka Nacua, the Rams were at the 35-yard line.
That’s when McVay got conservative . The Rams threw an incomplete pass from under center before McVay called a screen pass to Nacua and then a run on 3rd-and-5. It was as if he was content with a 48-yard field goal despite having a kicker that had struggled from range. Inside of 45 yards, Mevis had been solid. It was beyond 45 yards where he became more inconsistent.
For the Rams to feel comfortable about a field goal, they likely needed another 10-15 yards. Instead, McVay called a run on 3rd-and-5 that picked up zero yards. Mevis was called on for a field goal that would be blocked.
While it was Mevis who got cut on Tuesday morning, McVay deserves just as much of the blame for that sequence. McVay took the ball out of his MVP quarterback’s hands and instead put the game in the hands of his special teams unit that has consistently come up short this season. After the game, McVay was disgusted with the play call to run on third down.
“I wish I would have had a better play call and gone forward, got it a lot tighter. I'm sick right now with myself,” said McVay. “I'll be regretting kicking that and not having a better call to be able to go forward on third down and go to fourth or whatever it was. That's on me.”
Going into the game, Mevis had been 4-for-6 in his career from beyond 45 yards. He was just 1-for-3 from 48 yards out. By comparison, he had been 19-for-20 from inside of 45 yards. Everything in that moment said that the Rams needed to get closer. On Tuesday, McVay further explained his thought process behind calling a run in that spot.
“I had a thought of something on a third down and five. Then we had a little bit of time to think about it. Didn't want to leave us susceptible to maybe getting a penalty that moved us back,” McVay explained. “I certainly felt like that was the right decision based on some different things. Maybe it wouldn't have been the same call if I didn't have time to, if you want to say, overthink or have a couple of different things that talk to you out of it.”
It’s understandable that McVay wouldn’t want to take a penalty or a negative play in that spot. However, McVay treated the game as if it was over, when it wasn’t. Had the Rams had the ball at the 20-yard line instead of the 30, a run may have made more sense. Running into the middle of the Bills’ defensive line when the offense had a 39.1 percent rushing success rate was a questionable decision.
For much of the McVay era, the Rams have been one of the more disciplined teams in the NFL. In 2016 under Jeff Fisher, the Rams were the fifth-most penalized team. When McVay took over in 2017, they were the 13th-most penalized team. By 2020, the Rams were the third-least penalized team in the league. Last year, they were also the third-least penalized team.
There is a lot of room for interpretation for whistles that happen between the snaps. However, pre-snap penalties are a reflection of mental and coaching discipline. In 2016 under Fisher, the Rams had the seventh-most pre-snap penalties. That improved to 13th in 2017 and in 2018, they were the 12th-least penalized team pre-snap. For the most part, that’s where they’ve been under McVay.
Over the last three years, the Rams have been among the five least-penalized teams in the NFL when it comes to pre-snap penalties. They already have 13 pre-snap penalties this season and are the seventh-most penalized team in the NFL . Between 2021-2025, the Rams were penalized 10 or more times a total of two times. They’ve had 10 or more penalties in two of the last three games.

title: Rams Week 5 Snap Counts Reveal Major Shift in Wide Receiver Rotation
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams lost to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5, 37-34 in overtime. Throughout the season, the Rams have been adjusting their wide receiver rotation, which has seemingly changed on a weekly basis. Against the Philadelphia Eagles, Tutu Atwell got more snaps in the offense and that carried into Monday. Let’s take a deeper look at the Week 5 snap counts.
Last week, Tutu Atwell played just four snaps fewer than Konata Mumpfield . That changed drastically on Monday night as Atwell out-snapped Mumpfield 32 to six on offense. Mumpfield barely saw any time, while Atwell was used in motion and even had one catch for four yards that resulted in a first down.
It will be interesting to see whether this continues or if it was simply matchup-based. Jordan Whittington also outsnapped Mumpfield 11 to six. Mumpfield played almost 70 percent of the offensive snaps in Weeks 2 and 3 and was down to 7.3 percent on Monday night.
What makes the Atwell situation odd is that he seemed to fall out of favor in the offense last season. Atwell’s role was diminished so much that the team didn’t make an effort to re-sign him in free agency. However, they traded for him before the season. It's possible that with Xavier Smith gone, Atwell's role has opened back up, but it's certainly notable.
Over the past two seasons, Jaylen McCollough has been the dime linebacker for the Rams on defense. Last week, he played just three snaps. On Monday against the Bills, that was down to just one. This season, McCollough has arguably been the Rams’ best tackling safety, and his absence was noticeable against the Bills as the Rams struggled to tackle in the secondary.
Most of McCollough’s snaps over the last few weeks have come on special teams.It’s worth wondering if the Rams are sacrificing McCollough's role on defense so he can contribute more on the coverage units. However, McCollough had just a 32.5 special teams grade via PFF against the Bills.
Last week, the Rams had to abandon 12 and 13 personnel because of the injury to Colby Parksinon. With Parkinson back in the lineup on Monday, the Rams were able to return to what they do best .
With only three tight ends active against the Bills, Allen, Colby Parkinson, and Tyler Higbee were all very active. All three played at least 50 percent of the offensive snaps as they rotated in 12 and 13 personnel.
Davis Allen played 41 snaps, his highest total of the season. While Allen played a higher percentage of the offensive snaps in Week 2, Monday marked a season-high in total snaps. Allen finished with two catches for 24 yards.

title: Alaric Jackson's Suspension Puts Rams in Difficult Position on Offensive Line
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without starting left tackle Alaric Jackson for the next two games. Following Monday night’s game with the Buffalo Bills, Jackson was caught on camera throwing a punch at Bradley Chubb . ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Tuesday that Jackson has been suspended for two games by the NFL.
Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson is expected to be  suspended two games for punching Bills outside linebacker Bradley Chubb during Monday night’s postgame gathering, per sources. But the NFL has not yet notified the team nor the NFLPA. pic.twitter.com/ZR54be9z1n
There is the possibility that Jackson appeals the suspension and it gets dropped to one game. However, given Jackson's history, that may be unlikely.  Any appeal will be heard by either Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson, Ron Rivera, or James Thrash, the hearing officers jointly appointed and compensated by the NFL and NFLPA to decide appeals of on-field player discipline.
Through the first five games, the Rams have remained healthy on the offensive line. Outside of three snaps, the Rams have had the same offensive line all season. Due to a poor decision from Jackson after the game on Monday night in which he let his emotions get the best of him, the Rams will have to make a change at left tackle.
When the incident was brought up on Monday night after the game, a suspension was to be expected. This isn’t Jackson’s first incident with the NFL. Back in 2024, Jackson was suspended for recording a sexual interaction with a woman without consent. This past summer, Jackson was arrested on a felony domestic violence charge, and that is still a pending legal situation.
According to the NFL's release, Jackson will be eligible to return to the Rams’ active roster on Monday, October 26, following the team’s October 18 game against the Arizona Cardinals and October 25 game against the Las Vegas Raiders. If Jackson is set to miss the next two games, that would put him back in the lineup for Week 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers.
With Jackson potentially out for the next two games, the Rams will need to work on how to replace him. The most likely scenario is that the Rams would play David Quessenberry at left tackle for the next two weeks. Quessenberry is the more experienced option and is listed as Jackson’s backup on the depth chart.
However, it also wouldn’t be surprising if the Rams were to activate Keagen Trost off of injured reserve . The Rams drafted Trost in the third round, but he was placed on injured reserve before the season after injuring his hamstring.
Following Week 4, Trost was eligible to come off of injured reserve. McVay was asked last week if the team had discussed elevating Trost or Justin Dedich. “We could open that up, but that's not a conversation that we've had at this point,” said McVay.
Trost may not start, but he would provide good tackle depth behind Quessenberry and give the Rams another option if needed. Trost brings the versatility to play on both the left and right sides of the offensive line. While Trost is more comfortable on the right side, he does have the ability to play left tackle. In a worst-case scenario, the Rams could also move Warren McClendon to left tackle and play Trost on the right side.
As the Rams look ahead to their game against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, the most likely immediate solution will be Quessenberry at that spot. Even against the Cardinals, the loss of Jackson will be a significant one. Last season without Jackson, the Rams lost to the Atlanta Falcons. When Jackson was suspended in 2024, the Rams lost to the Cardinals, 41-10, while Dennis Gardeck had three sacks.
With the offensive line being one of the few areas where the Rams have had stability, Jackson's absence creates an unnecessary challenge. The Rams will now have to rely on their depth at one of the most important positions on offense because of a situation that could have been avoided.

title: Mr. Consistency: Raiders’ Adam Butler Dominating as a 'Beast'
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—The Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) face a legitimate Super Bowl contender on Sunday as the Buffalo Bills (4-1) and their elite franchise QB, Josh Allen, come to town.
Despite the Bills' home loss to the Patriots in Week 4, the level of competition goes up considerably from the Patriots last week to the Bills this week. Make no mistake, however; the Raiders are looking for an upset of the Bills.
Facing that enormous offensive juggernaut will not be easy, but one underrated Raider is standing out, and according to one NFL executive, he is noticed.
While talking with an NFL executive earlier this week about what people around the NFL are saying and the rumors about the NFL trade deadline moves they may make, he mentioned DT Adam Butler.
He told me, “If the Raiders become sellers at the trade deadline, don’t leave out [Adam] Butler. Spy [ GM John Spytek ] has him on a great deal with I think one year left (he is correct) and that guy is playing like a f---ing beast.”
He elaborated, “I think you got to go back to Richard Seymour before you have a DT for the Raiders that plays that consistent.”
His comments were prophetic. Not since 2011, when Richard Seymour and Tommy Kelly did, have the Raiders had a DT with back-to-back five-sack-or-more seasons. Butler did it in 2023 and 2024 and has been a mainstay of gap integrity, shining even when the Raiders weren’t.
Critics will point out his sack production going down, and that would be true, until you search the numbers and reasons and notice how teams are blocking him, and the way teams are scheming for him.
Either way, he is the most consistent Raiders defensive tackle, and he's far outplaying many of his much higher-paid colleagues in the league, based on where they played and where they were picked.
The pride of Duncanville, Texas, has an enormous football IQ, evidenced by playing at Vanderbilt, and was undrafted.
To go from an undrafted free agent to a nine-year elite veteran is something else, and it tells the story of the player's talent, but there is much more.
The Raiders' new leader, Klint Kubiak, is not one to offer personal praise. He prefers to make everything, good or bad, about the team, and I respect that.
But I asked him to set aside his personal preference for talking about the team and reflect on Butler's high level of play and production. He was more than willing to accommodate and praise the Commodore from Vanderbilt.
"Yeah, great question. I think AB [Adam Butler] just from the start has been such a leader here, just the way that he works, the type of professional that he is, and I think the guy's true character sticks out when you're when you're playing at the end of the game, you're down multiple scores, and look no further than his character showing up, making plays."
Butler won a Super Bowl in New England with Tom Brady. The greatest player of all time and now a partial owner, Tom Brady has no bigger supporter in this building than Butler.
Yesterday, in the locker room, I asked Butler about helping Brady institute the mentality that every year in the Silver and Black building is all about Super Bowls.
A mentality the two share. Butler was honest.
“Taking that mentality (Super Bowl or Bust) and trying to infect these younger players and get them to see the bigger picture, like is really what it is all about. That’s what I am all about. I try to do that on a daily basis, and that is why they see me as a leader.”

title: Three Storylines I'm Watching Most in Raiders' Matchup vs. Bills
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders look to end their losing streak at two games with a win over the Buffalo Bills at home on Sunday. Las Vegas is in the middle of a stretch of games against four of the league's best teams. The next two weeks will be pivotal.
The Raiders have one of the toughest schedules in the league, but they have no time and too many corrections to make to worry about their opponent. Las Vegas must look in the mirror if they hope to stop a bad two weeks from continuing.
Below are the storylines I am watching the most on Sunday.
Defensive backs are taught to have a short memory. By the time they reach the professional level, most defensive backs have all but mastered the skill. Yet, few position groups go through the kinds of growing pains that defensive backs do. Las Vegas' young defensive backfield is in the thick of theirs.
I will be watching how well they respond and whether the defensive backfield can eliminate the big plays. If they can't, I will also be watching they handle it.
With No.1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza developing in the background, the Raiders' front office is undoubtedly keeping an eye on its offensive line. Too much has been invested in the rookie to put him behind a questionable offensive line. Tyler Linderbaum has been as advertised.
DJ Glaze has been the unit's most consistent player over the past three seasons. While Kolton Miller has played well overall, some plays make it fair to wonder about his future with the team . Spencer Burford and Jackson Powers-Johnson have been serviceable.
Still, the Raiders' offense is limited overall, putting extra pressure on its offensive line. The unit did not allow a sack with Cousins throwing the ball over 50 times in Week 5. They allowed several sacks and even more pressures in Week 6, making it nearly impossible for the unit to establish a rhythm.
One of the top storylines I will be watching most on Sunday is not just how well the Raiders' offensive line plays, but how well Cousins moves around the pocket. When he has done so, as he did during the fourth quarter in Week 5, the Raiders' offense moved well.
The same goes for Mendoza's brief performance. When the rookie moved around in the pocket, the passing lanes opened up significantly. Part of football, and any sport, is working with what you have. Las Vegas has deficiencies along its line.
A quarterback who moves the pocket, even a little, will help a ton. A quarterback who cannot move behind an offensive line that is outnumbered is not sustainable. Las Vegas must find a way to move the ball with extra offensive linemen and tight ends on the field.
Las Vegas' defense is built to stop the run, but it faced several mobile quarterbacks who throw the ball well. This has shaped their approach to games, since their defensive backfield is a well-known vulnerability. Las Vegas has been unable to stop the pass, which has made it hard to stop the run.
During the past two weeks, once the Raiders' secondary allowed one too many big completions of size, importance, or both, Las Vegas adjusted, leaving running lanes open. Yet,the problem hasn't been only the secondary. The Raiders' normally stout run defense has been shaky.
Las Vegas' defense allowed the Los Angeles Chargers and New Orleans Saints to have success on the ground, but only in the past two weeks has the unit allowed such big runs and holes for running backs to run through.
This Sunday against the Bills, I will be watching to see whether they can make Buffalo one-dimensional. Even if they cannot do so completely, they have to do a better job of eliminating one aspect of the opponent's offense.
The Kansas City Chiefs and New England Patriots ran and passed the ball well against Las Vegas' defense. The unit has to stop one, or this Sunday's result will likely mirror the past two weeks. These past two weeks have only confirmed that this Raiders team is led by its defense.
Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard knows his unit has a lot to improve upon after five games. Leonard and the Raiders' coaching staff are gradually developing a team loaded with young, talented, but inexperienced players at several critical positions.
“You got to prioritize. Let's just fix this. Let's just fix this. We got to fix – anything else, can't just fix these 10 things. Focus on one thing at a time, and there's a lot. They did a good job, credit to the Patriots. But we've played good football this year, so we just got to focus on us,” Leonard said before practice on Thursday.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: ‘It Starts With Me.': How Kubiak, Raiders Can Improve Against Bills
full_text:
Five games into the regular season, the Las Vegas Raiders have already exceeded preseason expectations. They are certainly a better team than last fall, but challenges remain, as shown in their 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots.
The team came out flat and played as such last weekend. It wasn’t pretty, as you could imagine, and there were missed opportunities for players and coaches to take advantage of from Sunday’s loss. In his first year as Raiders head coach, Klint Kubiak took responsibility for a defeat that resembled much of the last few years.
First, you have to give credit where it is due: Kubiak is an innovative coach who molds the offense to fit his personnel. He has done a great job using his star tight ends, Michael Mayer and Brock Bowers, to their strengths, and the offense has reaped the benefits one way or another.
However, Kubiak is a first-time head coach, and the struggles and missteps will happen early on. You could argue that it happened on Sunday, and he stated earlier this week that he admits fault and failed to have a better game plan against the Patriots' defensive attack, which featured heavy, consistent pressure.
“I give a lot of credit to New England. They did an excellent job,” Kubiak admitted on Monday. “I just didn't have a good plan for our guys. We didn't execute well. We got behind early, and we weren't able to get the run game going. There's just a lot of reasons that that game didn't work out, and it starts with me.”
Kubiak also admitted that he needs to give rookie running back Mike Washington more opportunities. Washington had one carry for five yards, and when you watch him on tape, he fits gap-blocking schemes well and is very comfortable working within this style of play.
Another player who didn’t get enough opportunities was Mayer, as Kubiak said as much, though they needed his blocking presence in seven-man protections as New England dialed up blitz after blitz.
“Didn't give him enough opportunities. We gave him one early in the game,” Kubiak said. “I think they had a penalty on. So, I think overall, that was a game of a lot of seven-man protections that he was involved on. But at the end of the day, it's my job to get all players involved. So, when they are not involved, then it falls on me."
Against the Buffalo Bills, Kubiak must do better at getting guys like Washington and Mayer involved. If recent history told us anything, it is that these players will get their touches, especially coming back home with a chance to upset the AFC East leader.
Jared Feinberg, a native of western North Carolina, has written about NFL football for nearly a decade. He has contributed to several national outlets and is now part of our On SI team as an NFL team reporter. Jared graduated from UNC Asheville with a bachelor's degree in mass communications and later pursued his master's degree at UNC Charlotte. You can follow Jared Feinberg on Twitter at @JRodNFLDraft

title: How Raiders Can Navigate Ashton Jeanty's Increased Reps
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are entering Week 6 on a two-game skid after losing to the New England Patriots 45-17.
Following a 3-0 start to the season, the vibes in Las Vegas were exponentially high. However, the consecutive losses have brought the team back down to earth. Another reason the Raiders' success has stalled is running back Ashton Jeanty's health, which has kept him from playing at his highest level. During his press conference on Wednesday, head coach Klint Kubiak provided an update on Jeanty's status.
Kubiak was also asked if the reported internal discussions about Jeanty potentially being rested this week had transpired. The 39-year-old coach bluntly responded, “He's playing."
Barring any setbacks in practice this week, fans of the Silver and Black should expect the 22-year-old running back to suit up and start on Sunday against the Buffalo Bills. In last week's loss , Jeanty had 10 carries for 27 yards and three receptions for 50 yards. The receiving output was promising, but averaging 2.7 yards per carry shows what Jeanty is battling through.
Some of his lackluster production has been due to the offensive line, but it's clear that Jeanty isn't 100 percent healthy.
I'm not an injury expert by any means, but as long as Jeanty continues to play with these injuries, they won't heal. These ailments will be something the former 2025 first-round pick will deal with this season if he doesn't sit out any games. Or, even worse, Jeanty aggravates one of the injuries and worsens the condition, causing him to serve a stint on the IR.
Since the next two games are against Super Bowl-caliber opponents - Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams - and the Raiders are unlikely to win either game, this coaching staff should seriously consider giving Jeanty a two-week rest to heal. That would allow Jeanty to return in Week 8 against the New York Jets.
Las Vegas is still in a relatively good spot, but if its losing streak extends to four games and one of Jeanty's pre-existing injuries worsens, this team could be in major trouble. The Raiders are better off resting Jeanty for multiple weeks and having him as healthy as possible down the stretch.
