title: Breaking Down the Latest Dolphins Practice Squad Moves
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins' latest practice squad moves was most noteworthy for the player they let go than the one they brought back.
The team announced Tuesday morning they had signed quarterback Brady Cook to the practice and released running back Jarquez Hunter to make room.
The move with Cook should have been expected (and was predicted here) because the Dolphins need three quarterbacks, even if one of them is on the practice squad.
Cook was on the 53-man roster for the first four games before he was waived Saturday to make room for defensive tackle Kenneth Grant being activated off injured reserve.
The Dolphins did not a minor gamble in another team claiming Cook off waivers, though it seemed pretty safe that it wouldn't happen.
While it's always a possibility that he will be brought back to the practice squad, this move seems to end the Jarquez Hunter experiment that began when he was acquired in a summer trade from the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for veteran wide receiver.
A fourth-round pick out of Auburn in 2025, Hunter represented the kind of player the Dolphins have been looking to investigate and evaluate as they look for hidden gems to carry along beyond this season.
But Hunter never made enough of an impression to earn playing time in Miami.
While he didn't have a chance for the 53-man roster because he was acquired the day before the preseason finale, Hunter saw training camp running back Carlos Washington Jr. overtake him on the depth chart, with Washington getting the call the last two games with injuries at running back.
And then it really was over for Hunter when the Dolphins claimed rookie running back Kaytron Allen off waivers from the New Orleans Saints late last week.
While the move didn't pan out, acquiring Hunter still was a good move because it was a no-risk deal with the potential for good value, and that's because Atwell wasn't going to make the 53-man roster coming out of training camp. He was going to be released, and the trade actually took the Dolphins off the hook for the small guaranteed salary they had committed to Atwell.
Hunter panning out would have been a great bonus. That it didn't happen was no big deal, but it again proved the idea that we've repeated many times about tempering expectations whenever the Dolphins bring in a player who basically was discarded by another organization.

title: What the Week 5 Film Told Us About the Miami Dolphins
full_text:
In the Miami Dolphins' 31-24 loss against the Cincinnati Bengals, a poor mixture of talent and scheme was the difference, but the youth continued to shine. Let's take a look at some of the film from the Week 5 game, along with some key takeaways.
Joe Burrow picked apart the Dolphins’ defense underneath in Week 5. Pending Monday Night Football, he was sixth in EPA per dropback on dropbacks of less than 2.5 seconds and eighth in the same stat on throws of fewer than 10 air yards.
pic.twitter.com/KXcIrAzve5
Burrow was decisive against a defense that dedicated their second- and third-level defenders to stopping over-the-top throws to Ja’Marr Chase or Tee Higgins. On this play, Miami’s quarters look ends up playing similar to a prevent coverage, with the linebackers dropping too deep, leaving Chase Brown open for a ten-yard gain.
It’s a perfect storm of miscues for Miami right now. Their umbrella coverages put too much stress on the linebackers, who haven’t been up to snuff in coverage. Meanwhile, with Chop Robinson receiving chip help and double teams throughout this game, the Dolphins don’t have someone up front who can force the issue. It’s a marriage of below-average personnel with a scheme that’s sticking with the philosophy of limiting possessions, even when the quarterback is more than willing to take the checkdown.
Much like the defensive struggles, Miami’s passing offense garners blame for just about everyone involved. Bobby Slowik couldn’t consistently scheme targets open, the receivers struggled to create separation, and Malik Willis made several back-breaking errors.
Slowik’s designs clearly draw inspiration from his former boss, Mike McDaniel. The issue is, some of these concepts already had outworn their welcome, and without Tyreek Hill or Jaylen Waddle, they’re simply not an efficient way to use your eligible receivers.
pic.twitter.com/1NRVDNxXdi
On too many occasions, there are only two or three receivers out on routes, and in this case, it’s paired with a long-developing play-fake. On second-and-10, Cincinnati’s backers are able to drop into the intermediate window, and Chris Bell can’t sufficiently break the press.
Regardless of the long-term outlook for Bell or Kevin Coleman Jr., Miami does not have the quality of pass-catchers right now to make these looks a staple. To make things easier on Willis, it may be in their best interest to opt for quantity and attack more of the field with their route designs.
pic.twitter.com/sL0MxXtmgO
This doesn’t absolve Willis, who made multiple abysmal decisions in this game. His process has been slow, he hasn’t been willing to move off of his downfield reads, and his awareness of his immediate surroundings has made already poor situations worse.
One of the few positives from this game was that the rookie class continues to show out. This was easily the best game of Chris Johnson’s young career. On top of a forced fumble, I was particularly impressed by a pass-rush rep where he fought through the blocks of three different players to pressure Joe Burrow.
pic.twitter.com/s2uzbkfF7q
Kadyn Proctor and Will Kacmarek also have continued to showcase their physicality. On a toss play to Malik Washington, Proctor was able to cut off Dexter Lawrence while Kacmarek made a crucial crack block on Boye Mafe.
pic.twitter.com/3arYuNtlT4
This class already has shown considerable promise, and if they keep it up, they’ll set the foundation for this Dolphins team by the time they’re ready to compete.
Tyler DeSena is currently a journalism student at the University of Central Florida. Prior to joining Dolphins On SI in 2026, DeSena worked with dolphinstalk.com, and created independent social media content on X, YouTube and TikTok.

title: 3 Winners & 2 Losers From Vikings' Pre-Bye Week Performance
full_text:
While many fans, players, and coaches hate the idea of an early NFL bye, the 5-0 Vikings may be very thankful for theirs. The team has battled through its fair share of adversity on its undefeated start, including a mounting list of injuries and an offense that is only beginning to find its identity.
Still, several players have stood out for their consistency and performance, while others have disappointed early on.
Here are my three biggest winners and two glaring losers for the Vikings through five games.
A Vikings kicker getting this much hype means one thing: get ready for a nerve-racking NFC Championship Game. Kidding (hopefully).
If we’re being honest, every longtime Vikings observer is terrified of Reichard’s “inevitable” Minnesota moment of misery shared by so many kickers in franchise history. So far, there’s plenty of reason to believe he may just be the one to change the narrative.
His 34 straight successful field goals, dating back to last season, put him just ten shy of the 44-kick record held by the legendary Adam Vinatieri. We even have fans throwing his name out in MVP talks to start the season. Heck, even former Vikings linebacker Anthony Barr mentioned the idea of Reichard securing the honor on the Bent Outta Shape Podcast he hosts with former teammate Eric Kendricks (h/t: @BentOuttaShape_).
Could Vikings kicker Will Reichard win MVP?! 🤔 New episode of BOS is out now 💯 pic.twitter.com/ZBEJoXhtgj
Reichard’s 53 points currently place him third in the NFL behind Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (54) and Colts kicker Spencer Shrader (58).
The Jauan Jennings situation seems to be reaching a boiling point after he showed visible frustration on the sideline Sunday in New Orleans. His two receptions for only nine yards on five targets through four games played are frustrating enough, but the film is showing that he’s actually getting open fairly often (H/t: Janik Eckardt).
Kyler inexplicably turning down an open Jauan Jennings in the endzone two plays before the Myles Price fumble pic.twitter.com/zw9rjAMwzi
His slow start sparked trade speculation early on, with his former team, the 49ers, looking like a realistic partner. Hopefully, the Vikings and Jennings can work things out so he can build his connection with quarterback Kyler Murray. After all, the Vikings desperately need depth at wide receiver.
Despite missing almost two full games with a sprained ankle and catching only one touchdown from his starting QB, Jefferson’s three receiving TDs in five games have already surpassed his two-TD total from 2025. I know, not exactly a high bar to clear, but it's clear Jefferson is truly enjoying football again.
His touchdown against the Saints in his home state of Louisiana showed all the typical traits of a classic Jefferson highlight: a jaw-dropping catch, an endzone Griddy, and a sideline celebration with his teammates .
Whole sideline was hyped for the Kyler to Jettas TD. pic.twitter.com/rQfaBLPckT
The Vikings' offense still has room to grow, but it seems like the Justin Jefferson we all know and love is fully back in action.
Is it punching down to say a sixth-round rookie RB has been a disappointment? Maybe, but it’s hard to ignore how rough Demond Claiborne’s 2026 start has been , despite having more opportunities than many expected.
Training camp showed Claiborne’s explosive speed and potential, but it also gave a laundry list of reasons he’d be unlikely to see the field early. Ball security, pass blocking, catching, and vision were all concerns this summer.
The rookie was listed as inactive in Week 1, but Jordan Mason's injured reserve stint opened the door for him beginning in Week 2. Still, the team cycled through several RB additions and even placed recent signing DeeJay Dallas above Claiborne on the depth chart. When he did get opportunities, Claiborne often looked unprepared for the speed of the NFL game, missing a wide-open gap in Tampa that could have led to a TD with his blazing speed (h/t: Patrick Siepman).
Demond Claiborne struggled in the preseason and missed this massive hole yesterday. Should the Vikings try and trade for a RB? pic.twitter.com/mzurfKCTd2
Claiborne is physically gifted but still has a long way to go to process NFL defenses.
The third-year pass rusher did not register a sack in Week 5 and is still third in the league in sacks and first in the NFC with 5.5 through five games. Dallas Turner, who is still only 23, has been a key piece of the Vikings' dominant defensive start .
Some fans showed hesitation about Turner’s increased role this season after the team traded Jonathan Greenard to the Eagles during April’s draft. That was understandable, given Greenard’s impact over two seasons and Turner’s early-career inconsistencies. So far, Turner has put any of those concerns to rest in 2026.
The Vikings seem to have found their next in a long line of dominant pass rushers.

Jason Harmon grew up a diehard Vikings fan and has been doing Vikings content and coverage since 2023. He is the Vikings Content Curator for Sleeper and is a host on Purple Daily’s in-season spinoff podcast “Before I Die”. Jason and his family moved to the Twin Cities from Arizona in 2025 as he started covering the team full time.

title: 3 Vikings Firmly on Thin Ice During the Week 6 Bye (Josh Metellus Is Becoming an Issue)
full_text:
The Week 6 bye couldn't have come sooner for a Vikings team dealing with a long list of injuries. Despite those ailments, the Purple and Gold are 5-0 and sitting atop the NFC North as they reach the second half of their bye week.
Although the Vikings are undefeated, there are still issues to be addressed . While some players are thriving this season, others are struggling to make a positive impact when on the field.
Some of the Vikings' players are on thin ice after multiple weeks of ineffectiveness. The clock is ticking on them to find their role on the team. If they can't, they may end up losing snaps or even their job on the team
Minnesota's big free-agent wide receiver signing this offseason has been a flop this season. In the team's first five games, Jauan Jennings has played 201 offensive snaps and has only caught two of the five passes thrown his way for nine yards. Not exactly worth the $8 million cash he's earning this season, per Spotrac.
There are already rumblings that Jennings could potentially be on the trade block since he has struggled to contribute to the Vikings' passing attack this year. Minnesota would be silly not to listen to offers to try to recoup an asset before the trade deadline. Needless to say, don't be surprised if he's traded, assuming that he remains on thin ice.
The Vikings prepared to limit the defensive snaps of veteran safety Harrison Smith by drafting Miami defensive back Jakobe Thomas in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft and signing undrafted free agent Jacob Thomas out of James Madison.
While both those rookies are growing and developing, Minnesota has played Josh Metellus on every defensive snap this season. In 295 defensive snaps and four special teams snaps, he has earned a putrid Pro Football Focus grade of 40.2 , ranking him 90th out of 96 qualifying safeties this year.
Metellus has played well in previous seasons, but hasn't found his footing in 2026. Minnesota will be patient with the versatile defender because they know he can rise above the recent struggles, but until one of the Thomas rookies is ready for a bigger role, he will need to be a workhorse .
Sometimes the hype around a player gets so out of hand that they can't possibly live up to the expectations. The Vikings brought back Aaron Jones Sr. on a reworked deal and have Jordan Mason returning to injured reserve after the bye
The Vikings drafted Demond Claiborne in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft to hopefully become a contributor for Minnesota. Instead, Claiborne and DeeJay Dallas have been unable to share the burden of rushing the ball with Jones.
Claiborne isn't in danger of losing his job, but his ineffectiveness could lead the Vikings to look for a more reliable third option in the backfield . So far, he has run the ball six times for 13 yards and caught two passes for eight yards while only playing 18 offensive snaps.

title: Revisiting 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Five Weeks Into the Season (Has Flores's Defense Exceeded Expectations?)
full_text:
Before the Vikings even took a snap, I wrote about three bold predictions that could make or break the 2026 season. Some still have life; another is already buried six feet under. It's easy to throw guesses at the wall and see what sticks, but it's another thing to confront those and even admit defeat.
The 5-0 Vikings have surprised many and shocked even more with a perfect start to the campaign, so let's see how close (or far) I sit with these preseason predictions as their Week 6 bye continues .
Get back up off the floor, cut the laughter, and hear me out on this one.
The Vikings really headed into the season looking folks straight in the eye and said, "We're starting a pair of Kwesi Adofo-Mensah Day 3 picks and a former UFL player up front, and we're going to win." So you may forgive me if I didn't have the utmost confidence in Levi Drake Rodriguez, Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, Jalen Redmond and—oh yeah—a pair of rookies who didn't exactly dominate the preseason.
And yet, here we are six weeks into the season .
The Vikings currently have the NFL's fifth-best run defense, allowing just 86.6 yards per game, and clearly a far cry from a bottom-five unit. And while they almost certainly won't drop to that level, their toughest days still lie ahead. The defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit still has yet to face Jahmyr Gibbs (twice), Bijan Robinson, Jonathan Taylor, Christian McCaffrey, and 2025's rushing champion James Cook this season.
I don't think this hot take will ring true come Week 18, but I also don't think they'll remain in the top 10 after this gauntlet either.
Hey, now we're talking. Despite featuring a line with Christian Darrisaw and Brian O'Neill, this prediction was shaping up to be mostly true until Jackson suffered a season-ending injury in Week 4. Up until that point, he had just two allowed pressures on the year, and zero quarterback hits or sacks. Not too shabby.
After an up-and-down rookie season plagued by a wrist injury, Jackson showed enough of what made him a first-round pick. But now, with two seasons cut short due to injury, he will also face an uphill battle to continue his impressive trajectory.
Meanwhile, Darrisaw remains as talented as they come, but now has a sixth straight season of missing at least a game due to injury . O'Neill is steady as usual and may take this year's crown as the Vikings' top protector.
This one still has some juice, and at 5-0, anything and everything is on the table. The division will stay tight all the way to the finish, and despite the perfect record, the Vikings have just a two-game lead over every other team in the NFC North. So their playoff seed, barring a repeat of 2016, could be anything from one to seven at this point.
Initially, my biggest worry about making the playoffs in 2026 was Kyler Murray getting off to a slow start, and sure enough, his start with the Vikings took off about as fast as Linval Joseph's 40-time. I recall wondering how he might mesh with head coach Kevin O'Connell.
But despite the rough start in Green Bay and another dud against Tampa Bay, Murray has strung together some really nice weeks as of late, completing 76% of his passes over the last two weeks. O'Connell has also adjusted and run more shotgun against Miami than he ever has before.
Is an NFC Championship Game in the cards? Absolutely, but the defense's health and Murray's ascension will be key.

title: 3 Free-Agent TEs for Vikings to Sign as T.J. Hockenson Injury Remains a Concern During Bye Week
full_text:
The Vikings were already hurting at tight end entering Week 5, but when T.J. Hockenson left the game with a suspected concussion against the Saints, that situation got even worse for head coach Kevin O'Connell. As of Thursday morning, there have been no updates on Hockenson's condition, and even though the Vikings have extra time due to their bye , the last thing they need is another offensive concern.
After all, Josh Oliver has been on injured reserve with a potentially season-ending biceps tear. He was typically used as a blocking specialist as well as a sneaky option in the passing attack. Not having him available is tough, and the TE-related struggles will compound if Hockenson misses extended time.
Against the Saints, the Vikings used a combination of Gavin Bartholomew and Ben Yurosek at tight end. Bartholomew took on the role of the receiving tight end , while Yurosek was more of a blocker in the offense.
If O'Connell isn't sure he can trust Bartholomew and Yurosek if Hockenson is sidelined indefinitely, the Vikings need to explore other options to provide depth and talent at the position.
Here are three potential reinforcement options for O'Conell & Co. to consider.
A Swiss Army knife of a player, Taysom Hill is a player who could do a lot of things for the Vikings. While with the Saints, he was known for being a tight end, quarterback, receiver, or special teams player when he was needed.
Hill is 36 years old, so he wouldn't be a long-term asset for Minnesota, but that's not what they need him to be. The Vikings would want him to run routes and be a receiver, which he has shown the ability to do over his nine previous NFL seasons.
Catching 110 passes for 1,034 yards and 11 touchdowns is great, but he also has 489 rushing attempts for 2,551 yards and 34 TDs. However, due to his age and with his complicated skill set, the Vikings may be looking for a more traditional and complete tight end. Still, it's worth considering.
Will Dissly is six years younger than Hill, but has eight years of NFL experience. Although he is better known for his time with the Seahawks, he spent the last two seasons with the Chargers, playing 24 games in which he caught 61 passes for 578 yards and two touchdowns.
Dissly fits more of the traditional TE role, like Hockenson. He catches about 80% of his targets and could be a reliable target for starting Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray if Hockenson can't suit up.
A six-foot-four, 265-pound tight end, Dissly has the size to be a blocker if needed as well. He posted run-block and pass-block grades of 64.1 and 74.3 , respectively, according to Pro Football Focus last season.
Even if Minnesota only wants a temporary player to fill in until Hockenson returns, it makes sense to take a look at the former NFC West standout.
Bringing a former Vikings tight end back to Minnesota can make a lot of sense. Drafted 157th overall in 2018, Tyler Conklin spent his first four seasons with the Purple and Gold before moving to the Jets, Chargers and Lions before becoming a free agent in 2026.
At one time, Conklin was a hot commodity. After leaving the Vikings, he signed a three-year deal with the Jets worth $21 million and played out his entire contract. Last season, his one-year deal with Detroit was worth $1.3 million, so it isn't unfathomable to imagine he'd be a relatively inexpensive player to sign six weeks into the season.
Conklin could be an interesting practice-squad stash who could be elevated if needed while Hockenson is out. He could help Bartholomew and Yurosek without taking away from their development and growth, providing security and depth in the meantime.

title: Vikings Week 6 Mailbag: Trade Targets, Kyler Murray's Outlook, Kirk Cousins Prediction & More
full_text:
The 5-0 Vikings are spending this week resting and recovering with an early Week 6 bye , but we’re still here to talk about the Purple and Gold in this week’s mailbag. As usual, I took to X to ask for your questions and bold predictions, and was not left disappointed.
Let’s dive in to what's on the fan base's mind halfway through October.
To submit your questions, reach out to Jason Harmon on X .
This is an interesting name I’ve seen pop up recently, admittedly not for the Vikings.
Jonathan Taylor in purple would be an absolute blast, but I don’t see it happening for a few reasons. First, current starting back Aaron Jones is having an impressive season. I’ll admit, I wasn’t sure what he’d have left in the tank at age 31, but he’s pushed through injury to keep the running game afloat (h/t: NFL).
Aaron Jones runs it in and puts the Vikings out in front 🔥 @MINvsNO on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/O0wqkr3LTP
Jones's 610 yards on the ground are tied for the sixth-most in the league. Where the Vikings could use help is in the rest of the running back room, given the current lack of effective depth. Luckily, Jordan Mason seems set to return from the injured reserve soon.
The trade cost a team would have to spend on the recently extended Taylor would be more than Minnesota could invest, given the number of holes the team faces this offseason .  His cap hit of $16,187,000 would also far exceed Minnesota’s current cap space of $5,972,901 per OverTheCap .
While there are ways to possibly make it work, that would only increase the cost and effort for something that isn't currently a glaring need.
This may be a bold take, but I think there’s a decent chance that anything short of multiple playoff wins ends with Kyler Murray playing elsewhere in 2027, and it is in no way a slight on him.
If Murray continues to grow and succeed with the Vikings this year, he’ll almost certainly earn a hefty free-agent deal this offseason, a reminder of the no-tag clause wisely inserted into his contract.  Last Sunday was a great example of how his accuracy and mobility can still help a team win (h/t: Ian Hartitz)
Next-Gen Stats fastest ball carrier speed in Week 5: Kyler Murray (20.82 MPH) Also the fastest ball carrier speed by a QB this season. pic.twitter.com/GSZ61DBqzc
If his price compares to that of, say, Mac Jones, head coach Kevin O’Connell and general manager Nolan Teasley may be left with a dilemma: Run it back with the QB you just found success with, despite having to adjust your offense? Or spend similar money on a QB who fits your preferred offensive system?
My gut tells me O’Connell would lean toward the latter. Murray has shown flashes, and I'm confident he will only get better, but we still haven't seen how the marriage holds up against the league's best opponents.
I’ve seen a few different calculations of Will Reichard’s 2026 scoring pace, and my personal calculations come to 180. His 53 points through five games come out to 10.6 points per game. Multiply that by 17 games, and you get a pace of 180.2 points for the fan-favorite kicker.
Either way, it's incredibly impressive and would put him just six points shy of Tomlinson’s record of 186. It would also pass Seahawks kicker Jason Meyers (171 in 2025) for the most points in a season by a kicker.
He’s also on pace for a whopping 180 total points which would be second most in NFL history (LaDanian Tomlinson had 186 in 2006) and 9 more than the kicking record held by Jason Meyers (171 in 2025). https://t.co/u5bQlxn8oA
Now, can a kicker win NFL MVP? Yes! It happened in a strike-shortened nine-game 1982 season, as Washington kicker Mark Moseley took home the MVP honors with a 41.7% vote share. Moseley went 20-of-21 on field goals and 16-of-19 on extra points for a total of 76 points, per Pro-Football-Reference.
Needless to say, some unique circumstances were at play, and while we’re unlikely to see that again, Reichard may be one of the few kickers who could actually make an MVP case.
On top of the questions, I asked for bold takes, and this one is a great one!
I think it would be hard to pull off in the middle of this week, since Kirk Cousins seems to be starting for the Raiders against the Bills this weekend, but I wouldn’t rule it out completely by the trade deadline. I put the overall chances at less than 5%, but a number of things could happen to make it more likely.
First, the Vikings would need serious concerns about Murray depending on what happens against the Colts in Week 7 and the Lions in Week 8 to even consider it. They also host the Bills in Week 9 for Monday Night Football on Nov. 9, the night before the trade deadline.
If Murray completely fails to show up in those games, the Vikings may consider their options.
The Raiders would also likely need to lose at least three of their next four games ahead of the deadline before even considering moving on from Cousins, who has had an impressive start to the season (h/t: NFL).
Kirk Cousins ➡️ Brock Bowers for a Raiders touchdown! @LVvsNE on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/imBWPFJpvw
After hosting the Bills, the Raiders then host the Rams, face the Jets at MetLife Stadium before heading west to face the Niners, all before Nov. 10.
While I think a Cousins trade is unlikely,  it's not impossible.

title: 5 Roster Concerns Vikings Must Address Before Bye Week Is Over
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are fortunate to be 5-0 entering their bye week. An anemic offense has been helped out immensely by a stout defense and excellent special teams play, but that formula will not last all season long.
There are some issues that the Vikings need to address during their bye week to stay competitive for the rest of the season. Some of those changes can be made internally, while others may need to come from free agency or a trade.
Let's take a look at some areas Minnesota needs to evaluate while they have no game in Week 6. Unsurprisingly, most of these areas are on the offensive side of the ball.
Aaron Jones Sr. has done an admirable job carrying the running back position while Jordan Mason was on injured reserve healing from thumb surgery. Jones played through a knee injury during that time and got little to no help from rookie Demond Claiborne and veteran DeeJay Dallas.
Mason can return in Week 7 and take some of the pressure off Jones, but that is still a lot of wear and tear on the veteran's back. Unless head coach Kevin O'Connell thinks he can get some help out of Claiborne or Dallas, the Vikings may need to look for an established rusher to add to the mix for the remainder of the season.
Health has been an issue for the Vikings this season. Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison both missed time due to injuries, but it is the ineffectiveness of Jauan Jennings that is truly hurting Minnesota.
While Jefferson and Addison are great players, having a third wide receiver option would be a great benefit for quarterback Kyler Murray, but Jennings hasn't been that guy, and neither have Tai Felton or Myles Price.
Unless someone can step into that role, Minnesota will have to continue relying on tight ends or putting a lot of focus on their top two receivers, which isn't ideal for the offense.
T.J. Hockenson left the game against the Saints with a possible concussion and is currently in protocol. With blocking tight end Josh Oliver on IR with a torn bicep, Gavin Bartholomew and Ben Yurosek are left to pick up the slack.
Bartholomew and Yurosek looked good against New Orleans, so there might be enough trust in them not to look outside Minnesota for help, but nonetheless, it is a situation that general manager Nolan Teasley will need to keep an eye on.
Starting left tackle Christian Darrisaw missed last week's game due to a concussion, and starting left guard Donovan Jackson suffered a torn meniscus and will miss the remainder of the season. Those injuries raise concern for the left side of the offensive line.
Ryan Van Demark filled in at left tackle and Joe Huber covered left guard on Sunday. They held their own, but can they be trusted if they need to fill in for an extended time? That's the biggest question facing the offensive line.
The Vikings' defense has been amazing this year, but the team has an issue at safety. Veteran Harrison Smith is playing a much smaller number of snaps than in the past, which puts pressure on his teammates to play at a high level.
Josh Metellus has a Pro Football Focus grade of 40.2 this season. He is ranked No. 91 out of 96 qualifying safeties, which is definitely not good for a player who has been on the field for all 295 defensive snaps that Minnesota has played this year.
Minnesota has options at the position, but some are untested. Jacob Thomas and Jakobe Thomas are unproven, but could use an opportunity to see if they can help out the defensive backs until Metellus can get back on track.

title: 3 Vikings Changes I'd Make Over the Bye If I Were Kevin O'Connell
full_text:
The Vikings are undefeated at the bye, and it now provides the perfect break to implement a few changes going forward. While 5-0 is an impressive feat, things haven't always been sunshine and rainbows, and head coach Kevin O'Connell needs to take this extra time to fix a few troublesome spots.
After a perfect start, here's how I would handle the bye week if I were O'Connell, starting with a problem on offense.
With just two catches on the year, it's no secret things haven't been going according to plan with the addition of Jennings. Brought in to round out what was supposed to be one of the best receiving trios  in the league, Jennings is now at the forefront of NFL trade rumors after a less-than-ideal start with Minnesota.
While I do think the Vikings eventually move on from their prized free agent, I also don't think they should be in any rush to do it. The deadline is still weeks away, and if O'Connell and company can salvage this thing at all, it's going to happen over the bye. There are nearly a dozen other Vikings with more receiving yards than Jennings this season, so if they Vikings do truly value his skillset, there's no reason he can't get a few designed plays each game.
If Jennings comes out in Week 7 against the Indianapolis Colts without any obvious role in the offense, though, he's probably on his way out. It just doesn't make sense for either side to stay if neither is benefiting from the relationship.
After T.J. Hockenson exited just two plays into last week's win over the Saints, Bartholomew stepped up, and the drop-off was virtually non-existent . Maybe it's time the Vikings start to give their potential future starter some more looks.
Outside of his Week 4 13-catch eruption, Hockenson has just 10 catches for 83 yards in his other starts. That's certainly not unproductive, but after seeing Bartholomew notch five catches and what could have been another long touchdown if he were an inch or two taller, it's easy to see his role expanding in the future. With Hockenson turning 30 on an expiring deal, there's no guarantee he'll return to Minnesota in 2027. If the Vikings think that Bartholomew could be his successor, the litmus test couldn't have gone better, and it might be time to start splitting time.
Hockenson is currently in the protocol, but regardless of whether he clears in time for Week 7, O'Connell should try and work toward a 50/50 split between his two pass-catching tight ends.
The duo of Harrison Smith and Joshua Metellus have been the weak link on the otherwise dominant Vikings defense, and at 5-0, it's probably time the Vikings get serious about the position. Of the 96 safeties graded by Pro Football Focus , Smith and Metellus rank 95th and 91st respectively . They both still provide value, with Smith's brains and Metellus' downhill attacking, but adding a ball-hawking safety via trade may be the final piece to this defensive puzzle.
There are plenty of bad teams who may be sellers at the deadline, including the Los Angeles Chargers or Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and adding Derwin James Jr. or Antoine Winfield Jr. would be huge upgrades. Still, if O'Connell and general manager Nolan Teasley agree that the price isn't right for a trade, they'll have to start to get more production out of that group somehow. Potentially, one or both of the Thomas rookies could be ready for an increased snap count?
Either way, the already elite defense could become generational with some upgraded safety play, and the coaching staff needs to identify a different path forward.

title: Ranking 3 Vikings Most Likely to be Traded Before the Deadline
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 entering their Week 6 bye. Despite being undefeated, there is a lot of improvement that can be made on the roster to not only improve their situation this season but also prepare for the future.
There is no urgency for the Vikings to make a move before the November 10 trade deadline, but if a deal can be made that makes sense for both teams, it would be silly for Minnesota to dismiss the possibility of a change.
The defense is playing amazingly, and special teams have been great, but there could be some changes on offense for the Purple and Gold. Head coach Kevin O'Connell needs to find an offensive spark to complement the other phases of the game.
Last season, Jauan Jennings was a major offensive weapon for the San Francisco 49ers. In 15 games, he caught 55 passes for 643 yards and nine touchdowns. That production gave the Vikings hope that he could be a significant contributor for Minnesota this season.
Instead, Jennings has been a non-factor in 2026. In four games, he has caught two passes for nine yards on five targets while playing 201 offensive snaps. That production does not match his $8 million contract that Minnesota paid for his services this season.
The Vikings could attempt to get some kind of asset for him before the trade deadline instead of continuing to put him on the field. ESPN and NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport stated on "The Pat McAfee Show" that he " wouldn't be surprised " to see interest in him on the trade market.
Trading him would save Minnesota about $2.6 million against the salary cap.
Let's be honest, the Vikings probably don't want to trade away Jordan Addison. Minnesota announced that they will use the fifth-year option on his rookie contract, which will cost the team approximately $18 million.
If Addison plays on that fifth-year option in Minnesota, the team will need to sign him to a long-term extension to keep him around. Recent extensions for other WR2s around the league have been expensive, and the Vikings might not be willing to fork over around $20 million per year to retain his services.
Minnesota could get a decent draft pick or a quality player for Addison if they trade him. The team would likely rather not ship him out, but there are teams out there who might be willing to make the Vikings an offer they can't refuse.
This preseason, it was unclear how Ivan Pace Jr. would fit into the Vikings' defense . Eric Wilson and Blake Cashman are cemented as the starters, and rookie Jake Golday is working to find his role in Brian Flores' defense.
Pace could be a contributor on another team in need of a defender in the middle. This season, he has played 47 defensive snaps for Minnesota and 113 snaps on special teams, putting him on the field for 160 total snaps in five games played.
The bad part is that Pace has only accumulated 12 combined tackles, with two quarterback pressures and one QB knockdown in those reps. If Minnesota can get a mid-round pick for him, they could give his snaps to Golday and not lose production.

title: What the Vikings' Week 5 Win Changed About Their Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
The Vikings are coming off their most complete game of the season and are now a perfect 5-0 as they head into their Week 6 bye . With the trade deadline less than a month away, the time off will provide the perfect opportunity to examine the needs of the roster.
And as one of the few remaining undefeated teams left, Minnesota will surely be buyers, right?
Despite the unblemished record, there are still plenty of skeptics downplaying the Vikings' perfect start. As of Tuesday afternoon, Minnesota was only tied for the ninth-best Super Bowl odds (+2000)—along with the Bears, Broncos and Patriots. And yet, it's hard to find a team playing better football than the Vikings right now.
Of course, the offense was quite literally the worst in the league early on, and the combined record of the opponents the Vikings have defeated is a lowly 8-17, so there's some fair criticism.
Still, barring another 2016 collapse, the Vikings are well on their way towards a playoff berth and could look to boost the roster via trade over the next few weeks.
After the bye, Minnesota will essentially be at full strength with the likely returns of Jordan Mason, Christian Darrisaw and T.J. Hockenson. Donovan Jackson is the only offensive starter already gone for the year, but finding a starting-caliber guard is typically easier said than done. Reserve lineman Joe Huber has filled in admirably and, given time, could be a solid replacement.
Beyond that, the Vikings don't seem keen on adding another running back unless it's to give him a week-long stay on the practice squad, and Gavin Bartholomew stepped up at tight end in the absence of Josh Oliver. The only logical move appearing to be gaining steam is dealing wide receiver Jauan Jennings, who has just two catches on the year. NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported on Tuesday that he wouldn't be surprised if the buzz increases moving forward.
From @PatMcAfeeShow : In the wake of the Marvin Harrison Jr trade, another WR whose trade market is expected to heat up is #Vikings WR Jauan Jennings. Would a #49ers reunion make sense? pic.twitter.com/DR6mY1OvYb
What was supposed to be the big-ticket free-agent signing (you remember all the Golden State Warriors/Big 3 comparisons), Jennings has instead been a complete afterthought in the Vikings' offense. There are 11 other Vikings with more receiving yards than Jennings after Week 5, and right now he's getting paid a lot of money to just get in some cardio on Sundays.
While moving Jennings for a pick clearly doesn't help the 2026 Vikings, maybe it'll give them the capital to go out and get someone who does.
On defense, the Vikings have been the best unit in the league through five weeks and have very few weaknesses to exploit. One looming issue, however, may be their concerning depth. Minnesota has stayed healthy so far, but if injuries rear their ugly heads, there are a lot of question marks behind the starters.
Eight of the defensive starters have played 80% of the snaps so far (h/t ESPN 's Kevin Seifert), including several untested rookies who haven't needed to step up yet. Caleb Banks, Domonique Orange, Jake Golday and others have played just sparingly, and Minnesota may not be ready to give them the nod just yet.
It's certainly something to watch, and if a key starter goes down, the Vikings may look to add a veteran, especially if they continue their march toward a potential playoff run.
Despite their record suggesting the Vikings should be buyers at the deadline, they will likely sit tight. Injuries haven't ravaged them like certain teams, and general manager Nolan Teasley has seemed very intent on holding onto his 2027 draft picks.
Apologies to the fans hoping for a splash trade, but unless a big injury hits, Jennings might be the only player on the move.

title: The Biggest Decision Kevin O’Connell Got Right vs. Saints (And What It Means Moving Forward)
full_text:
The 5-0 Vikings have certainly been one of the more fascinating teams in the NFL in 2026.
The only other undefeated teams are the 49ers and Chiefs, both widely seen as serious contenders across the league. The Vikings, on the other hand, have raised more questions than answers for some. The squad clearly has a dominant defense and an elite special teams group, but the offense has taken time to find an identity.
Luckily, that seemed to shift against the Saints.
Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell is starting to embrace an offensive identity that often contradicts many of the core principles he had previously set in place, and it may just be the best way to let the offense thrive.
Kyler Murray looked good on Sunday , made even more impressive by the sheer amount of adversity the Vikings’ offense faced due to injuries. The offense took the field without wide receiver Jordan Addison, running back Jordan Mason, left tackle Christian Darrisaw and left guard Donovan Jackson, and they lost tight end T.J. Hockenson to a concussion on the team’s first drive. Not exactly ideal.
Luckily, Justin Jefferson was cleared to play after being labeled a game-time decision with an ankle injury.
Despite all of that adversity, the offense had its most complete day so far, and O’Connell deserves credit for trusting his QB to make it happen.
Murray delivered the ball effectively to ten different pass catchers in the afternoon. Unfortunately for an already frustrated Jauan Jennings, he was the only Viking targeted who didn't catch a pass. Murray, though, was precise, effective, and most importantly, played his game.
His 229 yards through the air and 51 on the ground didn’t fit the traditional O’Connell mold of deep shots and passes over the middle, but they led to an impressive 109.6 passer rating and an offense that flashed exciting potential (H/t: Bring Me the Sports ' Will Ragatz).
Lotta green dots for the Vikings' QB1, who understands the power of stacking completions. And this doesn't even show his 50 rushing yards. pic.twitter.com/UKs6mgKkIo
The Vikings’ passing game certainly didn't get off to a hot start this season. They lost Murray early in Week 1 to a concussion, opening the door for a three-TD day on only 133 yards from Carson Wentz after he was given incredible field position by his defense all game.
Murray returned in Week 3 against the Buccaneers but never quite found his footing. The film often looked awkward, with wide receivers’ breaks often coming after Murray’s internal timer had already sent him scrambling.
But Sunday showed the building blocks for something special, and I can’t overstate how impressive that is given the injury woes on that side of the ball. If the team comes out of the bye with a relatively clean bill of health, their Week 7 matchup against the Colts suddenly gives them a chance to put it all together against a defense that allows the fifth-most yards per game before entering a truly challenging November stretch .
This is where champions are forged. pic.twitter.com/ETt56Vk2fU
O’Connell is progressing and learning to lean into his offense's strengths. If he keeps growing, the sky is the limit for this Vikings squad in 2026.

title: History of the Patriots vs. Jets Matchup Ahead of Week 6 Battle
full_text:
Sunday will be the 135th meeting between the New York Jets and New England (or former Boston) Patriots. The Patriots lead the all-time series, dominating their division rival 77-56-1. The Patriots' 77 total wins over the Jets are the second most of any team over one opponent (second to themselves, with 81 wins over the Buffalo Bills).
Of course, a majority of these wins can be contributed to the Tom Brady-Bill Belichick era, where from 2001 (the year Brady became the starter) to 2024 (Belichick's final year coaching the Patriots) the Patriots went 38-10 over the Jets.
Speaking of the old dynasty, the Jets introduced the league to the legacy of TB12, when on September 23, 2001, New York linebacker Mo Lewis took out quarterback Drew Bledsoe as he ran to the sideline. Brady entered a game that the Patriots would end up losing 10-3, then go on to lead the Pats to their first Super Bowl win.
Brady and the Pats met the Jets in the playoff twice. Once in 2006, a wild-card round win for New England, then again four years later, where the Patriots were stunned by quarterback Mark Sanchez in the divisional Round. The two teams also met in 1985, during the Patriots run to their first Super Bowl appearance.
Prior to the dynasty, an infamous game defined this rivalry: The 1997 Week 3 match, which saw the return of Hall of Fame head coach Bill Parcells to New England. Just 9 months after leading the Patriots to an AFC Championship, Parcells was now on the opposite side of the field. In this 27-24 overtime victory for the Patriots, Curtis Martin ran the ball 40 times and notched 199 yards.  The following season, Martin would join Parcells' Jets.
Another meeting between these two teams made league history, but not for its score or anything that happened on the field. On September 9, 2007, the Patriots eased their way past the Jets 38-14 — however, the result of this match would create the term SpyGate . Belichick's Patriots, accused of stealing signals from the Jets sideline, made sports history with their record-setting fine punishments and removal of a first-round pick.
Both the Patriots and Jets are under new regimes with head coaches Mike Vrabel and Aaron Glenn beginning their tenures in the 2025 season. The Patriots swept the Jets in the season series a year ago, winning by a total margin of 69-24.
Each team has some linemen familiarity, as well. The Patriots currently roster or reserve four offensive linemen that formerly played for the New York Jets (Greg Van Roten, Morgan Moses, Alijah Vera-Tucker, and Xavier Newman-Johnson). Former Patriots offensive tackle Chukwuma Okorafor is currently a Jet.
Geno Smith, in his second stint with the team that originally drafted him, is very familiar with the Patriots. As a starting quarterback, Smith is 2-4 against the Pats, winning the last two in 2024 with the Seahawks and 2025 with the Raiders.
While each team has different goals for the season, both are relying on their young stars to push them into the conversation of great NFL teams.
The Jets are relying on their young talent, which is very recently acquired. After trading cornerback Sauce Gardner and defensive linemen Quinnen Williams, the Jets stacked six first-round picks in two straight drafts (2026-27). Former first-round picks WR Garrett Wilson and EDGE Will McDonald IV are already impact players.
In this past draft, they selected EDGE David Bailey fourth overall, whose already proven to be a hit, reaching top five in the NFL in sacks (five). They also selected WR Omar Cooper Jr. and TE Kenyon Sadiq with their remaining two first-round picks. Their second-round pick in CB D'Angelo Ponds has shown promise defensively.
The Patriots have seemingly hit on most of their first-round picks over the course of the past few drafts. CB Christian Gonzalez just became the highest paid cornerback in the league , and Drake Maye was runner-up for MVP last season. Offensive linemen Will Campbell and Caleb Lomu round out the remaining quarters of a four-season rebuild built through first-round talent.
The Patriots future also depends on home grown talent such as EDGE Gabe Jacas , S Craig Woodson, and RB TreVeyon Henderson.
Will the next best chapter of this rivalry start on Sunday? With each team currently placd second and third in the division, Sunday's battle could have major effects on how the AFC East shapes up.

title: Patriots Hall of Fame Center Jon Morris Dies at 84
full_text:
Jon Morris, one of the greatest offensive linemen in New England Patriots history, has died, the team announced Thursday. He was 84.
Morris was one of the stalwarts of the upstart Boston Patriots in the American Football League, anchoring the offensive line for 11 seasons. He was a fourth round draft pick (29th overall) by the club in 1964, and remained with the Patriots until 1974. He was named a team captain and was named an AFL All-Star six times from 1964 to 1969.
"Jon Morris was one of the great players who helped build the foundation of our franchise," Patriots Chairman and CEO Robert Kraft said in a statement released by the team. "For generations of Patriots fans, he represented the toughness, dedication and pride of those early teams.
"It meant so much to me to call Jon in 2011 and tell him he had been selected to our Hall of Fame, ensuring that his contributions would always be remembered. On behalf of our family and the entire Patriots organization, we extend our deepest condolences to Jon's family, friends and former teammates."
He was the first Patriots player to ever ben selected to the Pro Bowl following the 1970 merger with the NFL, and added that accolade onto his previous five All-AFL Team honors (one First Team, four Second Team). Morris was also named to the franchise's All-1960s Team, as well as their 35th and 50th Anniversary Teams.
Morris chose the Patriots over the NFL's Green Bay Packers, who had selected in the fourth round of the 1964 draft.
"I was 22, and Boston was a lively town, and I felt comfortable there," Morris said, via Holy Cross Magazine in 2010 . "Green Bay seemed dead outside football."
Morris played in 130 games with the franchise and helped lead the way for fullback Jim Nance in the running game. He'd close his pro career with stops on the Detroit Lions (1975-77) and the Chicago Bears (1978).
A Holy Cross alum, Morris would also become a radio broadcaster for the Patriots from 1979 to 1987. He became the third offensive lineman inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame (behind John Hannah and Bruce Armstrong) in 2011 — and the first to be inducted by the newly-formed senior committee.
Morris called the induction "the crowning achivement of my football life."
"I'm thrilled beyond words," Morris said at the time of his name being nominated for the Patriots Hall of Fame three years prior in 2008 . "It's really nice for an old-timer like me. I played with Nance, so I know how good he was. ... But this is almost like a once-in-a-lifetime situation for me, because there are so many great players in the organization."
Morris' name also appeared on the i nitial ballot for induction into Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2026 , but he did not move further into the voting process.

title: Patriots' Christian Gonzalez Full Participant in Practice for the First Time in 2 Weeks
full_text:
On Wednesday, cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) returned to New England Patriots practice after missing two straight weeks of practice. One day later, he was upgraded to a full participant in their fully-padded session.
The fourth-year star was sidelined after sustaining a shoulder injury in the Patriots' Week 3 game against Jacksonville. Following six-straight "did not participate" practice designations, Gonzalez was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday. A day later, he's back in full pads and participating in every drill.
Gonzalez told the media on Wednesday that he was feeling, "good, ready to go for Sunday." He also said, "I've been itching, kind of going a little crazy when I'm not getting to play."
The 24-year-old had his rookie season cut short with a labrum injury in 2023. His injury history extends to following two seasons where in 2024, he suffered a concussion and in 2025, he started the season with a hamstring injury.
Christian Gonzalez back at practice today 👏 #Patriots #NEPats pic.twitter.com/2epMq6XKjw
The 2024 second-team All-Pro cornerback made history in the offseason by signing a four-year, $135 million extension with $130 million guaranteed. The contract, announced a day before the start of the 2026 season, made Gonzalez the highest paid at his position in the NFL.
On Thursday, Patriots defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr told media members, "It's always great to have (No.) 0 out there. ... He's been flying around, good energy, good communication with the guys. Doesn't look like he missed a step, and we're excited to have him out there for sure."
Patriots defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr on CB Christian Gonzalez: Flying around out there, doesn’t look like he missed a step. pic.twitter.com/W4W54BuWpW
With the 2023 first-round pick returning to the lineup, the Patriots become larger favorites over the New York Jets (2-3).
With cornerback Carlton Davis (neck) still sidelined in practice , Gonzalez's lockdown coverage will be needed to contain the likes of Garrett Wilson, who's been the Jets' leading receiver through five games.
Additionally, New York could have rookie first-round wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. back from an ankle injury, and Adonai Mitchell back from a finger injury.
Last week, along with Gonzalez and Davis, the Patriots were without defensive backs Karon Prunty and Channing Canada — both rehabbing hamstring injuries. As a result, the team trotted out just three active cornerbacks to face the Las Vegas Raiders' passing attack.
While Canada was listed as limited participant in Thursday's practice, having the 24-year-old star back on the field to face a divisional opponent, in what some are calling a trap game , makes all the difference for this banged up Patriots secondary.
After receiving an historic extension, Gonzalez will almost certainly suit up for the Patriots on Sunday for his fourth game of the season.

title: Patriots Week 6 Injury Report: A.J. Brown Returns, OTs Banged Up Bad
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots have gone through a lot of injuries these last five weeks. They've been forced to put more players on injured reserve at this point in the season (19) than they did all of last season. They've been banged up , but have still won two-straight games to improve to 3-2.
But they're getting some players back this week ahead of their matchup with the New York Jets.
"I mean, I think that we'll just focus on this week and see if guys are ready to go," Mike Vrabel said Wednesday about handling injuries ahead of this week and next week's Thursday Night Football game. "We obviously know we have a shortened week next week. It can’t impact our decisions to try to do everything we can to win this week. Then we’ll figure out where we are after that."
Here's the initial injury report for the Patriots, including some returners off of injured reserve.
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (illness)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (neck)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (hamstring)
Here's the Jets' initial injury report for Week 6, including a few major pieces of their offense sidelined.
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (quad)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (finger)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (knee)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (ankle)
The biggest story for the Patriots? The return of A.J. Brown, who missed Weeks 2 through 5 with a high-ankle sprain . He was designated to return off of IR this week, and will work to try and play this week against a Jets team he should thrive against.
But the Patriots aren't sure yet how he'll impact the offense ... or if he'll even be activated by Saturday. The Patriots will have three weeks to officially decide if they'll remove him off of IR and stick him on the 53-man roster.
"He hasn't been out there, so I can't tell you until we actually see it," Vrabel said. "He hasn't been out there for four weeks, so we'll get him back out there practicing and see if he's ready to go in a couple days. And if not, then we have a 21-day window, and we'll go from there."
Brown participated in practice , going through drills with his receivers coach, Todd Downing. There didn't seem to be any limitations in how he looked (at least when reporters were present).
A.J. Brown goes through a catch possession drill with WRs coach Todd Downing: pic.twitter.com/ipUvbBZmUx
The Patriots also started the 21-day window for second-year offensive tackle Marcus Bryant, who was placed on IR ahead of the regular season with an ankle injury.
Last week against the Raiders, the Patriots lost both TreVeyon Henderson and Will Campbell in a matter of minutes. Both players would leave the game and wouldn't return, and after tests on Monday, could end up missing some time .
When reporters were present during Wednesday's practice, neither of them were spotted on the field with their teammates. Campbell did speak prior to going out to practice, but he only participated in a limited capacity.
When Campbell was ruled out, the Patriots turned to first round rookie Caleb Lomu . He would play pretty good football from the left side — allowing just one pressure in 47 snaps.
"I think all the times that they have to be able to get some game action, whether that's at the jumbo tight end or getting some snaps in there at different times in practice and being able to work on both sides is critical," Vrabel said Monday on Lomu's first month. "I think that's something that the swing tackle has to be able to do. He has to be ready to go in the game. I know he's working hard, and he's going to try to take advantage of whatever opportunity comes his way."
As for how the Patriots can replace Henderson's skills at running back , they'll have to rely a lot on third-string Corey Kiner, and practice squad players Lan Larison and Hassan Haskins. The team had Haskins in the building during the preseason and the first two weeks of the season, but just signed him back this week just in case.
After starting the week as a limited participant, Christian Gonzalez was upgraded to a full participant for Thursday. He's been on the field working as a starter after missing the past two weeks of practice, and is now in line to make his return to the game field.
Earlier this week, Gonzalez told reporters that he was "ready to go" for his battle with the Jets. Now that he's a full go in practice, the Patriots coaching staff is looking forward to seeing their top cornerback return to action.
"He's the same guy," cornerbacks coach Justin Hamilton said. "He came back out and prepares, going to work, playing the game in his head like what he always has done."

title: Patriots DT Leonard Taylor III Pays Respect to Fan Favorite With 'Fire' Sack Celebration
full_text:
FOBXORO — After Leonard Taylor III wrapped up Kirk Cousins in the second half of the New England Patriots' 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders , he got up off the ground and immediately knew what his celebration was going to be.
He raised his right arm up to the sky and dragged it across his face. It was an ode to former Patriots edge rusher Matthew Judon, who made that motion (along with his red sleeves under his playing jersey) iconic in New England.
For any Patriots fan who saw that celebration and smiled, Taylor did it intentionally.
"I seen that brodie play here and he popped up on my for you page one day scrolling," he told Patriots On SI in the locker room Thursday. "Then I see he played for the Pats. Then I see his celebration after getting sacks, and I was like, 'that's fire.'
"I was telling (defensive tackle Jeremiah) Pharms, I'm like, 'That's tough.' It was just a coincidence I got on the red sleeves and all that. ... Next thing I know, I just did it."
The sack came pretty late in a game that the Patriots had in the bag already. At that point, Taylor got some snaps along the defensive line. He finished the game with just 11 defensive snaps, but made that one count.
Taylor, in his second season with the Patriots, never overlapped with Judon in New England. He wasn't ever a teammate with the 34-year-old veteran. Still, Taylor is aware of what Judon — and his red sleeves — meant for the Patriots and their fans.
"They were putting his images, the little gif. They spammed his gifs all under my post, all on Twitter," Taylor said of the fans commenting on his social media posts of the celebration.
Respect cuh 🦇!! pic.twitter.com/Muq3HcrI6c
But the defensive tackle isn't the only one who's used Judon as inspiration. Gabe Jacas, who didn't even notice that Taylor hit the celebration, said after being drafted that he modeled his game after Judon.
"I didn't know that was his signature celebration," Jacas told Patriots On SI on Taylor's sack. "So once I seen it on social media, I thought that was pretty cool that he hit it. It was pretty cool. I just didn't know that point in time."
The Patriots signed Judon in free agency ahead of the 2021 season to a four-year, $56 million contract. That season, he burst onto the scene and racked up 12.5 sacks . He was named to the Pro Bowl in 2021 and 2022, and instantly became one of the shining stars on some of the dullest Patriots teams.
Ultimately, the Patriots would trade Judon away prior to the 2024 season for a 2025 third round pick. Through more transactions, the Patriots eventually ended up the picks that landed them center Jared Wilson, edge rusher Bradyn Swinson (who was released in August) and offensive tackle Caleb Lomu. Judon's New England tenure ended with133 total tackles, 32 career sacks and 62 quarterback hits.
Taylor says he'll consider doing the celebration again if he racks up another sack. But made sure to credit the one who made it popular.
"If brodie accepts," Taylor laughed. "It's kind of his."

title: Patriots Face Trap Game vs. Solid Jets Defense
full_text:
The New England Patriots have rarely had trouble with the New York Jets over the years.
Especially during the Bill Belichick era, there was never trepidation about heading to MetLife Stadium (or hosting the Jets at Gillette Stadium). In fact, for Patriots fans at least, it was the opposite feeling, like making easy money for a simple job.
But this year, the Jets appear more resilient than usual led by a solid journeyman QB in Geno Smith.
Smith dumped 362 passing yards on the Patriots ’ defense last year as a member of the Las Vegas Raiders. He ended the contest with a victory and a 102.8 quarterback rating.
The reason why Smith is truly dangerous lies in the fact that he may not have to put up gaudy numbers against New England because the Jets’ defense can keep them in the game.
Aaron Glenn haters will have to somewhat respect what he’s done so far, as New York is fourth in total defense (293 yards allowed per game), fourth against the pass (175 yards per game), fifth in points allowed (19.2 per game) and 10th in defensive EPA/play.
There’s a fair argument that New York’s defensive stats can be attributed to weak points on the schedule. The Jets have faced the Titans and Browns, two offenses that have struggled to move the ball consistently this season.
But the season has gone on for more than two games, and Glenn’s defense went against more legitimate offensive teams.
New York also battled the Detroit Lions, Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears.
Against Green Bay, the Jets’ defense looked sturdy. They held the Packers to 199 total yards, only 63 rushing yards and 1-of-9 on third down in a 20-17 overtime loss. Jordan Love threw for just 145 yards, although he did have two touchdowns and no interceptions.
"This team is going to present a lot of challenges, and I don't think we can take this lightly,” Patriots safety Kevin Byard said of the Jets on Wednesday.
On the flip side, the Bears rolled up 492 yards of offense, including 232 on the ground, during a 23-12 win over New York. The Patriots’s downtrodden run game will look at this game to see what’s possible to take advantage of.
Additionally, the Lions were the toughest challenge of the bunch, managing to hang 31 points on the Jets.
New York blitzed Jared Goff on 44.4% of his dropbacks , and Goff went 14-for-14 for 148 yards and a touchdown against the blitz. He completed 11 of 13 play-action passes for 181 yards.
That play action success bodes well for the Patriots and offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels , who want to open up the passing game further for Drake Maye, albeit their struggling run game.
New York can play more zone to keep eyes on the quarterback (maybe with a spy as well) in order to prevent Maye from breaking contain when the pocket collapses. The Jets have leaned that way this season, using zone 68.8% of the time over straight man coverage.
But sitting back means they’ll have to push pressure since Maye destroyed the Raiders last week with ample time in the pocket.
Maye’s patience to take what the defense gives him has been a work in progress, though it has improved since coming into the league in 2024. McDaniels also has much experience attacking zone coverage with underneath concepts, crossing routes and throws into empty spots along the sidelines.
The spotlight really falls on New York’s linebackers and safeties to make correct choices. Step forward too aggressively, and Maye can find space behind them. Drop too deep, and the Patriots can take the easy completion, or Maye can take off to keep moving the chains.
Glenn’s best answer might be making everything look muddy before the snap. New York can show pressure but then bail defenders into coverage, occasionally sending extra rushers when Maye is expecting a softer look.
Assuming Maye sees man coverage and gets a lane up the middle, there may be nobody accounting for him once he escapes the pocket. If the Jets sit in zone, New England can try to pick away underneath until New York becomes more aggressive.
So, in the end, It’s a chess match that will end up deciding whether the Jets’ defense really deserves its lofty early-season rankings.

title: 3 Winners, 4 Losers of A.J. Brown's Potential Return to Patriots Roster
full_text:
On Wednesday, New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel officially activated A.J. Brown's return to play period , meaning that he can be elevated off of the injured reserve anytime in the next 21 days. Brown, who the Patriots acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick, went down in the team's season opener against the Seattle Seahawks 36 days ago with a high ankle sprain.
Brown practiced in a limited capacity for the first time since Week 1. With his 21-day return-to-play window opened, the Super Bowl-winning wide receiver could return to play as soon as this week against the New York Jets.
But how does his return affect the rest of the Patriots? How does Brown's presence provide more or less opportunity for the players and coaches on and off the field? Here are some winners and losers of Brown's return:
For practically a game and a half, McDaniels has been running the Patriots offense with just four wide receivers. After Mack Hollins went down in the third quarter of Week 4 against the Buffalo Bills, the veteran offensive coordinator was forced to reach deep in his bag of tools to utilize the potential of his Patriots passing game.
Since being cut to four receivers, the Patriots receiving corps have hauled in five touchdowns (not including Drake Maye's pass to Hunter Henry, read more for details). McDaniels' effectiveness with spreading the ball and utilizing alternative targets in the wake of both Brown's and Hollins' injuries, have been nothing short of stellar.
Now, with Brown re-entering the fold, McDaniels can expand his playbook — one that he designed specifically with Brown as the number one option. The Patriots get the length of the field to work with and the ability to spread out opposing defenses, as Brown's downfield receiving skills come to play.
In light of a weakened receiver room, Efton Chism III has stepped up in ways not many had expected. In Week 4, he scored the game-winning touchdown on a league-wide highlight reel worthy play. Chism also hauled in a career high five receptions and 57 yards in their win over Las Vegas on Sunday.
However, Chism's unforeseen impact is in part because of the absences at receiver. In Week 1 — the only week where the entire receiver room entered the game healthy, the second-year undrafted free agent was a healthy scratch. From Weeks 2-5, Chism's snap percentage rose an average of 12% per week, playing 76% of snaps in Week 5.
While Brown's return will certainly sideline Chism more than he's seen in the past couple weeks, the scrappy and super athletic receiver may have earned himself more playing time than the Patriots originally planned on giving him this season.
Doubs was the Patriots first big free agent signing at receiver in years. He entered the season expecting to be the team's number two target, lining up opposite to Brown.
After Brown's injury, Doubs became the most targeted player on the Pats' offense. But of the 23 looks quarterback Drake Maye has given him, he's only hauled in 13. Doubs inefficiency to make catches has surrounded his first several games in New England.
Upon Brown's return, Doubs will slot back into the secondary receiver postion, which doesn't only allow him to play the position he learned all summer but also keeps defenses' top secondary players off of him.
Similar to Chism, the tight end group has also thrived in Brown's absence. Both the veteran Henry and rookie acquisition Eli Raridon have caught a touchdown this year and have been reliable presences in the passing game.
Henry, who's played with Maye in all three years of the young star's career, is a common safety net on third or fourth down plays. While Henry will still be the number one tight end, Brown will be a reliable out for Maye, as well.
Raridon, on the other hand, may see less involvement in the passing game. Because the receiving group was limited to just four players, often times, Raridon found himself on the field with Henry  — operating in two tight end sets. Adding a fifth receiver to the group reduces the need for Raridon to be on the field at the same time as Henry.
Prior to Sunday's game, Raridon was averaging one per game across his three games with playing time.
After a definitively slow start to the season, Drake Maye has been the best quarterback in the NFL across the past two weeks , throwing for 643 yards and notching seven total touchdowns.
Though it feels like Maye has finally gotten used to a new — yet dwindled — receiving group, having his number one receiver back in the fold can only beneft the young quarterback who's found confidence and caught fire in recent weeks.
On Wednesday, Maye had a lot to say about practicing with Brown, including, "I think it definitely opens up other parts of the field and other parts of the game for guys. I think you see it in the NBA; it's probably the closest thing that I can think of."
Drake Maye says that having A.J. Brown back at practice was “awesome.” pic.twitter.com/yuN3mD9i6x
Over the summer, reports indicated that Brown and Maye's connection was fantastic. In the less than three quarters of real game action they saw, the pair connected for three catches and 26 yards and missed on one deep shot to the end zone. Brown will provide more opportunity for Maye to move the ball through the air.
Williams is another player whose playing time has increased significantly in response to the injuries.
A third-round pick in last year's draft, Williams hasn't provided the level of use you'd expect from a player taken so highly. His ability to spread the field and haul in deep passes has been exhilirating, but his average reception yardage of 27 yards per catch isn't sustainable nor consistant.
Williams has just five catches on the year, three of which came against the Raiders in Week 5. With Chism showing flashes of success, Williams may find himself on the bottom of the depth chart at the wide receiver position.
Offensive tackle Marcus Bryant returned to practice along with Brown, signaling that the two (when officially elevated to the active roster) will be the third and fourth players the Patriots reactivate off of injured reserve/non-football injurt.
New England can only activate eight players off of the injured reserve, and have already done so with four (including Brown and Bryant). They'll be stuck with 11 players on IR, and will only be able to activate four of them.
You start with EIGHT spots to use for a “designated-to-return” player. 1️⃣ - ST Brenden Schooler 2️⃣ - OT Marcus Bryant 3️⃣ - WR A.J. Brown 4️⃣ - WR Mack Hollins 5️⃣ - 6️⃣ - 7️⃣ - 8️⃣ - Who are your other four? 🤔 ⬇️ https://t.co/QM0uOzFeot pic.twitter.com/JlVQ4n9fse
Taking into account future injuries, as well, the team will have to be very cautious of which injuries deserve IR designation and which players can stay on the active roster while they rehabilitate their injuries.
Several starters like Hollins, FB Reggie Gilliam, and P Bryce Baringer are expected to make full recoveries of their injuries at some point this season.
Brown's return — though a worthwhile one, takes up another IR return designation of which the Patriots have very few.

title: How the Patriots Offense, WR Room Changes After Getting A.J. Brown Back
full_text:
FOXBORO — He's yet to be officially added to the 53-man roster, but New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown was back at practice Wednesday. The star wideout, who has been on IR since after the team's season-opening loss in Seattle, now has 21 days to be activated to the active roster as the team designated him to return .
Brown has been present in the locker room over the past two weeks , often walking in with cleats on and a slight wrap on his right ankle. His high-ankle sprain held him off the field, but hasn't kept him away from his teammates.
"I think he's stayed engaged. I think it's difficult sometimes to stay engaged, but I think his routine was really good," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters Wednesday. "(His) ability to be around guys in the meetings, and then also focus on his rehab and just treat everything as a pro and be where he's supposed to be and work hard to get back."
Now that Brown is in uniform practicing and nearing his return, here's how the Patriots' wide receiver room is impacted .
Brown's ability to stretch the field and be the team's go-to weapon past the sticks is part of the reason why the Patriots traded a first round pick for him in June. We haven't been able see that part of his game yet, but it's coming.
Drake Maye did try to take a shot deep to Brown in Week 1 , but Josh Jobe was flagged for defensive pass interference and the ball fell incomplete. The Patriots would score on that drive on a pass to Eli Raridon, but Brown wasn't used in any deep routes for the remainder of his time on the field.
Since he's been out, the Patriots have relied a lot of Romeo Doubs and Kyle Williams to stretch the field down the sidelines. It's worked in spurts, but it hasn't been as consistent as the Patriots might have hoped. Getting Brown back will unlock that part of Maye's passing arsenal.
Maye has thrown for seven touchdowns in the last two weeks, and has seemingly found his groove slinging the football. He was able to connect with Doubs twice, DeMario Douglas twice, and Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III once each.
That's a group that really doesn't offer the same level of threat that Brown has, but the Patriots got outstanding production out of them four. With Brown now sliding into that mix, his ceiling is far higher than any other wideout on the team.
If Maye has been able to tap into the skills he had a season ago with that group, imagine what he can do once Brown straps the pads on Sundays.
But because Brown is returning, that means that the snaps that Douglas and Williams got a week ago might start to dwindle . Last week against Las Vegas, the Patriots were down Mack Hollins ( who was placed on IR with a calf injury suffered in Buffalo ). His absence allowed the likes of Douglas, Williams and Chism to step into larger roles they might not have been in otherwise.
With Brown back in the WR1 role, he'll certainly get the lion's share of targets and receptions outside the numbers. The Patriots will still rely on Doubs across the middle and Douglas/Chism in the slot, but one would imagine that the passing game will now flow through Brown — and not the others.
A few weeks ago, you could make the argument that the Patriots might entertain a trade for a receiver like Brian Thomas Jr. or Marvin Harrison Jr. (who's now been sent to the Houston Texans). While that felt unlikely considering the captial the team gave up to get Brown in the first place, if the Patriots didn't expect him to come back quickly, they could have gotten on the phone to try and make a move.
Instead, this is their big "trade" acqusition. Getting Brown back, a healthy Brown back, should be the cherry on top of what was back-to-back great offensive showings. If he can remain on the field and a legit threat every single week, the Patriots will enjoy their return on investment they made back in June .
