title: Future of Jets' Offense Hangs on Garrett Wilson-Geno Smith Duo's Next Steps
full_text:
In case it wasn't already clear, the central game plan for the Jets' offense each week should be five simple words.
"Get. Garrett. Wilson. The. Ball."
Five words. Every single week. That's the game plan.
Jokes aside, it is no coincidence the Jets defeated the Cleveland Browns thanks in large part to their top receiver. Wilson recorded seven catches for another 100-yard game and a touchdown catch (h/t NFL).
What a play by Garrett Wilson for the touchdown! @CLEvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6mepGsdHbd
New York may have only put up 17 points, but the game plan and operation made perfect sense for the group, according to head coach Aaron Glenn.
“When you’ve got players like Garrett, you try to do everything you can to try to make sure you feed him the ball,” Glenn said.
Of course, while Wilson remains a star in the league, the quarterback getting him the ball hasn't been too bad himself. It's that partnership that appears to be getting better and putting the Jets in rare territory as an offense.
On paper, the stats don't look too dominant. The Jets are 23rd in the league in passing, with some questions about protection and a lack of big plays.
But the partnership between Wilson and quarterback Geno Smith remains the most important for the Jets as the 2026 season rolls on. Gang Green needs their top quarterback and receiver on the same page at all times, even if Wilson isn't always going to get the ball, and Smith knows it.
Smith has played well in his return to New York. He has yet to throw an interception and is completing just under 70% of his passes. His 73.1 passing grade on Pro Football Focus is also the 15th-best among 51 qualified QBs.
Meanwhile, Wilson ranks seventh in receptions and 11th in the league in receiving yards. This has all come as the Jets have struggled with injuries at the receiver position behind him (Omar Cooper Jr., Adonai Mitchell, Arian Smith, etc.).
"(Garrett's) got great range in terms of you can put the ball anywhere, he goes and gets it, and it's hard for guys to cover him out there," Smith said. "We have to find ways to get him the ball as many times as we can."
The pile of injuries hasn't mattered. Wilson has still played well, and that's a credit Smith respects more than anything.
Still, it wasn't always pretty, of course.
In Week 4's loss to the Bears, Wilson was targeted just four times on 32 plays run by the Jets' offense. The fact that the Jets made a focused effort to change that early in Sunday's win over the Browns, though, shows the team understands the importance of getting the ball to their best offensive player.
As Gang Green prepares for their Week 6 showdown with the Patriots , that game plan will be put to the test. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel is notorious for trying to take the opposing team's best player out of the game entirely.
It's something the receiver is geared for in the organization's first AFC East game of the season.
"If the looks look how they did during the week, all of a sudden you have an idea," Wilson said. "They can always do unscouted looks, throw wrenches at you, things like that. You’ve got to be ready for it all as a player.”
The Patriots may try to take him away, but the Jets should be well prepared for that by now. There won't be an excuse if New York struggles to get its No. 1 playmaker on Sunday.
Wilson is good enough to dominate any opponent. It seems his quarterback and team are ready to allow that to happen now.

title: Aaron Glenn's Conflicting Injury Updates Raise New Questions for Jets
full_text:
Gamesmanship knows no bounds in the modern NFL. Coaches will try to conceal the severity of injuries for as long as they possibly can in order to get a small advantage over their opponents, even if it means confusing their fanbase for weeks.
That's what has happened to the New York Jets in their latest injury report. Head coach Aaron Glenn has always been coy on injuries.
This week, though, he went back on previous comments made just last week. When it comes to wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, the former second-round pick has missed the last three weeks due to a finger injury. Glenn provided this update on the wideout last week:
"He's progressing faster than we thought that he would," Glenn said last Friday. "Once we got to the end of it of knowing exactly what the prognosis was when it comes to his finger."
When asked outright if Mitchell received a procedure during his time off, Glenn was adamant:
"No, he didn't. He didn't."
Wednesday, Glenn provided a different update, and it leaves more questions than answers.
Glenn confirmed to reporters on Wednesday that Mitchell did in fact have a procedure done early into the recovery on his finger.
"I think he waited like a week, week and a half before he had to see how he actually was going to progress and then we wanted to go ahead and get it knocked out," Glenn said.
The lack of transparency is nothing new. Glenn is not doing anything different than 31 other coaches around the league do. At the same time, it does open questions about other injured players that the team is dealing with.
Running back Breece Hall, edge rusher Joseph Ossai, and left guard Dylan Parham are all week to week. Ossai has been going back and forth on the field with a foot injury that has been bothering him since training camp.
There is good news on the injury front, though. Rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. had his practice window open and was a limited participant in New York's walkthrough. The Indiana product being back on the field is huge for their offense.
"He's a really good player, but you never want any rookie to actually miss time because the reps are valuable for these guys," Glenn said. "And I think all of our rookies that's been getting these reps have been valuable, and we have a number of guys that's been out of practice."
But can Jets fans trust he'll actually have a chance to play in the next few weeks? Remember, the ankle injury suffered has kept him off the field for four of the first five games of his NFL career. Those are valuable reps, both in practice and in games, that Cooper has missed.
Expecting him to walk into Week 6 and be able to be productive isn't fair to the player.
But it also adds additional questions. If Cooper's practice window is open, that positions the Jets to open up a short-term IR slot. Will someone take his place? Mitchell, Hall, and Parham are all still week-to-week which means they aren't close to practicing yet.
Will fans get to know how serious the injuries are? Glenn may be practicing a normal gamesmanship tactic other coaches use, but it does bring in more questions the Jets shouldn't have to answer.

title: Why Omar Cooper Jr.'s Return Is Even More Crucial for the Jets' 2026 Outlook
full_text:
Although the Jets’ offense is significantly better than last year, the unit hasn’t been great. Through five games, Gang Green is tied for 27th in points (18.6) and 23rd in passing yards per game (190).
Geno Smith and Garrett Wilson have done everything they can to keep the offense afloat; however, injuries to New York’s key offensive players have held them back. Fortunately, head coach Aaron Glenn gave fans some good news on Wednesday, announcing that rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. will return to practice this week.
The former Indiana Hoosier sustained an ankle injury in New York’s Week 1 win over the Titans and was placed on injured reserve.
The news couldn’t come at a better time, as Gang Green is currently without Breece Hall and Adonai Mitchell, both week-to-week, while Kenyon Sadiq remains in the concussion protocol after suffering a head injury in the Jets' Week 5 victory over the Browns.
With Cooper nearing a return in the lineup, New York hopes he can help improve the unit's play immediately and emerge as the second option behind Wilson.
The Smith-Wilson connection has been strong. Over the first five weeks, Wilson is tied for seventh in receptions with 31 and ranks 11th in receiving yards with 374.
Besides Wilson, the Jets haven’t gotten consistent production from their other pass catchers. Sadiq ranks second on the team in catches (14) and third in yards (146). However, most of the rookie tight end’s production came in Week 3 against the Lions, where he posted seven receptions for 105 yards.
Isaiah Williams ranks behind Sadiq with 11 receptions for 151 yards, although 58 of those yards came on a touchdown in Week 3’s loss to the Bears.
We’ve only seen Cooper play five snaps, but in that small sample, he proved that he can be an impact player.
In the Jets' first offensive drive of the season, Cooper caught a short pass on third-and-nine and turned it into a 30-yard gain. His 26 yards after the catch put New York inside the 10-yard line and helped set up a touchdown two plays later.
Cooper’s playmaking ability was a major reason why New York traded back into the first round to select him.
In his final collegiate season, Cooper recorded 494 yards after the catch, which ranked 16th among qualifying receivers, per Pro Football Focus. He also averaged 7.2 yards after the catch per reception, highlighting his ability to generate extra yards.
The Jets’ offense has desperately missed this playmaking ability. New York has struggled to find consistent production from the rest of its receiving corps and continues to rely on Wilson to move the ball downfield.
Mitchell ranks second on the team in receiving first downs, but his absence over the last three games has further limited Smith’s options. Cooper’s return could help fill that void. He’s already shown that he can make plays with the ball in his hands and give Smith another reliable target.
With another playmaker in the receiver corps, defenses would have to account for Cooper, which could create more opportunities for Wilson.
Getting Cooper back could be crucial for the Jets heading into this week’s matchup against the Patriots. With New England’s defense ranking 11th in passing yards allowed (212.2), the rookie’s skill set could give Gang Green an extra boost against their rival.

title: How Jets Can Continue Unlocking Darrell Jackson Jr.'s Full Potential in Week 6 (And Beyond)
full_text:
Behind a dominant defensive performance up front and a career day from running back Braelon Allen, the Jets prevailed in a hard-fought 17-12 win over the Browns last Sunday in the sloppy conditions at MetLife Stadium.
As the Jets prepare for their first AFC East matchup of the season when they face the Patriots on Sunday, all eyes will be on Gang Green to see how they fare with a record of 25-65 against division opponents since 2011.
If anything was clear from the Week 5 win over the Browns, it was that they found a defensive blueprint that can succeed long term after head coach Aaron Glenn called blitz plays on more than 50% of the snaps.
While rookie David Bailey was the force behind that success with three of the team's eight sacks in the game, fellow rookie Darrell Jackson Jr. was a stud in his own right with his first career NFL sack and two huge pass deflections in the fourth quarter. As David Onyemata remains on injured reserve after undergoing core muscle surgery, the opportunity remains in front of Jackson to make a strong impression and become a steal as a fourth-round draft pick.
Jackson had more of a rotational role on the depth chart to begin the season, but he had the type of performance that everyone was waiting for against Cleveland. Jackson had four tackles, one sack, two pressures and two pass deflections in 29 defensive snaps in his best NFL showing to date and showed what he is truly capable of in an increased role .
Through the first four games, Jackson only had seven tackles and zero pressures in 85 defensive snaps and was primarily expected to be a rotational run-plugger in the middle of Glenn's defensive schemes. He was far from quiet against the Browns and proved that it could be difficult to take snaps away from him if he can build off the all-around performance from last Sunday.
According to Pro Football Focus , Jackson has the 77th-ranked overall grade (56.2) and 93rd-ranked pass-rush grade (57.7) out of 133 qualified interior defenders. Jackson still needs to continue to develop as a pass rusher, but his 50th-ranked run-defense grade (59.5) speaks to the potential he brings when defending the ground game.
The 6-foot-5, 315-pounder out of Florida State was solid during his collegiate career with 77 total tackles (seven for loss), 7.5 sacks and 35 hurries. That said, it was his dirty work that perhaps led to him getting overlooked when the draft rolled around and why he was flying under the radar coming into the season .
In addition to tying for the 16th-most run stops (23) among interior defenders in college football last season, per PFF , Jackson's size and run-stuffing ability make him a key early-down contributor who can give T'Vondre Sweat or Harrison Phillips a breather. He needs to continue growing as a pass rusher if he wants to improve his snap count going forward, but the ceiling is certainly high after a breakout Week 5 performance.
For starters, the Patriots are dealing with multiple offensive line injuries, notably starting left tackle Will Campbell (right knee sprain). While quarterback Drake Maye is coming off a five-TD performance against the Raiders and is capable of using his legs when he needs to, continuing to move Jackson along the front could create some mismatches against a banged-up New England unit and keep Maye out of his rhythm amid a turnover-prone start to the season.
With a 7'2" wingspan and 11-inch hands, Jackson has the ability to utilize his massive frame to disrupt passing lanes and make life difficult on opposing QBs by recording deflections and batting passes down at the line of scrimmage. If he can take advantage of the increased opportunities that he could be in line for while Onyemata is out of action, Jackson could turn into a matchup nightmare.
Going forward, the Jets need to capitalize on Jackson's unconventional "Big End" 4-technique and 5-technique positions to use his rare length to his advantage, in addition to aligning him over the A and B gaps to test New England's front. If they can do that and reap the rewards, Jackson could have a bright future in Gang Green for years to come.

title: Jets' Special Teams Unit Takes a Turn Thanks to Rams
full_text:
Remember when the New York Jets tried out nine different kickers in order to find the right man to trust throughout the 2026 season? So many fans and analysts were concerned that the team's special teams unit would take a massive drop because of it.
Not only has that concerned not been the case, but the rest of the league seemingly wants New York's kickers again. Seriously.
The Los Angeles Rams, the team many predicted to win the Super Bowl after acquiring Myles Garrett in the offseason, have signed Blake Grupe off the Jets' practice squad this week after a struggling start to the season from Ex-Jet Harrison Mevis.
You read that right. Los Angeles is going back to the Jets to solve its kicking problems.
The jokes write themselves.
Before he was cut on Tuesday, Mevis was easily the weakest link to the Rams roster. He went 5-9 on field goals including missing a potential game-winner on Monday night. Grupe, meanwhile, hasn't even attempted a kick for the Jets so far this season.
He was beat out in another competition with Jason Sanders to begin the year. Sanders has gone 8-9 on field goals including a solid 3-4 from beyond 50 yards out.
New York was right to keep Sanders on the roster, but the team losing Grupe highlights another part to their team. New York's special teams unit isn't as elite as they were last season, but they remain an integral part to their future success.
"I think it's been awesome," special teams coordinator Chris Banjo said. "We're talking about grit and resiliency. I think he's been able to show that so far early in the season."
It should not be overlooked that the Rams chose to sign Grupe over the likes of other veteran kickers on the open market like Justin Tucker. Los Angeles clearly thinks highly of Banjo's ability to get the best out of their kickers, and are hoping to get some of that production going forward.
"Appreciate (Mevis's) contributions," Rams head coach Sean McVay said in a video conference with reporters. "I thought he was a rock for us last year when we obviously struggled in that area. But ultimately we need better production, and that's what we're hoping to get out of from Blake."
New York and Los Angeles have the same record. Sounds crazy doesn't it? But in the case of the Jets' their special teams unit looks to be an improved group even with new faces at kicker.
And other teams around the league know it.

title: Breaking Down Jets' Potential TE Plans vs. Patriots If Kenyon Sadiq Can't Clear Concussion Protocol
full_text:
Just when it seemed like the New York Jets were getting healthy. Just when it appeared that the team could start to utilize their two top tight ends. A game like Sunday happens and pushes all the expectations out the door.
Late in the contest, rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq suffered a concussion on a play where he fumbled the ball after a hard hit near the goalline. New York was able to salvage the game by winning 17-12, but the injury from Sadiq could keep him out of Sunday's contest against the New England Patriots.
Much like the last several weeks, though, New York should be just fine with their tight end room. They have the horses now to handle an injury to a starter, because they have another one ready to go.
Sadiq being a first-round pick shows enough about the kind of investment the team has made at the tight end position. The fact that he was the second consecutive tight end taken in the last two drafts only enhances that.
Mason Taylor's 2026 season has been a quiet one so far . Through two and a half games played this season, the LSU product has just five receptions for 22 yards this season. This is after the second-year tight end was second in the team in both receptions and yards.
Without Sadiq, the Jets will need more from Taylor, even if the team believes the best is still yet to come from him.
“We put a lot of work in the offseason, he was always willing to get out there, it was super hot, but he didn’t mind it,” quarterback Geno Smith said. “South Florida kid, seemed to be that way. But he’s a guy who I think is going to be a great player in this league for a long time.”
Jeremy Ruckert and Jelani Woods are two other tight ends that are expected to be used in droves. They may not have the athleticism compared to when Sadiq is out on the field, Taylor's consistency is something that should help the offense in droves, especially against a New England Patriots defense with plenty of physicality across the board.
New York has also been consistent in using all their tight ends across the board this season.
“They’re a well-rounded group, very talented group,” Smith said. “They work extremely hard—kind of the glue guys. They bring everything together on the offense. And so it’s great to see all five of them out there on the field at once and we’ll try and get the ball to each one of them when we can.”
Not having both Sadiq and Taylor on Sunday together can be frustrating for the organization. Until then, however, the team can still rely on the room to be just as good as they have in recent weeks.

title: Jets Rookie Report Card: Grading 2026 Draft Picks After First Month of the Season
full_text:
It was not pretty, but the Jets found a way to take down the Browns in a 17-12 season-saving win in the sloppy conditions at MetLife Stadium. Regardless, New York is now 2-3 and in a much better position than it would have been at 1-4 heading into a Week 6 AFC East tilt against the Patriots on Sunday.
Fresh off the hard-fought win in the rain , the Jets put a three-game losing streak behind them and have their eyes set on continuing to make improvements and learn from their previous mistakes going forward. While the discipline and inability to close out each half remain a concern, there is a lot more to feel optimistic about coming off a win this week.
Before the season even got started, there was a lot of hype surrounding the Jets' 2026 draft class. Although injuries or inconsistent play in the early going have provided some mixed results for some, the rookies' talent has been on display, setting the stage for a promising future in Gotham .
With that in mind, let's hand out grades for each of the Jets' eight 2026 draft picks now that it's been over a month since their season opener.
Even though David Bailey led all NFL rookies in pressures during the first month of the season, a lot of fans were concerned about his early returns on the field . That said, he single-handedly took over the Week 5 win over the Browns with three of the team's eight sacks, in addition to seven tackles (five solo), three tackles for loss and four quarterback hits.
Bailey recorded his third sack of the game early in the fourth quarter (h/t NFL) after the defense forced Cleveland's offense into a third-and-30.
THIRD sack of the day for David Bailey @CLEvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QTqQqo79NN
The defensive line was easily the best unit on the field for the Jets , which was a huge turnaround from the disappointing play that same group displayed in the games coming in. According to Pro Football Focus , Bailey has the 43rd-ranked overall grade (68.6) and the 10th-most pressures (20) out of 106 qualified edge defenders.
It was a fairly slow start out of the gate for Bailey, but if the Week 5 performance proved anything, it is that he was more than worthy of being selected No. 2 overall and certainly appears to have all the tools to become a star in the league.
Kenyon Sadiq scored his first NFL TD in Week 1 courtesy of the ground game, but his true breakout performance came in Week 3 when he went off for seven catches, 105 yards and his first TD catch. Aside from that, Sadiq has rarely been targeted and has been completely limited in the pass game when the ball has come his way.
Sadiq only had two catches for three yards in the loss to Cleveland and also committed a fumble, so there is definitely some room for improvement . This was also the first game back for Mason Taylor, and it was clear he was going to be a focal point of the tight end group, with 41 snaps to Sadiq's 13.
Granted, the concussion was a setback and limited Sadiq's playing time, but the Jets appear to prefer leaning in Taylor's direction a little more at this stage of the season. Sadiq's raw athletic traits are unmatched and his route separation is elite, but it remains to be seen how much of a factor he will be in this offense when Taylor is on the field.
Omar Cooper Jr.'s NFL career immediately got off to a hot start when he turned a short pass into a 30-yard gain (h/t Glenn Naughton) to set up a TD a few plays later in New York's season-opening win over the Titans. However, that remains his only target and catch of his rookie season after suffering a high ankle sprain during the first quarter of that Week 1 game.
First career catch for @nyjets rookie WR Omar Cooper. Looks like a first round pick if you ask me. pic.twitter.com/NmQRKYSGCK
Cooper has since spent the last four weeks on injured reserve, though the possibility is there for him to play in Sunday's game against the Patriots, depending on the progress he has made in his recovery. The Jets finally figured things out with WR1 Garrett Wilson by looking his way more often and reaping those rewards with seven catches for 104 yards and a TD, but the depth at WR has been an issue, and getting Cooper back sooner rather than later would be a huge benefit.
The grade is not so much a knock on D'Angelo Ponds, but rather due to the lack of playing time he has received as more of a developmental player who is primarily serving a backup role in the secondary. That said, he played a career-high 18 snaps in relief of Jarvis Brownlee Jr. in Week 4 and showcased his run-defense skills when the opportunity presented itself.
It appeared that Ponds was suddenly staring at a bigger role after Brownlee went into concussion protocol following the Week 4 loss to the Bears, but the latter ultimately became a full participant in practice and even recorded his first career sack in Sunday's game, all while Ponds played just two defensive snaps and primarily appeared on special teams.
Darrell Jackson Jr. was expected to be a rotational run-plugger in the middle of head coach Aaron Glenn's defensive schemes. While he only had seven tackles and zero pressures in 85 defensive snaps across the first four games, the fourth-round selection finally broke out and made his impact felt against the Browns.
Jackson had four tackles, one sack, two pressures and two pass deflections in 29 defensive snaps, putting together his best overall game so far in Gang Green. David Onyemata's place on injured reserve has paved the way for Jackson to step up, and the Week 5 performance was the first true sign of what Jackson is capable of.
Veteran Geno Smith has done his part to take care of the ball and manage each game relatively well by completing 72.7% of his passes for 1,084 yards and six TDs. Although he was anything but flashy in the win over the Browns, this is still firmly Smith's job as long as he continues to protect the ball, which could only benefit Cade Klubnik more as the fourth-round pick gets some additional time to learn from Smith and develop under his leadership.
Anez Cooper, the sixth-round pick out of Miami, suffered a right shoulder injury during the preseason finale against the Giants and has been on injured reserve since.
While he is now eligible to return to the roster , it remains to be seen if Cooper will make his season debut or at least be available to play. The offensive line was better against the Browns, but with Dylan Parham dealing with a knee injury and the play up front looking suspect so far, it definitely would not hurt to have an extra body in Cooper to turn to if the opportunity presents itself.
The seventh-round pick suffered a significant bone bruise during training camp before being placed on short-term IR, forcing him to miss at least the first four games of the season. Much like Cooper, it remains to be seen whether VJPayne will be activated back to the 53-man roster soon.
However, this staff is particularly high on Payne's physical traits and special teams potential , which could prove valuable when he does get fully healthy and potential roster holes open up.

title: McMullen: Tanner McKee Could Provide Important Answers About Sean Mannion's Eagles Offense
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - The “week from hell,” as dubbed by star left tackle Jordan Mailata after a cascade of roster upheaval, a transatlantic trip, and a gut-wrenching loss in London, may have just been elevated to the “season from hell” for the Philadelphia Eagles.
As late as Sept. 28, Tanner McKee was the Eagles’ QB3 . On Sunday, the fourth-year pro will take over the struggling Eagles offense after Jalen Hurts was ruled out indefinitely Thursday with a superficial blood clot in his leg.
“I think I was a little early,” Mailata laughed when Eagles On SI asked about his team's bad luck this season. “I might have jumped the gun on that one. Holy cow! That's the NFL, man. It's the gift that keeps on giving."
The situation unfolded after Hurts asked the training staff to treat his calf late last week after taking a cleat to the leg during the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. The results of an ultrasound performed after the team flew to London in the subsequent days showed the superficial blood clot, but medical staff concluded the Super Bowl-winning quarterback could safely play.
From there, a follow-up ultrasound performed on Wednesday night revealed movement in the small clot. As a result, Hurts will sit out this weekend and possibly beyond that, depending on what needs to be done from a medical standpoint .
The Eagles’ medical staff say they are determining the appropriate course of treatment.
“Superficial blood clots form near the skin's surface and, while generally less dangerous than deep vein thrombosis (DVT), must be taken seriously. If a clot extends into deeper veins, it can cause severe complications, including traveling to the lungs," explains Dr. Alina Mitina, Emergency Medicine Physician at Hackensack University Medical Center (HUMC). "While many resolve with simple treatments like warm compresses and anti-inflammatories, the clot's size and location determine whether blood thinners are necessary.
“Recent trauma and prolonged inactivity are major risk factors. Although we can't definitively say the flight to London worsened his condition, combining long-distance air travel with a recent leg injury creates a higher-risk environment for a clot to progress."
With Hurts sidelined, the Eagles turn to McKee, a 6-foot-6 pocket passer drafted in the sixth round out of Stanford in 2023. He has just two career starts and limited regular-season snaps (54 of 88 for 597 yards, five touchdowns, and one interception), but he has impressed in spots, including a solid Week 18 performance in 2024.
The team recently released veteran Andy Dalton, solidifying McKee as the clear No. 2 before the injury elevated him further; rookie Cole Payton is now the primary backup.⁠
The change comes at a precarious moment for an offense that ranks near the bottom of the league in scoring, yards, and efficiency under first-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. Hired from the Packers (where he served as quarterbacks coach under Matt LaFleur) after playing under Sean McVay and in Kevin O’Connell’s system, Mannion has installed a scheme rooted in the McVay/Shanahan tree: the goals of more under-center work, heavy play-action, wide-zone running concepts, motion, and pure progression reads rather than the RPO-heavy, dual-threat-friendly attack that previously maximized Hurts.
That philosophical shift has been a work in progress and, by most accounts, an imperfect marriage for Hurts, whose strengths as a runner and off-schedule playmaker have been featured less amid the new structure.
Mannion, meanwhile, has repeatedly said the core tenets of the offense remain non-negotiable even as results lag, with the unit averaging under 15 points and struggling to sustain drives during a three-game skid. ⁠
McKee is perceived as a more traditional pocket passer, although his processing has been slow when given opportunities in training camp and the preseason.
That said, inserting the Stanford product could offer a clearer picture into whether the scheme’s issues stem primarily from execution, personnel, or a fundamental mismatch with Hurts’ skill set.
A better fit for McKee might allow Mannion’s preferred play-action and progression concepts to better shine, even if the Eagles lose Hurts’ unique dual-threat dimension.
How long Hurts remains out—and whether McKee’s stint reveals more about the long-term viability of Mannion’s offense—could shape Philadelphia’s path through the rest of the season and into the future.
For an offense still searching for identity, the next several games may serve as an unplanned but needed evaluation of both Hurts’ fit into Mannion’s vision and the system itself.

title: Everything Important Eagles Players Said About Jalen Hurts Injury After Today's Practice
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Markel Bell arrived at Thursday morning’s walkthrough, glanced about the field, and didn’t see the No. 1. Jalen Hurts wasn’t there.
Players then saw Tanner McKee in the huddle, and they began checking their phones. That was how the Eagles learned the news that their quarterback would not play on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers as the QB and the organization determine the best course of treatment for the superficial blood clot in his calf.
“I didn't hear about it until I got to my phone,” said the rookie right tackle. “I got to my phone after walk-through. I found out when you guys found out. I was sitting around and I'm like, ‘Dang,’ like, ‘Wow,’ this is crazy.”
Bell’s recollection of finding out about Hurts was echoed among others in the locker room on Thursday.
“I found out when you guys found out,” said left tackle Jordan Mailata. “It's insane.”
Added linebacker Zack Baun: “It was shocking, And then to find out that he had been dealing with it last game was very shocking. But it just shows his toughness, his grit, his attitude, his willingness to win. I hope he gets better soon. I really do.”
It’s been that kind of season so far for the Eagles, with one big injury, followed by another big injury, followed by Lane Johnson's retirement, the Cam Jurgens trade, and then another injury.
“It'll be a good story to tell once I get older and all that and in my career as well,” said Bell, “but right now, my vet retires, Cam gets traded, all the injuries, it’s just crazy.”
The Eagles don’t have time to dwell on crazy. They have a game on Sunday and are trying to find a way to snap a three-game losing streak. And they’ll have to do it without Hurts and several other players that could include DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley.
“Just gotta keep my brother up in prayers, and that's what we're doing,” said Darius Cooper, who has become a favorite target for Hurts, with four touchdown catches on just seven receptions. “We just have to continue to encourage him and continue to walk with him through it.”
The Eagles will turn to Tanner McKee, who began the season as the third-string quarterback but was elevated to No. 2 when they released Andy Dalton on Oct. 9. McKee said he found out before the team’s morning walkthrough that he would be the starter.
It was at his locker when Hurts turned to him and said, “It looks like you’re going to be the guy.”
“It was like, ‘OK, well I'm taking the one reps now, and let's move like I'm gonna be the guy," said McKee. “As a backup quarterback, that's the mindset you have to have. At any moment you can be ready to play. On Sunday, it could be the first play; it could be the last play; you have to be ready.”
The Eagles hope it will be every play for McKee against the Panthers because his backup is rookie Cole Payton.
“It's not like Tanner's a new guy,” said Mailata. “He's been here for four years. Love everything about him. His poise, his energy, too. High energy guy.
“It's not Jalen, where Jalen's like cool, calm, collected 24/7. Tanner provides great... there's a very calm nature about him, but there's also a lot of high energy in him, too, just the way he attacks the practice.”

title: 2 Winners & 4 Losers Following Jalen Hurts Blood Clot Health Scare
full_text:
Looking to end their growing losing streak in Week 6 , the Eagles were dealt a massive blow that will make defeating the Panthers even more difficult this weekend. On Thursday, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts will be sidelined for Sunday's clash due to a "superficial blood clot."
According to a statement released by the Eagles, Hurts has been dealing with the issue since he was "cleated" during the Week 4 clash with the Rams. Although he ultimately faced the Jaguars and even practiced to begin the new week, "a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement" on Wednesday, leading Philadelphia to opt to sit Hurts for at least one game.
Breaking: #Eagles QB Jalen Hurts is out for Sunday due to a superficial blood clot. Full statement from the #Eagles on QB Jalen Hurts: “On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf. He informed the medical staff he… pic.twitter.com/16hVutehsp
Hurts has been far from perfect this season (57.8% completion rate, 84.7 passer rating), but it isn't a secret that his absence in Week 6 will impact the Eagles—for better or worse. His upcoming absence will negatively impact at least four members of the Philadelphia organization this week, as well as a pair who could benefit from not having him around.
Anytime a starting QB misses a game, his head coach's job is usually tougher. That's about to be the case for Eagles HC Nick Sirianni, whose fate hinges on each passing game.
Sirianni's play-calling and leadership have come under question throughout the last two seasons, and that's been even more the case now that Philadelphia is on a three-game skid. The Eagles have averaged only 14.7 points during that stretch, all while being outscored by an average margin of 9.0 ppg. Now, it's going to be an even more uphill battle to put up points without Hurts in the mix, adding even more pressure to Sirianni's job.
Sirianni has been without Hurts seven times since the start of the 2021 season, and the results aren't promising. The Eagles own an uninspiring 3-4 record in those contests, which includes being held to 20 or fewer points in three of the last four. In other words, Sirianni needs to buck that trend to prove that he's still the right man for the job.
In terms of players, Darius Cooper might suffer the most from not having Hurts on the field this weekend.
After all, the former undrafted wideout out of Tarleton State is coming off the best performance of his young NFL career. Cooper recorded two catches for 71 receiving yards and a touchdown against the Jaguars in London, which included a beautiful 62-yard score late in the second quarter (h/t NFL).
DARIUS COOPER, 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN EAGLES TAKE THE LEAD. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/eKpCwhW8QZ
Cooper now has 104 receiving yards and three TDs in his last two games, which puts him on pace for a 43-884-25 stat line in 17 games. Obviously, scoring that many touchdowns would be nearly impossible, but the reception and yardage totals underscore what Cooper might be losing now that Hurts is out of commission for at least one week.
That said, Cooper has seen plenty of Eagles backup QB Tanner McKee in practice over the last two years, leaving time to tell whether that familiarity will produce in-game results.
When one door closes, another opens, and now all eyes are on McKee to see if he'll stroll through or stumble in the face of his new opportunity.
Barring any setbacks, McKee will be the Eagles' QB1 against the Panthers, marking his first start since a 24-17 loss to the Commanders in Week 18 of the 2025 season. The former 2023 sixth-rounder now has a decent amount of experience after making six appearances (two starts) for Philadelphia since being drafted, in which he completed 61.4% of passes for 597 yards, five touchdowns,  one interception and a 99.5 passer rating.
After a strong end to the preseason , all eyes will be on McKee to see what he can do against the Panthers, who might allow the 11th-most passing yards per game (230.8), but have also surrendered the fifth-worst completion rate (61.1%) and fourth-fewest passing TDs (4) so far.
Considering how he'll be an unrestricted free agent in March, capitalizing on any opportunities he sees during Hurts's time away could be huge for McKee's future, either in Philly or elsewhere.
Circling back to the coaching staff, offensive coordinator Sean Mannion is another Eagle impacted by Hurts's Week 6 absence.
The former Packers QBs coach hasn't had the expected impact after taking over the Eagles' OC role in the offseason. Philadelphia has entered the week ranked 29th in points, 31st in total yards, 28th in passing yards and T-10th in rushing yards, truly underscoring how disastrous the ball movement has been under Mannion's guidance.
Well, an already difficult job just became harder because now Mannion needs to prove to the Eagles that he's the right offensive coordinator without Hurts. His play-calling has already left little room for optimism, so it's hard to imagine that things will magically improve without the straw that stirs Philly's drink.
Having no Hurts on the field means that the Eagles' defense could see a lot more action this weekend.
The early offensive issues to begin the season mean that Philadelphia's defenders have already seen more action than the team would like. The Eagles' offense has only held the ball for an average of 27:50 per game, which ranks 27th in the NFL, making the defense one of the league's most-worked units.
For comparison, the offense controlled the ball for an average of 30:16 in 2025 (12th) and a league-leading 32:21 in 2024.
The Bears, Rams and Jaguars all beat the Eagles by controlling the ball, each finishing with 30 to 35 minutes of possession time, and that was with Hurts. Without their franchise signal-caller, the Eagles' defense will likely be on the field more often than not against the Panthers, who know how to tire teams out, as they average the third-most offensive plays per game this season (67.0).
Needless to say, expect the Eagles' defense to remain busy throughout Hurts's absence, no matter how long it lasts.
The Eagles raised some eyebrows when they traded a seventh-round pick to acquire Andy Dalton from the Panthers back in March. Although Dalton is an experienced backup QB, the fact that McKee was already around made the move somewhat redundant. Even Philadelphia seemingly admitted that it was a mistake by releasing Dalton last week after throwing an INT on his lone passing attempt of the year.
Fast-forward less than a week, and Hurts's injury may have paved the way for Dalton's return to the City of Brotherly Love. Even NFL insider Mark Garafolo thinks there's a chance for a reunion , despite the fact that Dalton has "had a few teams check in with him since the team released him."
Andy Dalton is an option to return for the #Eagles . He’s had a few teams check in with him since the team released him, per sources, though there’s familiarity and a clear role in Philly for him if he decides to return. https://t.co/bNeypdIjiO
That isn't to say Dalton should be the primary signal-caller without Hurts around (that should still be McKee). However, it certainly wouldn't hurt the Eagles to bring him back. Rookie QB Cole Payton is on the 53-man roster but lacks the experience to step in if something happens to McKee, and there aren't any other options on the practice squad.
Dalton's best days are behind him, but he'd at least provide a steady presence behind McKee, and his familiarity from being around Sirianni and company for the last nine-ish months is a bonus.

title: Medical Expert Weighs in on Jalen Hurts Blood Clot Situation as Questions Surround Eagles
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — There are several different angles to view the news that broke Thursday midafternoon about Eagles starting quarterback Jalen Hurts after it was announced that he has a superficial blood clot in his calf and will not play in Sunday’s game against the Panthers.
pic.twitter.com/9SeK1XzYRL
How did Hurts get cleared to play against the Jaguars on Sunday? More importantly, how was he able to fly such a great distance in such a short period of time, going from Philly to London?
He said he was cleated on the calf against the Rams, but didn't look for treatment until Friday, the day the Eagles flew to London.
Will he be OK in the long term? What about the short term? What is the prognosis for return to play? Could this be a one-week situation or multiple weeks?
There are more questions will emerge. Right now, the situation is still new, and there is a game to play in about three days.
Eagles on SI received an email from Dr. Alina Mitina, an emergency physician at Hackensack Medical Center, that helps make sense of Hurts's situation, reading:
“Superficial blood clots form near the skin’s surface and, while generally less dangerous than deep vein thrombosis (DVT), must be taken seriously. If a clot extends into deeper veins, it can cause severe complications, including traveling to the lungs. While many resolve with simple treatments like warm compresses and anti-inflammatories, the clot’s size and location determine whether blood thinners are necessary."
In the short term, the Eagles are down to just two quarterbacks: Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton. They released Andy Dalton last week , but may now look to bring him back to the practice squad to serve as the backup to McKee.
Dalton and McKee waged a summer-long battle to be the primary backup and by doing that, Payton probably didn’t get the development he needed to possibly be ready should something in-game happen to McKee.
Hurts’s injury is the latest in what has been a landslide of injuries this season. There were 17 players listed on Wednesday’s injury report : six of whom did not practice and 11 others who were limited.
Some key players weren’t at Thursday’s practice either, including wideout DeVonta Smith and running back Saquon Barkley.
So, it looks like the Eagles will take the field on Sunday with a backup quarterback, a fourth-string running back in Dameon Pierce and an offensive line that last week saw two undrafted free agents start, Willie Lampkin and Jake Majors, and a third-round rookie, Markel Bell, make just his second career start at right tackle.

title: Jalen Hurts Calls Gelling New Offense a 'Challenge' as Eagles as Key Reinforcements Loom
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles' practice report was 24 players deep on Wednesday as the team kicked off on-field preparation for their Week 6 game against the Panthers.
Days after a difficult 19-17 loss to the Jaguars in London, quarterback Jalen Hurts acknowledged that all the moving parts have affected the idea of “gelling” with a new offense.
“It's a challenge. It's a challenge,” the Eagles’ on-field leader admitted when asked about the current on-field snapshot by Eagles On SI . Philadelphia was down to its fourth running back and No. 3 options at center and left guard against the Jags.
“I don't think that's [a challenge] that we're naive of,” Hurts noted. “I think for me, it's always pushing for that connection and that synergy so everybody's on the same page.”
Hidden by the devastation of the latest setback , the team’s third consecutive loss, against a team many consider to be a legitimate Super Bowl contender, was that the Eagles persevered and were in a position to win with eight seconds left if they could have found a way to execute on kickoff coverage.
That part of the equation turned out to be true, just as it was in Week 4 when Philadelphia came up just short of the Rams, another well-regarded contender.
Fortunately, reinforcements are on the way.
The Eagles started the practice windows of four players on injured reserve Wednesday, most notably three-time Pro Bowl guard Landon Dickerson.
If Dickerson is healthy enough to be serviceable on the interior of the offensive line, that should be a big boost to Sean Mannion’s struggling offense . Getting back potential pass-catching tight ends Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers could also help Mannion vary his personnel groupings more consistently.
In what’s shaping up to be a poor division, there can be a strong argument that the Eagles remain the most likely team to come out of the NFC East as the slow trickle of contributors coming back continues over the coming weeks.
In the meantime, younger players are getting valuable reps to bank for the future.
“We've got a lot that we can be better at, a lot that we can learn from,” Hurts said. “But with the new guys and the preparation and the hunger that they have, it was a different feeling when I looked into their eyes in the huddle.”
That feeling encourages Hurts.
The larger purpose remains gelling to get back to the winning the Eagles are accustomed to.
“Just wanting to win and desire to win,” said Hurts. “When you talk about gelling and wanting to do things a certain way, can't forget what the larger purpose is. And that's to go out there and find ways to win. And so, we've got to find our identity and being able to do that.”
For Hurts, the past is the past, and the goal is getting this group—no matter what it looks like—up to speed.
“... It's hard for me to compare to the past because this is not the past,” he said. “We got where we are right now. So it's more of a focus of what do we do to get this right in this moment with this group and this team.”

title: 5 Eagles Trade Candidates If They Become Sellers With 4 Key Games Coming Up
full_text:
The Eagles have four games left before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, with three at Lincoln Financial Field and three against NFC East opponents. They head into their bye week after hosting the New York Giants on Nov. 8.
How different they will look when they emerge from their bye to host the Pittsburgh Steelers on Nov. 22 likely depends on how they navigate the next four games.
The Eagles, mired in a three-game losing streak to fall to 2-3, could be buyers or sellers. It’s been a long time since they were sellers. If they right the ship, they could cruise into the bye at 6-3 and become buyers. If they go 2-2 and fall to 4-5, then they could be sellers.
Here are five players who could be traded if the ship continues to sink:
The defensive tackle is probably a goner, whether it’s before the trade deadline or after the season. A buyer would need to pony up a nice price because the Eagles could get what they can from him this year, and when he leaves in the offseason—assuming they cannot afford to re-sign him—they would likely get a third-round compensatory pick. Anything the Eagles get back would have to be more than that.
The seven-year outside linebacker/edge rusher is fifth on the depth chart behind Jonathan Greenard, Nolan Smith, Jalyx Hunt, and A.J. Ebiketie. He’s probably expendable, but the return wouldn’t be much.
At 29, the running back has had trouble avoiding injury this season, suffering a stinger in Week 2 and missing last week’s game with a hamstring injury. He still looked like he has plenty in the tank when he was healthy, and if he is and can remain that way, he could help the Eagles avoid potentially being traded.
There would be an enormous dead money hit of $35 million if he is dealt, so the likelihood of him getting shipped out is small.
It might be easier to deal the veteran tight end if Eli Stowers were ready for a role, but the rookie second-round pick just had his practice window opened to return from IR, where he spent the first five weeks of the season. The Eagles could still deal Goedert, though, if they like the value they are getting back. Perhaps Stowers will be ready for a role in November, and maybe Zach Ertz has been added to the roster by then.
The Eagles would really have to bottom out to consider moving one of the league’s best off-ball linebackers. He is signed through next year with a salary-cap hit of $11.8 million, which isn’t a bad price for a player who has led the team in tackles in each of his first two seasons in town and could do it again this year.

title: Inside Jalen Hurts’ One-on-One Session with Darius Cooper (and Why it Mattered)
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts emphasized the importance of intentional relationship-building with his receivers during his weekly media session on Wednesday, highlighting a one-hour one-on-one session with Darius Cooper the week before the team’s recent loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.
With established wideout DeVonta Smith sidelined with a hamstring injury in recent weeks, Hurts has leaned on a group of less-experienced options including Cooper, Dontayvion Wicks, and rookie Makai Lemon.
The QB1 described the growing trust within that group amid the adversity of adjusting on the fly.
“We have a lot of trust, and I think, in essence, there’s value in that. There’s value in those experiences,” Hurts said.
The veteran quarterback drew from the experiences of his own career, noting how past periods of downtime and challenges helped him evaluate how teammates respond under pressure.
“When I reflect on my experiences as a quarterback, think about the downtime and think about the times where we had adversity in front of us, and I can look at the guys around me and see how we responded to that,” said Hurts. “And that gave me the utmost encouragement to be able to move forward and have confidence and overcome.”
Hurts pointed specifically to his meeting with Cooper as an example of raising the standard of his approach.
“As I gave an example of Darius Cooper, you know, last week we met one-on-one for an hour, and the product was that in itself,” Hurts said.
He added that while chemistry with longer-tenured teammates has often developed more naturally, the current situation calls for deliberate effort.
“I don’t think there can be any slight to prioritize that and building that bond, ’cause ultimately in the past, those bonds were very natural, and the chemistry was already there. So that’s just something that I would love to be intentional on.”
Cooper described the session as mostly conversation rather than pure football talk.
“We were really just talking. You know, of course we was talking a little ball. But really just talking, having a good conversation. And that just builds trust,” the second-year receiver said. “And we ended up connecting on a touchdown, so I think it goes hand-in-hand being able to have just a good relationship with your teammates. It makes you wanna play for them instead of just playing with them.
The connection between the two has grown since Cooper joined the team last year, according to the receiver.
Asked about the significance of Hurts seeking out that individual time, Cooper replied simply,
“Yeah. It’s pretty cool. It’s pretty cool, man. Me and Jaylen, our relationship has grown over the years since I’ve been here… and it would just keep improving,” the wideout said.
Cooper tied the chemistry directly to the 62-yard touchdown the pair connected on in the game, his fourth TD of the young season.
“I think it’s just… self-explanatory. Just you communicate with someone, you know them, and you trust them,” Cooper said. “So when moments like that come up in the game, it’s like we talked about it, you know? It’s like you kind of talking [it] to existence.”
Cooper added that continued reps and one-on-one communication will only strengthen the connection as the season progresses.

title: Concerns Grow as Eagles' First Week 6 Injury Report Includes a Third of the Team
full_text:
It’s not easy to know where to start when it comes to the Eagles’ Wednesday injury report, so let’s start at the beginning.
There were 17 players listed either as not participating or limited participants. That’s darn near a third of the team. Things can only get better as the week goes on, right? At least quarterback Jalen Hurts wasn’t on it.
The Eagles didn’t list the QB on their injury report until last Friday, just before boarding a plane to London. He had a calf injury that he said happened last week in the loss to the Rams.
“It was a very unique experience to say the least,” Hurts said on Wednesday. “I don't want to get into the details of kind of leading up to the game or whatnot, but I got nicked up in the Rams game.”
It’s why Hurts didn’t take the field at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium until just before kickoff. He was trying to get loose. That could explain why he ran just twice for two yards in the loss to the Jaguars, and the Eagles didn’t try a tush push in short-yardage situations.
So, maybe that’s good news for Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers, because there have to be some worries with an injury report the length of an arm.
Six players did not practice: running backs Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Will Shipley (foot); safety Michael Carter (abdomen); outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle); offensive lineman Drew Kendall (knee); and receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring/toe).
Barkley, Smith, and Kendall missed last week’s game. It was the Eagles’ first game without Kendall since he took over center duties in Week 2.
Smith was counted on to be the team’s No. 1 receiver this season after A.J. Brown was traded, but he missed the previous two games. He was on pace for a career season after three games, with 19 catches on 27 targets for 235 yards and one touchdown.
The Eagles have been in scramble mode. Well, Hurts has, anyway. He was asked about the trust factor with receivers not named Smith, each of them new to the team, except Darius Cooper, who is in just his second year with the Eagles.
“Building a lot of trust, and there's value in that,” said the QB. “There's value in those experiences, and ultimately there's time right now. When I reflect on my experiences as a quarterback, I  think about the down times; I think about the times where we had adversity in front of us, and I could look at the guys around me and see how we responded to that. And that gave me the utmost encouragement to be able to build forward and have confidence in what will come.
“And I think the same thing about where we are right now with this group. The plays that are being made and things that are being put on tape and then the conversations that are being had.”
Without Barkley, Shipley and Tank Bigsby, who was put on IR last week, the Eagles will be awfully thin at running back with Dameon Pierce and probably Carson Steele and possibly Jaydon Blue, who is on the practice squad.
Carter’s absence in the secondary could mean that Kenny Moore will have to start at safety, something he has never done before, though he had a good run at that position when Carter left early with his injury.
Players listed as limited were cornerback Jakorian Bennett (knee); receivers Tay Wicks (hamstring) and Hollywood Brown (ankle); tight ends Grant Calcaterra (back), Eli Stowers (quad), and E.J. Jenkins (toe); left guard Landon Dickerson (knee) and right guard Tyler Steen (shoulder); outside linebackers Jonathan Greenard (ankle) and A.J. Epenesa (back); and safety Marcus Epps (groin).

title: Sirianni-Hurts Duo Suddenly Reminding Eagles Fans of Painful History
full_text:
Before Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts arrived on the scene, the Philadelphia Eagles were no strangers to the funky loss.
Losses that had fans up for nights on end wondering how the team blew the game. Defeats that had fans wondering how positive the future would be. Sure, the team had won a Super Bowl during that time frame, but the Eagles had a history of losing in some of the most bizarre ways.
For five years, things were different. Sirianni had built a culture that never seemed to play down to competition. They had a quarterback who would never make the bone-headed play. Every time the Eagles were in a clutch situation, they always seemed to make the obvious and easy call to execute.
What makes the team's 2-3 start to the season so frustrating for Eagles fans isn't just the fact that they are on a three-game losing streak, or have the worst second-half offense in recent memory.
No, the underlying frustration in Philadelphia is because, for the first time in five years, Sirianni and Hurts look like every other coach and quarterback duo that had come before him. The logic has been lost. The clutch gene, nonexistent.
It's frustrating, because the most successful QB-HC duo in team history has finally come down to earth.
There are detractors to both Sirianni and Hurts citing the fact that it was general manager Howie Roseman who built such dominant rosters for the team over the last five years. The argument is that the head coach and quarterback only needed to not screw up, and they would win a lot of games.
Those arguments are disingenuous compared to what Eagles fans have gone through over the last nearly three decades.
Andy Reid, for example, had a top-five defense for most of his career, a franchise QB, a great running back, and failed to win a Super Bowl because he made decisions in big games that hurt the team. Chip Kelly lasted three seasons in Philadelphia. Doug Pederson caught lightning in a bottle, but was never able to duplicate the success in later seasons.
Pick a frustrating loss: every past head coach in team history has had them:
Sunday's loss to Jacksonville was not uncommon in Eagles history. In fact, they are a dime a dozen.
It's not just in Eagles history either. Kyle Shanahan and Sean McVay are considered two of the most elite coaches in football right now. Shanahan has a penchant for losing in big moments, and McVay hasn't been back to the Super Bowl since 2021. During that same stretch, the Eagles won a Super Bowl by 18, and went to a second one.
The level of consistent domination the franchise has put forth over five years under Sirianni and Hurts is unprecedented. In many ways, Eagles fans should be more patient and appreciative of the two going forward.
But that's not how this city is. People will argue about needing a new coach and quarterback so long as the losing continues.
The frustration stems, though, not just based on execution or missed calls from the coaching staff. It's based on the fact no one has won quite like Sirianni and Hurts.
And for the first time in years, it seems like they both are running out of wins.

title: What to Expect as Eagles Open Practice Window for Four Players on IR
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Help could soon be on the way for the Eagles, after the team opened the practice windows for four players before Wednesday’s first practice of Week 6.
Those players are left guard Landon Dickerson, cornerback Jakorian Bennett, and tight ends Grant Calcaterra and rookie second-round pick Eli Stowers. The Eagles have 21 days before having to make a decision to add them back onto the 53-man roster or shut them down for the season.
Some tough decisions will need to be made to find room on the roster when the time comes.
Here’s a closer look at the four who could return:
Dickerson: The three-time Pro Bowl left guard played in the opener but didn’t play well. He said he had a bone bruise in his right knee and admitted he was embarrassed by his performance in that Week 1 win against the Commanders.
“You guys know Landon well, he works hard, he's determined to get back, and I think he's done a nice job taking care of his body to get himself back,” said head coach Nick Sirianni before Wednesday’s practice and before the news was made official. “Landon's a hell of a player and he's been a hell of a player for us.”
The move to put Dickerson on IR created turmoil on the offensive line. Cam Jurgens was moved from center to left guard. Then new center Drew Kendall, in his second season from Boston College, was plugged in at center.
Jurgens was eventually traded and, when Kendall couldn’t play in London, Willie Lampkin made his first career start at left guard and Jake Majors was elevated from the practice squad to make his first pro start.
Getting Dickerson back would be a most welcome addition.
Stowers: In the days leading up to the opener, the rookie said he expected to have a role against Washington. Then, hours later, he was placed on IR with a quad strain. He still needs to develop, but he should make the team feel better at the position.
Dallas Goedert missed two games with a knee injury, and the Eagles signed Zach Ertz to try to make up for some of the offense that was gone when Goedert had to sit. Stowers is an offensive-minded tight end, albeit one who is in just his third year playing the position, and was the John Mackey Award winner for the nation’s best tight end while at Vanderbilt.
Calcaterra: Another offensive-minded tight end, who returned this offseason on a one-year contract. He will provide solid depth.
Bennett: The cornerback hasn’t done much since the Eagles acquired him in a trade last summer, but like Calcaterra, he could provide depth if needed.

title: No One Knows What Steelers Trade Deadline Plans Are
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have several needs across their roster. So, that means they will be aggressive buyers before this year's NFL trade deadline, right?
Well, that might be the case for the Steelers, depending on which beat writer you subscribe to. If you are an ardent believer in long-time insider Gerry Dulac, that feels like a stretch. In his recent mailbag article for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette , he shot down the idea of a trade, barring more significant injuries.
But if you are a Mark Kaboly fan, you're now expecting the exact opposite. Via an update on his X account, he shared that sources indicated to him that the Steelers are very interested in upgrading with a trade.
Getting strong indications that the Steelers are going to be active heading into the NFL trade deadline set for Nov. 10
So, which is it? Are the Steelers on the prowl or are they standing pat? The answer is more complicated than you think.
The short answer is that the Steelers are constantly trying to upgrade; it's just that their approach is hardly what you would expect. The team has already been active in trying to improve their roster. They added two veteran defensive backs via other organizations' practice squads, bringing in Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terrell Smith recently to bolster their depth.
That's the likeliest route this team will take when addressing their biggest issue currently: wide receiver. Down three players from their active roster, the offense needs a boost. This is where the varying opinions diverge.
The reality, however, is that the Steelers are extremely unlikely to give up the draft capital they just acquired or previously stockpiled on immediate wide receiver help. Despite sources indicating to Kaboly that the Steelers are shopping, don't buy the rumors that they are shopping for big-time names.
Instead, the focus should be on veteran names on practice squads, just like they did at cornerback. Names like K.J. Osbsorn, Mecole Hardman, Lil'Jordan Humphrey, Jalin Hyatt, Scotty Miller, Trey Palmer and Xavier Gipson make much more sense and fit the profile of their previous acquisitions.
Where I really expect a trade to occur for the Steelers is on the defensive side of the ball. The Steelers can probably get a temporary replacement at wide receiver by poaching a practice squad or signing one of the few NFL-caliber receivers available in free agency, but they cannot upgrade their defensive inefficiencies the same way.
Instead, the Steelers need a true upgrade outside of the organization at several positions. The first one still might be cornerback, unless Murphy-Bunting becomes that dependable outside presence. The second is safety, which continues to hamper their secondary. The third is inside linebacker, as the entire depth chart has underwhelmed to start the season.
If a trade is happening, it's on the defensive side of the ball.
But that's only if a deal gets done. And depending on who you trust and what you read, you will come away with various answers on the subject.

title: Steelers WR Outlook: Who's Replacing Roman Wilson?
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers need to replace two more wide receivers in Week 6. With Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek missing the team's matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the black and gold need to add to their depth chart. So, who is joining the mix?
It's unknown how much time Wilson (finger) and Skowronek (calf) will miss, so for now, the team is taking things week-to-week with their replacements. Pittsburgh is also without Michael Pittman Jr., who is on Injured Reserve with a foot injury, leaving DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Kaden Wetjen on their active roster.
Which is where we should begin.
Wetjen brings plenty of excitement as a kick and punt returner, but not much as a wideout. The Iowa product and fourth-round rookie has been the team's focal point on special teams, but isn't ready to be an offensive threat.
Head coach Mike McCarthy even said Wetjen hasn't done much to prepare for a larger role within the receiving core.
"He's hasn’t gotten a lot of work as far as our primary game plan and things like that, but he's developing," McCarthy said. "He's out here every day working, so as far as how we use him so forth, we’ll let the games dictate that."
That leaves Metcalf and Bernard. The veteran and rookie will be the WR1 and WR2 for the Steelers this weekend.
Metcalf continues to be the front-runner of the receiver room, with Bernard breaking out in Week 5 with an expanded role. The second-round pick tabbed six receptions for 80 yards against the Indianapolis Colts and is now looking at even more attention after the loss of Wilson.
They won't be alone, though. The Steelers are preparing to run a lot of two-tight end sets, utilizing Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington as much as possible.
Robert Tonyan will also be involved.
Enter Brandon Smith, Brandon Johnson and Isaiah Hodgins.
The Steelers are expected to call Smith up for a second straight game off of the practice squad. The 27-year-old wideout didn't record a catch last week, but was involved in a 50-yard touchdown by Jaylen Warren. Smith and Washington were the two downfield blockers as Warren found the seam.
Right now, Smith is the team's WR3 heading into Week 6.
"It seems like at this point it's just in-house options," Rodgers said. "So, we’vegot a talented [practice] squad group of guys and guys who played football at the highest level and made plays. Excited about getting those guys in. Obviously, [Tonyan] has played a lot of football and played at a high level, so I'm sure he'll get some more opportunities. [Brandon]Smith, Brandon Johnson, maybe Isaiah [Hodgins]. We'll get some guys who haven't seen a lot of time out there and expect them to play well."
It's likely the Steelers will call up two wide receivers from their practice squad this weekend. It's unknown whether it'll be Johnson or Hodgins, with both players having playing experience throughout their careers.
Johnson has 26 catches for 335 yards and five touchdowns throughout his career. Hodgins has 19 career starts, including five last year for the New York Giants. He's recorded 70 receptions for 749 yards and eight touchdowns during his career.
If Wilson needs to be placed on Injured Reserve, Smith will likely be signed to the active roster and Hodgins or Johnson will continue to be called up as needed.
There are a lot of moving parts for the Steelers' passing game in Week 6, and nothing is expected to slow down soon. Right now, there are no signs that the team will be looking outside of the organization for options. That could change.
But heading to Tampa Bay, this is how the Steelers will handle their wide receiver room.

title: Steelers Get Good Injury News Before Bucs Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have some positive developments on the injury front ahead of their Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
On their penultimate injury report of the week, running back Rico Dowdle (toe) was listed as a full participant, which is the first time that's been the case since he suffered his injury in Week 2 vs. the New England Patriots.
Furthermore, defensive tackle Keeanu Benton (ankle) and cornerback Jalen Ramsey (wrist) were both limited participants after registering as non-participants on the first injury report this week.
After missing three games in a row, Dowdle is finally on the precipice of a return for Pittsburgh.
He dislocated his toe twice against the Patriots, first in the second quarter and then in the third quarter in what was a 20-3 loss for the Steelers.
While speaking with reporters last week, the 28-year-old laid out how the entire process played out in that contest.
"The first time I did it, I came to the sideline and I was like, "I think my toe broke,'" Dowdle said. "So I went to the tent and it was dislocated and they popped it back in, did the X-rays. Nothing was broken or whatever, but once they popped it back in, I felt good, so I'm like, 'I wanna go back in the game and play.' Dr. [James] Bradley was like, 'No, we're playing on turf, think I'm gonna be done,' because when you get it, you hurt the plate at the bottom or whatever. So I ended up talking him into going back in, and he was like, 'If it pop out again, you've gotta be done,' and it popped out again, so I had to be done."
Following the team's Week 5 victory over the Indianapolis Colts, head coach Mike McCarthy stated that Dowdle was close to playing in that game .
Now, all the stars are aligning for him to be back on the field against the Bucs, even if it's not 100 percent official that he'll be active just yet.
Jaylen Warren will remain the feature back given that he has posted 491 yards in the three contests Dowdle has missed, but the latter will certainly still have a noticeable role in the offense.
Ramsey broke his wrist in Week 3 vs. the Cincinnati Bengals and has not been a full practice participant since, though he's still played since suffering that injury and his status for this week's bout with Tampa Bay was never really in question.
Benton was a surprise inclusion on the first injury report this week , though it doesn't appear that he's dealing with a serious ankle injury considering he's been upgraded to a limited participant alongside Ramsey.
The game designations for both players remains to be seen when the final injury report is put out on October 16, but it certainly would appear they'll each be active against the Bucs.

title: Steelers Chances vs. Bucs Skyrocket With QB News
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' chances of snagging a victory in Week 6 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers just rose.
Baker Mayfield was not practicing on October 15, as noted by Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times, meaning undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels is all but guaranteed to start against the Steelers.
Baker Mayfield is NOT practicing today so we can stop speculating. Jalon Daniels will start vs the Steelers barring something unforeseen. pic.twitter.com/GXWuYv23gp
Daniels has stepped in as the starter in each of the Buccaneers' last two games while Mayfield has dealt with a dislocated thumb that he suffered in Week 3 vs. the Minnesota Vikings.
While Daniels did help guide Tampa Bay to a victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football in Week 5, he still presents a far more favorable matchup at quarterback for Pittsburgh than Mayfield would.
Up to this point, Daniels has completed 38 of his 55 passing attempts for the Buccaneers for 337 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions.
He was not sharp in his first start against the Green Bay Packers, which was a 17-14 loss for Tampa Bay, as he went 19-of-27 for 148 yards, a touchdown and two picks.
Daniels was far more efficient vs. Dallas, however, completing 19 of his 25 attempts for 185 yards, a touchdown and no interceptions.
The 23-year-old has proven to be a real weapon with his legs as well, rushing for 55 yards on eight attempts against Green Bay and 23 yards on seven attempts vs. the Cowboys.
Daniels isn't going to push the ball down the field much at all, which could work to Pittsburgh's benefit, as his current average depth of target stands at 6.2 (per Pro Football Focus ).
The Buccaneers' offensive line has been quite good in pass protection with an allowed pressure rate of 37.6 percent (per SumerSports ), however, so the Steelers also can't afford to let Daniels sit back and pick them apart in the short and intermediate areas of the field like he did against Dallas.
Daniels has shown that he can win at the NFL level, though the Steelers ’ defense is far more stout than the Cowboys’ and is better equipped to stop a Tampa Bay offense that is led by him.
The Buccaneers are more competitive than their 1-4 record would suggest, but Pittsburgh is simply the better team.
Sure, it's never easy to win on the road and Tampa Bay has some form of momentum. At the same time, the Steelers ' defense really shouldn't have many issues getting the better of Daniels while also finding some level of success on offense against a Buccaneers defense that's been really strong thus far.
If Pittsburgh really is a playoff contender in the AFC moving forward, it has to come away with wins in situations like this.

title: Aaron Rodgers Leaks Steelers WR Plan
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have decisions to make at wide receiver. With Roman Wilson out with a finger injury and Michael Pittman Jr. on Injured Reserve with a foot injury, the team has lost two starters. Ben Skowronek (calf) is set to miss Week 6, and Pittsburgh needs to figure out how to add to their depth chart.
People are talking about outside options in Brian Thomas Jr. and Tyreek Hill. A reunion with JuJu Smith-Schuster has been floated around, and ESPN has even named five trade candidates the Steelers may be interested in.
But Aaron Rodgers has revealed their realistic plan, at least for Week 6. Speaking with media about the team's upcoming game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Rodgers was asked about the outlook at wideout, and gave love to the three players who may be filling in.
"It seems like at this point it's just in-house options," Rodgers said. "So, we’vegot a talented [practice] squad group of guys and guys who played football at the highest level and madeplays.Excited about getting those guys in. Obviously, [Tonyan] has played a lot of football and played at a high level, so I'm sure he'll get some more opportunities. [Brandon]Smith, Brandon Johnson, maybe Isaiah [Hodgins]. We'll get some guys who haven't seen a lot of time out there and expect them to play well."
Brandon Smith was impressive all summer. He caught the first pass during team drills during training camp, and immediately became the camp darling for the black and gold.
If not for an injury, he had a real chance of making the 53-man roster, and keeping him on the practice squad felt natural. He continued to make plays throughout training camp, and was expected to be the team's first call-up when needing wide receiver help this season.
At 27 years old, he's yet to record an in-game stat at the NFL level, but he'll need to with the Steelers over the next few weeks as he operates as WR3.
Brandon Johnson and Isaiah Hodgins have NFL experience. Johnson has 26 catches for 335 yards and five touchdowns throughout his career. He has one catch for nine yards with the Steelers in 2024.
Hodgins has 70 receptions for 749 yards and eight touchdowns. He's started 19 games during his NFL career, including five last year for the New York Giants.
Expect plenty of 12-personnel for Pittsburgh this weekend, trying to utilize Pat Freiermuth, Darnell Washington and Robert Tonyan more to make up for the loss of Wilson, Pittman Jr. and Skowronek.
But when it comes to who's going to play wide receiver for the Steelers these next few weeks, Rodgers has already told us.
