title: Steelers Gamble on Rookie DT Paying Off
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers gambled in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. How else could you describe the decision to take defensive lineman Gabriel Rubio out of Notre Dame?
The thing about gambling, though, is that sometimes it pays off. The Steelers are learning that firsthand with Rubio.
With injuries necessitating the rookie defensive tackle's NFL debut. Rubio went out there are did exactly what was asked of him. It was a small sample size in his first NFL action, but so far the gamble on Rubio is providing an impressive return.
Rubio is a massive human being. Walking by him in the locker room is a task, because he simply takes up a ton of space. Listed at 6'5" and 321 pounds on the team's official website, he's every bit of it in person.
Having the physical gifts is one thing, but you have to match that with drive, energy, technique and a desire to get better. Rubio possesses all of that.
The 23-year-old played in just 14 defensive snaps in Week 5, but he made each one count. For starters, he recorded three assisted tackles over those 14 plays, which is already impressive.
Even with the acknowledgment that he was in the game primarily in running situations, Rubio was an active player along the line of scrimmage. He displayed a never-ending motor after the snap, allowing him to shed blocks and continue toward the ball carrier.
That's what stuck out the most to me. He was taking on solid offensive linemen, but he was able to win the point of contact and get off the blocks in enough time to be the first one or close to the ball carrier. It's a credit to his ability to utilize his lower-body strength and large frame to his advantage. He doesn't have the fastest hands, yet, but his power and agility makes up for it, even at the NFL level.
Imagine where he will be as his technical abilities improve.
One play in particular highlighted Rubio's best traits. The Colts came out in 12 personnel, which they had been running out of frequently in Week 5. This time, however, it was a play-action passing play. Rubio was engaged with the left guard at the snap, fighting for ground. The play eventually turned into a pass to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor in the flat.
Rubio kept his head up the entire time, keeping a close eye on the quarterback. As soon as he noticed the pass, Rubio smartly disengaged with the guard, tried to get his hand up to bat the ball down, and when that failed, he took off toward the ball. Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson was the first man on the ball carrier, but Rubio was second. Despite being roughly 10 to 15 yards away from the ball when Taylor caught it, he closed in and helped end the play.
The Steelers might be ready to make some changes on defense, much like they did on offense after their Week 2 loss. Perhaps it's a linebacker trade , or perhaps it's an addition to the secondary.
But what will remain is the depth up front, which has become the strongest piece of the Steelers' defense. Rubio is a key cog in the machine. As second-year lineman Derrick Harmon recovers, Rubio will continue to get a hat on game day. If he keeps playing like this, whether it's 14 or 41 snaps, he will prove his long-term value to the franchise.
For a sixth-round flyer, that's pretty impressive. Rubio might not be an All-Pro in the future, but he gives the Steelers another legitimate defensive lineman to consider in their plans for the rest of 2026 and beyond.

title: Steelers WR Options Revealed: Who's Coming to Pittsburgh?
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers should have a pretty good idea of what wide receivers can be had via trade ahead of the November 10 deadline.
Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano , five receivers who may end up being the best remaining player dealt at the position after Marvin Harrison Jr. landed with the Houston Texans are Brian Thomas Jr. (Jacksonville Jaguars), Rashod Bateman (Baltimore Ravens), Quentin Johnston (Los Angeles Chargers), Jauan Jennings (Minnesota Vikings) and Jerry Jeudy (Cleveland Browns).
With nine picks in both the 2027 and 2028 NFL Drafts, Pittsburgh has the necessary assets to wheel and deal if it so chooses in the lead-up to the deadline.
Receiver stands out as one of the team's biggest needs with Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on the reserve/injured list while both Roman Wilson (hand/finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have already been ruled out for the Steelers' Week 6 bout with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Of the names Fowler and Graziano mentioned, however, who are the best fits for Pittsburgh?
Intra-division trades aren't commonplace in the NFL, and there's always going to be some extra layers when such a deal takes place that could complicate the entire process.
For that reason, it's hard to imagine a scenario in which Bateman or Jeudy ends up in Pittsburgh before the deadline.
The Ravens currently sit atop the AFC North at 4-1 and are Super Bowl contenders, meaning trading away a key piece at receiver in Bateman wouldn't be practical even if rookie Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) returns from IR and makes a huge impact.
That doesn't even factor in the rarity of a deal between Pittsburgh and Baltimore, as previously alluded to. The sides have made just two trades involving players, with the most recent example coming in 2020 when defensive end Chris Wormley went from the Ravens to the Steelers.
Pittsburgh and Cleveland have swapped players more frequently within the past decade or so, as the Browns rerouted Justin Gilbert to the Steelers in 2016 while the black and gold sent Sammie Coates the other way in 2017.
Still, the organizations aren't at all likely to link up on a trade involving Jeudy, who has just 81 yards through five games this season.
Jennings was there for the taking for Pittsburgh in the offseason considering he was a free agent through early May. He ended up signing a one-year deal worth $8 million with the Vikings, but he has just two catches for nine yards this season despite playing 201 offensive snaps over four games.
NFL Network's Ian Rapoport stated this week that Jennings' trade market is expected to heat up. He's an intriguing name to watch for the Steelers as a buy-low candidate who has proven to be a quality starter in the past, evidenced by the fact that he put up a combined 1,618 yards and 15 touchdowns for the San Francisco 49ers between the 2024 and 2025 campaigns.
Jennings will likely command a strong market on an expiring contract due to his surprising lack of production when compared to his total body of work, but Pittsburgh should certainly be in the mix.
Thomas Jr. has only logged 105 yards in five contests for Jacksonville in 2026 as he continues to fade following a standout rookie campaign back in 2024, during which he put up 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns.
He's been floated as a potential trade candidate dating back to last season, though it always seemed as if the price tag was too high.
Now that he's failed to make much of a splash under Liam Coen for a second straight year, however, perhaps the Steelers could swoop in and get him at a discount.
The Ringer's Tom Pelissero wrote in "The Sweep" on October 10 that the Jaguars haven't shown any interest in dealing Thomas Jr., though that could theoretically change before November 10.
Johnston also hasn't done much for the Chargers this year, having recorded 108 yards in four games, but that could be attributed to the team's disastrous start at 0-5 that's seen the offense completely fall apart.
The 2023 first-round pick did post a combined 1,446 yards and 16 touchdowns between the 2024 and 2025 seasons, and Los Angeles picked up his fifth-year option for the 2027 campaign at a fully guaranteed $18 million (per Over the Cap ).
Johnston wouldn't come cheap for Pittsburgh from a salary cap perspective, and he may fetch a valuable pick for the Chargers as well.
Between Jennings, Thomas Jr. and Johnston, Jennings feels like the most logical trade option for the Steelers when taking the asking price and salary cap ramifications into place.
From an upside perspective, though, Thomas Jr. is quite easily the most fascinating name of the bunch.

title: Steelers Could Lose Another Starting DT After Ankle Injury
full_text:
Another interior defensive linemen for the Pittsburgh Steelers is dealing with an injury.
On their first injury report ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Steelers listed Keeanu Benton as a non-participant with an ankle injury.
Cornerback Jalen Ramsey (wrist), wide receivers Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) and defensive tackle Cameron Heyward (NIR/Rest) all didn't practice as well.
Running back Rico Dowdle (toe), cornerback Jamel Dean (ankle), safety DeShon Elliott (knee) and EDGE rusher T.J. Watt (NIR/Rest) were all limited participants.
Elliott is still in his 21-day practice window , which was opened last week, while remaining on the reserve/injured list.
After watching Nick Herbig (four years, $100 million) and Darnell Washington (four years, $42 million) sign their extensions in early June, Benton had to wait until mid-August to get his own new deal from Pittsburgh.
When the time came, the 2023 second-round pick inked a four-year contract worth $72 million after recording a career-high  5.5 sacks in 2025.
The Steelers' new coaching staff has made it a point to move Benton around the defensive line more instead of having him primarily serve as a nose tackle, which was largely targeted at granting him more opportunities to get after the quarterback.
Benton has not posted a sack through five games up to this point while playing 190 defensive snaps, though, and he has seven pressures (per Pro Football Focus ).
It's too early to know whether or not Benton is in danger of missing Pittsburgh's bout with Tampa Bay this week.
Considering the Steelers are already down a key piece along the interior of their defensive line in Derrick Harmon, however, they could really use Benton vs. the Buccaneers.
Harmon was placed on IR last week with a foot injury he suffered in Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss at the hands of the Cleveland Browns.
He missed the Steelers' win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5 as a result, and he'll be out for a minimum of three more games as well.
Harmon's absence led to rookie sixth-round pick Gabriel Rubio being active for the first time this season vs. Indianapolis, however, and he flashed some really promising signs as a run defender while recording three assists on tackles over 14 defensive reps.
Rubio's snap count will likely rise if Benton can't suit up against Tampa Bay, and undrafted rookie Kevin Jobity Jr. could make his NFL debut as well after being inactive for each of the first five weeks of the campaign.

title: Elandon Roberts Clears the Air on Steelers Feelings
full_text:
Elandon Roberts shut down the notion that he had any issues with the Pittsburgh Steelers upon his return to the team.
Roberts, who signed to the Steelers' practice squad earlier this week , said that he has no hard feelings stemming from his surprise release at final roster cuts in late August and that he wouldn't have come back if that were the case since he would've been a distraction.
"It's real comfortable still," Roberts said. "Know the playbook still, know the expectation... I mean I have a great relationship with everybody upstairs. Coaches, everybody, so it's no hard feelings. If I had hard feelings, I wouldn't have came back because then that's a distraction to the team, and I'm here to do whatever it takes for the team to win and whatnot, so now I'm all good."
Inside linebacker was one of the position groups that was most in need of outside reinforcements during the offseason for Pittsburgh.
The organization didn't select any players at the position in the 2026 NFL Draft despite using 10 picks, and the group was ultimately the same heading into training camp as it was in 2025 after re-signing Cole Holcomb to a two-year, $5 million deal in March.
Given the unit's struggles last season, the lack of change was a pretty big surprise. Because Roberts was still on the free agent market come August, however, it wasn't too late for the Steelers to bring back the fan-favorite on a one-year contract and reunite him with Patrick Graham, who was Roberts' defensive coordinator with the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025.
Roberts was impressive throughout the preseason, finishing with 10 tackles over two games, and it felt like he was playing himself into a sizable role heading into the regular season.
Instead, the Steelers let him go in what ended up being the team's most unforeseen transaction on roster cutdown day.
With little improvement at inside linebacker in Graham's system, Pittsburgh had to make a move to supplement the group.
Payton Wilson has shown some growth as a run defender, though he's run into issues finishing tackles at times and isn't as stout in coverage as he should be for a player with his athletic tools.
Patrick Queen , in the final season of a three-year, $41 million deal, has continued to be inconsistent and potentially would have already lost his grasp on his starting spot if the Steelers were confident Cole Holcomb or even Carson Bruener could take on his workload.
Though Roberts is currently on the practice squad, it's not far-fetched to believe he'll eventually take snaps away from Queen in the near future.
A thumper who's always specialized as a downhill run defender with clear limitations in coverage, Roberts is the type of high-floor veteran that Pittsburgh has desperately needed at the position since his departure ahead of the 2025 campaign. It also helps that Roberts picked up experience playing alongside Wilson and Queen for the Steelers in 2024.
He isn't going to patch up all of the problems in the middle of Pittsburgh's defense, but he'll certainly make a difference whenever he is out there.

title: Mike Tomlin is Still a Steelers Fan - And That's Awesome
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Life without Mike Tomlin has been a roller coaster ride for the Pittsburgh Steelers. That's to be expected after Tomlin's 19-year tenure as head coach came to an end after the 2025 campaign.
Now, the Steelers have a new head coach in Mike McCarthy, while Tomlin shines in a new commentary role.
But even as both sides move on, there is a deep respect and mutual love. It's showed up during Tomlin's first season as an NFL analyst. Some have accused him of showcasing his Steelers bias while on television. When asked about it on an appearance on the New Heights podcast, he told Jason and Travis Kelce that he doesn't care if that bias shows. The way he sees it, it's inevitable after spending two decades in Pittsburgh.
"To be honest with ya, I don't care if I do," he said. "How can you be somewhere 19 years, man, and had really a personal stake in most of the guys being there and not care for 'em? Not root for 'em? Not be for 'em? I'm not gonna pretend that I'm not. I can't do that. Certainly, I got a job to do and I'm gonna do it. But everybody knows where my heart is and where my support is, and I'm not apologizing for that."
That's one looming question as the Steelers navigate their first season without Tomlin. Under McCarthy, the team is 3-2 entering Week 6. It hasn't been perfect, but the brightest spot so far is their 3-0 record at home and a slightly improved offense.
Right now, the Steelers miss him like you miss an old pal. You loved the times and reminiscing, but you aren't eager for them to return. Currently, eyes are forward for both Tomlin and Pittsburgh.
Even with all of that love, it's clear that Tomlin doesn't miss being a head coach. Speaking about his new gig, he referred to it as "part-time work" for "full-time pay." Despite rising speculation that the NFL wants Tomlin back on the sidelines, the former Steelers coach is enjoying life on the call at Sunday Night Football.
The Steelers see light at the end of the tunnel when it comes to implementing a new coaching staff. A rocky start is hopefully in the rearview after an impressive win over the Indianapolis Colts.
Things won't be fully decided until the calendar flips. The Steelers brought McCarthy to Pittsburgh to help end their decade-long playoff win drought. If he can accomplish that, he'll have the fanbase's trust for the rest of his contract.
If he fails, the sentimentality for Tomlin will certainly grow. The fanbase already misses the person that Mike Tomlin is, but it remains to be seen how badly they miss him as their head coach.
Through it all, Tomlin is a huge fan of his former team, and that's great news for the Steelers organization.

title: 3 Observations as Sam Darnold, Seahawks Lose vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are losers of consecutive games for the first time in nearly two years after falling to the Denver Broncos 17-14 in an overtime matchup on Thursday Night Football.
The Seahawks trailed 14-3 for most of the game, but a touchdown from running back George Holani, a two-point conversion from Rashid Shaheed, and a field goal from Jason Myers in the final seconds of the game tied it up and sent it to overtime.
Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold threw two interceptions, including one in overtime that set the Broncos up in field goal range, leading to a Will Lutz 53-yard field goal to finish the game. Here's a look at the three observations from the game.
Darnold continues to struggle with taking care of the football. A pair of key interceptions during the game ultimately cost the Seahawks a victory. The Seahawks are 3-3, but they could easily be 6-0 if Darnold wasn't out here throwing interceptions.
The first one came late in the fourth quarter, inside the two-minute warning, when Seattle could have gone on a game-winning touchdown drive. The pick from Kris Abrams-Drain would have solidified the win for the Broncos, but they could not get a first down. That led to Seattle receiving the ball once more with little time left.
While Darnold was able to get the Seahawks into field goal range, all of that went into the trash bin when he threw another pick to Ja'Quan McMillian in overtime.
Simply put, this game was lost because Darnold was not taking care of the football. In a game where the Seahawks outgained the Broncos 353-168, they should have win, but they don't get the tally in the win column.
For three and a half quarters, the Seahawks' offense looked lifeless, and it wasn't just Darnold contributing to that. The offensive line put Darnold in uncomfortable situations throughout the evening. The team was unable to generate much rhythm on offense, and it starts in the trenches.
The Seahawks' offensive line has been up and down over the years, but last year they found some success, which ultimately made a massive difference. The offensive line plays such an important role on the team that if it is not performing at a championship level, this team is not a contender.
If there's any solace in tonight's loss, it's that the defense continues to play at an elite level. While they surrendered a pair of touchdown drives in the second quarter, most teams win football games when they only allow 17 points.
That wasn't the case tonight for the Seahawks, but they put the team in a position to win. Unfortunately, the offense didn't have their back, but there were some strong defensive plays all night long, even without any turnovers.
This team remains a defensive juggernaut and it can be a contender with this unit, but they may need to pick up even more of the slack if the Seahawks want to return to their winning ways.

title: 4 Winners & 2 Losers From Seahawks Frustrating OT Loss vs. Broncos
full_text:
The uniform matchup between the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football was easily the best of the season thus far. Both teams wore their throwbacks, reminding old-school fans of their time as AFC West rivals. Seattle was in that division from 1977-2001 and sported the royal blue jerseys from that era Thursday, while the Broncos had their orange crush look.
The game itself was a throwback as well, with both defenses playing lights out. The Broncos had a 14-3 lead at the half, but the Seahawks fought back, scoring 11 in the fourth quarter to send the game to overtime.
Once in the extra period, the Seahawks had the ball first but an interception from Sam Darnold set the Broncos up for the win. With this one in the books, let's see who stood out as winners and losers in the Week 6 loss.
A fumble in the first half from Rashid Shaheed cost Seattle points, but he was able to make up for it after that. Not only did he haul in a 42-yard reception to give the offense a spark in the second half, but he also made a beautiful catch on a two-point conversion in the fourth quarter to make it a 14-11 game.
Shaheed then set the offense up to tie the game when he had a 31-yard punt return with less than a minute to play. He also had a key reception on their final drive in regulation, picking up 10 yards on third-and-six.
Sam Darnold struggled in this game as the Denver defense had his number. While we knew the Broncos would make things difficult, Darnold was rattled by the pass rush and didn't do a good job avoiding pressure throughout the night.
The @Broncos defense get back-to-back sacks to close out the opening drive SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NRDh4ZbGVA
Darnold made several plays in the final quarter, but also had a late interception that could have cost them the game in regulation. He then threw another in overtime, which gave the Broncos the ball on the edge of field-goal range. Those picks will be a hot topic, especially since it was a problem for Darnold coming into the game.
Nick Emmanwori is healthy again. The second-year safety had ankle surgery in July and missed their Week1 win over the Patriots. He returned in Week 2 and eased his way back in over the next couple of weeks. On Thursday, he looked like the chess piece we remember from 2025.
Emmanwori was lined up all over the defense, playing safety, slot, and linebacker. He was even used as a pass rusher on multiple snaps, including a key third-down play in the fourth quarter. On that play, Emmanwori sacked Bo Nix, forcing the Broncos to punt following a three-and-out immediately after the Seahawks cut the lead to three.
While some of the sacks in this one were due to Darnold being unable to escape pressure, the fact remains that he was under pressure all night. It was hard to pinpoint any single offensive lineman as the one who struggled most, because the pressure was coming from everywhere. This was the second week in a row where Darnold was sacked at least five times and it's become a major issue.
The Seahawks finally got into the end zone more than halfway through the fourth quarter, and it was George Holani who scored the touchdown. What was most impressive was that he had consecutive impressive runs, beginning with a 13-yarder which included the offensive line helping to push him closer to the end zone.
George Holani gets in the end zone for the @Seahawks SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MzSqMm3DVs
He was finally taken down at the one-yard line and scored on the next play. This time, he avoided a tackle in the backfield and got into the end zone, which allowed the Seahawks to cut the lead to 14-11. Of course, the turnover by Darnold on the following drive doomed them, but Holani deserves credit for giving them a chance.
Throughout the night, the Seattle offense was sleepwalking. That wasn't the case with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who was once again their best weapon. JSN had 134 yards on 12 receptions, which wasn't enough to salvage the win, but was a reminder that he's one of the most dominant wide receivers in the NFL.

title: Elijah Arroyo Injury Update: Seahawks Tight End Leaves Late In Second Quarter
full_text:
It was about as bad a first half as you could have for the Seattle Seahawks, and it just got worse. With time running down towards the end of the first half, on a play where the Seahawks lost a fumble as well, they also may have lost Elijah Arroyo. Going down to dive on the ball, his arm was caught in a scrum and has gotten injured.
He was seen being led into the locker room with team staff holding his forearm, indicating an injury in that area. Not clearly related to the knee injury he had last season that placed him on IR late in the season, but its significance is to be determined. With the score 14-3 and Seattle trying to salvage some points before the half, nothing is going the way of the Seahawks tonight.
A few minutes later, he was declared by the Seahawks to be doubtful to return with a shoulder injury. All things considered, I can only assume he's not coming back today. Seattle has much bigger issues than their second string (at best) tight end, of course, but he remains a playmaker of note even if the team hasn't been able to unlock his abilities and potential yet.
The Seahawks actually had four tight ends active for this game anyway, five if you count Brady Russell, so I can't say there will be a massive impact from this. Arroyo is a complete afterthought in this offense for the time being. If anything, adding better blockers like Eric Saubert and Nick Kallerup to the mix might be more beneficial to this current situation.
Seattle needs to find a way to get into better situations on 2nd and 3rd down so they can sustain drives and give Darnold easier throws to convert. Arroyo, in theory, could help with that, but clearly the team hasn't figured that part out yet. And with the distinct possibility that he misses extended time given how quickly he was declared doubtful, that may not change.
Arroyo came into tonight's game having been targetted on only two passes this year, one a 17-yarder from Drew Lock and the other intercepted by the trailing defender. He's seen less than 30% of the total snaps. Eric Saubert has actually been on the field more than Arroyo, and despite his player profile has made more of an impact as a pass catcher. Onward.

title: New Seahawks 2027 NFL Mock Draft Lands Physical WR
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have one of the league's most complete defenses, which helped them win the second Super Bowl in franchise history last year. Offensively, they're very efficient as they enter Week 6 as the No. 8 team in points scored while being just 17th in overall yardage,.
Much of that has been thanks to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the 2025 NFL Offensive Player of the Year, who is off to another sensational start . In five games, JSN has 37 receptions for 583 yards with seven touchdowns. Considering their struggles on the ground, JSN has been the offense thus far, with the second-most receptions belonging to tight end A.J. Barner (12). As for yardage, only Barner and veteran Cooper Kupp have topped the 100-yard mark on the year.
That's why Bleacher Report's Brent Sobleski has the Seahawks targeting a wide receiver in the first round of his latest 2027 NFL mock draft, with Indiana's Nick Marsh being their pick.
As Sobleski said, Smith-Njigba has more targets than the next three players combined in Seattle. While that strategy led to a title in 2025, it's not sustainable, which is why he sees Marsh as a fit .
"Jaxon Smith-Njigba can't do it all. Or can he? The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year has been targeted more times this season than the Seattle Seahawks' next three receivers combined. Eventually, the Seahawks must find another threat in the passing game. Indiana's Nick Marsh has a similar playing style to Cooper Kupp's, which should make his inclusion an easy transition," Sobleski wrote.
"Marsh is a densely built and physical wide receiver. He has powerful hands and plays through the catch-point. The 6'3, 215-pound target is surprisingly quick in short areas and at the top of his routes. He's a good route-runner who creates space working against man coverage. The Michigan State transfer is also shifty after the catch to provide a well-rounded playmaker."
Through six games with the Hoosiers, Marsh has 29 receptions for 528 yards and six touchdowns. He's quickly approaching career highs during his first year with Indiana and has asserted himself as a first-round target.
In Seattle, they wouldn't ask Marsh to be a WR1, which could help him become an efficient player at the next level. Putting him opposite Smith-Njigba would give the Seahawks two smooth route runners, which would open up the offense for Sam Darnold.

title: Seahawks Could Break 661-Day Streak vs. Broncos on Thursday Night Football
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have experienced a lot of success over the last year or so, and losses have not come often.
Since the start of last season, the Seahawks have won 20 out of 25 games, including their three postseason wins en route to Super Bowl LX.
During that time frame, the Seahawks have not lost consecutive games. The last time the Seahawks were on a losing streak was in December 2024, when they lost a pair of games: Week 15 against the Green Bay Packers and Week 16 against the Minnesota Vikings, both at home. Those losses ultimately pushed the Seahawks out of the postseason picture, causing them to miss the playoffs despite winning in Weeks 17 and 18 to finish the year with a 10-7 record.
It's been an impressive run over the last two seasons for the Seahawks, but what they have shown is resilience in bouncing back after a loss. When they dropped the season opener against the San Francisco 49ers last season, they pulled out a two-score victory against the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road the following week. That's something the Seahawks will have to do once again if they want to keep pace in a very competitive NFC West.
In Week 5 of last year, the Seahawks dropped a tough three-point loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at home. Much like they did this past week against the Niners at Lumen Field, they were able to pull out a 20-12 victory against the Jacksonville Jaguars on the road, which was a tough AFC West opponent. The circumstances appear to be very similar with the Broncos now on deck.
Given the fact that the Seahawks are two games back of the 49ers in the division standings, a win in Week 6 is incredibly crucial for their long-term success.
The Seahawks returned to practice earlier in the week with a renewed focus and a sense of urgency, knowing that they had just dropped a game. They have proven every time in the last two seasons that they can turn the page quickly and come out of adversity on top. This is another big test of that, and they will get to prove themselves on a national stage.

title: Seahawks Confidence Meter: Passing Game Could Develop vs. Broncos
full_text:
It has been a rough few weeks for the Seattle Seahawks (3-2). After seeing some solid production in the Week 2  win over the Arizona Cardinals, the Seahawks' offense has stalled significantly in the last three games. One of the key factors has been the passing game seeing serious limitations. There is a chance that the Seahawks will see their passing game improve in Week 6 as they take on the Denver Broncos on the road.
​Last season, the Broncos finished with the third-best scoring defense, the seventh-best passing defense and the second-best run defense. The Broncos made a lot of moves that changed their defense, including the departure of linebacker Dre Greenlaw and safety Taylor Rapp. There are some big differences this season. Denver isn't as efficient at defending the running or passing game this season.
​Denver possesses the 11th-best passing defense and the third-worst run defense. One of the biggest reasons the Broncos are still good at defending the passing game during their rough defensive start is the stellar play of cornerback Pat Surtain II and safety Talanoa Hufanga. Both of those players are listed as out for the Thursday Night Football matchup . Riley Moss, the other starting cornerback opposite Surtain, is listed as questionable due to a rib injury.
​The Seahawks have a chance to create one of the most efficient and dynamic offenses again this season, despite a new offensive coordinator. The biggest concern is the self-inflicted mistakes within the last three weeks. The Seahawks turned the ball over eight times in the last three games, including four in the 32-29 Week 5 home loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Turnovers have cost the Seahawks two wins.
​There have been five interceptions from quarterback Sam Darnold over the last three weeks since returning from his glute injury. Darnold has to stop throwing interceptions and ruining great performances from wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Darnold is on pace to throw 25 interceptions this season, which is unacceptable for a Super Bowl-winning quarterback.
It hasn’t helped that the running game has been inefficient , inconsistent and turning the ball over. The offense got much worse since rookie running back Jadarian Price went on IR. Veterans Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have been turnover machines and, oftentimes, non-factors. The offensive line has struggled to get push at the line of scrimmage. There is more pressure for the passing game to come alive with Price out and Zach Charbonnet yet to return.
​The Seahawks’ passing offense has an opportunity to have a great breakout game with a good portion of the Broncos’ secondary out or injured. JSN is the league's leader in receiving yards (583), touchdowns (7) and big plays of 20 or more yards (9) through the first five weeks. He has been one of the most impressive pass-catchers this season, but the team can't put too much pressure on him or target him too often.
​The Seahawks will need more pass-catchers like wide receiver Rashid Shaheed, wide receiver Tory Horton and tight end A.J. Barner to step up. If Darnold and the passing game continue to struggle for a fourth consecutive week, it might be a long season for the reigning Super Bowl champions.

title: Seahawks vs. Broncos Week 6 Expert Pick Roundup: Can Seattle Bounce Back?
full_text:
Mike Macdonald has a short week to get his Seattle Seahawks ready following their frustrating loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 5. This week, the Seahawks will visit the Denver Broncos for a Thursday Night Football showdown .
Sometimes the short week can be a blessing, since it gives Seattle a chance to get the bad taste out of its mouth from their latest loss. Of course, it won't be easy since the Broncos are no pushover. They haven't been the same team we saw in 2025, but they were in the AFC Championship Game for a reason and can win against anyone.
With the stage set, let's checkout what various media outlets expect to happen on Thursday with a roundup of expert selections.
Pete Prisco is also chosing Seattle, and he believes the Broncos' offensive struggles will be the reason they fall short in this one.
"The Seahawks lost a tough one to the 49ers last week and now face a short week on the road against Denver. The Broncos' offense has struggled, even with Sean Payton taking over as the play-caller. Bo Nix has to pick it up, but this is a tough defense to try and fix things. Seattle takes a tough road game," Prisco wrote. "Pick: Seahawks 23, Broncos 17"
The experts are heavily favoring the Seahawks, with only one pick going for the home team. Of course, with the game being on Thursday, not every outlet had their full predictions ready, but it's still interesting to see how heavily favored Seattle is going into this one.
For me, I see Macdonald being able to get his team focused following the loss. The Seahawks should go into this one with the right mindset, which is the norm for them following a defeat. That said, the Broncos aren't a team that should be overlooked and Sean Payton is an elite coach in his own right. That said, the Seahawks escape with a win on the road, setting them up for a mini-bye before taking on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7.
Prediction: Seahawks 24, Broncos 20

title: 3 Bold Predictions For Seahawks vs. Broncos in Week 6
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have a short week as they travel to the Mile High City to take on the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football in Week 6.
Seattle is coming off a disheartening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 5, falling 32-29 to their undefeated NFC West rival. They're now 3-2, which is the same record as the Broncos, who are also 2-0 at home this season and fresh off a win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
For the Seahawks, a win would do wonders for their confidence and would allow them to stay within strking distance of the 49ers. Securing a win could be more possible for them should they make good on the following three bold predictions.
Emanuel Wilson has been taking a lot of heat his year since stepping into a more prominent role. With Jadarian Price injured, Wilson has taken the top spot in the backfield but has yet to take off. In Week 5, he had just 3.1 yards per attempt, going for 61 yards on 20 attempts. He did score a touchdown, but also lost a fumble.
The good news for Wilson is that Denver hasn't been great against the run this year. They're ranked 29th against the run, surrendering 726 yards through five games . That should help Wilson put together a strong performance, and in this bold prediction, he rushes for over 100 yards for the first time as a Seahawk.
Byron Murphy II was a disruptive force once again in Week 5, recording two sacks against the 49ers. He's now tied with fellow defensive lineman Leonard Williams for the team lead with three on the year.
Bo Nix has been sacked six times in five games, which isn't terrible, but the Seahawks have the talent to add to that total. In our second bold prediction, both Murphy and Williams record a sack on Nix as the Seattle defense makes life tough on the home team.
Sam Darnold had a rough outing in Week 5, throwing two interceptions. He now has five interceptions over the past three games, which has been a major concern for the Seattle offense. If they're going to get a win on Thursday, the Seahawks need Darnold to protect the ball. In our final bold prediction, he does that as he plays the entire game without a turnover.

title: Seahawks Should Give Velus Jones Jr. Chance to Contribute vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks made minor adjustments to their roster on Wednesday, signing running back Velus Jones Jr. from the practice squad and releasing wide receiver Irv Charles. Seattle re-signed Charles to the practice squad afterward.
It was mostly just small roster manipulation , as the move comes one day after activating Charles from injured reserve, releasing Jones and re-signing him to the practice squad. Those players have now swapped places, as the Seahawks had to initially activate Charles to the active roster.
Jones has been on the 53-man roster but has only played two offensive snaps in his four appearances this season. Will he play a bigger role in Week 6?
Despite being active for four games, Jones has mostly been a contributor on special teams. He's played 61 snaps in that phase, which is 49% of the team's total special teams snaps.
The Seahawks aren't getting Zach Charbonnet back this week, and Jadarian Price is also still on injured reserve. That leaves them with the same stable of Emanuel Wilson, George Holani and Jones. Holani and Wilson have a combined four fumbles between the two of them, and two of them resulted in turnovers.
Seattle needs a spark at running back. Jones might not be the top option to provide that, but he's the third rusher for a reason. If the Seahawks are going to keep him on the roster, not sign anyone else, and the rest of their backs are struggling, it only makes sense to use all their depth.
Charbonnet will hopefully return in Week 7, but Seattle still has to get through a tough matchup against the Denver Broncos on Thursday night. A loss would give the San Francisco 49ers an even bigger lead in the NFC West standings, and that could be tough to battle back from if they don't get back on track.
At full strength, Charbonnet and Price should be the Seahawks' top two running backs. They don't have either, so Jones could be a change of pace that helps them get a win. He's a speedy runner who has returned kicks for the team this season, providing open-field upside.
It can't get much worse in the backfield. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury has nothing to lose by giving Jones a few carries and seeing how he performs.

title: 49ers Have Bigger Problem Than Pass Rush at Deadline
full_text:
As the San Francisco 49ers get closer to the trade deadline , there are going to be many suggestions for the team to add a pass rusher. However, as the days get closer to the deadline, it is becoming clearer that the run defense is the area San Francisco must pay attention to.
The 49ers edge rusher room entered the year thin. However, they just got Mykel Williams back, and they are expected to see Nick Bosa in the lineup any week. In the time that those two were out, they were able to get rookie Romello Height some experience. With Keion White in the mix, they could be set here.
The issue is run defense, particularly along the interior. Osa Odighizuwa and Gracen Halton lead the 49ers in snaps on the interior. They are both much better as pass rushers than run defenders. Odighizuwa has a 66 pass rush grade and 32 run defense grade, per PFF. Halton is at 72 in pass rush grade and 53 in run defense.
Whether the grades are entirely accurate, they do represent the difference in play. The two interior linemen who were supposed to be run defenders were C.J. West and Alfred Collins. Those two are on the IR.
So far, the 49ers have not had to pay for this. They have been able to gain leads, and teams have to shift away from the run.
That is why they rank 4th in run defense according to EPA/play but 24th in success rate. On a down-by-down basis, the team is giving up yards. However, it is not costing them overall because teams cannot lean on it, and they are not allowing big plays, thanks to Fred Warner and the back end.
Still, they rank 24th in success rate despite not facing a rushing attack in the top 15 so far this season. That includes the Rams, who have improved, but trailed against San Francisco and veered away from the running game.
Miami, Seattle, Denver, and Arizona have all had problems in their run game for one reason or another. At some point, the team is going to face a team that is able to move the ball and stick to running the ball against the 49ers. Until then, the 49ers will try to find a solution on the front line.

title: 49ers Have New Reason to Pass on WR Trade
full_text:
One of the positions that is most tied to the San Francisco 49ers in trade talks is wide receiver. The team has been linked to aging options, rentals, and long-term options. However, while the room looks thin right now, it might not be a position the team needs to address.
The  49ers just opened the 21-day practice window for wide receiver Christian Kirk. Kirk has been on the PUP since the start of training camp, but when he is healthy, he is still a reliable wideout. The team is just a couple of weeks away from activating him.
Demarcus Robinson suffered an ankle injury in Week 2. He is expected to have his practice window opened in the next week or two. So, Kirk could be back by Week 7, and Robinson as soon as Week 8.
Deebo Samuel is out now, but is only expected to miss a couple of weeks. A return before Week 10 is likely. Lastly, the expected return date for De’Zhaun Stribling is around Week 12.
By the time the 49ers leave the Thanksgiving weekend of football, they might have a healthy wide receiver room. That is still a ways away, but the team is sitting at 5-0. They are not planning to lose, but they do realize that even if they did lose a few games, they would get to Week 12 with a record that has them firmly in the mix.
If they went 3-3 over the next six games while their wide receiver corps is banged up, they will be 8-3 and will be getting healthy at the right time. Considering the 5-0 start, 3-3 sounds like a worst-case scenario for this team.
As things stand, the room looks questionable at best. However, if they are sitting at 8-3 or better and have Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, De’Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, and Christian Kirk, it will look like one of the best rooms in the NFL.
Staying patient, letting each receiver come back on their timeline, and having the room at full strength for the playoffs is the 49ers' top priority. With all of the risks for re-injury, it would not be out of the question for the 49ers to trade for a wide receiver.
At the same time, if the 49ers stay firm and lean on their depth at receiver it could be better than they realize.

title: 49ers WR Mike Evans Misses Week 6 Practice With New Injury
full_text:
49ers star wide receiver Mike Evans is being held out of the first Week 6 practice with a new injury. Along with his rib fracture, Kyle Shanahan revealed that Evans is out with an Achilles injury.
Shanahan said Evans was dealing with soreness and that there isn't any significant concern about it. However, anytime you hear Achilles being associated with a player, it's difficult not to worry.
Evans is coming off a big-time performance with big-time usage against the Seahawks. He's four days removed from the game. Yet he's still feeling soreness in his Achilles.
It's smart of the 49ers to hold out on Evans, which they'd probably do anyway since he has a rib injury. But now that he has an Achilles issue, it's something to keep a close eye on.
I'd guess the 49ers will keep Evans out of practice on Friday as well, then let him on the field on Saturday in a limited capacity.
That said, if Evans continues to feel soreness in his Achilles in a few days, they shouldn't play him against the Commanders on Monday night. It would be reckless of them to allow him to play.
An Achilles injury is no joke. I'm sure Evans will think he's good to go, but this is a case of protecting the player for himself. It doesn't matter if the 49ers are thin at wide receiver.
There's never a desperate enough scenario in a regular-season game for a player to tough out an Achilles issue. Saturday will be the biggest indicator of where he's at with it.
Evans wasn't the only player to be held out of Thursday's practice. Five other players were missing due to injury.
All five were the usual suspects: Nick Bosa (calf), James Thompson Jr. (ankle), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Marques Sigle (ankle), and Garrett Wallow (hamstring).
On Monday, Shanahan insinuated that Bosa might play against the Commanders , but that doesn't seem likely anymore given his comments when he was asked about today.
It's safe to say that all of the players who were out of practice today, minus Evans, will not be active in Week 6. All eyes will and should be on Evans' status throughout the week.
If the 49ers have any doubt about his Achilles, they must hold him out no matter what.

title: The Trade the 49ers Must Make Before the Deadline if they're Serious
full_text:
If the 49ers don't win the Super Bowl this season, they might never win it.
They have the best team in the NFL. They're injured, but they still have roughly six future Hall of Famers on the field who are still playing at a high level. They just beat the defending Super Bowl champions in their stadium. This is the year to go all-in. If that means trading a first-round pick, so be it.
But which position should the 49ers target before the deadline?
Two jump to mind: wide receiver and defensive line. Let's discuss wide receiver first . The 49ers have so many injuries at this position that they currently are down to Mike Evans (who has broken ribs), Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing and Brandin Cooks. If Evans misses time, the 49ers are in trouble.
At defensive line, the 49ers are coming off a five-sack performance. Rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton has been a revelation. Veteran defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa is a good player. And former Defensive Player of the Year Nick Bosa should be returning from a knee/calf injury soon.
So it seems that wide receiver is the bigger need.
But it's not. Head coach Kyle Shanahan is creative enough to work around his lack of depth at wide receiver. He did it just a few days ago when he orchestrated a touchdown drive against the Seahawks in the fourth quarter after Deebo Samuel left the game with a hamstring injury.
In addition, the 49ers' injured wide receivers should come back at some point. Demarcus Robinson, De'Zhaun Stribling and Samuel did not suffer season-ending injuries. Theoretically, all or some of them will contribute down the stretch.
Bosa's return is less clear. He's trying to recover from his third ACL repair, and it's not going smoothly. He still hasn't been a full participant in a practice yet this year. He might be limited for the rest of the season. Which means he might be in and out of the lineup depending on the week.
The 49ers can't just cross their fingers and hope that Bosa makes a full recovery this season. They have to trade for a closer on the defensive line who can sack the quarterback to end the game if Bosa isn't healthy enough to do that.
The 49ers defense is good without Bosa, but it lacks a closer. Last year in Seattle, Bosa ended the game by stripping the ball away from Sam Darnold on the final drive. This year in Seattle, the 49ers won because Jaxon Smith-Njigba dropped a pass when he was wide open downfield, and then Cooper Kupp got pushed out of bounds a foot in front of the first-down marker. They got lucky.
That's why they need to trade for a designated edge rusher. That's why Bryce Huff was last season, and that's what Romello Height is supposed to be now. But he's a rookie with one sack. They can't rely on him.
They should trade for Khalil Mack. The Chargers aren't going anywhere, which means they need to trade their aging vets for draft picks.
If the 49ers can find a better edge rusher than Mack, go for it. But they have to get someone at this position.

title: One 49ers Position is Surpassing Preseason Expectations
full_text:
It’s not that surprising to see the San Francisco 49ers start the season 5-0. They were always going to be a strong playoff contender.
Maybe they’re a little better than projected, but it’s not stunning. What is surprising is the performance of one 49ers position group. This group is surpassing every preseason expectation of them.
The safety position. By far, it was the seemingly weakest position on the 49ers entering 2026. They made zero significant additions to it, which meant it was stagnant.
The 49ers were content to roll with the same trio from last year. Ji’Ayir Brown has never lived up to his promising rookie season. He was penciled in as a mediocre player and a liability if he were the starter.
Malik Mustapha struggled last season as well after coming back from a torn ACL. His pass coverage skills left a lot to be desired, and his best strength, which is playing in the box, was lost last year. He missed numerous tackles and took poor angles towards ball carriers.
Marques Sigle was the only safety with a real chance to ascend this year. He was solid in run support, aggressive, and fairly sound in coverage. However, he’d freak out when he was targeted.
Sigle showed zero ball skills. Almost every time he was targeted, he’d allow a catch. But that all changed in five games this season. Brown, Mustapha, and Sigle are all playing incredibly well.
The fact that Brown hasn’t been at the forefront of mistakes is telling. It means he’s playing much more disciplined than he ever has. Now, he’s still made a few mistakes this season, but it’s not much.
Mustapha looks like he’s stepped up from last year and is picking up where he left off in his rookie season. He got his first start this season against the Seahawks and made his hard-hitting presence known.
“I thought he played unbelievable,” said Kyle Shanahan. “He’s been waiting for that moment and he was ready for it. He did a hell of a job.”
Mustapha is making it difficult to keep him off the field as the starter, with Sigle on the mend. It’s a bummer because Sigle was soaring before he suffered a high ankle sprain.
“I think he's been playing his ass off in the run and pass game,” Shanahan said. “The way he's filled on some of these tackles, just how solid he's hit people and how quickly he's done it getting up in there. I thought he's done it good in the pass game too.”
All three safeties deserve credit for how well they’re playing, but especially defensive coordinator Raheem Morris for unlocking them. They were never a mediocre bunch.
They just needed the right coach.

title: How the 49ers Will Likely Lose Their First Game This Season
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are riding high with a 5-0 record.
They show no signs of slowing down, and there’s zero reason to think they will. Their next two opponents will be the Washington Commanders and the Atlanta Falcons.
Those two teams shouldn’t cause much of a struggle for the 49ers. However, there is one aspect of their team that’s been a struggle all season, and it will likely be the reason they lose their first game this season.
It will be kicker Eddy Pineiro missing multiple kicks. Maybe it’ll be one missed extra point and one missed field goal, or it’ll be multiple missed extra points or multiple missed field goals.
Whichever way it plays out, their first loss of the season feels like it will come when Pineiro shanks his kicks. He’s been doing it already, and it hasn’t cost the 49ers yet.
But given how electric the 49ers have started the year, this is the most likely way for them to lose a game. Pineiro will be their undoing and cost them a game.
Now, it probably won’t be 100% on him. Brock Purdy could end up having one of his multi-interception games. He’s good for at least one a season. And perhaps the defense has an extremely off day.
But when it comes down to it, Pineiro will be the one who sinks them. He’s arguably been their biggest liability this season. It just hasn’t been an issue because they’ve been winning.
Imagine if Pineiro missed the game-winning field goal against the Seattle Seahawks. I mean, he almost missed it. His kick wasn’t clean, so he clearly has a bit of the yips.
It isn’t Jake Moody level, but it’s a scary spot for the 49ers to be in nonetheless. This puts added pressure on them to avoid games becoming a kicker battle. They can’t have a win be determined by Pineiro.
Just look at what happened to the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. Sean McVay left it up to his kicker, and what happened? They lost the game.
The circumstances are different because the kick was blocked, and the Rams have the worst special teams unit in the league. But their kicker isn’t reliable, and the fact that they left it up to a field goal cost them.
That cannot be the 49ers. But it’s likely going to happen at least once. They'd better hope Pineiro finds his rhythm soon. If his struggles continue as the playoffs approach, they’ll be in a sketchy spot.

title: Examining Cost for 49ers Potential Garrett Wilson Blockbuster Trade
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have been connected to many wide receivers on the trade market. However, the biggest name brought up so far would have to be Garrett Wilson of the New York Jets. Kay Adams had Rob Guerrera of ESPN Radio on her U p and Adams Sho w, and he made the case for the 49ers to add the 26-year-old.
“You’re 5-0; you control the division now,” Guerrera told Adams. “You desperately need a wide receiver; I'm sorry, Jacob Cowing ain't it.”
Despite the New York Jets being 2-3 and winning in Week 5, Guerrera suggests the 49ers call them to inquire about a Wilson trade.
Garrett Wilson or Terry McLaurin in red and gold? Rob "Stats" Guerrera says the 49ers front office should be AGGRESSIVE in the trade market 🍿 @StatsOnFire | @heykayadams pic.twitter.com/LRVLJq3lQb
“I would call the Jets up,” said Guerrera. “Where are the Jets going? Nowhere fast. What do you want for Garrett Wilson? Do you want a first-round pick? Let's talk about it.”
The cost of a first-round pick likely stems from Jaylen Waddle, whom the Denver Broncos traded for this offseason. Denver sent the 30th overall pick, along with a third- and fourth-round pick for Waddle and a fourth-round pick. Considering San Francisco is likely to pick late in round one, this is a fair consideration for return.
When the Broncos traded for Waddle, he had just signed a three-year, $85M deal, averaging $28.2M per year. Meanwhile, Wilson signed a four-year, $130M deal. So, he is averaging $32.5M per year.
Wilson has 346 career catches for 4,018 yards and 21 touchdowns. This year, he has 31 receptions for 374 yards. Meanwhile, Waddle has 391 receptions for 5,243 yards and 27 touchdowns. Waddle is two years older and has one more year of NFL experience.
The other factor that might lean toward Wilson costing more than Waddle is the reality that the Jets General Manager who extended Wilson is still employed. The General Manager who extended Waddle is no longer with the Miami Dolphins. Miami was interested in moving on from Waddle, while the Jets would need to be enticed to move on from Wilson.
He is younger and signed for longer. He might cost more, but that would speak to his talent being on par with, or greater than, Waddle. So, the 49ers would need more than a first-round pick. The question is how much more?
Expecting the 49ers to add at the deadline is fair, but going all-in on Wilson might be costly.

title: Raheem Morris is Already Proving the 49ers Right for Hiring Him
full_text:
Arguably, the best offseason addition the San Francisco 49ers made this year was hiring Raheem Morris as defensive coordinator.
The level at which he has the 49ers' defense performing is astonishing. Through five games this season, the 49ers are allowing 297.2 yards per game, the sixth-fewest in the NFL.
Most importantly, they're only allowing 18.6 points per game, the third-lowest in the league. Those numbers are impressive, but even those stats don't perfectly represent Morris' impact.
Look no further than how the 49ers' secondary is playing. They've been lights-out, which you couldn't fathom last year. They weren't remotely impressive under Robert Saleh.
That's the key difference between Saleh and Morris . It's why Morris is already proving the 49ers right for hiring him. His secondary is performing incredibly well, and they're doing it without much help from their pass rush.
The 49ers rank as the 12th-lowest-pressure-rate defense at 34.2%. And I know they balled out against the Seattle Seahawks, sacking Sam Darnold five times.
However, that can be a credit to the secondary. Darnold wasn't confident enough to throw to his receivers since they were guarded so tightly.
And when he did have confidence, he was picked off twice by Renardo Green. He's been balling out this year, along with the rest of the defensive backs, and it's thanks to Morris' scheme.
“It doesn't surprise me with Raheem. I've just been around him for too long. He's one of the best people and best coaches I've ever been around," Kyle Shanahan said. "I tried to bring him here originally when I left Atlanta. They wouldn't let him out. So, it's been a long time coming to get him here.
"He's done an unbelievable job this year, especially with the injuries, but just overall everything he's mixed up schematically. I love the confidence he's given our DBs and the way they've been playing since training camp. He's had a real huge effect on this team and we're very lucky to have him.”
Morris has the secondary playing at a different level. They're playing with a ton of fire thanks to him. It's no wonder every defensive back said they were excited to play for Morris.
And to think, it's only been five games. How much better can this defense get as they continue to ascend?
Just imagine how this secondary will look with Bosa back, and maybe another pass rusher. They will take their already sweet defense to nightmarish heights.

title: 2 Overlooked Stats Show How Elite the 49ers Offense Is
full_text:
The 49ers' offense has been on a tear this season. Brock Purdy is playing as sharp as ever, Mike Evans is dominating, George Kittle is insane, and the offensive line is elite.
All of that is contributing to the 49ers averaging 30.8 points per game, the third-most in the NFL. They also average 365 yards per game, the ninth-most in the NFL.
Those stats are nice and all, but there are a couple of overlooked ones that show how elite the 49ers' offense is. Let's dive into what those two overlooked stats are.
Negative Play % through Week 5 pic.twitter.com/Uun49NjhMS
One reason the 49ers put up a bunch of yards is that they consistently gain positive yardage. They have the second-lowest negative play percentage in the NFL at just under 4%.
You could argue that they're truly the top offense at limiting negative plays instead of the Broncos, since their quarterback, Bo Nix, loves to play it safe, as he did against the 49ers with a ton of checkdown throws.
In any case, having 96% of the plays called and executed going for a positive gain is vastly impressive. This shows that Purdy is connecting well with his receivers and kept clean on his dropbacks.
The running game is also running effectively with Christian McCaffrey and rookie Kaelon Black. Kyle Shanahan deserves a round of applause as well.
His game plan and feel for calling the right plays at the right time play a crucial role in their offense being ranked the second-lowest for negative plays. They're easily an unstoppable force with this depiction.
red zone touchdown rate this season: 87.5% - San Francisco 49ers 83.3% - Dallas Cowboys 81.3% - New Orleans Saints 77.3% - Detroit Lions 73.7% - Baltimore Ravens 71.4% - Buffalo Bills 69.2% - Atlanta Falcons 68.4% - Los Angeles Rams 66.7% - Indianapolis Colts 64.7% - Carolina…
The reward for having less than 4% negative plays and tallying a bunch of yards is red zone trips. And whenever the 49ers get there, they maximize their opportunity.
The 49ers are scoring a touchdown on 87.5% of their red zone trips this season, the most in the league. This is crucial to why their offense has been a problem for opposing defenses.
Anytime the 49ers get into the red zone, they're most likely going to score a touchdown. That is the difference between elite and good offenses.
They don't settle for field goals, which is a testament to Evans. He's given the 49ers a phenomenal boost in the red zone, especially when they're near the goal line.
Purdy has done an excellent job of putting it in the perfect spot for Evans. The 49ers' offense is riding high, and now that they've gotten past the Seahawks, it's unlikely any defense will slow them down in the near future.

title: How the 49ers’ Improved Defense Takes them to Another Level
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers (5-0) defeated the Seattle Seahawks (3-2) 32-29, beating their divisional foe and the defending Super Bowl champions after the 49ers' loss to Seattle in two pivotal games to end last season.
The 49ers' offense is similar to last season's, but has improved with Brock Purdy taking a step forward and the free-agent signing of Mike Evans. But what stood out in the 49ers' win in Seattle was the improvement from their defense.
In three games last season, San Francisco forced just two turnovers against the Seahawks; on Sunday, the team doubled that, with four turnovers: two interceptions and two fumbles recovered.
“I thought the D was unbelievable today. I mean to get us those four turnovers that was the difference between winning and losing today,” coach Kyle Shanahan said postgame.“To be able to get those points off those turnovers I thought they limited their explosives defended the run well.”
Seattle's offense has gotten weaker, losing running back Kenneth Walker to the Kansas City Chiefs in free agency.
But the 49ers' hiring of defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, offseason additions, and young players developing from last year have helped the unit reach a new level.
So far, Morris’ defense allows 18.6 points per game, down from 22.7 that the 49ers averaged last season.
49ers linebacker Fred Warner, who missed the last two games against Seattle last season, returned to the rivalry, forcing one fumble while leading the team with 10 tackles.
His presence alone improved the defense's outlook, along with a standout performances from rookie defensive lineman Gracen Halten who had three tackles, two tackles for loss a sack and a forced fumble in which he recovered for a touchdown.
Linebacker Jayden Dugger, who had one sack and two tackles for loss. Dugger filled in well for outside linebacker Dre Greenlaw, who was disqualified in the second quarter . This 49ers rookie class has made a meaningful impact.
Morris has also improved the team's secondary, allowing 199 passing yards per game, down from 222 passing yards in 2025.
Morris has significantly helped develop cornerback Renardo Green, who leads the team with three interceptions this season, two against Seattle. In previous seasons, Green has only had one interception in his career.
“Renardo’s ceiling is very high. I think he can be a very good corner in this league and he’s showing that,” Shanahan said. “I mean, he was big time today; it wasn’t just the two picks but stopping the slant there at the end when they were right in that field goal range.”
A big surprise has been its safeties, which are a unit many had concerns about heading into this season.
Ji'Ayir Brown has taken a step forward, already recording 34 tackles, nearly half as many as he had in any other full season (76.5).
Additionally, Morris has improved one of the 49ers' most injury-plagued units, the defensive line. Morris has been more aggressive with his pass rush than previous coordinators, getting 2.2 sacks per game. Last year, the 49ers averaged 1.2 sacks per game.
The 49ers will also get defensive end Nick Bosa back, who sustained a calf injury in Week 1. He has been limited and has struggled with injuries over the last two seasons, but anything he provides will help the unit.

title: 3 Questions Facing Buccaneers Against Steelers in Week 6: Will Tampa Bay Stop This Crucial Steelers Player?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a tough task on Sunday. They're looking to move to 1-4, but they'll try and do it against a stout 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers team heading into Tampa Bay.
The Bucs got their first win of the year against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5, but now, they'll have another test. Here are three questions we have for head coach Todd Bowles' squad as Sunday rolls around:
It's rare that one player leads a team in both rushing and receiving, but Jaylin Warren is a rare player. Warren has 410 yards and one touchdown on the ground, but he also has 230 yards and a touchdown receiving, too.
At +0.131 EPA/play, Warren is the sixth-best running back in the NFL by that metric, and he's slated to do some serious damage on Sunday. The Bucs have to know where he is at all times and be able to contain him on the ground and through the air, and Bowles knows very well how good Warren is.
“I mean, he's been playing outstanding at running, blocking and pass receiving. You really don't see [all of that] from one guy," Bowles said. "He's doing everything. He's a very good pass protector. He's an outstanding runner, and he can catch the ball very well, and he makes you miss. [If] you miss a tackle, a guy like that, if you don't wrap up, he's going to take it to the house. So, he's been playing great football.”
Bucky Irving went off for 165 yards against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday night. He probably won't do that again (probably) — but how well will he and the Bucs do?
The Steelers give up 103.4 rushing yards per game on average. They rank 13th there and 17th in the NFL in yards per rush (4.0), so they're a decent run-stopping unit. Tampa Bay had a great game in Week 5 to inflate the average, but they're fifth in the NFL in yards per rush (4.9) and they're seventh in rush yards per game (133.0).
If Tampa Bay is going to win this game against the Steelers, they'll simply have to get the ground game rolling. Irving instills a lot of confidence that this will happen, but it remains to be seen until game day comes around.
Aaron Rodgers, so far this season, has a sack rate of 6.97%, the 11th-most-sacked quarterback in the NFL. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers can't really get to the quarterback at all — the entire defense has a sack rate of 3.49%, which is good for 30th in the league.
Rodgers is largely immobile at his age, but the Bucs haven't been able to generate a pass rush at all. It will be Rodgers' instinct to get rid of the ball quickly, which will make it harder for Tampa Bay to bring him down. That obviously includes the edge rushers, but interior pass rushers like Calijah Kancey could have a day against Rodgers — if the middle collapses, Rodgers has nowhere to go.
Tampa Bay has been trying to figure out its pass rush for years now. Rodgers is a prime candidate to do so, but can players like Kancey, Yaya Diaby and Rueben Bain Jr. get home on Sunday?

title: Todd Bowles May Have Revealed The Buccaneers’ Next Breakout Star
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers expected a lot out of their rookie class in 2026. They really focused on defense and drafted an edge rusher in the first round, bringing in Rueben Bain Jr. from Miami, and they also selected a linebacker in the second round by picking Missouri's Josiah Trotter.
Some of those picks, like Bain, haven't yet panned out the way the Bucs have hoped. Others, like Trotter, have looked really strong so far this season — but there's one defensive rookie who may have impressed more than any Bucs draft pick.
Head coach Todd Bowles spoke to media on Wednesday, and he revealed which Bucs player he thinks has been one of the best players on the team so far — and it's one of Tampa Bay's drafted rookies.
Bowles said that nickel cornerback Keionte Scott, whom the Bucs drafted in the fourth round in April out of Miami, has been one of his best players so far in 2026, and he commended his ability to tackle and his work ethic throughout the week.
“[Scott has] been one of our best players this year. I mean, he doesn't say much. He's been very solid with his fundamentalist technique, and he tackles way more than he weighs. He tackles almost like a linebacker. He's a very tough kid, wants to be good, wants to be great, extremely tough, puts in the work during the week. That's what you really like about him. He really studies and gets it down for Sunday, and he executes well.”
Scott has played well at the nickel position so far. The Bucs defense puts up −0.179 EPA with him on the field and +0.011 with him off, showing that the team is more effective when he is playing. So far this season, he has 24 solo tackles (one tackle for loss) and two passes defended.
"I think first is the want-to," Scott said. "That's something you can just tell right away about a back, if he wants to stick his head in the fan... I'm one of those guys that's proud to have that in my toolbox, have that in my game — I just wanna get in there."
Scott will continue to get snaps at nickel as the defense starts to gel. He'll have a big test on Sunday when the Bucs face off against the Steelers in Raymond James Stadium at 1 p.m.

title: Buccaneers Thursday Practice All But Confirms Starting Quarterback vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers play the Pittsburgh Steelers in just three days. Every game for the Bucs is important from here on out, as the team is 1-4 and needs to start stacking wins if it has any hope of making the playoffs.
Head coach Todd Bowles said after the team's win against the Dallas Cowboys last Thursday that undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who is filling in for starter Baker Mayfield as he recovers from a dislocated thumb, was preparing to start again against the Steelers.
But Mayfield was reportedly pushing to play, per NFL insider James Palmer, and the Buccaneers tested his grip ability by watching him throw on Wednesday afternoon.
Coach Baker Mayfield could return to player Baker Mayfield next week against the Steelers. I'm told Mayfield is pushing to play but it's 10 days out and it's too early for the Bucs to know medically if he can go. The stitches were taken out Monday and it's a matter of his thumb…
The Buccaneers conducted practice on Thursday, though, and that practice virtually confirmed Mayfield's status against the Steelers this Sunday.
Mayfield once again did not practice on Thursday, with Jalon Daniels taking the brunt of the first-team reps. It's unknown how Mayfield's throwing session went, but the team doesn't seem to want him back at practice just yet.
With that, Daniels is set for his third NFL start. Daniels comes into the game having thrown for 337 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions — he's also run for 87 yards. The undrafted rookie hasn't played perfectly, but he's impressed with his ability to run the offense competently, and he's gone a long way to prove the Bucs made the right decision to have him as QB2.
A likely target for Mayfield's return will be in Week 7. The Buccaneers play the Carolina Panthers in their first divisional game, and Mayfield will be beyond the three-week minimum that Bowles previously revealed after he was injured against the Minnesota Vikings.
For now, though, the Bucs remain Daniels' team to lead heading into Week 6. The Bucs will face off against the Steelers at 1 p.m. on Oct. 18 in Raymond James Stadium and will look to continue what would be the start of a long and grueling turnaround in 2026.

title: Have the Buccaneers Found Their Offensive Identity for the 2026 Season?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got their first win of the season against the Dallas Cowboys. It was a back-and-forth game where the defense was able to do enough to help get the win, but a bigger storyline coming out of the game is the offense.
It feels like for the first time this season, the Bucs offense was in sync and able to find its footing. This was mainly due to the work of Zac Robinson, which limited what Jalon Daniels needed to do for this offense and the great running ability of back Bucky Irving.
Irving really has come back to form this season, posting 21 carries for 165 yards and a rushing touchdown against Dallas as well as two catches for ten yards and a touchdown as well. Irving already has 77 carries for 406 rushing yards and two touchdowns this season, only 182 yards away from his total last year in 2025, playing in half as many games to this point.
I believe that the Bucs' offensive identity in 2026 will literally run through Bucky Irving, something that shouldn't be too surprising when we look at Zac Robinson's history as offensive coordinator in Atlanta.
Robinson ran both Bijan Robinson and Tyler Allgeier wild in 2024 and 2025, with both backs combined having 441 carries for 2100 rushing yards and 17 rushing touchdowns as well as 74 receptions for 519 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown in 2024. In 2025, it was 430 carries for 1992 rushing yards and 15 rushing touchdowns along with 93 receptions for 916 receiving yards and four receiving touchdowns.
I think that the team does need to see more usage from Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker going forward, but it's very clear that Robinson plans to use Irving in some type of Bijan role going forward with this team.
There are pros and cons to this type of identity, as many expected players like Baker Mayfield, Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. to lead the way for this offense this season. However, the positive is that it could help Mayfield button up some of the offensive struggles he had before his injury this season and limit turnovers overall.
Time will tell if this formula will work for Tampa Bay in the long run, but it seems like we've had a glimpse into what Robinson wants to do going forward.

title: Buccaneers Wednesday Practice Updates: Is Baker Mayfield Back?

Mayfield has been trying to work his way back sooner rather than later. But did he return to practice on Wednesday to test out his thumb ahead of the Steelers matchup Sunday? We have the latest update on Mayfield and more from Wednesday's practice:
Mayfield did not return to practice on Wednesday. He appears to still be recovering from his dislocated thumb — the stitches in his thumb have reportedly been taken out, but he still needs to find the strength to grip the football, and he may not be there yet.
In other injury news, both running back Sean Tucker and cornerback Ayden Garnes were working off to the side with a trainer on Wednesday.

title: Buccaneers Could Get Wide Receiver Back vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers had what they considered to be quite a deep wide receivers corps heading into 2026. Unfortunately, that idea hasn't exactly shown up on the turf through Week 5.
Wideouts Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, both considered to be focal points of the offense, haven't produced relative to expectations. Jalen McMillan, expected to be a valuable weapon for the Bucs, has played just one game so far this season, and he's currently recovering from a knee injury.
Other wideouts, like rookie Ted Hurst and second-year player Tez Johnson, have had to step up in McMillan's place.
But now, the Bucs may be getting back another wide receiver they've been missing all year to help bolster that receiving corps, and he could come back as soon as Sunday when the Buccaneers play the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Bucs wideout David Sills V, who injured himself during training camp with a hamstring injury and was placed on injured reserve, opened his 21-day practice window on Monday. Sills will get his first bit of practice for the first time in a long time on Wednesday as the Bucs prepare for the Steelers.
Sills is a big-bodied wideout who could help Tampa Bay on the outside. He played with Zac Robinson last season with the Atlanta Falcons, so Robinson knows how to use him and the two understand each other's offensive goals quite well.
With McMillan still out, Sills could end up being valuable depth for the Bucs — if Tampa Bay wants to make use of him. Sills has 21 days from Oct. 12 to get back on the field and return to Tampa Bay's active roster. If he does not do so within those 21 days, he remains on IR and must remain there until the end of the season.
As it stands, Tampa Bay's 53-man roster is full. That means that if the Bucs want Sills on the active roster, they'll have to move another player off to make room — that player could go to Tampa Bay's practice squad or get released entirely.
If Sills is able to get back in time for Tampa Bay's game against the Steelers, quarterback Jalon Daniels will have another weapon to work with on offense. If not, he could shoot for the week after against the Carolina Panthers, where starting QB Baker Mayfield will likely be quarterback after he recovers from his thumb injury.
The Bucs play the Steelers on Oct. 18 in Raymond James Stadium.
